Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 33, verse 1–3:

Tafsir of Surat al-Ahzab

It is a Madinan surah.

ʿAbdullah ibn al-Imam Ahmad said: Khalaf ibn Hisham narrated to us, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from ʿAsim ibn Bahdalah, from Zirr, who said: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb said to me: "How many verses do you recite in Surat al-Ahzab, or how many do you count it as?" I said: "Seventy-three verses." He said: "Qat! I have seen it when it was equal to Surat al-Baqarah, and we used to recite in it: 'The old man and the old woman, if they commit adultery, then stone them absolutely as a punishment from Allah, and Allah is Mighty and Wise.'" [Musnad (5/132).]

An-Nasa'i narrated it through another chain, from ʿAsim, who is Ibn Abi al-Nujud, who is Ibn Bahdalah, with the same wording. [Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (7150).] This is a sound (hasan) chain, and it implies that there was once a Qur'an in it which was abrogated in both its wording and its ruling. And Allah knows best.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

This is an alert from the greater to the lesser: since Allah commands His servant and Messenger with this, it is all the more fitting and more appropriate that others be commanded with it. Talq ibn Habib said: Taqwa (God-consciousness) is that you act in obedience to Allah, upon a light from Allah, hoping for the reward of Allah, and that you abandon disobedience to Allah, upon a light from Allah, fearing the punishment of Allah.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾, meaning: do not listen to them and do not consult them. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾, meaning: He is more worthy that you follow His commands and obey Him, for He is Knowing of the outcomes of affairs and Wise in His sayings and actions. And for this reason He said: ﴿And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord﴾, meaning: of the Qur'an and the Sunnah. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted﴾, meaning: nothing hidden is concealed from Him.

﴿And rely upon Allah﴾, meaning: in all your affairs and circumstances. ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs﴾

Meaning: Allah is sufficient as a Disposer of affairs for whoever relies upon Him and turns to Him in repentance.

﴿And rely upon Allah﴾, meaning: in all your affairs and circumstances. ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs﴾

Meaning: Allah is sufficient as a Disposer of affairs for whoever relies upon Him and turns to Him in repentance.

Allah, the Exalted, says, preceding the intended meaning with a familiar sensory matter: just as a single person cannot have two hearts within his body, and just as a wife whom he likens to his mother by saying, "You are to me like the back of my mother," does not become his mother, so too an adopted son (da'i) does not become a son of the man who adopts him and calls him his son. He said: ﴿Allah has not made for any man two hearts within his body, nor has He made your wives whom you declare unlawful (by zihar) your mothers﴾, similar to His saying: ﴿They are not their mothers. Their mothers are only those who gave birth to them, and indeed they utter an objectionable word and a falsehood﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 3].
* *
As for His saying: ﴿nor has He made your adopted sons your sons﴾, this is the intended matter of negation. It was revealed concerning Zayd ibn Harithah, the freedman (mawla) of the Prophet ﷺ. The Prophet ﷺ had adopted him before prophethood, and he was called "Zayd ibn Muhammad." Allah, the Exalted, willed to sever this attachment and this ascription by His saying: ﴿nor has He made your adopted sons your sons﴾, just as He said elsewhere in the surah: ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any man among you, but he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets, and Allah is ever Knowing of all things﴾ [al-Ahzab: 40]. And He said here: ﴿That is your saying by your mouths﴾, meaning: your adopting them is merely a statement which does not necessitate that one be a true son, for he was created from the loins of another man, and it is not possible for him to have two fathers, just as it is not possible for a single human to have two hearts.
﴿And Allah says the truth, and He guides to the way﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿says the truth﴾ means: the justice. Qatadah said: ﴿and He guides to the way﴾ means: the straight path.
Many have mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning a man of Quraysh who was called "Dhu al-Qalbayn" (the Man of Two Hearts), and who claimed that he had two hearts, each with full intelligence. So Allah revealed this verse refuting him. This is what al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, and it was said by Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan, and Qatadah, and Ibn Jarir chose it.
Imam Ahmad said: Hasan narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, from Qabus—meaning Ibn Abi Zabyan—that his father narrated to him, saying: I said to Ibn 'Abbas: Tell me about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Allah has not made for any man two hearts within his body﴾, what did He mean by it? He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood one day praying, and he made a slight error (in his recitation/movement). The hypocrites who prayed with him said: "Do you not see that he has two hearts, one with you and one with them?" So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Allah has not made for any man two hearts within his body﴾ [[Al-Musnad (1/267).]].
At-Tirmidhi narrated it likewise from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi, from Sa'id al-Harrani, and from 'Abd ibn Humayd, from Ahmad ibn Yunus—both of them from Zuhayr, namely Ibn Mu'awiyah, with it. Then he said: "This is a hasan hadith." Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it from the hadith of Zuhayr, with it. [[Sunan at-Tirmidhi no. (3199) and Tafsir at-Tabari (21/74).]]
'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, regarding His saying: ﴿Allah has not made for any man two hearts within his body﴾, he said: "It has reached us that this was concerning Zayd ibn Harithah, when a parable was struck for him: 'The son of another man is not your son.'" [[Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (2/92).]]
Likewise Mujahid, Qatadah, and Ibn Zayd said that it was revealed concerning Zayd ibn Harithah. This agrees with what we have already mentioned in the interpretation, and Allah knows best.
* *
As for His saying: ﴿Call them by their fathers; that is more just in the sight of Allah﴾, this is a command abrogating what was in the beginning of Islam of permissibility of ascribing foreign sons (al-ad'iya', i.e. adopted sons), so Allah, the Exalted, commanded returning their lineages to their fathers in reality, and that this is the justice and the equity.
Al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Mu'alla ibn Asad narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn al-Mukhtar narrated to us, Musa ibn 'Uqbah narrated to us, saying: Salim narrated to me from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, that Zayd ibn Harithah, the freedman of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ—we used not to call him except "Zayd ibn Muhammad," until the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿Call them by their fathers; that is more just in the sight of Allah﴾. Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i also narrated it through various chains from Musa ibn 'Uqbah, with it. [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4782), Sahih Muslim no. (2425), Sunan at-Tirmidhi no. (3209), and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (11397).]]
They used to treat them in every respect as sons, including in seclusion with those who are forbidden to them (mahram) and other matters. For this reason Sahlah bint Suhayl, the wife of Abu Hudhayfah, said: "O Messenger of Allah, we used to call Salim 'son,' and Allah has revealed what He has revealed, and he used to enter upon me, and I find in the soul of Abu Hudhayfah something about that." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Nurse him, and he will become unlawful to you," the hadith. [[The hadith is in Sahih Muslim no. (1453), from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.]]
For this reason, when this ruling was abrogated, Allah permitted the wives of adopted sons, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married Zaynab bint Jahsh, the former wife of Zayd ibn Harithah, and He said: ﴿so that there will be no restriction upon the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they have concluded their need from them﴾ [al-Ahzab: 37]. In the verse of prohibition He said: ﴿and the wives of your sons who are from your loins﴾ [al-Nisa': 23], excluding the wife of an adopted son, since he is not from the loins. As for a foster son (ibn al-rada'ah), he is placed in the legal status of a biological son by the saying of the Prophet ﷺ in the two Sahihs: "Make unlawful through nursing what is made unlawful through lineage." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4796) and Sahih Muslim no. (1445), from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.]] As for calling another man "son" out of honour and affection, this is not what is forbidden in this verse, by the evidence of what Imam Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan (except al-Tirmidhi) narrated from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from al-Hasan al-'Uranni, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "We came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, we the young boys of the sons of 'Abd al-Muttalib, on our donkeys from Jam'. He began slapping our thighs and saying: 'Little sons (uby'ayya), do not throw the pebbles until the sun rises.'" [[Al-Musnad (1/311), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (1940), Sunan al-Nasa'i (5/270), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3025).]] Abu 'Ubayd and others said: "Uby'ayya" is a diminutive of "bunayya" (my little son). This is clearly indicative, for this occurred at the Farewell Pilgrimage in the tenth year, whereas ﴿Call them by their fathers﴾ concerned Zayd ibn Harithah, who was killed on the day of Mu'tah in the eighth year. Also, in Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Abu 'Awanah al-Wadday ibn 'Abdullah al-Yashkuri, from al-Ja'd Abi 'Uthman al-Basri, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "O my son (ya bunayya)." Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi also narrated it. [[Sahih Muslim no. (2151), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4964), and Sunan at-Tirmidhi no. (4831).]]
* *
As for His saying: ﴿But if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion and your clients (mawali)﴾, Allah, the Exalted, commanded returning the lineages of adopted sons to their fathers if they are known. If they do not know their fathers, then they are their brothers in religion and their clients (mawali), meaning: in place of the lineage that they have missed. For this reason the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, on the day he left Makkah in the year of the 'Umrat al-Qada', when the daughter of Hamzah followed them calling: "O uncle, O uncle!" 'Ali took her and said to Fatimah: "Take your cousin's daughter and carry her." 'Ali, Zayd, and Ja'far then disputed over which of them would take charge of her, each presenting an argument. 'Ali said: "I am more entitled to her, and she is the daughter of my uncle's..." (Ibn 'Umays). Zayd said: "She is the daughter of my brother." Ja'far ibn Abi Talib said: "She is my cousin's daughter, and her maternal aunt is under me"—meaning Asma' bint 'Umays. So the Prophet ﷺ judged in favour of her maternal aunt, and said: "The maternal aunt is in the position of a mother." He said to 'Ali: "You are from me, and I am from you." He said to Ja'far: "You resemble my form and my character." He said to Zayd: "You are our brother and our mawla." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih no. (2699), from the hadith of al-Bara', may Allah be pleased with him.]]
In this hadith there are many rulings, among the finest of which: he ﷺ judged with the truth and satisfied each of the disputants, and he said to Zayd: "You are our brother and our mawla," as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿then they are your brothers in religion and your clients﴾.
Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from 'Uyaynah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from his father, who said: Abu Bakrah said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Call them by their fathers; that is more just in the sight of Allah. But if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion and your clients﴾, so I am one whose father is not known, and I am from your brothers in religion. Ubayy said: "By Allah, I think that if he knew that his father was a donkey, he would have claimed him."
It has also come in a hadith: "Whoever claims to be [the son] of other than his father, while knowing it, has committed kufr." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih no. (3508), from the hadith of Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, with a similar wording.]] This is a strong emphasis, threat, and firm warning concerning disowning a known lineage. For this reason He said: ﴿Call them by their fathers; that is more just in the sight of Allah. But if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion and your clients﴾.
Then He said: ﴿And there is no blame upon you for what you have done in error﴾, meaning: if you ascribe some of them to other than their father in reality by mistake, after exerting effort and striving one's utmost; for Allah has lifted hardship from error and removed its sin, as He guided to it when commanding His servants to say: ﴿Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err﴾ [al-Baqarah: 286]. And it is established in Sahih Muslim that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah said: 'I have done so.'" [[Sahih Muslim no. (126), from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]] And in Sahih al-Bukhari, from 'Amr ibn al-'As, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If a judge exerts effort and is correct, he has two rewards; and if he exerts effort and errs, he has one reward." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (7352).]] And in another hadith: "Allah has lifted from my ummah error, forgetfulness, and what they are compelled to do."
Here He said: ﴿And there is no blame upon you for what you have done in error, but what your hearts have intended [is blameworthy]. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾, meaning: sin is only upon the one who intentionally pursues falsehood, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned﴾ [al-Baqarah: 225]. And in the hadith previously mentioned: "Whoever claims to be [the son] of other than his father, while knowing it, has committed kufr." And in the abrogated Qur'an: "Indeed, it is kufr for you to turn away from your fathers."

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Utbah ibn Mas'ud, from Ibn Abbas, from Umar that he said: Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ with the truth and sent down the Book with him. Among what was sent down to him was the verse of stoning (ayat al-rajm), so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stoned [adulterers], and we stoned after him. Then he said: "We used to recite: ﴿And do not turn away from your fathers, for it is disbelief in you [or: indeed, disbelief in you is that you turn away from your fathers]﴾." And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not overpraise me as Isa ibn Maryam was overpraised, for I am only a servant, so say: His servant and His Messenger." And sometimes Ma'mar said: "as the Christians overpraised the son of Maryam."

Imam Ahmad narrated it in another hadith with the words: "Three things among the people are disbelief: slandering lineage, wailing over the dead, and seeking rain by the stars." [Ahmad's Musnad (5/342), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (934), both from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari with the wording: "Four things among my Ummah from the matters of the Jahiliyyah they will not abandon: boasting about lineages," and then he mentioned these three.]

(1445), from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.]] As for calling another man "son" out of honour and affection, this is not what is forbidden in this verse, by the evidence of what Imam Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan (except al-Tirmidhi) narrated from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from al-Hasan al-'Uranni, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "We came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, we the young boys of the sons of 'Abd al-Muttalib, on our donkeys from Jam'. He began slapping our thighs and saying: 'Little sons (uby'ayya), do not throw the pebbles until the sun rises.'" [[Al-Musnad (1/311), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (1940), Sunan al-Nasa'i (5/270), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3025).]] Abu 'Ubayd and others said: "Uby'ayya" is a diminutive of "bunayya" (my little son). This is clearly indicative, for this occurred at the Farewell Pilgrimage in the tenth year, whereas ﴿Call them by their fathers﴾ concerned Zayd ibn Harithah, who was killed on the day of Mu'tah in the eighth year. Also, in Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Abu 'Awanah al-Wadday ibn 'Abdullah al-Yashkuri, from al-Ja'd Abi 'Uthman al-Basri, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "O my son (ya bunayya)." Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi also narrated it. [[Sahih Muslim no. (2151), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4964), and Sunan at-Tirmidhi no. (4831).]]
* *
As for His saying: ﴿But if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion and your clients (mawali)﴾, Allah, the Exalted, commanded returning the lineages of adopted sons to their fathers if they are known. If they do not know their fathers, then they are their brothers in religion and their clients (mawali), meaning: in place of the lineage that they have missed. For this reason the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, on the day he left Makkah in the year of the 'Umrat al-Qada', when the daughter of Hamzah followed them calling: "O uncle, O uncle!" 'Ali took her and said to Fatimah: "Take your cousin's daughter and carry her." 'Ali, Zayd, and Ja'far then disputed over which of them would take charge of her, each presenting an argument. 'Ali said: "I am more entitled to her, and she is the daughter of my uncle's..." (Ibn 'Umays). Zayd said: "She is the daughter of my brother." Ja'far ibn Abi Talib said: "She is my cousin's daughter, and her maternal aunt is under me"—meaning Asma' bint 'Umays. So the Prophet ﷺ judged in favour of her maternal aunt, and said: "The maternal aunt is in the position of a mother." He said to 'Ali: "You are from me, and I am from you." He said to Ja'far: "You resemble my form and my character." He said to Zayd: "You are our brother and our mawla." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih no. (2699), from the hadith of al-Bara', may Allah be pleased with him.]]
In this hadith there are many rulings, among the finest of which: he ﷺ judged with the truth and satisfied each of the disputants, and he said to Zayd: "You are our brother and our mawla," as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿then they are your brothers in religion and your clients﴾.
Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from 'Uyaynah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from his father, who said: Abu Bakrah said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Call them by their fathers; that is more just in the sight of Allah. But if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion and your clients﴾, so I am one whose father is not known, and I am from your brothers in religion. Ubayy said: "By Allah, I think that if he knew that his father was a donkey, he would have claimed him."
It has also come in a hadith: "Whoever claims to be [the son] of other than his father, while knowing it, has committed kufr." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih no. (3508), from the hadith of Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, with a similar wording.]] This is a strong emphasis, threat, and firm warning concerning disowning a known lineage. For this reason He said: ﴿Call them by their fathers; that is more just in the sight of Allah. But if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion and your clients﴾.
Then He said: ﴿And there is no blame upon you for what you have done in error﴾, meaning: if you ascribe some of them to other than their father in reality by mistake, after exerting effort and striving one's utmost; for Allah has lifted hardship from error and removed its sin, as He guided to it when commanding His servants to say: ﴿Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err﴾ [al-Baqarah: 286]. And it is established in Sahih Muslim that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah said: 'I have done so.'" [[Sahih Muslim no. (126), from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]] And in Sahih al-Bukhari, from 'Amr ibn al-'As, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If a judge exerts effort and is correct, he has two rewards; and if he exerts effort and errs, he has one reward." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (7352).]] And in another hadith: "Allah has lifted from my ummah error, forgetfulness, and what they are compelled to do."
Here He said: ﴿And there is no blame upon you for what you have done in error, but what your hearts have intended [is blameworthy]. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾, meaning: sin is only upon the one who intentionally pursues falsehood, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned﴾ [al-Baqarah: 225]. And in the hadith previously mentioned: "Whoever claims to be [the son] of other than his father, while knowing it, has committed kufr." And in the abrogated Qur'an: "Indeed, it is kufr for you to turn away from your fathers."

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Utbah ibn Mas'ud, from Ibn Abbas, from Umar that he said: Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ with the truth and sent down the Book with him. Among what was sent down to him was the verse of stoning (ayat al-rajm), so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stoned [adulterers], and we stoned after him. Then he said: "We used to recite: ﴿And do not turn away from your fathers, for it is disbelief in you [or: indeed, disbelief in you is that you turn away from your fathers]﴾." And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not overpraise me as Isa ibn Maryam was overpraised, for I am only a servant, so say: His servant and His Messenger." And sometimes Ma'mar said: "as the Christians overpraised the son of Maryam."

Imam Ahmad narrated it in another hadith with the words: "Three things among the people are disbelief: slandering lineage, wailing over the dead, and seeking rain by the stars." [Ahmad's Musnad (5/342), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (934), both from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari with the wording: "Four things among my Ummah from the matters of the Jahiliyyah they will not abandon: boasting about lineages," and then he mentioned these three.]

Allah the Exalted has known the compassion of His Messenger ﷺ towards his Ummah and his counsel for them, so He made him more entitled to them than they are to themselves, and made him their judge, preferred over their own choice for themselves, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves, and then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have decided and submit completely.﴾ [An-Nisa: 65]. In the Sahih: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, none of you truly believes until I am more beloved to him than his own self, his wealth, his children, and all of mankind." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 14]. Also in the Sahih: that 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, you are dearer to me than everything except my own self." He said: "No, O 'Umar, until I am dearer to you than your own self." So he said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, you are now dearer to me than everything, even my own self." He said: "Now, O 'Umar." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 6632].

Therefore Allah the Exalted said in this verse: ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves.﴾

Al-Bukhari said regarding it: [In some copies: "at this noble verse"] Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir narrated to us, [Muhammad ibn] Fulayh narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Hilal ibn 'Ali, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Amra, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "There is no believer except that I am the closest of people to him in this world and the Hereafter. Recite if you wish: ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves.﴾ So whichever believer leaves wealth, his heirs, whoever they are, shall inherit it. And if he leaves debt or dependants, let him come to me, for I am his guardian." Al-Bukhari alone narrated it [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4781].

He also narrated it in "al-Istiqraḍ" (Loans), and Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it through several routes from Fulayh, with the same meaning [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2399, and Tafsir al-Tabari (21/77)]. Imam Ahmad narrated it from the hadith of Abu Husayn, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in similar wording [Musnad (2/334)].

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri regarding His saying: ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves﴾, from Abu Salamah, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who used to say: "I am closer to every believer than his own self. Whichever man dies leaving debt, it falls to me; and whoever leaves wealth, it is for his heirs." [In Ibn Kathir's text, variant in another copy: "then it is for his heirs"]. Abu Dawud narrated it from Ahmad ibn Hanbal [Musnad (3/296) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. 2956], with similar wording.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And his wives are their mothers﴾, meaning in respect of prohibition, honour, reverence, veneration and magnification. However, it is not permissible to be alone with them, and the prohibition does not extend to their daughters and sisters, by consensus. Although some scholars called the daughters of (the wives) "sisters of the believers", as is the explicit statement of al-Shafi'i in al-Mukhtasar, this is a matter of the usage of expression, not the establishment of a ruling. Is Mu'awiyah and his like called "the maternal uncle of the believers"? There are two opinions among the scholars on this. Al-Shafi'i explicitly stated that such a title is used. And is it said of them: "Mothers of the believing women", so that women are included under the masculine sound plural by way of precedence? There are two opinions on this: it is authentically reported from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: "That is not said." And this is the more correct of the two views in the school of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him.

It has been narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Ibn 'Abbas that they recited: "The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves, and his wives are their mothers, and he is a father to them." Similar has been narrated from Mu'awiyah, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah and al-Hasan. This is one of the two views in the school of al-Shafi'i, related by al-Baghawi and others, and they relied on it by the hadith narrated by Abu Dawud:

'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Nufayli narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan, from al-Qa'qa' ibn Hakim, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I am to you as a father, teaching you. When any of you goes to relieve himself, let him not face the qiblah nor turn his back to it, and let him not wipe with his right hand," and he used to command three stones and forbade dung and bones.

It was also recorded by al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah, from the hadith of Ibn 'Ajlan [Sunan Abi Dawud no. 8, Sunan al-Nasa'i (1/38), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. 313].

The second view is that it is not said, and they argued with His saying: ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men﴾ and His saying: ﴿And blood relatives are more entitled to one another in the Book of Allah﴾, meaning in the ruling of Allah, ﴿than the believers and the emigrants﴾, meaning: relatives are more entitled to inheritance than the emigrants and the helpers. This verse abrogated what preceded it of inheritance by alliance and the brotherhood that existed among them, as Ibn 'Abbas and others said: the emigrant used to inherit from the helper to the exclusion of his relatives and kin, because of the brotherhood which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ established between them. Likewise said Sa'id ibn Jubayr and many of the early and later scholars.

Ibn Abi Hatim included a hadith on this from al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam, may Allah be pleased with him, saying: Abu Hatim narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Abi Bakr al-Mus'abi, from the residents of Baghdad, narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed about us specifically, the company of Quraysh and the Ansar: ﴿And blood relatives are more entitled to one another﴾. That was because when we, the company of Quraysh, came to Madinah, we came with no wealth, and we found the Ansar excellent brothers, so we made brotherhood with them and inherited from them. Abu Bakr established brotherhood with Kharijah ibn Zayd, 'Umar established brotherhood with a certain man, and 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, established brotherhood with a man from Banu Zuraiq, Sa'd al-Zuraqi, though some people say other than him. Al-Zubayr said: I made brotherhood with Ka'b ibn Malik, and I came to him and took him, and I found that the weapons had made him heavy, as it appeared. By Allah, my son, had he died in this world that day, no one but I would have inherited him, until Allah revealed this verse about us, the company of Quraysh and the Ansar specifically, and we returned to our inheritances.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿except that you do to your allies a kindness﴾, meaning: inheritance is gone, but support, righteousness, kinship, goodness and bequest remain.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿That is inscribed in the Book as a decree﴾, meaning: this ruling, that blood relatives are more entitled to one another, is a decree from Allah, predetermined and written in the Primordial Book, which is not changed or altered. This was said by Mujahid and others. Yet it may be said: He, the Exalted, has legislated its opposite at a time because of the profound wisdom He has in that, and He knows that He will abrogate it to what runs in His eternal decree and His legislative, decreed judgement.

Ibn Kathir says, in Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim: Allah, exalted is He, informs us about the five *Ulul-'Azm* (the Messengers of firm resolve) and the rest of the prophets. He took from them a covenant and a binding pledge to establish the religion of Allah, to convey His message, and to cooperate, support one another, and remain united. As Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of the prophets: "Whatever I give you of Scripture and wisdom, and then there comes to you a Messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him." He said: "Do you affirm and accept My covenant on this condition?" They said: "We affirm it." He said: "Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses."﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 81]. This covenant and pledge was taken from them after they were sent as Messengers, and so is this one.

He specified these five from among them, namely the Ulul-'Azm, and this is of the type of mentioning the specific after the general (*'atf al-khass 'ala al-'amm*). He also explicitly named them in this verse and in His saying: ﴿He has prescribed for you of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah, and that which We revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses, and Jesus: that you establish the religion and do not divide over it.﴾ [Ash-Shura: 13]. Thus He mentioned the two extremes and the middle: the first (Noah) and the last (Muhammad), and those between them in order. This is the charge by which they were bound to the covenant, as He said: ﴿And when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus son of Mary.﴾ In this verse He began with the last (Muhammad), because of his nobility, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, and then arranged them according to the order of their appearance, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them all.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah al-Dimashqi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Bakkar narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Bashir narrated to us, Qatadah narrated to me, from al-Hasan, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah﴾ to the end of the verse: The Prophet ﷺ said: "I was the first of the prophets in creation and the last of them in being sent, [but I was given precedence] over them." (Abu Nu'aym narrated it in *Dala'il al-Nubuwwah*, p. 6, and Ibn 'Adi in *al-Kamil* (3/373), and Tammam in *al-Fawa'id* (no. 1003), by various routes from Sa'id ibn Bashir from Qatadah. Its chain has two defects. The first: al-Hasan al-Basri is a *mudallis* (one who conceals weak sources) and narrates with "'an'anah" (the "from" formula). The second: Sa'id ibn Bashir is weak, and he has been contradicted. Abu Hilal and Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah opposed him, as the author mentions, and they said: from Qatadah as a *mursal* (a report where the Successor omits the Companion). End of quotation, taken from *al-Silsilah al-Da'ifah*, no. 661, by Shaykh Nasir al-Albani.) Sa'id ibn Bashir is weak in this report.

Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated it from Qatadah as a *mursal*, and that is more likely. Some narrated it from Qatadah as a *mawquf* (a report ending at a Companion or Successor and not traced to the Prophet). And Allah knows best.

Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: 'Amr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, Abu Ahmad narrated to us, Hamzah al-Zayyat narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Thabit narrated to us, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "The best of the children of Adam are five: Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad, and the best of them is Muhammad ﷺ, all of them." (Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 2368, Kashf al-Astar.) It is *mawquf*, and Hamzah in it is weak.

It has been said that the covenant taken from them refers to the time when they were brought forth in the form of tiny particles (*dharr*) from the loins of Adam, as Abu Ja'far al-Razi said, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: "[Allah] raised their father Adam and looked at them, meaning his descendants. Among them were the rich and the poor, the beautiful and those less so. [Adam] said: 'My Lord, why did You not make Your servants equal?' He said: 'I wished to be thanked.' He saw among them the prophets like lamps, upon whom was a light, and they were singled out with another covenant concerning the Message and Prophethood. This is what Allah, exalted is He, refers to: ﴿And when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah [and Abraham, Moses, and Jesus son of Mary]﴾ and so on." This is also the view of Mujahid.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "The solemn covenant (*al-mithaq al-ghalid*) is the pledge."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿that He may question the truthful about their truthfulness﴾, Mujahid said: "They are those who convey and deliver the messages of the Messengers."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and He has prepared for the disbelievers﴾, that is, from among their nations, ﴿a painful punishment﴾, that is, a grievous one. So we testify that the Messengers have conveyed the messages of their Lord, advised their nations, and made clear to them the manifest truth, evident and plain, free of confusion, doubt, or dispute, even if those ignorant, obstinate, apostate, and deviant people denied them. What the Messengers brought is the truth, and whoever opposes them is in error.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and He has prepared for the disbelievers﴾, that is, from among their nations, ﴿a painful punishment﴾, that is, a grievous one. So we testify that the Messengers have conveyed the messages of their Lord, advised their nations, and made clear to them the manifest truth, evident and plain, free of confusion, doubt, or dispute, even if those ignorant, obstinate, apostate, and deviant people denied them. What the Messengers brought is the truth, and whoever opposes them is in error.

He, may He be exalted, says, informing of His blessing, favour and kindness to His believing servants in turning back their enemies and defeating them, on the occasion when they gathered against them in confederate groups (al-Ahzab), and that was the Battle of the Trench (al-Khandaq). It took place in Shawwal of the fifth year after the Hijrah, according to the correct and well-known view.

Musa ibn Uqbah and others said it was in the fourth year.

The cause of the coming of the confederates was that a group of the nobles of the Jews of Banu al-Nadir, whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had expelled from Madinah to Khaybar, among them Sallam ibn Abi al-Huqayq, Sallam ibn Mishkam, and Kinanah ibn al-Rabi', went out to Makkah, met the nobles of Quraysh, incited them to war against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and promised them support and assistance from themselves. They agreed to this. Then they went out to Ghatafan and invited them, and they also responded. Quraysh set out with its Ahabish and those who followed them, and their commander was Abu Sufyan Sakhr ibn Harb. The commander of Ghatafan was Uyaynah ibn Hisn ibn Badr. All of them numbered about ten thousand. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard of their march, he ordered the Muslims to dig a trench around Madinah on the side facing the east. This was on the advice of Salman al-Farisi. The Muslims worked on it diligently, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) himself carried the earth with them and dug. In that digging there were clear signs and manifest proofs.

The polytheists came and camped east of Madinah near Uhud, and a group of them camped on the high ground of Madinah, as Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿When they came upon you from above you and from below you﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out with the Muslims who were with him, who were about three thousand, and it is said seven hundred. They put their backs to Sal' and faced the enemy. The trench lay between them and the enemy, without water, preventing the infantry and cavalry from reaching them. He placed the women and children in the fortified houses of Madinah. The Banu Qurayzah, a group of the Jews, had a fortress east of Madinah, and they had a covenant and a pact with the Prophet (ﷺ). They numbered about eight hundred fighters. Huyayy ibn Akhtab al-Nadri [al-Yahudi] [[Addition from manuscript T.]] went to them and did not cease working on them until they broke the covenant and aided the confederates against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The matter became grave, the situation became severe, and their circumstances became straitened, as Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿There the believers were tested and shaken with a severe shaking﴾.

They remained besieging the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions for nearly a month, but they could not reach them, and no real fighting took place between them, except that Amr ibn Abd Wudd al-Amiri, who was among the famous brave horsemen of the Jahiliyyah, rode out with some horsemen, forced their way across the trench, and reached the side of the Muslims. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called the Muslim cavalry to face him, but no one came out to him. So he ordered Ali to go out to him. Ali went out to him, they fought for a while, and then Ali killed him, may Allah be pleased with him. This was a sign of victory.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent upon the confederates a wind of very violent and powerful blowing, so that it left them no tent and nothing, and no fire could be kindled for them, and they could find no settled place, until they departed, frustrated and losing, as Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿O you who believe, remember the favour of Allah upon you when hosts came against you, so We sent upon them a wind﴾ [[In manuscript F, after this: (and hosts you did not see).]].

Mujahid said: It was the Sabā (east wind). This is supported by the other hadith: "I was given victory by the Sabā, and 'Ad was destroyed by the Dabūr (west wind)."

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Ikrimah, who said: The southern winds said to the northern wind on the night of the confederates: "Come, let us go and help the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." The northern wind replied: "A free woman does not travel by night." He said: So the wind that was sent against them was the Sabā.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Dawud, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, and mentioned it.

Ibn Jarir also said: Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Umar narrated to me, from Nafi', from Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: My maternal uncle Uthman ibn Maz'un sent me on the night of the Trench, in severe cold and wind, to Madinah, saying: "Bring us food and a blanket." He said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for permission, and he permitted me, and said: "Whomever you meet of my companions, tell them to return." He said: I went, and the wind was scattering everything, and I did not meet anyone without ordering him to return to the Prophet (ﷺ). He said: None of them turned his neck (to look back). He said: I had a shield with me, and the wind was striking it against me, and it had iron in it. He said: The wind struck it until some of that iron fell on my palm, and it pushed it down to the ground. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (21/80).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿and hosts you did not see﴾ refers to the angels. They shook them and cast terror and fear into their hearts. The leader of every tribe would say: "O Banu so-and-so, come to me!" They would gather around him, and he would say: "Escape! Escape!" because of the terror Allah, may He be exalted, had cast into their hearts.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated, from Yazid ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: A young man from the people of Kufah said to Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman: "O Abu Abdullah, did you see the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and keep his company?" He said: "Yes, O my nephew." He said: "What did you used to do?" He said: "By Allah, we used to strive hard." The young man said: "By Allah, if we had reached him, we would not have let him walk on the earth, and we would have carried him on our necks." He said: Hudhayfah said: "O my nephew, by Allah, if you had seen us with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the Trench, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed a portion of the night, then turned to us and said: 'Who will stand up and go and see for us what the people are doing?' — the Prophet (ﷺ) stipulated that he would return — 'Allah will admit him to Paradise.'" He said: No man stood up. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed another portion of the night, then turned to us and said the same, and none of us stood up. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed another portion of the night, then turned to us and said: "Who will stand up and go and see what the people are doing, then return — the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stipulates his return — I ask Allah that he be my companion in Paradise." No man of the people stood up, because of the severity of the fear, the severity of the hunger, and the severity of the cold. When no one stood up, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called me, and when he called me I had no choice but to stand. He said: "O Hudhayfah, go and enter among the people, and see what they are doing, and do not do anything until you come back to us." He said: I went and entered among the people, while the wind and the soldiers of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, were doing to them what they were doing, leaving them no cooking pot, no fire, and no building standing. Abu Sufyan stood up and said: "O assembly of Quraysh, let each one look at who is sitting beside him." Hudhayfah said: I took the hand of the man beside me and said: "Who are you?" He said: "I am so-and-so, son of so-and-so." Then Abu Sufyan said: "O assembly of Quraysh, by Allah, you have not woken in a place where you can stay. The horses and camels have perished, the Banu Qurayzah have broken their word to us, and we have received from them what we dislike, and we have suffered from this wind that you see. By Allah, no cooking pot stays firm for us, no fire stands for us, and no building holds for us. So depart, for I am departing." Then he stood up to his camel, which was tied, sat on it, and struck it, and it leapt up on three legs, and he did not release its tether until it was standing. Had it not been for the covenant of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with me, "Do not do anything until you come back to me," and had I wished, I would have killed him with an arrow.

Hudhayfah said: I returned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who was standing praying in a striped cloak belonging to one of his wives, wrapped and folded. When he saw me, he drew me between his legs and threw the edge of the cloak over me, then he bowed and prostrated while I was still with him. When he finished the prayer, I told him the news. Ghatafan heard what Quraysh had done, so they turned back to their lands.

[[Sirah of Ibn Hisham (2/231).]]

Muslim narrated it in his Sahih from the hadith of al-A'mash, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from his father, who said: We were with Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, may Allah be pleased with him, and a man said to him: "If I had reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), I would have fought with him and shown my valour." Hudhayfah said to him: "Would you have done that? We saw ourselves with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the night of the confederates, on a night of violent wind and cold. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Is there not a man who will bring us news of the people, who will be with me on the Day of Resurrection?' None of us answered him. Then he said it a second time, and a third time the same. Then he said: 'O Hudhayfah, stand up and bring us news of the people.' I had no choice, when he called me by my name, but to stand. He said: 'Bring me news of the people, and do not frighten them against me.' He said: So I went as if I were walking in a bathhouse, until I reached them, and there was Abu Sufyan warming his back at the fire. I placed an arrow on the belly of my bow and wanted to shoot him, then I remembered the words of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): 'Do not frighten them against me.' Had I shot him, I would have hit him. He said: I returned as if I were walking in a bathhouse, and came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Then the cold struck me when I finished and became chilled, and I told the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He put on me some of the surplus of a cloak he used to pray in, and I kept sleeping until morning. When I woke up, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Get up, O sleeper [[In manuscript A: "nawwam".]].'" [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1788).]]

Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated it from Hisham ibn Sa'd, from Zayd ibn Aslam, that a man said to Hudhayfah, may Allah be pleased with him: "We complain to Allah about your companionship with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). You met him and we did not meet him; you saw him and we did not see him." Hudhayfah said: "And we complain to Allah about your faith in him when you have not seen him. By Allah, you do not know, O my nephew, how you would have been had you met him. We saw ourselves with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the night of the Trench, on a cold rainy night..." and then he mentioned something similar to what preceded, at length. [[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (3/454), through Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Yunus ibn Bukayr.]]

Bilal ibn Yahya al-Absi also narrated something similar from Hudhayfah. [[Narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (3/31), and from his route al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (3/450), from Musa ibn Abi al-Mukhtar, from Bilal al-Absi, from Hudhayfah.]]

And Al-Hakim and Al-Bayhaqi (in "Al-Dala'il") narrated, from the hadith of Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar, from Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah al-Du'ali, from 'Abd al-'Aziz, the nephew of Hudhayfah, who said: Hudhayfah mentioned their stands (in battle) with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and his companions said: "By Allah, if we had witnessed that, we would have done such-and-such and such-and-such." Hudhayfah said: "Do not wish for that. We were on the night of the Confederates (al-Ahzab), when we were standing and sitting, and Abu Sufyan and those with him of the Confederates were above us, and Qurayzah the Jews were below us, and we feared them for our children. Never did a darker or fiercer wind come upon us; in the sound of its wind were like thunderbolts, and it was a darkness in which one of us could not see his own finger. The hypocrites began to ask permission of the Prophet ﷺ, saying: 'Indeed our houses are exposed,' and they were not exposed. None of them asked his permission except that he was granted it, and he would give them permission, and they would slip away. We were three hundred and some. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us, man by man, until he reached me, and I had nothing to protect me from the enemy or from the cold except a cloak belonging to my wife, which did not reach past my knees." He said: "The Prophet ﷺ came to me while I was crouching on my knees, and said: 'Who is this?' I said: 'Hudhayfah.' He said: 'Hudhayfah.' So I lowered myself to the ground and said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah,' out of dislike of standing up. [He said: 'Stand up.'] So I stood, and he said: 'Indeed there is news among the people, so bring me news of the people.'" He said: "I was among the most terrified of people and the most afflicted by cold." He said: "So I went out, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'O Allah, protect him from before him and behind him, from his right and from his left, and from above him and from below him.'" He said: "By Allah, Allah created no fear or cold within my body except that it left my body, so I found nothing in it." He said: "When I turned to leave, he said: 'O Hudhayfah, do not do anything among the people until you come back to me.'" He said: "I went out, and when I approached the camp of the people, I looked by the light of a fire they had blazing, and there was a dark, large man rubbing his hands over the fire and stroking his side, saying: 'Depart, depart!' I had not known Abu Sufyan before that. So I drew an arrow from my quiver, white-feathered, and placed it on the middle of my bow, intending to shoot him by the light of the fire. Then I remembered the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: 'Do not do anything among them until you come back to me.' So I held back and returned my arrow to my quiver. Then I encouraged myself until I entered the camp, and the nearest of the people to me were the Banu 'Amir, saying: 'O family of 'Amir, depart, depart! There is no staying for you.' The wind in their camp did not pass beyond their camp by a span. By Allah, I could hear the sound of stones in their saddles, and the wind was striking their tents and their bedding with them. Then I went out toward the Prophet ﷺ, and when I had gone half the way or about that, I found about twenty riders or so, wrapped up, who said: 'Inform your companion that Allah, the Exalted, has sufficed the people.' So I returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he was wrapped in a garment, praying. By Allah, no sooner had I returned than the cold overcame me and I began to tremble. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gestured to me with his hand while he was praying, so I drew near to him, and he wrapped his garment around me. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, whenever a matter distressed him, would pray. So I informed him of the news of the people, and told him that I had left them preparing to depart." And Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿O you who believe, remember the favour of Allah upon you when hosts came against you, so We sent upon them a wind and hosts you did not see. And Allah is ever Seeing of what you do.﴾ [Dala'il al-Nubuwwah of al-Bayhaqi (3/451).]

And Abu Dawud in his Sunan narrated from it: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, whenever a matter distressed him..." from the hadith of Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar, with it. [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1319.]

As for His saying: ﴿when they came at you from above you and from below you﴾, meaning: the Confederates came from above you and from below you. Hudhayfah's report mentioned earlier says they were the Banu Qurayzah. ﴿And when the eyes shifted and the hearts reached the throats﴾, meaning: from the intensity of fear and terror. ﴿And you assumed about Allah assumptions﴾.

Ibn Jarir said: Some of those who were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ thought that the reverse would befall the believers, and that Allah would do that. [Tafsir al-Tabari (21/83).]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said regarding His saying: ﴿And when the eyes shifted and the hearts reached the throats, and you assumed about Allah assumptions﴾: the believers entertained every kind of assumption, and hypocrisy surfaced, until Mu'attib ibn Qushayr, brother of Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf, said: "Muhammad used to promise us that we would eat the treasures of Khosrow and Caesar, while not one of us can go out to relieve himself."

Al-Hasan said regarding His saying: ﴿and you assumed about Allah assumptions﴾: various assumptions. The hypocrites assumed that Muhammad and his companions would be uprooted, while the believers were certain that what Allah and His Messenger had promised was true, and that He would make it prevail over all religion, even if the polytheists disliked it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn 'Asim al-Ansari narrated to us, Abu 'Amir narrated to us (and) my father narrated to us, Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi narrated to us, al-Zubayr, that is Ibn 'Abdullah, freedman of 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, narrated to us, from Rutayj ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa'id, from his father, from Abu Sa'id who said: On the day of the Trench we said: "O Messenger of Allah, is there something we can say, since the hearts have reached the throats?" He ﷺ said: "Yes, say: 'O Allah, conceal our faults, and secure our fears.'" He said: So he struck the faces of his enemies with the wind, and defeated them with the wind.

Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal also narrated it likewise, from Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi. [Al-Musnad (3/3).]

He, may He be exalted, says, informing of His blessing, favour and kindness to His believing servants in turning back their enemies and defeating them, on the occasion when they gathered against them in confederate groups (al-Ahzab), and that was the Battle of the Trench (al-Khandaq). It took place in Shawwal of the fifth year after the Hijrah, according to the correct and well-known view.

Musa ibn Uqbah and others said it was in the fourth year.

The cause of the coming of the confederates was that a group of the nobles of the Jews of Banu al-Nadir, whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had expelled from Madinah to Khaybar, among them Sallam ibn Abi al-Huqayq, Sallam ibn Mishkam, and Kinanah ibn al-Rabi', went out to Makkah, met the nobles of Quraysh, incited them to war against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and promised them support and assistance from themselves. They agreed to this. Then they went out to Ghatafan and invited them, and they also responded. Quraysh set out with its Ahabish and those who followed them, and their commander was Abu Sufyan Sakhr ibn Harb. The commander of Ghatafan was Uyaynah ibn Hisn ibn Badr. All of them numbered about ten thousand. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard of their march, he ordered the Muslims to dig a trench around Madinah on the side facing the east. This was on the advice of Salman al-Farisi. The Muslims worked on it diligently, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) himself carried the earth with them and dug. In that digging there were clear signs and manifest proofs.

The polytheists came and camped east of Madinah near Uhud, and a group of them camped on the high ground of Madinah, as Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿When they came upon you from above you and from below you﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out with the Muslims who were with him, who were about three thousand, and it is said seven hundred. They put their backs to Sal' and faced the enemy. The trench lay between them and the enemy, without water, preventing the infantry and cavalry from reaching them. He placed the women and children in the fortified houses of Madinah. The Banu Qurayzah, a group of the Jews, had a fortress east of Madinah, and they had a covenant and a pact with the Prophet (ﷺ). They numbered about eight hundred fighters. Huyayy ibn Akhtab al-Nadri [al-Yahudi] [[Addition from manuscript T.]] went to them and did not cease working on them until they broke the covenant and aided the confederates against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The matter became grave, the situation became severe, and their circumstances became straitened, as Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿There the believers were tested and shaken with a severe shaking﴾.

They remained besieging the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions for nearly a month, but they could not reach them, and no real fighting took place between them, except that Amr ibn Abd Wudd al-Amiri, who was among the famous brave horsemen of the Jahiliyyah, rode out with some horsemen, forced their way across the trench, and reached the side of the Muslims. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called the Muslim cavalry to face him, but no one came out to him. So he ordered Ali to go out to him. Ali went out to him, they fought for a while, and then Ali killed him, may Allah be pleased with him. This was a sign of victory.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent upon the confederates a wind of very violent and powerful blowing, so that it left them no tent and nothing, and no fire could be kindled for them, and they could find no settled place, until they departed, frustrated and losing, as Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿O you who believe, remember the favour of Allah upon you when hosts came against you, so We sent upon them a wind﴾ [[In manuscript F, after this: (and hosts you did not see).]].

Mujahid said: It was the Sabā (east wind). This is supported by the other hadith: "I was given victory by the Sabā, and 'Ad was destroyed by the Dabūr (west wind)."

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Ikrimah, who said: The southern winds said to the northern wind on the night of the confederates: "Come, let us go and help the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." The northern wind replied: "A free woman does not travel by night." He said: So the wind that was sent against them was the Sabā.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Dawud, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, and mentioned it.

Ibn Jarir also said: Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Umar narrated to me, from Nafi', from Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: My maternal uncle Uthman ibn Maz'un sent me on the night of the Trench, in severe cold and wind, to Madinah, saying: "Bring us food and a blanket." He said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for permission, and he permitted me, and said: "Whomever you meet of my companions, tell them to return." He said: I went, and the wind was scattering everything, and I did not meet anyone without ordering him to return to the Prophet (ﷺ). He said: None of them turned his neck (to look back). He said: I had a shield with me, and the wind was striking it against me, and it had iron in it. He said: The wind struck it until some of that iron fell on my palm, and it pushed it down to the ground. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (21/80).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿and hosts you did not see﴾ refers to the angels. They shook them and cast terror and fear into their hearts. The leader of every tribe would say: "O Banu so-and-so, come to me!" They would gather around him, and he would say: "Escape! Escape!" because of the terror Allah, may He be exalted, had cast into their hearts.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated, from Yazid ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: A young man from the people of Kufah said to Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman: "O Abu Abdullah, did you see the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and keep his company?" He said: "Yes, O my nephew." He said: "What did you used to do?" He said: "By Allah, we used to strive hard." The young man said: "By Allah, if we had reached him, we would not have let him walk on the earth, and we would have carried him on our necks." He said: Hudhayfah said: "O my nephew, by Allah, if you had seen us with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the Trench, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed a portion of the night, then turned to us and said: 'Who will stand up and go and see for us what the people are doing?' — the Prophet (ﷺ) stipulated that he would return — 'Allah will admit him to Paradise.'" He said: No man stood up. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed another portion of the night, then turned to us and said the same, and none of us stood up. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed another portion of the night, then turned to us and said: "Who will stand up and go and see what the people are doing, then return — the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stipulates his return — I ask Allah that he be my companion in Paradise." No man of the people stood up, because of the severity of the fear, the severity of the hunger, and the severity of the cold. When no one stood up, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called me, and when he called me I had no choice but to stand. He said: "O Hudhayfah, go and enter among the people, and see what they are doing, and do not do anything until you come back to us." He said: I went and entered among the people, while the wind and the soldiers of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, were doing to them what they were doing, leaving them no cooking pot, no fire, and no building standing. Abu Sufyan stood up and said: "O assembly of Quraysh, let each one look at who is sitting beside him." Hudhayfah said: I took the hand of the man beside me and said: "Who are you?" He said: "I am so-and-so, son of so-and-so." Then Abu Sufyan said: "O assembly of Quraysh, by Allah, you have not woken in a place where you can stay. The horses and camels have perished, the Banu Qurayzah have broken their word to us, and we have received from them what we dislike, and we have suffered from this wind that you see. By Allah, no cooking pot stays firm for us, no fire stands for us, and no building holds for us. So depart, for I am departing." Then he stood up to his camel, which was tied, sat on it, and struck it, and it leapt up on three legs, and he did not release its tether until it was standing. Had it not been for the covenant of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with me, "Do not do anything until you come back to me," and had I wished, I would have killed him with an arrow.

Hudhayfah said: I returned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who was standing praying in a striped cloak belonging to one of his wives, wrapped and folded. When he saw me, he drew me between his legs and threw the edge of the cloak over me, then he bowed and prostrated while I was still with him. When he finished the prayer, I told him the news. Ghatafan heard what Quraysh had done, so they turned back to their lands.

[[Sirah of Ibn Hisham (2/231).]]

Muslim narrated it in his Sahih from the hadith of al-A'mash, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from his father, who said: We were with Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, may Allah be pleased with him, and a man said to him: "If I had reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), I would have fought with him and shown my valour." Hudhayfah said to him: "Would you have done that? We saw ourselves with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the night of the confederates, on a night of violent wind and cold. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Is there not a man who will bring us news of the people, who will be with me on the Day of Resurrection?' None of us answered him. Then he said it a second time, and a third time the same. Then he said: 'O Hudhayfah, stand up and bring us news of the people.' I had no choice, when he called me by my name, but to stand. He said: 'Bring me news of the people, and do not frighten them against me.' He said: So I went as if I were walking in a bathhouse, until I reached them, and there was Abu Sufyan warming his back at the fire. I placed an arrow on the belly of my bow and wanted to shoot him, then I remembered the words of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): 'Do not frighten them against me.' Had I shot him, I would have hit him. He said: I returned as if I were walking in a bathhouse, and came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Then the cold struck me when I finished and became chilled, and I told the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He put on me some of the surplus of a cloak he used to pray in, and I kept sleeping until morning. When I woke up, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Get up, O sleeper [[In manuscript A: "nawwam".]].'" [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1788).]]

Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated it from Hisham ibn Sa'd, from Zayd ibn Aslam, that a man said to Hudhayfah, may Allah be pleased with him: "We complain to Allah about your companionship with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). You met him and we did not meet him; you saw him and we did not see him." Hudhayfah said: "And we complain to Allah about your faith in him when you have not seen him. By Allah, you do not know, O my nephew, how you would have been had you met him. We saw ourselves with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the night of the Trench, on a cold rainy night..." and then he mentioned something similar to what preceded, at length. [[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (3/454), through Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Yunus ibn Bukayr.]]

Bilal ibn Yahya al-Absi also narrated something similar from Hudhayfah. [[Narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (3/31), and from his route al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (3/450), from Musa ibn Abi al-Mukhtar, from Bilal al-Absi, from Hudhayfah.]]

And Al-Hakim and Al-Bayhaqi (in "Al-Dala'il") narrated, from the hadith of Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar, from Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah al-Du'ali, from 'Abd al-'Aziz, the nephew of Hudhayfah, who said: Hudhayfah mentioned their stands (in battle) with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and his companions said: "By Allah, if we had witnessed that, we would have done such-and-such and such-and-such." Hudhayfah said: "Do not wish for that. We were on the night of the Confederates (al-Ahzab), when we were standing and sitting, and Abu Sufyan and those with him of the Confederates were above us, and Qurayzah the Jews were below us, and we feared them for our children. Never did a darker or fiercer wind come upon us; in the sound of its wind were like thunderbolts, and it was a darkness in which one of us could not see his own finger. The hypocrites began to ask permission of the Prophet ﷺ, saying: 'Indeed our houses are exposed,' and they were not exposed. None of them asked his permission except that he was granted it, and he would give them permission, and they would slip away. We were three hundred and some. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us, man by man, until he reached me, and I had nothing to protect me from the enemy or from the cold except a cloak belonging to my wife, which did not reach past my knees." He said: "The Prophet ﷺ came to me while I was crouching on my knees, and said: 'Who is this?' I said: 'Hudhayfah.' He said: 'Hudhayfah.' So I lowered myself to the ground and said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah,' out of dislike of standing up. [He said: 'Stand up.'] So I stood, and he said: 'Indeed there is news among the people, so bring me news of the people.'" He said: "I was among the most terrified of people and the most afflicted by cold." He said: "So I went out, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'O Allah, protect him from before him and behind him, from his right and from his left, and from above him and from below him.'" He said: "By Allah, Allah created no fear or cold within my body except that it left my body, so I found nothing in it." He said: "When I turned to leave, he said: 'O Hudhayfah, do not do anything among the people until you come back to me.'" He said: "I went out, and when I approached the camp of the people, I looked by the light of a fire they had blazing, and there was a dark, large man rubbing his hands over the fire and stroking his side, saying: 'Depart, depart!' I had not known Abu Sufyan before that. So I drew an arrow from my quiver, white-feathered, and placed it on the middle of my bow, intending to shoot him by the light of the fire. Then I remembered the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: 'Do not do anything among them until you come back to me.' So I held back and returned my arrow to my quiver. Then I encouraged myself until I entered the camp, and the nearest of the people to me were the Banu 'Amir, saying: 'O family of 'Amir, depart, depart! There is no staying for you.' The wind in their camp did not pass beyond their camp by a span. By Allah, I could hear the sound of stones in their saddles, and the wind was striking their tents and their bedding with them. Then I went out toward the Prophet ﷺ, and when I had gone half the way or about that, I found about twenty riders or so, wrapped up, who said: 'Inform your companion that Allah, the Exalted, has sufficed the people.' So I returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he was wrapped in a garment, praying. By Allah, no sooner had I returned than the cold overcame me and I began to tremble. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gestured to me with his hand while he was praying, so I drew near to him, and he wrapped his garment around me. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, whenever a matter distressed him, would pray. So I informed him of the news of the people, and told him that I had left them preparing to depart." And Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿O you who believe, remember the favour of Allah upon you when hosts came against you, so We sent upon them a wind and hosts you did not see. And Allah is ever Seeing of what you do.﴾ [Dala'il al-Nubuwwah of al-Bayhaqi (3/451).]

And Abu Dawud in his Sunan narrated from it: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, whenever a matter distressed him..." from the hadith of Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar, with it. [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1319.]

As for His saying: ﴿when they came at you from above you and from below you﴾, meaning: the Confederates came from above you and from below you. Hudhayfah's report mentioned earlier says they were the Banu Qurayzah. ﴿And when the eyes shifted and the hearts reached the throats﴾, meaning: from the intensity of fear and terror. ﴿And you assumed about Allah assumptions﴾.

Ibn Jarir said: Some of those who were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ thought that the reverse would befall the believers, and that Allah would do that. [Tafsir al-Tabari (21/83).]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said regarding His saying: ﴿And when the eyes shifted and the hearts reached the throats, and you assumed about Allah assumptions﴾: the believers entertained every kind of assumption, and hypocrisy surfaced, until Mu'attib ibn Qushayr, brother of Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf, said: "Muhammad used to promise us that we would eat the treasures of Khosrow and Caesar, while not one of us can go out to relieve himself."

Al-Hasan said regarding His saying: ﴿and you assumed about Allah assumptions﴾: various assumptions. The hypocrites assumed that Muhammad and his companions would be uprooted, while the believers were certain that what Allah and His Messenger had promised was true, and that He would make it prevail over all religion, even if the polytheists disliked it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn 'Asim al-Ansari narrated to us, Abu 'Amir narrated to us (and) my father narrated to us, Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi narrated to us, al-Zubayr, that is Ibn 'Abdullah, freedman of 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, narrated to us, from Rutayj ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa'id, from his father, from Abu Sa'id who said: On the day of the Trench we said: "O Messenger of Allah, is there something we can say, since the hearts have reached the throats?" He ﷺ said: "Yes, say: 'O Allah, conceal our faults, and secure our fears.'" He said: So he struck the faces of his enemies with the wind, and defeated them with the wind.

Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal also narrated it likewise, from Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi. [Al-Musnad (3/3).]

Ibn Kathir said, informing about that state when the confederates (al-Ahzab) gathered around Madinah, while the Muslims were besieged in extreme hardship and distress, with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) among them, that they were tested and tried and shaken with a severe shaking. Then hypocrisy appeared, and those in whose hearts was a sickness spoke out what was in their souls.

﴿And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease said, "Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion."﴾ As for the hypocrite, his hypocrisy showed itself openly. As for the one in whose heart there is a doubt or a resentment (hasikah), his condition weakened, so he gave vent to what he found of whisperings in his soul, because of the weakness of his faith and the severity of the narrow straits he was in.

Other people said, as Allah said: ﴿And when a group of them said, "O people of Yathrib"﴾, meaning Madinah, as came in the Sahih: "I was shown [in a dream] the land of your migration: a land between two lava plains (harratayn). My thought went to it being Hajar, but it was Yathrib," [Note: the narration of al-Bukhari no. (7035) from Abu Musa, may Allah be pleased with him.] and in another wording: "al-Madinah."

As for the hadith which Imam Ahmad narrated: Ibrahim ibn Mahdi narrated to us, Salih ibn Umar narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from al-Bara', may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever names Madinah Yathrib, let him seek forgiveness from Allah; it is Taba, it is Taba." [al-Musnad (4/285).]

Imam Ahmad alone narrated it, and in its chain there is weakness, and Allah knows best.

It is said that the original naming of it "Yathrib" was after a man of the Amalekites who settled there, called Yathrib ibn Ubayd ibn Mahlabil ibn Awd ibn Imlaq ibn Lawidh ibn Iram ibn Sam ibn Nuh. This was stated by al-Suhayli, who said: It was also narrated from some of them that it has eleven names in the Torah: al-Madinah, Taba, Taybah, al-Miskinah, al-Jabirah, al-Muhibbah, al-Mahbubah, al-Qasimah, al-Majburah, al-Adhra', and al-Marhumah.

And from Ka'b al-Ahbar, who said: We find in the Torah that Allah says to Madinah: "O Taybah, O Taba, O miskinah [do not reject the treasures; I raise your stones above the stones of the villages]."

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on surah 33, verses 18–19:

Allah the Exalted informs of the comprehensiveness of His knowledge regarding those who hinder others (al-mu'awwiqin) from witnessing the battle, and those who say to their brothers, i.e., their companions, their associates and their close friends: ﴿Come over to us﴾, i.e., to what we are in of residing in the shade and the fruits. Yet they ﴿do not come to the battle except a little, being niggardly towards you﴾, i.e., stingy with affection and compassion towards you.

Al-Suddi said: ﴿being niggardly towards you﴾ means in regard to the spoils of war.

﴿So when fear comes, you see them looking at you, their eyes rolling like one who has fainted from death﴾, i.e., from the intensity of their fear and dread, and such is the fear of these cowards from fighting. ﴿But when fear departs, they lash you with sharp tongues﴾, i.e., when there is safety, they speak eloquent, fluent, loud words, and claim for themselves lofty ranks in courage and valour, while they are lying in that.

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿lash you﴾ means they confronted you (istaqbalukum).

Qatadah said: As for at the time of the spoils, they are the most niggardly of people and the worst in dividing them, saying: "Give us, give us, for we have witnessed with you." As for at the time of danger, they are the most cowardly of people and the most forsaking of the truth.

Yet they are, along with that, ﴿niggardly regarding good﴾, i.e., there is no good in them. They have combined cowardice, lying and scarcity of good. They are, as the poet said about their likes:

"In peace, you are boors of coarse and rough manners,
and in war, like the women who are menstruating."

I.e., in a state of peace they are like donkeys, and in war like menstruating women. Al-A'yar is the plural of 'ir, which is the donkey (al-himar).

Therefore Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Those have not believed, so Allah has nullified their deeds, and that is ever easy for Allah﴾, i.e., easy and effortless with Him.

This is also one of their ugly traits: cowardice, fear, and feebleness. ﴿They think the confederates have not withdrawn﴾ — but they are close to them, and they will return to them. ﴿And if the confederates should come, they would wish that they were in the desert among the Bedouins, asking about your news﴾. That is, they would wish, when the confederates come, that they were not present with you in Madinah but in the desert, asking about your news and what happened between you and your enemy. ﴿And had they been among you, they would not have fought except a little﴾. That is, even if they were among you, they would not have fought with you except a little, because of their great cowardice, their abjectness, and the weakness of their certainty.

This noble verse is a great foundation for emulating the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in his sayings, actions, and conditions. For this reason, people were commanded to emulate the Prophet (ﷺ) on the day of the Confederates (al-Ahzab), in his patience, his steadfastness, his guarding of the frontier, his striving, and his waiting for relief from his Lord, Mighty and Majestic. May the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him always, until the Day of Recompense.
