Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 33, verse 23–24:

When He mentioned concerning the hypocrites that they had broken the covenant they had made with God that they would not turn their backs, He described the believers as having persisted in the covenant and the pledge, and [He said], ﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they covenanted with God. Among them are those who have fulfilled their vow (nahb) [by death], and among them are those who await [their turn]. And they have not changed in the least.﴾ Some of them said: "[Nahb means] their term (ajal)."

Al-Bukhari said: "[Nahb means] their pledge (ahd)," and this returns to the first [meaning].

﴿And among them are those who await, and they have not changed in the least.﴾ That is: they did not alter the covenant of God, nor break it, nor substitute it.

Al-Bukhari said: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Shu'ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Kharijah ibn Zayd ibn Thabit informed me, from his father [[In T: "Al-Bukhari narrated from Zayd ibn Thabit."]] who said: "When we copied out the scrolls [[In T and A: "the muṣḥaf."]], I lost a verse from Surat al-Ahzab which I used to hear the Messenger of God ﷺ recite. I could not find it with anyone except Khuzaymah ibn Thabit al-Ansari, whose testimony the Messenger of God ﷺ made equal to the testimony of two men: ﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they covenanted with God.﴾"

Al-Bukhari alone narrated it, without Muslim. Ahmad included it in his Musnad, and al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i in the Tafsir sections of their Sunans, from the hadith of al-Zuhri, with the same chain [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4784), al-Musnad (5/188), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3104), and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (11401).]]. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih."

Al-Bukhari also said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Ansari narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from Thumamah, from Anas ibn Malik who said: "We consider that this verse was revealed concerning Anas ibn al-Nadr: ﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they covenanted with God.﴾" [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4783).]]

Al-Bukhari alone narrated it through this route, but it has corroborating routes from other chains. Imam Ahmad said:

Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, from Thabit, who said: Anas said: "Anas ibn al-Nadr was named after [his uncle]. He did not witness the Battle of Badr with the Messenger of God ﷺ, and that grieved him. He said: 'The first battle the Messenger of God ﷺ witnessed, I was absent from it. If God lets me witness a battle with the Messenger of God ﷺ in the future, God will surely see what I do.'" He said: "He was afraid to say anything other than that, so he witnessed Uhud with the Messenger of God ﷺ. He met Sa'd ibn Mu'adh and said to him: 'O Abu 'Amr, [I smell] the scent of Paradise! I find it beyond Uhud.' He fought them until he was killed." He said: "There were found in his body eighty-some wounds from a strike, a stab, and an arrow." His sister — his paternal aunt al-Rubay' bint al-Nadr [[In T: "The aunt of al-Rubay' bint al-Nadr."]] — said: "I did not recognize my brother except by his fingertips." He said: "Then this verse was revealed: ﴿Men who have been true to what they covenanted with God. Among them are those who have fulfilled their vow, and among them are those who await, and they have not changed in the least.﴾" He said: "They used to consider that it was revealed concerning him and his companions."

Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i narrated it through the hadith of Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah, with the same chain [[al-Musnad (4/193), Sahih Muslim no. (1903), and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3200).]]. Al-Nasa'i also narrated it, and Ibn Jarir [al-Tabari] through the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit, from Anas, with similar wording [[al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (11404) and Tafsir al-Tabari (21/93).]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Humayd narrated to us, from Anas that his uncle — meaning Anas ibn al-Nadr — was absent from the Battle of Badr, and he said: "I was absent from the first battle the Messenger of God ﷺ fought against the polytheists. If God lets me witness a battle against the polytheists, God will surely see what I do." He said: "When the day of Uhud came and the Muslims fled, he said: 'O God, I apologize to You for what these men have done' — meaning his companions — 'and I disassociate myself before You from what these have come with' — meaning the polytheists." Then he advanced and met Sa'd — meaning Ibn Mu'adh — short of Uhud, and said: "I am with you." Sa'd said: "I could not do what he did." He said: "He was found with eighty-some wounds from sword strikes, spear thrusts, and arrow shots." They used to say: "It was revealed concerning him and his companions: ﴿Among them are those who have fulfilled their vow, and among them are those who await.﴾"

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in the Tafsir from 'Abd ibn Humayd, and al-Nasa'i also in it, from Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, both from Yazid ibn Harun, with the same chain [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3201) and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (11403).]]. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan." Al-Bukhari narrated it in al-Maghazi from Hassan ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Talhah ibn Musarrif, from Humayd, from Anas, with the same chain [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4048).]], but he did not mention the revelation of the verse. Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman, from Humayd, from Anas, with the same chain [[Tafsir al-Tabari (21/93).]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn al-Fadl al-'Asqalani narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Ayyub ibn Sulayman ibn 'Isa ibn Musa ibn Talhah ibn 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from my grandfather, from Musa ibn Talhah, from his father Talhah who said: "When the Prophet ﷺ returned from Uhud, he climbed the pulpit, praised God and extolled Him, consoled the Muslims for what had befallen them, and informed them of the reward and treasure they would have in it. Then he recited this verse: ﴿Men who have been true to what they covenanted with God﴾ [[After it in T, F, A: (Among them are those who have fulfilled their vow, and among them are those who await, and they have not changed in the least).]]. A man among the Muslims stood up and said: 'O Messenger of God, who are these?' I came forward, wearing two green Hadrami garments, and he said: 'O questioner, this one is among them.'"

Ibn Jarir likewise narrated it from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Ayyub al-Talhi, with the same chain [[Tafsir al-Tabari (21/94).]]. al-Tirmidhi also narrated it in the Tafsir and al-Manaqib, and Ibn Jarir, from the hadith of Yunus ibn Bukayr, from Talhah ibn Yahya, from Musa and 'Isa, the sons of Talhah, from their father, with the same chain [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3203).]]. He said: "Hasan gharib; we do not know it except from the hadith of Yunus."

He also said: Ahmad ibn 'Isam al-Ansari narrated to us, Abu 'Amir — meaning al-'Aqadi — narrated to us, Ishaq — meaning Ibn Talhah ibn 'Ubayd Allah — narrated to me, from Musa ibn Talhah who said: "I entered upon Mu'awiyah, may God be pleased with him. When I left, he called me and said: 'Shall I deposit with you, nephew, a hadith you heard from the Messenger of God ﷺ? I testify that I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: "Talhah is among those who have fulfilled their vow."'" [[Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in al-Sunan no. (3202) through the route of 'Amr ibn 'Asim, from Ishaq ibn Yahya ibn Talhah, with the same chain. Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a gharib hadith; we do not know it except through this route, and it is only narrated from Musa ibn Talhah, from his father."]].

Ibn Jarir also narrated it: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, 'Abd al-Hamid al-Himmani narrated to us, from Ishaq ibn Yahya ibn Talhah al-Talhi, from Musa ibn Talhah who said: Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan stood up and said: "I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: 'Talhah is among those who have fulfilled their vow.'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (21/93).]]

For this reason Mujahid said regarding His words, ﴿Among them are those who have fulfilled their vow﴾, he said: "[Nahb means] their pledge," and ﴿Among them are those who await﴾, he said: "a day."

Al-Hasan said: ﴿Among them are those who have fulfilled their vow﴾ means: their dying upon truthfulness and fidelity. ﴿And among them are those who await﴾ means: awaiting death upon the same [state]. And among them are those who have not changed in the least. Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said likewise.

Some of them said: ﴿Nahb﴾ means their vow (nadhr).

* *

As for His words, ﴿And they have not changed in the least﴾: that is, they did not alter their covenant, nor replace fulfilment with treachery. Rather, they persisted in what they had pledged to God, and did not break it, unlike the hypocrites who said: ﴿Indeed our houses are exposed, though they were not exposed. They only intended to flee﴾, and ﴿They had already covenanted with God before that they would not turn their backs.﴾

* *

As for His words, ﴿That God may reward the truthful for their truthfulness and punish the hypocrites if He wills, or accept their repentance﴾: that is, He tests His servants with fear and turmoil in order to distinguish the wicked from the good, so that the conduct of this person is made manifest in action, and the conduct of that person is manifest in action, even though He, exalted is He, knows a thing before it occurs. But He does not punish creatures for His knowledge of them until they act upon what He knows of them, as He said: ﴿And We will surely test you until We know those of you who strive and endure, and We will test your reports﴾ [Muhammad: 31]. So this is knowledge of a thing after its occurrence, even though the prior knowledge was already attained before its existence. Likewise He said: ﴿God would not leave the believers in the state you are in until He distinguishes the wicked from the good, nor would God inform you of the unseen﴾ [Al 'Imran: 179]. For this reason He said here: ﴿That God may reward the truthful for their truthfulness﴾, that is, for their patience in what they pledged to God, their standing by it, and their guarding it. ﴿And punish the hypocrites﴾: they are the ones who break the covenant of God and oppose His commands, so they deserve His punishment and retribution. But they are under His will in this world: if He wills, He keeps them upon what they did until they meet Him with it, and He punishes them for it; and if He wills, He accepts their repentance by guiding them to abandon hypocrisy for faith and to do righteous deeds after sinfulness and disobedience. And since His mercy and compassion toward His creatures prevail over His anger, He said: ﴿Indeed God is Ever-Forgiving, Most Merciful.﴾

So He sent upon them a wind that scattered their unity, just as the cause of their gathering had been desire (al-hawa). They gained no good in this world, from what they had hoped for in themselves of victory and spoils, nor in the Hereafter, for the sins they bore in opposing the Messenger, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, with hostility, their intent to kill him, and their plan to destroy his army. Whoever intends something and sincerely resolves to do it by action is, in reality, like its doer.

* *

His saying: ﴿And Allah sufficed the believers in fighting﴾ means: they did not need to engage them in combat or duel with them until they expelled them from their lands. Rather, Allah alone sufficed, supported His servant and strengthened His army. For this reason the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is no god but Allah alone; He fulfilled His promise, supported His servant, strengthened His army, and defeated the confederates alone; there is nothing after Him." Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4114) and Sahih Muslim no. (2724), with variation in wording.]].

In the Two Sahihs, from the hadith of Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ invoked against the confederates, saying: "O Allah, Revealer of the Book, swift in reckoning, defeat the confederates. O Allah, defeat them and shake them" [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2933) and Sahih Muslim no. (1742).]].

As for His saying ﴿And Allah sufficed the believers in fighting﴾, it indicates the ending of war between them and Quraysh, and so it happened afterward: the polytheists did not invade them; rather, the Muslims invaded them in their lands.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: When the people of the trench (al-Khandaq) departed from the trench, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, as we have been told: "Quraysh will not invade you after this year of yours, but you will invade them." So Quraysh did not invade after that, and he ﷺ used to invade them afterward, until Allah granted him the conquest of Makkah.

This hadith which Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned is sound, as the Imam Ahmad said: Yahya narrated to us, from Sufyan, who said: Abu Ishaq narrated to me, saying: I heard Sulayman ibn Surad say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day of the Confederates: "Now we will invade them, and they will not invade us."

Likewise al-Bukhari narrated it in his Sahih, from the hadith of al-Thawri and Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, with the same chain [[Al-Musnad (4/262) and Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4109).]].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah was ever Powerful and Mighty﴾, it means: by His power and strength He turned them back defeated, having gained no good. Allah exalted Islam and its people, fulfilled His promise, and supported His Messenger and His servant. So to Him belongs all praise and grace.

It has already been mentioned that when the Confederates' armies came and camped around Madinah, the Banu Qurayzah broke the covenant that existed between them and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. This was brought about by the instigation of Huyayy ibn Akhtab al-Nadri, may Allah curse him, who entered their fortress and kept working on their leader Ka'b ibn Asad until he broke the covenant. Among what he said to him was: "Woe to you! I have brought you the honour of the age. I have brought you Quraysh and their allies, and Ghatafan and their followers, and they will not leave here until they have uprooted Muhammad and his companions." Ka'b said to him: "Rather, by Allah, you have brought me the humiliation of the age. Woe to you, O Huyayy, you are ill-omened, so leave us alone." But Huyayy kept coaxing and cajoling him until he agreed. When the Banu Qurayzah broke the covenant and this reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, it grieved him greatly, and it was very hard for him and the Muslims. He said: "Have you laid down the weapons, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes." Jibril said: "But the angels have not laid down their weapons. This is my return from pursuing the people. Indeed Allah commands you to rise up against the Banu Qurayzah."

In another narration, he said to him: "Well done for a fighter! Have you laid down the weapons?" He said: "Yes." Jibril said: "But we have not yet laid down our weapons. Get up and go against these people." He said: "Where?" Jibril said: "The Banu Qurayzah, for Allah has commanded me to shake (the fortress) down upon them." He said: "None of you should pray the 'Asr except in the land of the Banu Qurayzah." The people set out, but the time of prayer overtook them on the way. Some of them prayed on the road and said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only intended us to hasten our march." Others said: "We will not pray it except in the land of the Banu Qurayzah." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ besieged them and laid siege to them for twenty-five nights. When the situation became prolonged for them, they agreed to submit to the judgement of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, the chief of the Aws, because they had been their allies in the Jahiliyyah, and they believed he would treat them kindly in this matter, just as Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul had done with his clients, the Banu Qaynuqa', when he asked (the Prophet) to release them from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So these people thought that Sa'd would act toward them as Ibn Ubayy had acted toward those. But they did not know that Sa'd, may Allah be pleased with him, had been struck by an arrow in his forearm (akhal) during the day of the Trench, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had cauterised his forearm, and had placed him in a tent in the mosque so that he could visit him from nearby. Sa'd had supplicated, saying: "O Allah, if You have left any of the war with Quraysh, then preserve me for it. And if You have ended the war between us and them, then let this wound burst open and do not let me die until my eye is comforted regarding the Banu Qurayzah."

So Allah answered his supplication, and decreed that they should come down to submit to his judgement, by their own choice, seeking it of their own accord. At that point the Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned him from Madinah to judge over them. When he came, riding a donkey [upon which they had spread a cushion for him], the Aws began to cling to him, saying: "O Sa'd, they are your clients, so treat them well." They tried to soften him toward them and sway him, while he remained silent and did not answer them. When they insisted, he said: "The time has come for Sa'd that he should not fear the blame of any blamer in the cause of Allah." They realised then that he would not spare them. When he drew near to the tent in which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Stand up for your chief." The Muslims rose to him and helped him down, out of reverence, honour and respect for him in the place of his authority, so that his judgement over them would be more binding. When he sat down, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "These people – and he pointed to them – have submitted to your judgement, so judge over them as you wish." He said: "And is my judgement binding over them?" He said: "Yes." He said: "And over those in this tent?" He said: "Yes." He said: "And over the one here?" – and he pointed to the side where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was, while he turned his face away from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ out of exaltation, honour and reverence – and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Yes." Then he said: "I judge that their fighting men be killed, their children and their wealth be taken as captives." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "You have indeed judged by the judgement of Allah from above seven heavens." [Narrated by Ibn Ishaq in al-Sirah, as in al-Bidayah wa'l-Nihayah (4/123), through the chain of Asim ibn Umar, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Umar, from Alqamah ibn Waqqas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, and then he mentioned it; I suspect there is an error in the chain. Its origin is in Sahih al-Bukhari, without the phrase "from above seven heavens," under no. (3043), from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.] In another narration: "You have judged by the judgement of the King." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered the trenches to be dug in the ground, and they were brought bound, and he struck their necks. They numbered between seven hundred and eight hundred. He took captive those who had not yet grown (to puberty) along with the women, and their wealth. [Al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (2/239).] All of this is set out in detail with its evidence and hadiths, and its full exposition, in the book of Sirah, which we have dedicated to it in a concise and summarised form. And to Allah belong all praise and grace.

* *

It was said: Makkah; Malik narrated this from Zayd ibn Aslam. It was said: Persia and Rome. Ibn Jarir said: It is permissible that all of these are intended.

﴿And Allah has power over all things﴾. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Muhammad ibn Amr informed us, from his father, from his grandfather Alqamah ibn Waqqas, who said: "Aishah informed me, saying: 'I went out on the day of the Trench, following the people, and I heard the sound of the earth behind me. Then I saw Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, and with him his nephew al-Harith ibn Aws carrying his shield.' She said: 'I sat down on the ground, and Sa'd passed by wearing an iron coat of mail from which its edges protruded, and I was afraid for the edges of Sa'd.' She said: 'Sa'd was one of the greatest and tallest of people, and he passed by reciting verse and saying:

"Wait a little, let the battle see the one who will fight.
How good is death when its appointed time has come..."'"

She said: I got up, rushed into an enclosure, and there was a group of Muslims there, and 'Umar ibn al-Khattab was among them, and with them was a man wearing a *tasbighah* (a coif of mail) over his head, meaning the helmet. 'Umar said: "What brought you here? By my life, by Allah, you are indeed bold, and what assures you that there will not be a calamity or that you will not be exposed?" She said: He kept reproaching me until I wished that the earth would split open for me at that moment so that I could enter it. Then the man lifted the coif from his face, and it was Talhah ibn 'Ubaid Allah. He said: "O 'Umar, woe to you! You have been excessive since today. Where is there any veering aside or fleeing except to Allah, the Exalted?"

She said: A man from Quraysh, called Ibn al-'Araqah, shot an arrow at Sa'd, and said: "Take this, and I am the son of al-'Araqah." It struck his *akhal* (the vein of the arm) and severed it. Sa'd supplicated to Allah, saying: "O Allah, do not let me die until my eyes are gladdened by [the punishment of] Qurayzah."

She said: They had been his allies and clients in the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam). She said: Then his blood stopped flowing, and Allah sent the wind upon the polytheists, and Allah spared the believers from fighting, and Allah is Strong and Mighty. Abu Sufyan and those with him went back to Tihamah, and 'Uyaynah ibn Badr and those with him went back to Najd, and the Banu Qurayzah returned and fortified themselves in their fortresses. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned to Madinah and ordered a tent of leather to be pitched for Sa'd in the mosque.

She said: Then Jibril, peace be upon him, came to him, and upon his front teeth was dust from the road, and he said: "Have you put down your weapons? No, by Allah, the angels have not yet put down their weapons. Go out to Banu Qurayzah and fight them."

She said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ put on his armor and called out to the people to set out, [and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out] and passed by Banu Ghanm, who were the neighbors of the mosque, around it, and he said: "Who passed by you?" They said: "Dihyah al-Kalbi passed by us," and Dihyah al-Kalbi had a beard, age and face resembling Jibril, peace be upon him. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to them and besieged them for twenty-five nights. When their siege intensified and the hardship grew severe, it was said to them: "Surrender to the judgment of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." They consulted Abu Lubabah ibn 'Abd al-Mundhir, and he signaled to them that it meant slaughter. They said: "We will surrender to the judgment of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh." [The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Surrender to the judgment of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh." So they surrendered, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent for Sa'd ibn Mu'adh] and he was brought on a donkey, on which was a pack-saddle of palm fiber, and his people surrounded him. They said: "O Abu 'Amr, these are your allies, your clients, and the people of your strength, as you know." She said: He did not respond to them at all, nor did he turn to them, until when he approached their houses he turned to his people and said: "The time has come for me that I should not fear the blame of any blamer for the sake of Allah."

He [the narrator] said: Abu Sa'id said: When he came into view, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Stand up for your master and bring him down." 'Umar said: "Our master is Allah." He said: "Bring him down." So they brought him down. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Judge concerning them." Sa'd said: "I judge concerning them that their fighting men be killed, their children be taken captive, and their wealth be divided." The Messenger of Allah said: "You have judged concerning them by the judgment of Allah and the judgment of His Messenger."

Then Sa'd supplicated, saying: "O Allah, if You have left anything of the war with Quraysh for Your Prophet, then keep me alive for it. And if You have ended the war between him and them, then take me to You." He said: Then his wound burst open, and it had healed except for a mark the size of a ring, and he returned to his tent which the Messenger of Allah had pitched for him.

'A'ishah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abu Bakr and 'Umar attended him. She said: By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, I could recognize the weeping of Abu Bakr from the weeping of 'Umar while I was in my chamber. And they were, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿compassionate among themselves﴾.

'Alqamah said: I said: "O mother, how did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ behave?" She said: "His eye did not shed tears for anyone, but when he was moved, he would take hold of his beard."

Then I saw Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, and with him his nephew al-Harith ibn Aws carrying his shield.' She said: 'I sat down on the ground, and Sa'd passed by wearing an iron coat of mail from which its edges protruded, and I was afraid for the edges of Sa'd.' She said: 'Sa'd was one of the greatest and tallest of people, and he passed by reciting verse and saying:

"Wait a little, let the battle see the one who will fight.
How good is death when its appointed time has come..."'"

She said: I got up, rushed into an enclosure, and there was a group of Muslims there, and 'Umar ibn al-Khattab was among them, and with them was a man wearing a *tasbighah* (a coif of mail) over his head, meaning the helmet. 'Umar said: "What brought you here? By my life, by Allah, you are indeed bold, and what assures you that there will not be a calamity or that you will not be exposed?" She said: He kept reproaching me until I wished that the earth would split open for me at that moment so that I could enter it. Then the man lifted the coif from his face, and it was Talhah ibn 'Ubaid Allah. He said: "O 'Umar, woe to you! You have been excessive since today. Where is there any veering aside or fleeing except to Allah, the Exalted?"

She said: A man from Quraysh, called Ibn al-'Araqah, shot an arrow at Sa'd, and said: "Take this, and I am the son of al-'Araqah." It struck his *akhal* (the vein of the arm) and severed it. Sa'd supplicated to Allah, saying: "O Allah, do not let me die until my eyes are gladdened by [the punishment of] Qurayzah."

She said: They had been his allies and clients in the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam). She said: Then his blood stopped flowing, and Allah sent the wind upon the polytheists, and Allah spared the believers from fighting, and Allah is Strong and Mighty. Abu Sufyan and those with him went back to Tihamah, and 'Uyaynah ibn Badr and those with him went back to Najd, and the Banu Qurayzah returned and fortified themselves in their fortresses. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned to Madinah and ordered a tent of leather to be pitched for Sa'd in the mosque.

She said: Then Jibril, peace be upon him, came to him, and upon his front teeth was dust from the road, and he said: "Have you put down your weapons? No, by Allah, the angels have not yet put down their weapons. Go out to Banu Qurayzah and fight them."

She said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ put on his armor and called out to the people to set out, [and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out] and passed by Banu Ghanm, who were the neighbors of the mosque, around it, and he said: "Who passed by you?" They said: "Dihyah al-Kalbi passed by us," and Dihyah al-Kalbi had a beard, age and face resembling Jibril, peace be upon him. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to them and besieged them for twenty-five nights. When their siege intensified and the hardship grew severe, it was said to them: "Surrender to the judgment of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." They consulted Abu Lubabah ibn 'Abd al-Mundhir, and he signaled to them that it meant slaughter. They said: "We will surrender to the judgment of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh." [The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Surrender to the judgment of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh." So they surrendered, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent for Sa'd ibn Mu'adh] and he was brought on a donkey, on which was a pack-saddle of palm fiber, and his people surrounded him. They said: "O Abu 'Amr, these are your allies, your clients, and the people of your strength, as you know." She said: He did not respond to them at all, nor did he turn to them, until when he approached their houses he turned to his people and said: "The time has come for me that I should not fear the blame of any blamer for the sake of Allah."

He [the narrator] said: Abu Sa'id said: When he came into view, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Stand up for your master and bring him down." 'Umar said: "Our master is Allah." He said: "Bring him down." So they brought him down. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Judge concerning them." Sa'd said: "I judge concerning them that their fighting men be killed, their children be taken captive, and their wealth be divided." The Messenger of Allah said: "You have judged concerning them by the judgment of Allah and the judgment of His Messenger."

Then Sa'd supplicated, saying: "O Allah, if You have left anything of the war with Quraysh for Your Prophet, then keep me alive for it. And if You have ended the war between him and them, then take me to You." He said: Then his wound burst open, and it had healed except for a mark the size of a ring, and he returned to his tent which the Messenger of Allah had pitched for him.

'A'ishah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abu Bakr and 'Umar attended him. She said: By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, I could recognize the weeping of Abu Bakr from the weeping of 'Umar while I was in my chamber. And they were, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿compassionate among themselves﴾.

'Alqamah said: I said: "O mother, how did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ behave?" She said: "His eye did not shed tears for anyone, but when he was moved, he would take hold of his beard."

Al-Bukhari and Muslim have narrated, from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Numayr, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, something similar to this, but it is more concise than it, and in it is the supplication of Sa'd, may Allah be pleased with him.

This is a command from Allah to His Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him,^[In T: "may Allah bless him and grant him peace."] to give his wives the choice of parting from him, in which case they may go to another man who can provide them with the life of this world and its adornments, or of remaining patient with what he has of hardship, and for them with Allah in that is abundant reward. They chose Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Abode, may Allah be pleased with them and make them pleased. After that, Allah combined for them the good of this world and the happiness of the Hereafter.

Al-Bukhari said: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Shu'ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman informed me that 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, informed him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to her when Allah commanded him to give his wives the choice, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began with me and said: "I am going to mention a matter to you, and there is no harm in you not hurrying until you consult your two parents." She knew that her parents would not have commanded her to part from him. She said: Then he said: "Indeed Allah said: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives…﴾" up to the end of the two verses. I said to him: "About this matter should I consult my parents? I want Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Abode."^[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4785).]

It was also narrated in mu'allaq form from al-Layth: Yunus narrated to me, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, from 'Aishah, and he mentioned it and added: She said: Then the wives of the Prophet ﷺ did the same as I did.^[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4786).]

Al-Bukhari also relates that Ma'mar was inconsistent: at times he narrated it from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, and at other times he narrated it from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'Aishah.^[Sahih al-Bukhari (8/520), Fath.]

Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn 'Abdah al-Dabbi narrated to us, Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from 'Umar ibn Abi Salamah, from his father, who said: 'Aishah said: When the option was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "I want to mention a matter to you, so do not decide anything about it until you consult your two parents." She said: I said: "And what is it, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: So he repeated it to her. She said: "What is it, O Messenger of Allah?" She said: So he recited to her: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the life of this world and its adornment…﴾ up to the end of the verse. She said: I said: "Rather, we choose Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Abode." She said: So the Prophet ﷺ was delighted by that.^[Tafsir al-Tabari (21/100).]

Ibn Waki' also narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Abu Salamah, from 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: When the verse of the option was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began with me and said: "O 'Aishah, I am presenting to you a matter, so do not give me a ruling about it [anything]^[Addition from T, F, and al-Tabari.] until you present it to your two parents, Abu Bakr and Umm Ruman." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is it?" He said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the life of this world and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and release you with a fair release. And if you desire Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Abode, then indeed Allah has prepared for the good-doers among you a great reward.﴾" She said: "Then I desire Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Abode, and I will not consult my two parents, Abu Bakr and Umm Ruman about that." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed, then he looked at the chambers and said: "Indeed 'Aishah said such and such." They said: "We too say the same as what 'Aishah said, may Allah be pleased with them all."^[Tafsir al-Tabari (21/101).]

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it from Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj, from Abu Usamah, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, with the same wording.

Ibn Jarir said: Sa'id ibn Yahya al-Umawi narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, from 'Amrah, from 'Aishah: that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came down to his wives, he was commanded to give them the choice. He entered upon me and said: "I will mention a matter to you, so do not hurry until you consult your father." I said: "And what is it, O Prophet of Allah?" He said: "I have been commanded to give you the choice." He recited to her the verse of the choice up to the end of the two verses. She said: I said: "And what is this that you say, 'Do not hurry until you consult your father'? Indeed, I choose Allah and His Messenger." So he was pleased by that, and he presented it to his wives, and they all followed suit, so they chose Allah and His Messenger.^[Tafsir al-Tabari (21/101).]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yazid ibn Sinan al-Basri narrated to us, Abu Salih 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, al-Layth narrated to me, 'Uqayl narrated to me, from al-Zuhri, who said: 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Thawr informed me, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: The verse of the choice was revealed, and he began with me, the first of his wives, and said: "I am mentioning a matter to you, so is there no harm in you not hurrying until you consult your two parents?" She said: "He knows that my parents would not have commanded me to part from him." She said: Then he said: "Indeed Allah said: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives…﴾" the two verses. 'Aishah said: I said: "About this should I consult my parents? Indeed I want Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Abode." Then he gave the choice to all his wives, and they all said the same as what 'Aishah said, may Allah be pleased with them all.

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrated it, from Qutaybah, from al-Layth, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'Aishah, a similar report.^[So it is, but I have not found it with this isnad in either of them, nor did al-Mizzi mention it in Tuhfat al-Ashraf; perhaps I will check it later.]

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Muslim ibn Subayh, from Masruq, from 'Aishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave us the choice, so we chose him, and he did not count it against us as anything. Both of them (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated it from the hadith of al-A'mash.^[Al-Musnad (6/45), Sahih al-Bukhari no. (5262), and Sahih Muslim no. (1477).]

Imam Ahmad also said: Abu 'Amir 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Amr narrated to us, Zakariyya ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, came seeking permission to enter upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while people were sitting at his door and the Prophet ﷺ was sitting, but he was not given permission. Then 'Umar came and sought permission, but he was not given permission. Then permission was given to Abu Bakr and 'Umar, and they entered while the Prophet ﷺ was sitting with his wives around him, and he was silent. 'Umar said: "I will speak to the Prophet ﷺ so that perhaps he will laugh." So 'Umar said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you had seen the daughter of Zayd, the wife of 'Umar, who asked me for maintenance a moment ago, and I struck her neck." So the Prophet ﷺ laughed until his molar teeth showed,^[In F: "his molars."] and said: "They are around me, asking me for maintenance." Then Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, rose toward 'Aishah to strike her, and 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, rose toward Hafsah, both of them saying: "You ask the Prophet ﷺ for what he does not have." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade them, and his wives said: "By Allah, we will not ask the Messenger of Allah for what he does not have after this sitting." He said: Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed the option, so he began with 'Aishah and said: "I am mentioning a matter to you about which I do not like you to hurry until you consult your two parents." She said: "And what is it?" He said: So he recited to her: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives…﴾ the verse. 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "Should I consult my parents about you? Rather, I choose Allah and His Messenger, and I ask you not to mention to any of your wives what I have chosen." He said: "Indeed Allah, the Exalted, did not send me as one who harasses, but He sent me as a teacher and one who makes things easy. None of them will ask me about what you have chosen except that I will inform her."

Muslim alone narrated it without al-Bukhari, and he and al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Zakariyya ibn Ishaq al-Makki, with the same chain.^[Al-Musnad (3/328), Sahih Muslim no. (1478), and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (9208).]

'Abd Allah ibn Imam Ahmad said: Surayj ibn Yunus narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Hashim ibn al-Barid narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd [Allah ibn 'Ali]^[Addition from T, F, and al-Musnad.] ibn Abi Rafi', from 'Uthman ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave his wives the choice between this world and the Hereafter, and did not give them the choice of divorce.^[Zawa'id al-Musnad (1/78).]

This report is disconnected (munqati'), and similar reports have been narrated from al-Hasan, Qatadah, and others. It is contrary to the apparent meaning of the verse, for He said: ﴿Then come, I will provide for you and release you with a fair release,﴾ meaning: I will give you your rights and set you free.

The scholars differed over whether it is permissible for another man to marry them if he divorced them, in two opinions. The more correct of the two is yes, should it occur, so that the purpose of the release is achieved. And Allah knows best.

'Ikrimah said: On that day he had nine wives, five of them from Quraysh: 'Aishah, Hafsah, Umm Habibah, Sawdah, and Umm Salamah. Also married to him ﷺ were Safiyyah bint Huyayy al-Nadriyyah, Maymunah bint al-Harith al-Hilaliyyah, Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyyah, and Juwayriyah bint al-Harith al-Mustaliqiyyah, may Allah be pleased with them all and make them pleased.

[He did not marry any of them except after Khadijah bint Khuwaylid ibn Asad ibn 'Abd al-'Uzza ibn Qusayy ibn Kilab died. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married her in Makkah when he was twenty-five years old. She remained with him until Allah honored him with His message; she believed in him and supported him, and she was a worthy companion to him. She died three years before the Hijrah, according to the most sound view, may Allah be pleased with her. She had special virtues, among them that he did not marry another woman in addition to her, and among them that all his children were from her, except Ibrahim, who was from his concubine Mariyah. And among them that she was the best of the women of this Ummah.

Scholars differed over whether she is preferred over 'Aishah, in three opinions, the third being to withhold judgment.

Our shaykh Abu al-'Abbas ibn Taymiyyah was asked about the two of them and said: Each of them was distinguished by a particular quality. Khadijah's influence was at the beginning of Islam; she would console the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, strengthen him, calm him, and spend her wealth for him. She experienced the early dawn of Islam, bore harm for the sake of Allah and His Messenger, and her support for the Messenger came at the greatest times of need. So she had a station of support and sacrifice that no one else had. 'Aishah's influence was at the end of Islam; she had a depth of understanding of the religion and conveying it to the Ummah, and her sons benefited from the knowledge she passed on to them, which no one else had. This is the meaning of his words, may Allah be pleased with him.]

**Among her distinctions:** God, glorified is He, sent peace (salam) to her through Jibril, and the Messenger of God ﷺ conveyed it to her. Al-Bukhari related in his Sahih, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Jibril, peace be upon him, came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of God, this is Khadijah, who has come to you carrying a vessel containing a condiment, or food, or drink. When she comes to you, convey to her peace from her Lord and from me, and give her the good news of a house in Paradise, made of reed, with no clamor in it and no fatigue." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3820.] By the Lord's life, this distinction was hers alone and was not given to anyone else. As for Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, Jibril conveyed greetings to her through the tongue of the Prophet ﷺ. Al-Bukhari related with his chain that Aishah said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said one day: "O Aishah, this is Jibril, who sends you his greetings." I said: "And upon him be peace, and the mercy of God and His blessings. You see what I do not see," meaning the Messenger of God ﷺ. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3768.]

Among the distinctions of Khadijah, may Allah be pleased with her, is that he was never displeased by her, she never angered him, he never swore an oath of abstention (ila') against her, and he never reproached her or shunned her. This alone is sufficient as a virtue and an excellence.

**Among her distinctions:** she was the first woman to believe in God and His Messenger from this Ummah.

**Section:**
When God took her, he married after her Sawdah bint Zam'ah, may Allah be pleased with her. She was Sawdah bint Zam'ah ibn Qays ibn Abd Shams ibn Abd Wudd ibn Nasr ibn Malik ibn Jabal ibn Amir ibn Lu'ayy. She grew old in his household, and he intended to divorce her, but she gave her day to Aishah, and so he kept her. This is among her distinctions: she preferred the love of the Prophet ﷺ with her day, seeking nearness to the Messenger of God ﷺ and out of love for him, and preferring to remain with him. So he would allot Aishah her day and Sawdah's day, and he would allot his other wives their days, and he did not allot a day to Sawdah, while she was content with that and preferred it, in order to please the Messenger of God ﷺ.

He married the truthful one (al-Siddiqah), the daughter of the truthful one (al-Siddiq), Aishah bint Abi Bakr, may Allah be pleased with both of them. She was six years old two years before the Hijrah, and it was said three years. He consummated the marriage with her in Madinah at the start of his arrival, in the first year, when she was nine. He died leaving her at eighteen. She died in Madinah and was buried in al-Baqi', and she bequeathed that Abu Hurayrah should lead the funeral prayer over her, in the year fifty-eight. Among her distinctions: she was the most beloved of the wives of the Messenger of God ﷺ to him, as was established from him in al-Bukhari and others, when he was asked: "Which of the people is most beloved to you?" He said: "Aishah." It was said: "And among the men?" He said: "Her father." [I have not found it in Sahih al-Bukhari. It is in Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3879, from the hadith of Amr ibn al-As, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Also among her distinctions: he did not marry a virgin other than her, and among her distinctions: revelation would descend upon him while he was under her quilt, and not under anyone else's.

Among her distinctions: when God, mighty and majestic, sent down to him the verse of choice (ayat al-takhyir), he began with her and offered her the choice, saying: "And there is no blame on you if you do not hasten until you consult your two parents." She said: "Am I to consult my parents about this? I want God, His Messenger, and the Last Abode." The rest of his wives followed her example, and they said what she said.

Among her distinctions: God, glorified is He, cleared her of what the people of the slander (ahl al-ifk) had accused her of, and He sent down, concerning her excuse and her innocence, a revelation that is recited in the prayer niches (mihrabs) of the Muslims and their prayers until the Day of Resurrection. He bore witness that she was among the good women, and He promised her forgiveness and generous provision. God, glorified is He, informed that what was said about her of falsehood was good for her, and that what was said about her was not an evil for her, nor a defect in her, nor a lowering of her status. Rather, God elevated her by it, raised her rank, magnified her station, and made her remembered with purity and innocence among the people of the earth and the heavens. How great a virtue this is! Reflect on this honor and dignity, which arose from her extreme humility and her belittling of herself, when she said: "My affair in my own eyes was too insignificant for God to speak concerning me with a revelation that is recited; but I hoped that the Messenger of God ﷺ would see a dream by which God would clear me." So she is the truthful one of this Ummah, the Mother of the Believers, and the beloved of the Messenger of God ﷺ. She knew she was innocent and wronged, and that her accusers were wrongdoers who had fabricated against her. Their harm reached her parents and the Messenger of God ﷺ. This was her belittling of herself and her diminishing of her own status. So what do you think of one who has fasted a day or two, or a month or two, or stood in prayer for a night or two, and then some of the states appeared upon him, and they regarded themselves through the lens of deserving miracles (karamat), and that they are among those whose meeting is sought for blessing and whose good supplications are sought, and that the people must honor them, revere them, exalt them, and venerate them, so that their garments are touched for blessing and the dust of their thresholds is kissed; and that they hold such a station with God that God avenges them immediately upon whoever belittles them, and that whoever commits a breach of etiquette against them is seized without delay? Indeed, a breach of etiquette against them is a sin that nothing expiates except their pleasure.

Had this been an outcome of sufficiency, it would be bearable; but it comes from deficiency. These follies and foolish excesses are the product of profound ignorance and a crooked intellect. Such conduct proceeds only from an ignorant person who is self-admiring, heedless of his own crime, faults, and sins, deceived by God's respite for him from seizing him for the arrogance and contempt he displays toward those who may be better than him in God's sight. We ask God for well-being in this world and the next. A servant should seek refuge in God from being great in his own eyes while being insignificant in God's sight.

Among the distinctions of Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her: when matters among the senior Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, became unclear to them regarding the religion, they would ask her for a ruling, and they would find her knowledge with her.

Among her distinctions: the Messenger of God ﷺ died in her house. Also among her distinctions: the angel showed her image to the Prophet ﷺ before he married her, in a piece of silk, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "If this is from God, He will make it come to pass." [Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 5078, from the hadith of Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her.] Also among her distinctions: the people used to seek out their gifts for the Messenger of God ﷺ on her day, seeking nearness to the Messenger ﷺ, so they would present him with what he loved at the home of his most beloved wife, may Allah be pleased with them all. She was known by the kunyah Umm Abd Allah. It is related that she miscarried a child from the Prophet ﷺ, but this is not established.

The Messenger of God ﷺ married Hafsah bint Umar ibn al-Khattab. She had previously been married to Khunays ibn Hudhafah, who was one of the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ and among those who witnessed Badr. She died in the year forty-five, or it was said fifty-eight. Among her distinctions is what the hafiz Abu Muhammad al-Maqdisi mentioned in his abridgment of the biography: that the Prophet ﷺ divorced her, and Jibril came to him and said: "God commands you to take Hafsah back, for she is a woman who fasts often and prays much at night, and she is your wife in Paradise."

Al-Tabarani said in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: Ahmad ibn Tahir ibn Harmalah ibn Yahya related to us, my grandfather Harmalah related to us, Ibn Wahb related to us, Amr ibn Salih al-Hadrami related to us, from Musa ibn Ali ibn Rabah, from his father, from Uqbah ibn Amir, that the Prophet ﷺ divorced Hafsah. When this reached Umar ibn al-Khattab, he put dust on his head and said: "God does not care for the son of al-Khattab after this." Then Jibril, peace be upon him, descended upon the Prophet ﷺ and said: "God commands you to take back Hafsah, as a mercy to Umar." [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (17/291). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (4/334): "In it is Amr ibn Salih al-Hadrami, whom I do not know, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy."]

The Messenger of God ﷺ married Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan, whose name was Ramlah bint Sakhr ibn Harb ibn Umayyah ibn Abd Shams ibn Abd Manaf. She emigrated with her husband Abd Allah ibn Jahsh to the land of Abyssinia, where he became a Christian, but God completed Islam for her. The Messenger of God ﷺ married her while she was in the land of Abyssinia. He gave her as dowry, through the Negus, four hundred dinars, and the Messenger of God ﷺ sent Amr ibn Umayyah al-Damri with her to the land of Abyssinia. Her marriage was arranged by Uthman ibn Affan, and it was said by Khalid ibn Sa'id ibn al-As. She is the one who guarded the bedding of the Messenger of God ﷺ from her father sitting upon it, when Abu Sufyan came to Madinah, and she told him: "You are a polytheist," and she prevented him from sitting on it.

The Messenger of God ﷺ married Umm Salamah, whose name was Hind bint Abi Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah ibn Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn Makhzum ibn Yaqzah ibn Murrah ibn Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy ibn Ghalib. She had previously been married to Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Asad. She died in the year sixty-two and was buried in al-Baqi'. She was the last of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ to die, though it was also said that it was Maymunah. Among her distinctions: Jibril entered upon the Prophet ﷺ while she was with him, and she saw him in the form of Dihyah al-Kalbi. In Sahih Muslim, from Abu Uthman, who said: "I was informed that Jibril came to the Prophet ﷺ while Umm Salamah was with him." He began to converse, then he rose, and the Prophet of God ﷺ said to Umm Salamah: "Who is this?" or words to that effect. She said: "This is Dihyah al-Kalbi." She said: "By God, I did not think him to be anyone but him, until I heard the Prophet's ﷺ sermon informing that he was Jibril," or words to that effect. Sulayman al-Taymi said: "I said to Abu Uthman: From whom did you hear this hadith?" He said: "From Usamah ibn Zayd." [Sahih Muslim, no. 2451.]

Her son Umar married her to the Messenger of God ﷺ. Some scholars rejected this on the grounds that her son at that time was not old enough to conduct a marriage contract. Imam Ahmad rejected this and denounced whoever said it. What supports the correctness of Ahmad's view is what Muslim related in his Sahih: that Umar ibn Abi Salamah, her son, asked the Prophet ﷺ about kissing for one who is fasting. He said: "Ask her," meaning Umm Salamah. She informed him that the Messenger of God ﷺ used to do it. He said: "We are not like the Messenger of God ﷺ, for God makes lawful for His Messenger whatever He wills." Then the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "I am the most God-fearing of you and the most knowing of Him," or words to that effect. [Sahih Muslim, no. 1108.] Such a thing is not said of a very young child, and Umar was born in the land of Abyssinia before the Hijrah. Al-Bayhaqi said: "The claim of one who asserts that he was a child is a mere assertion, and his youth has not been established by a sound chain."

The Messenger of God ﷺ married Zaynab bint Jahsh from the Banu Khuzaymah ibn Mudrikah ibn Ilyas ibn Mudar. She was the daughter of his paternal aunt Umaymah bint Abd al-Muttalib. She had previously been married to his freed slave Zayd ibn Harithah, but he divorced her, and God married her to him from above the seven heavens, and He sent down to him: "So when Zayd had accomplished his need from her, We married her to you." He then rose and entered upon her without seeking permission. She used to boast of this over the rest of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, saying: "Your families gave you in marriage, but God married me from above His seven heavens." This is among her distinctions. She died in Madinah in the year twenty and was buried in al-Baqi'.

The Prophet (ﷺ) married Zaynab bint Khuzaymah al-Hilaliyyah. She had previously been married to Abdullah ibn Jahsh. He married her in the third year after the Hijrah, and she was called Umm al-Masakin (the Mother of the Poor). She remained with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) only briefly, two or three months, and then she died, may Allah be pleased with her.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married Juwayriyah bint al-Harith of the Banu al-Mustaliq. She had been taken captive in the battle of the Banu al-Mustaliq and fell to the share of Thabit ibn Qays. He made a contract of manumission with her (kitabah, a written agreement by which a slave purchases her freedom in installments), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) settled her kitabah. He married her in the sixth year after the Hijrah, and she died in the fifty-sixth year. Because of her, the Muslims freed one hundred households of slaves, and they said, "They are the in-laws of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." This was among the blessings she brought to her people.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married Safiyyah bint Huyayy, who was of the lineage of Harun ibn Imran, the brother of Musa, in the seventh year. She had been taken captive from Khaybar. Previously she had been married to Kinanah ibn Abi al-Huqayq, whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) killed. She died in the thirty-sixth year, and it is said in the fiftieth year. Among her distinctive qualities is that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) freed her and made her freedom her dowry (mahr). Anas said, "He gave her freedom as her dowry," and this became a precedent for the slave-woman until the Day of Resurrection. It is permissible for a man to make the freedom of his slave-girl her dowry, and she becomes his wife, according to the explicit ruling of Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him.

At-Tirmidhi said: Ishaq ibn Mansur and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, both saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: It reached Safiyyah that Hafsah had said, "Safiyyah is the daughter of a Jew." So she wept. The Prophet (ﷺ) entered upon her while she was weeping, and he said, "What makes you weep?" She said, "Hafsah said to me, 'I am the daughter of a Jew.'" The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "You are indeed the daughter of a prophet, your uncle is a prophet, and you are under a prophet. So in what does she boast over you?" Then he said, "Fear Allah, O Hafsah." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3894), and he said: "This is a hasan sahih gharib hadith from this route."]] At-Tirmidhi said: This is a sahih gharib hadith from this route. And this is among her distinctive qualities, may Allah be pleased with her.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married Maymunah bint al-Harith al-Hilaliyyah. He married her at Sarif, which is nine miles from Makkah. She was the last of the Mothers of the Believers to be married. She died in the sixty-third year. She was the maternal aunt of Khalid ibn al-Walid and the maternal aunt of Ibn Abbas, since his mother was Umm al-Fadl bint al-Harith. Scholars have differed concerning the Prophet's (ﷺ) marriage to her: did he marry her while in the state of ihram or not? The sound view is that he married her while not in ihram, as Abu Rafi' al-Shafir said concerning her marriage.

Al-Hafiz Abu Muhammad al-Maqdisi and others said: He contracted marriage with seven women and did not consummate with them. Therefore, the prayers upon his wives follow from their honor and from their being forbidden to the community, and that they are his wives (ﷺ) in this world and the Hereafter. Whoever separated from a wife during her lifetime before consummation does not acquire the rulings that apply to the wives with whom he consummated the marriage. May Allah bless him, his wives, his family and his descendants, and grant them abundant peace. [[Addition from manuscript T.]]

This is a command from Allah to His Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him,^[In T: "may Allah bless him and grant him peace."] to give his wives the choice of parting from him, in which case they may go to another man who can provide them with the life of this world and its adornments, or of remaining patient with what he has of hardship, and for them with Allah in that is abundant reward. They chose Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Abode, may Allah be pleased with them and make them pleased. After that, Allah combined for them the good of this world and the happiness of the Hereafter.

Al-Bukhari said: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Shu'ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman informed me that 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, informed him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to her when Allah commanded him to give his wives the choice, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began with me and said: "I am going to mention a matter to you, and there is no harm in you not hurrying until you consult your two parents." She knew that her parents would not have commanded her to part from him. She said: Then he said: "Indeed Allah said: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives…﴾" up to the end of the two verses. I said to him: "About this matter should I consult my parents? I want Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Abode."^[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4785).]

It was also narrated in mu'allaq form from al-Layth: Yunus narrated to me, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, from 'Aishah, and he mentioned it and added: She said: Then the wives of the Prophet ﷺ did the same as I did.^[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4786).]

Al-Bukhari also relates that Ma'mar was inconsistent: at times he narrated it from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, and at other times he narrated it from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'Aishah.^[Sahih al-Bukhari (8/520), Fath.]

Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn 'Abdah al-Dabbi narrated to us, Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from 'Umar ibn Abi Salamah, from his father, who said: 'Aishah said: When the option was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "I want to mention a matter to you, so do not decide anything about it until you consult your two parents." She said: I said: "And what is it, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: So he repeated it to her. She said: "What is it, O Messenger of Allah?" She said: So he recited to her: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the life of this world and its adornment…﴾ up to the end of the verse. She said: I said: "Rather, we choose Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Abode." She said: So the Prophet ﷺ was delighted by that.^[Tafsir al-Tabari (21/100).]

Ibn Waki' also narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Abu Salamah, from 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: When the verse of the option was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began with me and said: "O 'Aishah, I am presenting to you a matter, so do not give me a ruling about it [anything]^[Addition from T, F, and al-Tabari.] until you present it to your two parents, Abu Bakr and Umm Ruman." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is it?" He said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the life of this world and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and release you with a fair release. And if you desire Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Abode, then indeed Allah has prepared for the good-doers among you a great reward.﴾" She said: "Then I desire Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Abode, and I will not consult my two parents, Abu Bakr and Umm Ruman about that." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed, then he looked at the chambers and said: "Indeed 'Aishah said such and such." They said: "We too say the same as what 'Aishah said, may Allah be pleased with them all."^[Tafsir al-Tabari (21/101).]

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it from Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj, from Abu Usamah, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, with the same wording.

Ibn Jarir said: Sa'id ibn Yahya al-Umawi narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, from 'Amrah, from 'Aishah: that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came down to his wives, he was commanded to give them the choice. He entered upon me and said: "I will mention a matter to you, so do not hurry until you consult your father." I said: "And what is it, O Prophet of Allah?" He said: "I have been commanded to give you the choice." He recited to her the verse of the choice up to the end of the two verses. She said: I said: "And what is this that you say, 'Do not hurry until you consult your father'? Indeed, I choose Allah and His Messenger." So he was pleased by that, and he presented it to his wives, and they all followed suit, so they chose Allah and His Messenger.^[Tafsir al-Tabari (21/101).]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yazid ibn Sinan al-Basri narrated to us, Abu Salih 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, al-Layth narrated to me, 'Uqayl narrated to me, from al-Zuhri, who said: 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Thawr informed me, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: The verse of the choice was revealed, and he began with me, the first of his wives, and said: "I am mentioning a matter to you, so is there no harm in you not hurrying until you consult your two parents?" She said: "He knows that my parents would not have commanded me to part from him." She said: Then he said: "Indeed Allah said: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives…﴾" the two verses. 'Aishah said: I said: "About this should I consult my parents? Indeed I want Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Abode." Then he gave the choice to all his wives, and they all said the same as what 'Aishah said, may Allah be pleased with them all.

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrated it, from Qutaybah, from al-Layth, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'Aishah, a similar report.^[So it is, but I have not found it with this isnad in either of them, nor did al-Mizzi mention it in Tuhfat al-Ashraf; perhaps I will check it later.]

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Muslim ibn Subayh, from Masruq, from 'Aishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave us the choice, so we chose him, and he did not count it against us as anything. Both of them (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated it from the hadith of al-A'mash.^[Al-Musnad (6/45), Sahih al-Bukhari no. (5262), and Sahih Muslim no. (1477).]

Imam Ahmad also said: Abu 'Amir 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Amr narrated to us, Zakariyya ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, came seeking permission to enter upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while people were sitting at his door and the Prophet ﷺ was sitting, but he was not given permission. Then 'Umar came and sought permission, but he was not given permission. Then permission was given to Abu Bakr and 'Umar, and they entered while the Prophet ﷺ was sitting with his wives around him, and he was silent. 'Umar said: "I will speak to the Prophet ﷺ so that perhaps he will laugh." So 'Umar said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you had seen the daughter of Zayd, the wife of 'Umar, who asked me for maintenance a moment ago, and I struck her neck." So the Prophet ﷺ laughed until his molar teeth showed,^[In F: "his molars."] and said: "They are around me, asking me for maintenance." Then Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, rose toward 'Aishah to strike her, and 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, rose toward Hafsah, both of them saying: "You ask the Prophet ﷺ for what he does not have." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade them, and his wives said: "By Allah, we will not ask the Messenger of Allah for what he does not have after this sitting." He said: Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed the option, so he began with 'Aishah and said: "I am mentioning a matter to you about which I do not like you to hurry until you consult your two parents." She said: "And what is it?" He said: So he recited to her: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives…﴾ the verse. 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "Should I consult my parents about you? Rather, I choose Allah and His Messenger, and I ask you not to mention to any of your wives what I have chosen." He said: "Indeed Allah, the Exalted, did not send me as one who harasses, but He sent me as a teacher and one who makes things easy. None of them will ask me about what you have chosen except that I will inform her."

Muslim alone narrated it without al-Bukhari, and he and al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Zakariyya ibn Ishaq al-Makki, with the same chain.^[Al-Musnad (3/328), Sahih Muslim no. (1478), and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (9208).]

'Abd Allah ibn Imam Ahmad said: Surayj ibn Yunus narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Hashim ibn al-Barid narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd [Allah ibn 'Ali]^[Addition from T, F, and al-Musnad.] ibn Abi Rafi', from 'Uthman ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave his wives the choice between this world and the Hereafter, and did not give them the choice of divorce.^[Zawa'id al-Musnad (1/78).]

This report is disconnected (munqati'), and similar reports have been narrated from al-Hasan, Qatadah, and others. It is contrary to the apparent meaning of the verse, for He said: ﴿Then come, I will provide for you and release you with a fair release,﴾ meaning: I will give you your rights and set you free.

The scholars differed over whether it is permissible for another man to marry them if he divorced them, in two opinions. The more correct of the two is yes, should it occur, so that the purpose of the release is achieved. And Allah knows best.

'Ikrimah said: On that day he had nine wives, five of them from Quraysh: 'Aishah, Hafsah, Umm Habibah, Sawdah, and Umm Salamah. Also married to him ﷺ were Safiyyah bint Huyayy al-Nadriyyah, Maymunah bint al-Harith al-Hilaliyyah, Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyyah, and Juwayriyah bint al-Harith al-Mustaliqiyyah, may Allah be pleased with them all and make them pleased.

[He did not marry any of them except after Khadijah bint Khuwaylid ibn Asad ibn 'Abd al-'Uzza ibn Qusayy ibn Kilab died. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married her in Makkah when he was twenty-five years old. She remained with him until Allah honored him with His message; she believed in him and supported him, and she was a worthy companion to him. She died three years before the Hijrah, according to the most sound view, may Allah be pleased with her. She had special virtues, among them that he did not marry another woman in addition to her, and among them that all his children were from her, except Ibrahim, who was from his concubine Mariyah. And among them that she was the best of the women of this Ummah.

Scholars differed over whether she is preferred over 'Aishah, in three opinions, the third being to withhold judgment.

Our shaykh Abu al-'Abbas ibn Taymiyyah was asked about the two of them and said: Each of them was distinguished by a particular quality. Khadijah's influence was at the beginning of Islam; she would console the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, strengthen him, calm him, and spend her wealth for him. She experienced the early dawn of Islam, bore harm for the sake of Allah and His Messenger, and her support for the Messenger came at the greatest times of need. So she had a station of support and sacrifice that no one else had. 'Aishah's influence was at the end of Islam; she had a depth of understanding of the religion and conveying it to the Ummah, and her sons benefited from the knowledge she passed on to them, which no one else had. This is the meaning of his words, may Allah be pleased with him.]

**Among her distinctions:** God, glorified is He, sent peace (salam) to her through Jibril, and the Messenger of God ﷺ conveyed it to her. Al-Bukhari related in his Sahih, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Jibril, peace be upon him, came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of God, this is Khadijah, who has come to you carrying a vessel containing a condiment, or food, or drink. When she comes to you, convey to her peace from her Lord and from me, and give her the good news of a house in Paradise, made of reed, with no clamor in it and no fatigue." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3820.] By the Lord's life, this distinction was hers alone and was not given to anyone else. As for Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, Jibril conveyed greetings to her through the tongue of the Prophet ﷺ. Al-Bukhari related with his chain that Aishah said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said one day: "O Aishah, this is Jibril, who sends you his greetings." I said: "And upon him be peace, and the mercy of God and His blessings. You see what I do not see," meaning the Messenger of God ﷺ. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3768.]

Among the distinctions of Khadijah, may Allah be pleased with her, is that he was never displeased by her, she never angered him, he never swore an oath of abstention (ila') against her, and he never reproached her or shunned her. This alone is sufficient as a virtue and an excellence.

**Among her distinctions:** she was the first woman to believe in God and His Messenger from this Ummah.

**Section:**
When God took her, he married after her Sawdah bint Zam'ah, may Allah be pleased with her. She was Sawdah bint Zam'ah ibn Qays ibn Abd Shams ibn Abd Wudd ibn Nasr ibn Malik ibn Jabal ibn Amir ibn Lu'ayy. She grew old in his household, and he intended to divorce her, but she gave her day to Aishah, and so he kept her. This is among her distinctions: she preferred the love of the Prophet ﷺ with her day, seeking nearness to the Messenger of God ﷺ and out of love for him, and preferring to remain with him. So he would allot Aishah her day and Sawdah's day, and he would allot his other wives their days, and he did not allot a day to Sawdah, while she was content with that and preferred it, in order to please the Messenger of God ﷺ.

He married the truthful one (al-Siddiqah), the daughter of the truthful one (al-Siddiq), Aishah bint Abi Bakr, may Allah be pleased with both of them. She was six years old two years before the Hijrah, and it was said three years. He consummated the marriage with her in Madinah at the start of his arrival, in the first year, when she was nine. He died leaving her at eighteen. She died in Madinah and was buried in al-Baqi', and she bequeathed that Abu Hurayrah should lead the funeral prayer over her, in the year fifty-eight. Among her distinctions: she was the most beloved of the wives of the Messenger of God ﷺ to him, as was established from him in al-Bukhari and others, when he was asked: "Which of the people is most beloved to you?" He said: "Aishah." It was said: "And among the men?" He said: "Her father." [I have not found it in Sahih al-Bukhari. It is in Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3879, from the hadith of Amr ibn al-As, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Also among her distinctions: he did not marry a virgin other than her, and among her distinctions: revelation would descend upon him while he was under her quilt, and not under anyone else's.

Among her distinctions: when God, mighty and majestic, sent down to him the verse of choice (ayat al-takhyir), he began with her and offered her the choice, saying: "And there is no blame on you if you do not hasten until you consult your two parents." She said: "Am I to consult my parents about this? I want God, His Messenger, and the Last Abode." The rest of his wives followed her example, and they said what she said.

Among her distinctions: God, glorified is He, cleared her of what the people of the slander (ahl al-ifk) had accused her of, and He sent down, concerning her excuse and her innocence, a revelation that is recited in the prayer niches (mihrabs) of the Muslims and their prayers until the Day of Resurrection. He bore witness that she was among the good women, and He promised her forgiveness and generous provision. God, glorified is He, informed that what was said about her of falsehood was good for her, and that what was said about her was not an evil for her, nor a defect in her, nor a lowering of her status. Rather, God elevated her by it, raised her rank, magnified her station, and made her remembered with purity and innocence among the people of the earth and the heavens. How great a virtue this is! Reflect on this honor and dignity, which arose from her extreme humility and her belittling of herself, when she said: "My affair in my own eyes was too insignificant for God to speak concerning me with a revelation that is recited; but I hoped that the Messenger of God ﷺ would see a dream by which God would clear me." So she is the truthful one of this Ummah, the Mother of the Believers, and the beloved of the Messenger of God ﷺ. She knew she was innocent and wronged, and that her accusers were wrongdoers who had fabricated against her. Their harm reached her parents and the Messenger of God ﷺ. This was her belittling of herself and her diminishing of her own status. So what do you think of one who has fasted a day or two, or a month or two, or stood in prayer for a night or two, and then some of the states appeared upon him, and they regarded themselves through the lens of deserving miracles (karamat), and that they are among those whose meeting is sought for blessing and whose good supplications are sought, and that the people must honor them, revere them, exalt them, and venerate them, so that their garments are touched for blessing and the dust of their thresholds is kissed; and that they hold such a station with God that God avenges them immediately upon whoever belittles them, and that whoever commits a breach of etiquette against them is seized without delay? Indeed, a breach of etiquette against them is a sin that nothing expiates except their pleasure.

Had this been an outcome of sufficiency, it would be bearable; but it comes from deficiency. These follies and foolish excesses are the product of profound ignorance and a crooked intellect. Such conduct proceeds only from an ignorant person who is self-admiring, heedless of his own crime, faults, and sins, deceived by God's respite for him from seizing him for the arrogance and contempt he displays toward those who may be better than him in God's sight. We ask God for well-being in this world and the next. A servant should seek refuge in God from being great in his own eyes while being insignificant in God's sight.

Among the distinctions of Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her: when matters among the senior Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, became unclear to them regarding the religion, they would ask her for a ruling, and they would find her knowledge with her.

Among her distinctions: the Messenger of God ﷺ died in her house. Also among her distinctions: the angel showed her image to the Prophet ﷺ before he married her, in a piece of silk, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "If this is from God, He will make it come to pass." [Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 5078, from the hadith of Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her.] Also among her distinctions: the people used to seek out their gifts for the Messenger of God ﷺ on her day, seeking nearness to the Messenger ﷺ, so they would present him with what he loved at the home of his most beloved wife, may Allah be pleased with them all. She was known by the kunyah Umm Abd Allah. It is related that she miscarried a child from the Prophet ﷺ, but this is not established.

The Messenger of God ﷺ married Hafsah bint Umar ibn al-Khattab. She had previously been married to Khunays ibn Hudhafah, who was one of the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ and among those who witnessed Badr. She died in the year forty-five, or it was said fifty-eight. Among her distinctions is what the hafiz Abu Muhammad al-Maqdisi mentioned in his abridgment of the biography: that the Prophet ﷺ divorced her, and Jibril came to him and said: "God commands you to take Hafsah back, for she is a woman who fasts often and prays much at night, and she is your wife in Paradise."

Al-Tabarani said in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: Ahmad ibn Tahir ibn Harmalah ibn Yahya related to us, my grandfather Harmalah related to us, Ibn Wahb related to us, Amr ibn Salih al-Hadrami related to us, from Musa ibn Ali ibn Rabah, from his father, from Uqbah ibn Amir, that the Prophet ﷺ divorced Hafsah. When this reached Umar ibn al-Khattab, he put dust on his head and said: "God does not care for the son of al-Khattab after this." Then Jibril, peace be upon him, descended upon the Prophet ﷺ and said: "God commands you to take back Hafsah, as a mercy to Umar." [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (17/291).
