Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (4/334): "In it is Amr ibn Salih al-Hadrami, whom I do not know, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy."]

The Messenger of God ﷺ married Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan, whose name was Ramlah bint Sakhr ibn Harb ibn Umayyah ibn Abd Shams ibn Abd Manaf. She emigrated with her husband Abd Allah ibn Jahsh to the land of Abyssinia, where he became a Christian, but God completed Islam for her. The Messenger of God ﷺ married her while she was in the land of Abyssinia. He gave her as dowry, through the Negus, four hundred dinars, and the Messenger of God ﷺ sent Amr ibn Umayyah al-Damri with her to the land of Abyssinia. Her marriage was arranged by Uthman ibn Affan, and it was said by Khalid ibn Sa'id ibn al-As. She is the one who guarded the bedding of the Messenger of God ﷺ from her father sitting upon it, when Abu Sufyan came to Madinah, and she told him: "You are a polytheist," and she prevented him from sitting on it.

The Messenger of God ﷺ married Umm Salamah, whose name was Hind bint Abi Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah ibn Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn Makhzum ibn Yaqzah ibn Murrah ibn Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy ibn Ghalib. She had previously been married to Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Asad. She died in the year sixty-two and was buried in al-Baqi'. She was the last of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ to die, though it was also said that it was Maymunah. Among her distinctions: Jibril entered upon the Prophet ﷺ while she was with him, and she saw him in the form of Dihyah al-Kalbi. In Sahih Muslim, from Abu Uthman, who said: "I was informed that Jibril came to the Prophet ﷺ while Umm Salamah was with him." He began to converse, then he rose, and the Prophet of God ﷺ said to Umm Salamah: "Who is this?" or words to that effect. She said: "This is Dihyah al-Kalbi." She said: "By God, I did not think him to be anyone but him, until I heard the Prophet's ﷺ sermon informing that he was Jibril," or words to that effect. Sulayman al-Taymi said: "I said to Abu Uthman: From whom did you hear this hadith?" He said: "From Usamah ibn Zayd." [Sahih Muslim, no. 2451.]

Her son Umar married her to the Messenger of God ﷺ. Some scholars rejected this on the grounds that her son at that time was not old enough to conduct a marriage contract. Imam Ahmad rejected this and denounced whoever said it. What supports the correctness of Ahmad's view is what Muslim related in his Sahih: that Umar ibn Abi Salamah, her son, asked the Prophet ﷺ about kissing for one who is fasting. He said: "Ask her," meaning Umm Salamah. She informed him that the Messenger of God ﷺ used to do it. He said: "We are not like the Messenger of God ﷺ, for God makes lawful for His Messenger whatever He wills." Then the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "I am the most God-fearing of you and the most knowing of Him," or words to that effect. [Sahih Muslim, no. 1108.] Such a thing is not said of a very young child, and Umar was born in the land of Abyssinia before the Hijrah. Al-Bayhaqi said: "The claim of one who asserts that he was a child is a mere assertion, and his youth has not been established by a sound chain."

The Messenger of God ﷺ married Zaynab bint Jahsh from the Banu Khuzaymah ibn Mudrikah ibn Ilyas ibn Mudar. She was the daughter of his paternal aunt Umaymah bint Abd al-Muttalib. She had previously been married to his freed slave Zayd ibn Harithah, but he divorced her, and God married her to him from above the seven heavens, and He sent down to him: "So when Zayd had accomplished his need from her, We married her to you." He then rose and entered upon her without seeking permission. She used to boast of this over the rest of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, saying: "Your families gave you in marriage, but God married me from above His seven heavens." This is among her distinctions. She died in Madinah in the year twenty and was buried in al-Baqi'.

The Prophet (ﷺ) married Zaynab bint Khuzaymah al-Hilaliyyah. She had previously been married to Abdullah ibn Jahsh. He married her in the third year after the Hijrah, and she was called Umm al-Masakin (the Mother of the Poor). She remained with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) only briefly, two or three months, and then she died, may Allah be pleased with her.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married Juwayriyah bint al-Harith of the Banu al-Mustaliq. She had been taken captive in the battle of the Banu al-Mustaliq and fell to the share of Thabit ibn Qays. He made a contract of manumission with her (kitabah, a written agreement by which a slave purchases her freedom in installments), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) settled her kitabah. He married her in the sixth year after the Hijrah, and she died in the fifty-sixth year. Because of her, the Muslims freed one hundred households of slaves, and they said, "They are the in-laws of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." This was among the blessings she brought to her people.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married Safiyyah bint Huyayy, who was of the lineage of Harun ibn Imran, the brother of Musa, in the seventh year. She had been taken captive from Khaybar. Previously she had been married to Kinanah ibn Abi al-Huqayq, whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) killed. She died in the thirty-sixth year, and it is said in the fiftieth year. Among her distinctive qualities is that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) freed her and made her freedom her dowry (mahr). Anas said, "He gave her freedom as her dowry," and this became a precedent for the slave-woman until the Day of Resurrection. It is permissible for a man to make the freedom of his slave-girl her dowry, and she becomes his wife, according to the explicit ruling of Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him.

At-Tirmidhi said: Ishaq ibn Mansur and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, both saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: It reached Safiyyah that Hafsah had said, "Safiyyah is the daughter of a Jew." So she wept. The Prophet (ﷺ) entered upon her while she was weeping, and he said, "What makes you weep?" She said, "Hafsah said to me, 'I am the daughter of a Jew.'" The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "You are indeed the daughter of a prophet, your uncle is a prophet, and you are under a prophet. So in what does she boast over you?" Then he said, "Fear Allah, O Hafsah." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3894), and he said: "This is a hasan sahih gharib hadith from this route."]] At-Tirmidhi said: This is a sahih gharib hadith from this route. And this is among her distinctive qualities, may Allah be pleased with her.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married Maymunah bint al-Harith al-Hilaliyyah. He married her at Sarif, which is nine miles from Makkah. She was the last of the Mothers of the Believers to be married. She died in the sixty-third year. She was the maternal aunt of Khalid ibn al-Walid and the maternal aunt of Ibn Abbas, since his mother was Umm al-Fadl bint al-Harith. Scholars have differed concerning the Prophet's (ﷺ) marriage to her: did he marry her while in the state of ihram or not? The sound view is that he married her while not in ihram, as Abu Rafi' al-Shafir said concerning her marriage.

Al-Hafiz Abu Muhammad al-Maqdisi and others said: He contracted marriage with seven women and did not consummate with them. Therefore, the prayers upon his wives follow from their honor and from their being forbidden to the community, and that they are his wives (ﷺ) in this world and the Hereafter. Whoever separated from a wife during her lifetime before consummation does not acquire the rulings that apply to the wives with whom he consummated the marriage. May Allah bless him, his wives, his family and his descendants, and grant them abundant peace. [[Addition from manuscript T.]]

Allah the Exalted says, admonishing the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, those who chose Allah, His Messenger and the Final Abode, and whose affair was settled under the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: that He would inform them of their ruling, specifically and apart from all other women, that whoever of them commits a clear immorality (fahishah mubayyinah). Ibn 'Abbas said: it is nushuz (disobedience toward the husband) and bad conduct. In any case, this is a conditional statement, and a condition does not necessarily imply that the condition occurs, as in His saying: ﴿And it has certainly been revealed to you and to those before you: If you should associate others with Allah, your deeds will surely be nullified﴾ [az-Zumar: 65], and His saying: ﴿And if they had associated others with Allah, what they used to do would have been nullified for them﴾ [al-An'am: 88], and ﴿Say: If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 81], and ﴿Had Allah intended to take a son, He would have chosen from what He creates whatever He willed. Exalted is He; He is Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾ [az-Zumar: 4]. Since their standing was elevated, it was fitting that the sin, if committed by them, be made more severe, to safeguard their dignity and their exalted sanctity; and therefore He said: ﴿Whoever of you commits a clear immorality, the punishment will be doubled for her, twofold﴾.

Malik narrated from Zayd ibn Aslam regarding ﴿the punishment will be doubled for her, twofold﴾ that he said: in this world and the Hereafter.

And from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

﴿And that is for Allah an easy matter﴾, i.e., simple and effortless.

Then He mentioned His justice and His bounty in His saying: ﴿And whoever of you devoutly obeys Allah and His Messenger﴾, i.e., obeys Allah and His Messenger and submits to them, ﴿We will give her her reward twice, and We have prepared for her a noble provision﴾, i.e., in Paradise. For they are in the dwellings of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in the highest of 'Illiyyin, above the dwellings of all of creation, in al-Wasilah, which is the nearest of the abodes of Paradise to the Throne.

Allah the Exalted says, admonishing the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, those who chose Allah, His Messenger and the Final Abode, and whose affair was settled under the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: that He would inform them of their ruling, specifically and apart from all other women, that whoever of them commits a clear immorality (fahishah mubayyinah). Ibn 'Abbas said: it is nushuz (disobedience toward the husband) and bad conduct. In any case, this is a conditional statement, and a condition does not necessarily imply that the condition occurs, as in His saying: ﴿And it has certainly been revealed to you and to those before you: If you should associate others with Allah, your deeds will surely be nullified﴾ [az-Zumar: 65], and His saying: ﴿And if they had associated others with Allah, what they used to do would have been nullified for them﴾ [al-An'am: 88], and ﴿Say: If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 81], and ﴿Had Allah intended to take a son, He would have chosen from what He creates whatever He willed. Exalted is He; He is Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾ [az-Zumar: 4]. Since their standing was elevated, it was fitting that the sin, if committed by them, be made more severe, to safeguard their dignity and their exalted sanctity; and therefore He said: ﴿Whoever of you commits a clear immorality, the punishment will be doubled for her, twofold﴾.

Malik narrated from Zayd ibn Aslam regarding ﴿the punishment will be doubled for her, twofold﴾ that he said: in this world and the Hereafter.

And from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

﴿And that is for Allah an easy matter﴾, i.e., simple and effortless.

Then He mentioned His justice and His bounty in His saying: ﴿And whoever of you devoutly obeys Allah and His Messenger﴾, i.e., obeys Allah and His Messenger and submits to them, ﴿We will give her her reward twice, and We have prepared for her a noble provision﴾, i.e., in Paradise. For they are in the dwellings of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in the highest of 'Illiyyin, above the dwellings of all of creation, in al-Wasilah, which is the nearest of the abodes of Paradise to the Throne.

These are etiquette that Allah commanded the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) to follow, and the women of the Ummah follow them in this. Allah addressed the wives of the Prophet [(ﷺ)] [[Addition from manuscript T; manuscript F reads: "may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him."]], saying that if they fear Allah as He has commanded them, then no woman will resemble them, and none will reach them in virtue and rank. Then He said: ﴿So do not be soft in speech, lest one in whose heart is a disease should covet, but speak in an appropriate manner.﴾

As-Suddi and others said: this means softening speech when they address men. For this reason He said: ﴿lest one in whose heart is a disease should covet﴾, meaning, one in whose heart is corruption (dagal). ﴿but speak in an appropriate manner﴾. Ibn Zayd said: "a good, beautiful speech, known for goodness."

The meaning of this is that she should address non-mahram men with speech that contains no softness (tarkhim), i.e., a woman should not address strangers the way she addresses her husband.

* *

His saying: ﴿And stay in your houses﴾, meaning: remain in your houses and do not go out without need. Among the legitimate needs is praying in the mosque under its conditions, as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not prevent the female servants of Allah from the mosques of Allah, but let them go out while unperfumed." In another narration: "And their houses are better for them." [[Abu Dawud related it with this wording in his Sunan, no. 565, from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, and with the second narration, no. 567, from the hadith of Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both. Its origin is in the Two Sahihs from the hadith of Ibn Umar.]]

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Humayd ibn Mas'adah [[In manuscript A: "Mas'ud."]] narrated to us, Abu Raja' al-Kalbi narrated to us, Rawh ibn al-Musayyab is trustworthy, Thabit al-Bunani narrated to us from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The women came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, the men have taken the merit and jihad in the way of Allah, so what deed do we have by which we can attain the deed of those who strive in the way of Allah?' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Whoever of you sits in her house, or words to that effect, she will attain the deed of the mujahidin in the way of Allah.'" [[In manuscript T: "the mujahid."]]

Then he said: "We do not know of anyone who narrated this from Thabit except Rawh ibn al-Musayyab, who is a well-known man from Basra" [[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 1475, Kashf al-Astar. Abu Ya'la related it in his Musnad (6/140) and Ibn Hibban in al-Majruhin (1/299) by the route of Abu Raja' al-Kalbi with similar wording. Ibn Hibban said: "Rawh was among those who narrate forgeries from trustworthy sources, invert chains, and raise statements that were only halted (mawquf). It is not permissible to narrate from him or write his hadith except for testing." Ibn Adi said in al-Kamil: "His hadiths are not preserved."]].

Al-Bazzar also said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Amr ibn Asim narrated to us, Hammam narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Muwarriq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abdullah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed, the woman is 'awrah. When she goes out, Satan makes her appealing, and she is closest to her Lord when she is in the innermost part of her house."

Al-Tirmidhi related it from Bundar, from Amr ibn Asim, with the same wording [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 1173, and al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith." Ibn Khuzaymah related it in his Sahih, no. 1685, and through him Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, no. 329 (Mawarid), from Amr ibn Asim, with the same chain. Ibn Khuzaymah doubted whether Qatadah heard this hadith from Muwarriq.]].

Al-Bazzar also narrated, with his earlier chain, and Abu Dawud too, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "A woman's prayer in her inner room (makhda') is better than her prayer in her house, and her prayer in her house is better than her prayer in her courtyard." [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 570.]] And this chain is good (jayyid).

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance﴾. Mujahid said: "A woman used to go out walking in front of men, and that is the display of the Jahiliyyah."

Qatadah said: ﴿And do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance﴾, meaning: when you go out of your houses, and they had a gait, an affectation, and a flirtatious manner, so Allah forbade that.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: ﴿And do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance﴾. Tabarruj is that she throws her head-covering (khimar) over her head without tying it, so that her necklaces, earrings, and neck are visible, and all of that appears from her; that is tabarruj. Then the women of the believers became general in tabarruj.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Zuhayr narrated to me, Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Dawud (i.e., Ibn Abi al-Furat) narrated to us, Ali ibn Ahmar narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who recited this verse: ﴿And do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance﴾, and said: "It was between Nuh and Idris, and it lasted a thousand years. Two clans of Adam's descendants, one of them lived in the plain and the other in the mountain. The men of the mountain were handsome, but the women were ugly. The women of the plain were handsome, but the men were ugly. Iblis came to a man from the people of the plain in the form of a youth and hired himself to him, serving him. Iblis made something similar to the instrument with which shepherds play, and he produced with it a sound that people had never heard the like of. This reached those around him, and they came to him to listen, and they took a festival which they would gather for once a year, where the women would display themselves to the men, and the men would adorn themselves for them. A man from the people of the mountain came upon them during that festival, saw the women and their beauty, went to his companions and informed them, so they moved to them, settled with them, and indecency spread among them. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance﴾." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (22/4).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And establish prayer, and give zakah, and obey Allah and His Messenger﴾. He first forbade them from evil, then commanded them to good, namely establishing prayer, which is the worship of Allah alone with no partner, and giving zakah, which is kindness to the created beings, ﴿and obey Allah and His Messenger﴾. This is a case of mentioning the general after the specific (atf al-'amm 'ala al-khass).

His saying: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with complete purification﴾. This is an explicit text that the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) are included among the People of the House here, because they are the cause of the revelation of this verse, and the cause of revelation is included in it without dispute, either alone according to one opinion or together with others according to the sound view.

Ibn Jarir related from Ikrimah that he used to call out in the marketplace: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with complete purification﴾, "It was revealed specifically concerning the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ)." And likewise Ibn Abi Hatim related, saying:

Ali ibn Harb al-Mawsili narrated to us, Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, Husayn ibn Waqid narrated to us, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, the People of the House﴾, he said: "It was revealed specifically concerning the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ)."

Ikrimah also said: "Whoever wishes, I will invoke a mutual curse (mubahalah) with him that it was revealed concerning the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ)."

If what is meant is that they were the cause of the revelation to the exclusion of others, then this is correct. But if what is meant is that they alone are intended to the exclusion of others, then there is room for consideration, for hadiths have come which indicate that what is meant is more general than that:

The first hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Ali ibn Zayd informed us, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to pass by the door of Fatimah for six months when he went out to the Fajr prayer, saying: 'The prayer, O People of the House! ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with complete purification﴾.'"

Al-Tirmidhi related it from Abd ibn Humayd, from Affan with it, and said: "Hasan gharib." [[Musnad (3/259) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3206.]]

Another hadith: Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Waki' narrated to us, Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq narrated to us, Abu Dawud informed me, from Abu al-Hamra' who said: "I stayed in Madinah for seven months during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). [I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)] [[Addition from manuscripts T, F, A, and al-Tabari.]] when dawn broke, he came to the door of Ali and Fatimah and said: 'The prayer, the prayer! ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with complete purification﴾.'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (22/6). Al-Tabarani related it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (22/200) by the route of Mansur ibn al-Aswad, from Abu Dawud, with similar wording.]]

Abu Dawud al-A'ma is Nufay' ibn al-Harith, a liar (kaddhab).

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad also said: Muhammad ibn Mus'ab narrated to us, al-Awza'i narrated to us, Shaddad Abu Ammar narrated to us, who said: "I entered upon Wathilah ibn al-Asqa' and there were some people with him, and they mentioned Ali, may Allah be pleased with him. When they left, he said to me: 'Shall I not inform you of what I saw from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'I came to Fatimah to ask her about Ali, and she said: He has gone to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So I sat waiting for him until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came, with Ali, Hasan, and Husayn, each of them holding one of his hands, until he entered. He brought Ali and Fatimah close and seated them before him, and seated Hasan and Husayn each on one of his thighs. Then he wrapped his garment around them, or he said his cloak, then recited this verse: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with complete purification﴾. Then he said: "O Allah, these are the People of my House, and the People of my House have more right."'" Abu Ja'far Ibn Jarir related it from Abd al-Karim ibn Abi Umayr [[In manuscript A: "Umar."]], from al-Walid ibn Muslim, from Abu Amr al-Awza'i with his chain, similarly, adding at its end: Wathilah said: "I said: 'And I, O Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless you, am I among your family?' He said: 'And you are among my family.'" Wathilah said: "Indeed, this is among the things I hope for most." [[Musnad (4/107) and Tafsir al-Tabari (22/6).]]

Then he also related it from Abd al-A'la ibn Wasil, from al-Fadl ibn Dukayn, from Abd al-Salam ibn Harb, from Kulthum al-Muharibi, from Shaddad Abu Ammar who said: "I was sitting with Wathilah ibn al-Asqa' when they mentioned Ali and insulted him. When they got up, he said: 'Sit, until I inform you about the one they insulted. I was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when Ali, Fatimah, Hasan, and Husayn came, and he (ﷺ) cast his cloak over them, then said: "O Allah, these are the People of my House. O Allah, remove from them the impurity and purify them with complete purification."' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, and I?' He said: 'And you.' He said: 'By Allah, indeed this is the most reliable of my deeds to me.'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (22/7). Al-Tabarani related it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (22/65) by the route of Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz, from al-Fadl ibn Dukayn, Abu Nu'aym with it.]]

**Another hadith:** Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman, from Ata ibn Abi Rabah, who said: One who heard Umm Salamah mention it narrated to me that the Prophet (ﷺ) was in her house. Fatimah, may Allah be pleased with her, came to him with a cooking pot (burmah) containing khazirah (a dish of meat and grain). She entered with it and gave it to him, and he said to her: "Call your husband and your two sons." She said: So Ali, Hasan and Husayn came and entered upon him, and they sat down eating from that khazirah. He was on his couch (manamah) on a raised platform (dukkan), beneath which was a Khaybari cloak. She said: I was in the room praying. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed this verse: ﴿Allah only wishes to remove impurity from you, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification.﴾ She said: He took the edge of the cloak and covered them with it. Then he extended his hand, raised it toward the sky, and said: "O Allah, these are the People of my House and my close family, so remove impurity from them and purify them thoroughly." She said: I put my head into the house and said: "And am I with you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "You are on the good, you are on the good."

(Musnad, 6/292. In a narration of al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (9/11), the teacher of Ata is named: he said, from Ata ibn Abi Rabah, from Umar ibn Abi Salamah, something similar.)

In its chain is an unnamed person, who is the teacher of Ata. The rest of its narrators are trustworthy.

**Another route:** Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Awf narrated to us, from Abu al-Mu'addil, from Atiyyah al-Tufawi, from his father, that Umm Salamah narrated to him, saying: One day while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was in my house, the servant said: "Fatimah and Ali are at the sudda (the porch)." She said: He said to me: "Get up and withdraw from the People of my House." She said: So I got up and withdrew a short distance within the house. Then Ali and Fatimah entered, with them Hasan and Husayn, who were two small boys. He took the two boys and placed them in his lap and kissed them. He embraced Ali with one of his arms and Fatimah with the other, and he kissed Fatimah and kissed Ali. He wrapped them in a black khamisah (a cloak) and said: "O Allah, to You, not to the Fire, (I come), I and the People of my House." She said: I said: "And I, O Messenger of Allah? May Allah bless you." He said: "And you."

(Musnad, 6/296.)

**Another route:** Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Atiyyah narrated to us, Fudayl ibn Marzuq narrated to us, from Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id, from Umm Salamah, that this verse was revealed in her house: ﴿Allah only wishes to remove impurity from you, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification.﴾ She said: I was sitting at the door of the house, and I said: "O Messenger of Allah, am I not of the People of the House?" He said: "You are on the good; you are of the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ)." She said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Ali, Fatimah, Hasan and Husayn were in the house, may Allah be pleased with them all.

(Tafsir al-Tabari, 22/7. Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (23/249) through Fudayl ibn Marzuq, in abridged form.)

**Another route:** Ibn Jarir also narrated it from Abu Kurayb, from Waki', from Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Umm Salamah, similar to the above.

(Tafsir al-Tabari, 22/6. Al-Tahawi narrated it in Mushkil al-Athar (no. 770) through Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram. Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (23/333) through Zubayd, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Umm Salamah.)

**Another route:** Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated to us, Musa ibn Ya'qub narrated to me, Hashim ibn Hashim ibn Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas narrated to me, from Abdullah ibn Wahb ibn Zam'ah, who said: Umm Salamah, may Allah be pleased with her, informed me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gathered Fatimah, Hasan and Husayn, then put them under his garment. Then he turned in supplication to Allah, mighty and majestic, and said: "These are the People of my House." Umm Salamah said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, let me enter with them." He said: "You are of my family."

(Tafsir al-Tabari, 22/7. Al-Tahawi narrated it in Mushkil al-Athar (no. 763) through Khalid ibn Makhlad al-Qatwani.)

**Another route:** Ibn Jarir also narrated it from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tusi, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Isbahani, from Yahya ibn Ubayd al-Makki, from Ata, from Umar ibn Abi Salamah, from his mother, similar to that.

(Tafsir al-Tabari, 22/7. Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (23/286) through Shurayk, from Ata, from Umm Salamah.)

**Another route:** Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Mus'ab ibn al-Miqdam narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Zarbi narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, from Umm Salamah, who said: Fatimah came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with a pot she had made, containing 'asidah (a porridge), carrying it on a tray. She placed it before him, and he said: "Where are your cousin and your two sons?" She said: "In the house." He said: "Call them." So she went to Ali and said: "Answer the Messenger of Allah, you and your two sons." Umm Salamah said: When he saw them approaching, he reached out his hand toward a cloak that was on the manamah. He pulled it, spread it out, and seated them on it. Then he gathered the four corners of the cloak in his left hand and drew it together above their heads. He pointed with his right hand toward his Lord, mighty and majestic, and said: "O Allah, these are the People of my House, so remove impurity from them and purify them thoroughly."

(Tafsir al-Tabari, 22/7.)

**Another route:** Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Quddus narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Hakim ibn Sa'd, who said: We mentioned Ali ibn Abi Talib in the presence of Umm Salamah, and she said: This verse was revealed in my house: ﴿Allah only wishes to remove impurity from you, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification.﴾ Umm Salamah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to my house and said: "Do not permit anyone to enter." Then Fatimah came, and I could not prevent her from entering to her father. Then Hasan came, and I could not prevent him from entering to his mother and grandfather. Then Husayn came, and I could not prevent him. Then Ali came, and I could not prevent him. So they gathered, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) covered them with a cloak he had, then said: "These are the People of my House, so remove impurity from them and purify them thoroughly." This verse was revealed when they had gathered on the bisat (the mat/carpet). She said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, and me?" She said: By Allah, he did not answer, and then he said: "You are on the good."

(Tafsir al-Tabari, 22/7. Al-Tahawi narrated it in Mushkil al-Athar (no. 762) through Jarir ibn Abd al-Hamid, from al-A'mash, similarly.)

**Another hadith:** Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakic narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, from Zakariyya, from Mus'ab ibn Shaybah, from Safiyyah bint Shaybah, who said: Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out one morning wearing a striped cloak of black wool. Then Hasan came and he took him in with him; then Husayn came and he took him in with him; then Fatimah came and he took her in with him; then Ali came and he took him in with him. Then he said: ﴿Allah only wishes to remove impurity from you, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification.﴾

Muslim narrated it from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Muhammad ibn Bishr, with the same chain.

(Tafsir al-Tabari, 22/5; Sahih Muslim, no. 2081.)

**Another route:** Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Surayj ibn Yunus Abu al-Harith narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Yazid narrated to us, from al-Awwam (meaning Ibn Hawshab), from a paternal uncle of his, who said: I entered with my father upon Aishah, and I asked her about Ali, may Allah be pleased with him. She said, may Allah be pleased with her: "You ask me about a man who was among the most beloved people to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and whose wife was his daughter, the most beloved person to him? I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) call Ali, Fatimah, Hasan and Husayn, then he threw a garment over them and said: 'O Allah, these are the People of my House, so remove impurity from them and purify them thoroughly.'" She said: I approached him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, and am I of the People of your House?" He said: "Step aside, for you are on the good."

**Another hadith:** Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna narrated to us, Bakr ibn Yahya ibn Ziban al-Anazi narrated to us, Mandal narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This verse was revealed concerning five: me, Ali, Hasan, Husayn, and Fatimah: ﴿Allah only wishes to remove impurity from you, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification.﴾"

(Tafsir al-Tabari, 22/5.)

It has already been mentioned that Fudayl ibn Marzuq narrated it from Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id, from Umm Salamah, as already stated.

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from the hadith of Harun ibn Sa'd al-Ijli, from Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id, as a mawquf (a report ending with a Companion), and Allah knows best.

**Another hadith:** Ibn Jarir said: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, Bukayr ibn Mismar narrated to us, who said: I heard Amir ibn Sa'd say: Sa'd said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, when revelation came down to him, and he took Ali, his two sons and Fatimah, and put them under his garment, then said: "My Lord, these are my family and the People of my House."

(Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (22/7) and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra (no. 8439) through Abu Bakr al-Hanafi, from Bukayr ibn Mismar, with the same chain.)

**Another hadith:** Muslim said in his Sahih: Zuhayr ibn Harb and Shuja' ibn Makhlad narrated to me, together, from Ibn Ulayyah. Zuhayr said: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Abu Hayyan narrated to me, Yazid ibn Hayyan narrated to me, who said: I set out with Husayn ibn Sabrah and Umar ibn Muslim to Zayd ibn Arqam. When we sat with him, Husayn said to him: "You have indeed attained much good, O Zayd. You saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), heard his hadith, fought alongside him, and prayed behind him. You have indeed attained much good, O Zayd. Tell us what you heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." He said: "O nephew, by Allah, my age has grown great, my time has passed, and I have forgotten some of what I used to memorize from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So accept what I narrate to you, and do not burden me with what I do not." Then he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood among us one day as a speaker at a body of water called Khumm, between Makkah and Madinah. He praised Allah and extolled Him, admonished and reminded, then said: 'To proceed: O people, I am only a human being; the messenger of my Lord is about to come to me and I will respond. I am leaving among you two weighty things: the first of them is the Book of Allah, in which is guidance and light, so take hold of the Book of Allah and hold fast to it.'" He urged them toward the Book of Allah and encouraged them to it. Then he said: "And the People of my House. I remind you of Allah regarding the People of my House, I remind you of Allah regarding the People of my House," three times. Husayn said to him: "And who are the People of his House, O Zayd? Are not his wives of the People of his House?" He said: "His wives are of the People of his House, but the People of his House are those for whom charity has been forbidden after him." He said: "And who are they?" He said: "They are the family of Ali, the family of Aqil, the family of Ja'far, and the family of Abbas." He said: "All of these are forbidden charity?" He said: "Yes."

(Sahih Muslim, no. 2408.)

Then he narrated it from Muhammad ibn Bakkar ibn al-Rayyan, from Hassan ibn Ibrahim, from Sa'id ibn Masruq, from Yazid ibn Hayyan [in A: "Hassan"], from Zayd ibn Arqam, and he mentioned the hadith in a manner similar to what preceded, and in it: "We said to him: Who are the people of his household? Are they his wives?" He said: "No, by Allah, a woman may be with a man for a period of time, then he divorces her and she returns to her father and her people. The people of his household are his root and his 'asabah (agnatic kin) who are forbidden the charity after him." [Sahih Muslim, no. (2408)].

This is how it occurs in this narration. The first (report) is more preferable, and acting upon it is more appropriate. This second report allows for the possibility that he intended to explain the "household" mentioned in the hadith he narrated, that the intended meaning is only his family who are forbidden the charity; or that the intended meaning of "household" is not only the wives, but they together with his family. This latter possibility is more probable, in order to reconcile it with the previous narration, and also to reconcile the Qur'an with the earlier hadiths, if they are authentic, for in some of their chains there is scrutiny. And Allah knows best. Then, what no one who reflects upon the Qur'an doubts is that the wives of the Prophet ﷺ are included in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with thorough purification﴾, for the context of the speech is with them. Therefore, after all of this, He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and wisdom﴾, meaning: act upon what Allah sends down to His Messenger in your houses of the Book and the Sunnah. This was said by Qatadah and others. And remember this blessing with which you have been singled out from among the people, that revelation descends in your houses to the exclusion of the rest of the people. 'A'isha [al-Siddiqah] [addition from A] daughter of al-Siddiq was the foremost of them in this blessing, the most favored of them with this bounty, and the most specially given of them from this widespread mercy, for revelation did not descend upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the bed of any woman other than her, as the Prophet, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, affirmed. Some of the scholars, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Because he did not marry a virgin other than her, and no man lay with her in her bed other than him, so it was fitting that she be singled out with this distinction and be given this exalted rank. But if his wives are from the people of his household, then his relatives are more worthy of this designation, as preceded in the hadith: "And the people of my household are more deserving." This resembles what is established in Sahih Muslim: that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about the mosque that was founded upon piety from the first day, he said: "It is this mosque of mine" [Sahih Muslim, no. (1398), from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him]. So this is of this kind, for the verse was revealed concerning the Mosque of Quba, as occurs in the other hadiths. But if that one was founded upon piety from the first day, then the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is more worthy of being named thus. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu al-Walid narrated to us, Abu 'Awana narrated to us, from Husayn ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Jamila [in T: "And Ibn Abi Hatim narrated with his chain"] who said: Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali was appointed as caliph when 'Ali was killed, may Allah be pleased with both of them [in T, F, A: "with him"]. He said: While he was praying, a man leapt upon him and stabbed him with a dagger. Husayn claimed that it reached him that the one who stabbed him was a man from the Banu Asad, and Hasan was prostrating. He said: They claim that the stab struck his hip, so he fell ill from it for months, then he recovered and sat upon the pulpit and said: "O people of Iraq, fear Allah concerning us, for we are your rulers and your guests, and we are the People of the House about whom Allah said: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with thorough purification﴾." He said: He kept saying it until no one remained in the mosque except that he was weeping aloud.

And al-Suddi said, from Abu al-Daylam, who said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn said to a man from the people of Syria: Have you not read in al-Ahzab: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with thorough purification﴾? He said: Yes. And are you them? He said: Yes.

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle and Acquainted﴾, meaning: by His subtlety toward you, you have reached this station, and by His knowledge of you and that you are worthy of it, He gave you that and singled you out with it.

Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, said: And remember the blessing of Allah upon you in that He placed you in houses in which the verses of Allah and wisdom are recited, so thank Allah for that and praise Him.

﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle and Acquainted﴾, meaning: possessor of subtlety toward you, in that He placed you in the houses in which His verses and wisdom are recited, and wisdom is the Sunnah, Acquainted with you, in that He chose you as wives for His Messenger.

Qatadah said concerning ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and wisdom﴾: He bestows favour upon them by that. Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

'Ata' al-'Awfi said concerning His saying ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle and Acquainted﴾: meaning, Subtle in extracting them (the verses), Acquainted with their place. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Then he said: Likewise al-Rabi' ibn Anas narrated from Qatadah.

These are etiquette that Allah commanded the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) to follow, and the women of the Ummah follow them in this. Allah addressed the wives of the Prophet [(ﷺ)] [[Addition from manuscript T; manuscript F reads: "may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him."]], saying that if they fear Allah as He has commanded them, then no woman will resemble them, and none will reach them in virtue and rank. Then He said: ﴿So do not be soft in speech, lest one in whose heart is a disease should covet, but speak in an appropriate manner.﴾

As-Suddi and others said: this means softening speech when they address men. For this reason He said: ﴿lest one in whose heart is a disease should covet﴾, meaning, one in whose heart is corruption (dagal). ﴿but speak in an appropriate manner﴾. Ibn Zayd said: "a good, beautiful speech, known for goodness."

The meaning of this is that she should address non-mahram men with speech that contains no softness (tarkhim), i.e., a woman should not address strangers the way she addresses her husband.

* *

His saying: ﴿And stay in your houses﴾, meaning: remain in your houses and do not go out without need. Among the legitimate needs is praying in the mosque under its conditions, as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not prevent the female servants of Allah from the mosques of Allah, but let them go out while unperfumed." In another narration: "And their houses are better for them." [[Abu Dawud related it with this wording in his Sunan, no. 565, from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, and with the second narration, no. 567, from the hadith of Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both. Its origin is in the Two Sahihs from the hadith of Ibn Umar.]]

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Humayd ibn Mas'adah [[In manuscript A: "Mas'ud."]] narrated to us, Abu Raja' al-Kalbi narrated to us, Rawh ibn al-Musayyab is trustworthy, Thabit al-Bunani narrated to us from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The women came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, the men have taken the merit and jihad in the way of Allah, so what deed do we have by which we can attain the deed of those who strive in the way of Allah?' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Whoever of you sits in her house, or words to that effect, she will attain the deed of the mujahidin in the way of Allah.'" [[In manuscript T: "the mujahid."]]

Then he said: "We do not know of anyone who narrated this from Thabit except Rawh ibn al-Musayyab, who is a well-known man from Basra" [[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 1475, Kashf al-Astar. Abu Ya'la related it in his Musnad (6/140) and Ibn Hibban in al-Majruhin (1/299) by the route of Abu Raja' al-Kalbi with similar wording. Ibn Hibban said: "Rawh was among those who narrate forgeries from trustworthy sources, invert chains, and raise statements that were only halted (mawquf). It is not permissible to narrate from him or write his hadith except for testing." Ibn Adi said in al-Kamil: "His hadiths are not preserved."]].

Al-Bazzar also said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Amr ibn Asim narrated to us, Hammam narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Muwarriq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abdullah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed, the woman is 'awrah. When she goes out, Satan makes her appealing, and she is closest to her Lord when she is in the innermost part of her house."

Al-Tirmidhi related it from Bundar, from Amr ibn Asim, with the same wording [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 1173, and al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith." Ibn Khuzaymah related it in his Sahih, no. 1685, and through him Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, no. 329 (Mawarid), from Amr ibn Asim, with the same chain. Ibn Khuzaymah doubted whether Qatadah heard this hadith from Muwarriq.]].

Al-Bazzar also narrated, with his earlier chain, and Abu Dawud too, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "A woman's prayer in her inner room (makhda') is better than her prayer in her house, and her prayer in her house is better than her prayer in her courtyard." [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 570.]] And this chain is good (jayyid).

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance﴾. Mujahid said: "A woman used to go out walking in front of men, and that is the display of the Jahiliyyah."

Qatadah said: ﴿And do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance﴾, meaning: when you go out of your houses, and they had a gait, an affectation, and a flirtatious manner, so Allah forbade that.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: ﴿And do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance﴾. Tabarruj is that she throws her head-covering (khimar) over her head without tying it, so that her necklaces, earrings, and neck are visible, and all of that appears from her; that is tabarruj. Then the women of the believers became general in tabarruj.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Zuhayr narrated to me, Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Dawud (i.e., Ibn Abi al-Furat) narrated to us, Ali ibn Ahmar narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who recited this verse: ﴿And do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance﴾, and said: "It was between Nuh and Idris, and it lasted a thousand years. Two clans of Adam's descendants, one of them lived in the plain and the other in the mountain. The men of the mountain were handsome, but the women were ugly. The women of the plain were handsome, but the men were ugly. Iblis came to a man from the people of the plain in the form of a youth and hired himself to him, serving him. Iblis made something similar to the instrument with which shepherds play, and he produced with it a sound that people had never heard the like of. This reached those around him, and they came to him to listen, and they took a festival which they would gather for once a year, where the women would display themselves to the men, and the men would adorn themselves for them. A man from the people of the mountain came upon them during that festival, saw the women and their beauty, went to his companions and informed them, so they moved to them, settled with them, and indecency spread among them. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance﴾." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (22/4).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And establish prayer, and give zakah, and obey Allah and His Messenger﴾. He first forbade them from evil, then commanded them to good, namely establishing prayer, which is the worship of Allah alone with no partner, and giving zakah, which is kindness to the created beings, ﴿and obey Allah and His Messenger﴾. This is a case of mentioning the general after the specific (atf al-'amm 'ala al-khass).

His saying: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with complete purification﴾. This is an explicit text that the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) are included among the People of the House here, because they are the cause of the revelation of this verse, and the cause of revelation is included in it without dispute, either alone according to one opinion or together with others according to the sound view.

Ibn Jarir related from Ikrimah that he used to call out in the marketplace: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with complete purification﴾, "It was revealed specifically concerning the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ)." And likewise Ibn Abi Hatim related, saying:

Ali ibn Harb al-Mawsili narrated to us, Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, Husayn ibn Waqid narrated to us, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, the People of the House﴾, he said: "It was revealed specifically concerning the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ)."

Ikrimah also said: "Whoever wishes, I will invoke a mutual curse (mubahalah) with him that it was revealed concerning the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ)."

If what is meant is that they were the cause of the revelation to the exclusion of others, then this is correct. But if what is meant is that they alone are intended to the exclusion of others, then there is room for consideration, for hadiths have come which indicate that what is meant is more general than that:

The first hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Ali ibn Zayd informed us, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to pass by the door of Fatimah for six months when he went out to the Fajr prayer, saying: 'The prayer, O People of the House! ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with complete purification﴾.'"

Al-Tirmidhi related it from Abd ibn Humayd, from Affan with it, and said: "Hasan gharib." [[Musnad (3/259) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3206.]]

Another hadith: Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Waki' narrated to us, Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq narrated to us, Abu Dawud informed me, from Abu al-Hamra' who said: "I stayed in Madinah for seven months during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). [I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)] [[Addition from manuscripts T, F, A, and al-Tabari.]] when dawn broke, he came to the door of Ali and Fatimah and said: 'The prayer, the prayer! ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with complete purification﴾.'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (22/6). Al-Tabarani related it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (22/200) by the route of Mansur ibn al-Aswad, from Abu Dawud, with similar wording.]]

Abu Dawud al-A'ma is Nufay' ibn al-Harith, a liar (kaddhab).

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad also said: Muhammad ibn Mus'ab narrated to us, al-Awza'i narrated to us, Shaddad Abu Ammar narrated to us, who said: "I entered upon Wathilah ibn al-Asqa' and there were some people with him, and they mentioned Ali, may Allah be pleased with him. When they left, he said to me: 'Shall I not inform you of what I saw from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'I came to Fatimah to ask her about Ali, and she said: He has gone to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So I sat waiting for him until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came, with Ali, Hasan, and Husayn, each of them holding one of his hands, until he entered. He brought Ali and Fatimah close and seated them before him, and seated Hasan and Husayn each on one of his thighs. Then he wrapped his garment around them, or he said his cloak, then recited this verse: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with complete purification﴾. Then he said: "O Allah, these are the People of my House, and the People of my House have more right."'" Abu Ja'far Ibn Jarir related it from Abd al-Karim ibn Abi Umayr [[In manuscript A: "Umar."]], from al-Walid ibn Muslim, from Abu Amr al-Awza'i with his chain, similarly, adding at its end: Wathilah said: "I said: 'And I, O Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless you, am I among your family?' He said: 'And you are among my family.'" Wathilah said: "Indeed, this is among the things I hope for most." [[Musnad (4/107) and Tafsir al-Tabari (22/6).]]

Then he also related it from Abd al-A'la ibn Wasil, from al-Fadl ibn Dukayn, from Abd al-Salam ibn Harb, from Kulthum al-Muharibi, from Shaddad Abu Ammar who said: "I was sitting with Wathilah ibn al-Asqa' when they mentioned Ali and insulted him. When they got up, he said: 'Sit, until I inform you about the one they insulted. I was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when Ali, Fatimah, Hasan, and Husayn came, and he (ﷺ) cast his cloak over them, then said: "O Allah, these are the People of my House. O Allah, remove from them the impurity and purify them with complete purification."' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, and I?' He said: 'And you.' He said: 'By Allah, indeed this is the most reliable of my deeds to me.'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (22/7). Al-Tabarani related it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (22/65) by the route of Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz, from al-Fadl ibn Dukayn, Abu Nu'aym with it.]]

**Another hadith:** Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman, from Ata ibn Abi Rabah, who said: One who heard Umm Salamah mention it narrated to me that the Prophet (ﷺ) was in her house. Fatimah, may Allah be pleased with her, came to him with a cooking pot (burmah) containing khazirah (a dish of meat and grain). She entered with it and gave it to him, and he said to her: "Call your husband and your two sons." She said: So Ali, Hasan and Husayn came and entered upon him, and they sat down eating from that khazirah. He was on his couch (manamah) on a raised platform (dukkan), beneath which was a Khaybari cloak. She said: I was in the room praying. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed this verse: ﴿Allah only wishes to remove impurity from you, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification.﴾ She said: He took the edge of the cloak and covered them with it. Then he extended his hand, raised it toward the sky, and said: "O Allah, these are the People of my House and my close family, so remove impurity from them and purify them thoroughly." She said: I put my head into the house and said: "And am I with you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "You are on the good, you are on the good."

(Musnad, 6/292. In a narration of al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (9/11), the teacher of Ata is named: he said, from Ata ibn Abi Rabah, from Umar ibn Abi Salamah, something similar.)

In its chain is an unnamed person, who is the teacher of Ata. The rest of its narrators are trustworthy.

**Another route:** Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Awf narrated to us, from Abu al-Mu'addil, from Atiyyah al-Tufawi, from his father, that Umm Salamah narrated to him, saying: One day while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was in my house, the servant said: "Fatimah and Ali are at the sudda (the porch)." She said: He said to me: "Get up and withdraw from the People of my House." She said: So I got up and withdrew a short distance within the house. Then Ali and Fatimah entered, with them Hasan and Husayn, who were two small boys. He took the two boys and placed them in his lap and kissed them. He embraced Ali with one of his arms and Fatimah with the other, and he kissed Fatimah and kissed Ali. He wrapped them in a black khamisah (a cloak) and said: "O Allah, to You, not to the Fire, (I come), I and the People of my House." She said: I said: "And I, O Messenger of Allah? May Allah bless you." He said: "And you."

(Musnad, 6/296.)

**Another route:** Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Atiyyah narrated to us, Fudayl ibn Marzuq narrated to us, from Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id, from Umm Salamah, that this verse was revealed in her house: ﴿Allah only wishes to remove impurity from you, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification.﴾ She said: I was sitting at the door of the house, and I said: "O Messenger of Allah, am I not of the People of the House?" He said: "You are on the good; you are of the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ)." She said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Ali, Fatimah, Hasan and Husayn were in the house, may Allah be pleased with them all.

(Tafsir al-Tabari, 22/7. Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (23/249) through Fudayl ibn Marzuq, in abridged form.)

**Another route:** Ibn Jarir also narrated it from Abu Kurayb, from Waki', from Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Umm Salamah, similar to the above.

(Tafsir al-Tabari, 22/6. Al-Tahawi narrated it in Mushkil al-Athar (no. 770) through Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram. Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (23/333) through Zubayd, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Umm Salamah.)

**Another route:** Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated to us, Musa ibn Ya'qub narrated to me, Hashim ibn Hashim ibn Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas narrated to me, from Abdullah ibn Wahb ibn Zam'ah, who said: Umm Salamah, may Allah be pleased with her, informed me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gathered Fatimah, Hasan and Husayn, then put them under his garment. Then he turned in supplication to Allah, mighty and majestic, and said: "These are the People of my House." Umm Salamah said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, let me enter with them." He said: "You are of my family."

(Tafsir al-Tabari, 22/7. Al-Tahawi narrated it in Mushkil al-Athar (no. 763) through Khalid ibn Makhlad al-Qatwani.)

**Another route:** Ibn Jarir also narrated it from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tusi, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Isbahani, from Yahya ibn Ubayd al-Makki, from Ata, from Umar ibn Abi Salamah, from his mother, similar to that.

(Tafsir al-Tabari, 22/7. Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (23/286) through Shurayk, from Ata, from Umm Salamah.)

**Another route:** Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Mus'ab ibn al-Miqdam narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Zarbi narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, from Umm Salamah, who said: Fatimah came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with a pot she had made, containing 'asidah (a porridge), carrying it on a tray. She placed it before him, and he said: "Where are your cousin and your two sons?" She said: "In the house." He said: "Call them." So she went to Ali and said: "Answer the Messenger of Allah, you and your two sons." Umm Salamah said: When he saw them approaching, he reached out his hand toward a cloak that was on the manamah. He pulled it, spread it out, and seated them on it. Then he gathered the four corners of the cloak in his left hand and drew it together above their heads. He pointed with his right hand toward his Lord, mighty and majestic, and said: "O Allah, these are the People of my House, so remove impurity from them and purify them thoroughly."

(Tafsir al-Tabari, 22/7.)

**Another route:** Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Quddus narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Hakim ibn Sa'd, who said: We mentioned Ali ibn Abi Talib in the presence of Umm Salamah, and she said: This verse was revealed in my house: ﴿Allah only wishes to remove impurity from you, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification.﴾ Umm Salamah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to my house and said: "Do not permit anyone to enter." Then Fatimah came, and I could not prevent her from entering to her father. Then Hasan came, and I could not prevent him from entering to his mother and grandfather. Then Husayn came, and I could not prevent him. Then Ali came, and I could not prevent him. So they gathered, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) covered them with a cloak he had, then said: "These are the People of my House, so remove impurity from them and purify them thoroughly." This verse was revealed when they had gathered on the bisat (the mat/carpet). She said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, and me?" She said: By Allah, he did not answer, and then he said: "You are on the good."

(Tafsir al-Tabari, 22/7. Al-Tahawi narrated it in Mushkil al-Athar (no. 762) through Jarir ibn Abd al-Hamid, from al-A'mash, similarly.)

**Another hadith:** Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakic narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, from Zakariyya, from Mus'ab ibn Shaybah, from Safiyyah bint Shaybah, who said: Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out one morning wearing a striped cloak of black wool. Then Hasan came and he took him in with him; then Husayn came and he took him in with him; then Fatimah came and he took her in with him; then Ali came and he took him in with him. Then he said: ﴿Allah only wishes to remove impurity from you, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification.﴾

Muslim narrated it from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Muhammad ibn Bishr, with the same chain.

(Tafsir al-Tabari, 22/5; Sahih Muslim, no. 2081.)

**Another route:** Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Surayj ibn Yunus Abu al-Harith narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Yazid narrated to us, from al-Awwam (meaning Ibn Hawshab), from a paternal uncle of his, who said: I entered with my father upon Aishah, and I asked her about Ali, may Allah be pleased with him. She said, may Allah be pleased with her: "You ask me about a man who was among the most beloved people to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and whose wife was his daughter, the most beloved person to him? I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) call Ali, Fatimah, Hasan and Husayn, then he threw a garment over them and said: 'O Allah, these are the People of my House, so remove impurity from them and purify them thoroughly.'" She said: I approached him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, and am I of the People of your House?" He said: "Step aside, for you are on the good."

**Another hadith:** Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna narrated to us, Bakr ibn Yahya ibn Ziban al-Anazi narrated to us, Mandal narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This verse was revealed concerning five: me, Ali, Hasan, Husayn, and Fatimah: ﴿Allah only wishes to remove impurity from you, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification.﴾"

(Tafsir al-Tabari, 22/5.)

It has already been mentioned that Fudayl ibn Marzuq narrated it from Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id, from Umm Salamah, as already stated.

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from the hadith of Harun ibn Sa'd al-Ijli, from Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id, as a mawquf (a report ending with a Companion), and Allah knows best.

**Another hadith:** Ibn Jarir said: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, Bukayr ibn Mismar narrated to us, who said: I heard Amir ibn Sa'd say: Sa'd said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, when revelation came down to him, and he took Ali, his two sons and Fatimah, and put them under his garment, then said: "My Lord, these are my family and the People of my House."

(Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (22/7) and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra (no. 8439) through Abu Bakr al-Hanafi, from Bukayr ibn Mismar, with the same chain.)

**Another hadith:** Muslim said in his Sahih: Zuhayr ibn Harb and Shuja' ibn Makhlad narrated to me, together, from Ibn Ulayyah. Zuhayr said: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Abu Hayyan narrated to me, Yazid ibn Hayyan narrated to me, who said: I set out with Husayn ibn Sabrah and Umar ibn Muslim to Zayd ibn Arqam. When we sat with him, Husayn said to him: "You have indeed attained much good, O Zayd. You saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), heard his hadith, fought alongside him, and prayed behind him. You have indeed attained much good, O Zayd. Tell us what you heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." He said: "O nephew, by Allah, my age has grown great, my time has passed, and I have forgotten some of what I used to memorize from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So accept what I narrate to you, and do not burden me with what I do not." Then he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood among us one day as a speaker at a body of water called Khumm, between Makkah and Madinah. He praised Allah and extolled Him, admonished and reminded, then said: 'To proceed: O people, I am only a human being; the messenger of my Lord is about to come to me and I will respond. I am leaving among you two weighty things: the first of them is the Book of Allah, in which is guidance and light, so take hold of the Book of Allah and hold fast to it.'" He urged them toward the Book of Allah and encouraged them to it. Then he said: "And the People of my House. I remind you of Allah regarding the People of my House, I remind you of Allah regarding the People of my House," three times. Husayn said to him: "And who are the People of his House, O Zayd? Are not his wives of the People of his House?" He said: "His wives are of the People of his House, but the People of his House are those for whom charity has been forbidden after him." He said: "And who are they?" He said: "They are the family of Ali, the family of Aqil, the family of Ja'far, and the family of Abbas." He said: "All of these are forbidden charity?" He said: "Yes."

(Sahih Muslim, no. 2408.)

Then he narrated it from Muhammad ibn Bakkar ibn al-Rayyan, from Hassan ibn Ibrahim, from Sa'id ibn Masruq, from Yazid ibn Hayyan [in A: "Hassan"], from Zayd ibn Arqam, and he mentioned the hadith in a manner similar to what preceded, and in it: "We said to him: Who are the people of his household? Are they his wives?" He said: "No, by Allah, a woman may be with a man for a period of time, then he divorces her and she returns to her father and her people. The people of his household are his root and his 'asabah (agnatic kin) who are forbidden the charity after him." [Sahih Muslim, no. (2408)].

This is how it occurs in this narration. The first (report) is more preferable, and acting upon it is more appropriate. This second report allows for the possibility that he intended to explain the "household" mentioned in the hadith he narrated, that the intended meaning is only his family who are forbidden the charity; or that the intended meaning of "household" is not only the wives, but they together with his family. This latter possibility is more probable, in order to reconcile it with the previous narration, and also to reconcile the Qur'an with the earlier hadiths, if they are authentic, for in some of their chains there is scrutiny. And Allah knows best. Then, what no one who reflects upon the Qur'an doubts is that the wives of the Prophet ﷺ are included in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with thorough purification﴾, for the context of the speech is with them. Therefore, after all of this, He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and wisdom﴾, meaning: act upon what Allah sends down to His Messenger in your houses of the Book and the Sunnah. This was said by Qatadah and others. And remember this blessing with which you have been singled out from among the people, that revelation descends in your houses to the exclusion of the rest of the people. 'A'isha [al-Siddiqah] [addition from A] daughter of al-Siddiq was the foremost of them in this blessing, the most favored of them with this bounty, and the most specially given of them from this widespread mercy, for revelation did not descend upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the bed of any woman other than her, as the Prophet, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, affirmed. Some of the scholars, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Because he did not marry a virgin other than her, and no man lay with her in her bed other than him, so it was fitting that she be singled out with this distinction and be given this exalted rank. But if his wives are from the people of his household, then his relatives are more worthy of this designation, as preceded in the hadith: "And the people of my household are more deserving." This resembles what is established in Sahih Muslim: that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about the mosque that was founded upon piety from the first day, he said: "It is this mosque of mine" [Sahih Muslim, no. (1398), from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him]. So this is of this kind, for the verse was revealed concerning the Mosque of Quba, as occurs in the other hadiths. But if that one was founded upon piety from the first day, then the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is more worthy of being named thus. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu al-Walid narrated to us, Abu 'Awana narrated to us, from Husayn ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Jamila [in T: "And Ibn Abi Hatim narrated with his chain"] who said: Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali was appointed as caliph when 'Ali was killed, may Allah be pleased with both of them [in T, F, A: "with him"]. He said: While he was praying, a man leapt upon him and stabbed him with a dagger. Husayn claimed that it reached him that the one who stabbed him was a man from the Banu Asad, and Hasan was prostrating. He said: They claim that the stab struck his hip, so he fell ill from it for months, then he recovered and sat upon the pulpit and said: "O people of Iraq, fear Allah concerning us, for we are your rulers and your guests, and we are the People of the House about whom Allah said: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with thorough purification﴾." He said: He kept saying it until no one remained in the mosque except that he was weeping aloud.

And al-Suddi said, from Abu al-Daylam, who said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn said to a man from the people of Syria: Have you not read in al-Ahzab: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with thorough purification﴾? He said: Yes. And are you them? He said: Yes.

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle and Acquainted﴾, meaning: by His subtlety toward you, you have reached this station, and by His knowledge of you and that you are worthy of it, He gave you that and singled you out with it.

Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, said: And remember the blessing of Allah upon you in that He placed you in houses in which the verses of Allah and wisdom are recited, so thank Allah for that and praise Him.

﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle and Acquainted﴾, meaning: possessor of subtlety toward you, in that He placed you in the houses in which His verses and wisdom are recited, and wisdom is the Sunnah, Acquainted with you, in that He chose you as wives for His Messenger.

Qatadah said concerning ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and wisdom﴾: He bestows favour upon them by that. Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

'Ata' al-'Awfi said concerning His saying ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle and Acquainted﴾: meaning, Subtle in extracting them (the verses), Acquainted with their place. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Then he said: Likewise al-Rabi' ibn Anas narrated from Qatadah.

These are etiquette that Allah commanded the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) to follow, and the women of the Ummah follow them in this. Allah addressed the wives of the Prophet [(ﷺ)] [[Addition from manuscript T; manuscript F reads: "may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him."]], saying that if they fear Allah as He has commanded them, then no woman will resemble them, and none will reach them in virtue and rank. Then He said: ﴿So do not be soft in speech, lest one in whose heart is a disease should covet, but speak in an appropriate manner.﴾

As-Suddi and others said: this means softening speech when they address men. For this reason He said: ﴿lest one in whose heart is a disease should covet﴾, meaning, one in whose heart is corruption (dagal). ﴿but speak in an appropriate manner﴾. Ibn Zayd said: "a good, beautiful speech, known for goodness."

The meaning of this is that she should address non-mahram men with speech that contains no softness (tarkhim), i.e., a woman should not address strangers the way she addresses her husband.

* *

His saying: ﴿And stay in your houses﴾, meaning: remain in your houses and do not go out without need. Among the legitimate needs is praying in the mosque under its conditions, as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not prevent the female servants of Allah from the mosques of Allah, but let them go out while unperfumed." In another narration: "And their houses are better for them." [[Abu Dawud related it with this wording in his Sunan, no. 565, from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, and with the second narration, no. 567, from the hadith of Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both. Its origin is in the Two Sahihs from the hadith of Ibn Umar.]]

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Humayd ibn Mas'adah [[In manuscript A: "Mas'ud."]] narrated to us, Abu Raja' al-Kalbi narrated to us, Rawh ibn al-Musayyab is trustworthy, Thabit al-Bunani narrated to us from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The women came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, the men have taken the merit and jihad in the way of Allah, so what deed do we have by which we can attain the deed of those who strive in the way of Allah?' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Whoever of you sits in her house, or words to that effect, she will attain the deed of the mujahidin in the way of Allah.'" [[In manuscript T: "the mujahid."]]

Then he said: "We do not know of anyone who narrated this from Thabit except Rawh ibn al-Musayyab, who is a well-known man from Basra" [[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 1475, Kashf al-Astar. Abu Ya'la related it in his Musnad (6/140) and Ibn Hibban in al-Majruhin (1/299) by the route of Abu Raja' al-Kalbi with similar wording. Ibn Hibban said: "Rawh was among those who narrate forgeries from trustworthy sources, invert chains, and raise statements that were only halted (mawquf). It is not permissible to narrate from him or write his hadith except for testing." Ibn Adi said in al-Kamil: "His hadiths are not preserved."]].

Al-Bazzar also said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Amr ibn Asim narrated to us, Hammam narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Muwarriq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abdullah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed, the woman is 'awrah. When she goes out, Satan makes her appealing, and she is closest to her Lord when she is in the innermost part of her house."

Al-Tirmidhi related it from Bundar, from Amr ibn Asim, with the same wording [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 1173, and al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith." Ibn Khuzaymah related it in his Sahih, no. 1685, and through him Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, no. 329 (Mawarid), from Amr ibn Asim, with the same chain. Ibn Khuzaymah doubted whether Qatadah heard this hadith from Muwarriq.]].

Al-Bazzar also narrated, with his earlier chain, and Abu Dawud too, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "A woman's prayer in her inner room (makhda') is better than her prayer in her house, and her prayer in her house is better than her prayer in her courtyard." [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 570.]] And this chain is good (jayyid).

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance﴾. Mujahid said: "A woman used to go out walking in front of men, and that is the display of the Jahiliyyah."

Qatadah said: ﴿And do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance﴾, meaning: when you go out of your houses, and they had a gait, an affectation, and a flirtatious manner, so Allah forbade that.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: ﴿And do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance﴾. Tabarruj is that she throws her head-covering (khimar) over her head without tying it, so that her necklaces, earrings, and neck are visible, and all of that appears from her; that is tabarruj. Then the women of the believers became general in tabarruj.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Zuhayr narrated to me, Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Dawud (i.e., Ibn Abi al-Furat) narrated to us, Ali ibn Ahmar narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who recited this verse: ﴿And do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance﴾, and said: "It was between Nuh and Idris, and it lasted a thousand years. Two clans of Adam's descendants, one of them lived in the plain and the other in the mountain. The men of the mountain were handsome, but the women were ugly. The women of the plain were handsome, but the men were ugly. Iblis came to a man from the people of the plain in the form of a youth and hired himself to him, serving him. Iblis made something similar to the instrument with which shepherds play, and he produced with it a sound that people had never heard the like of. This reached those around him, and they came to him to listen, and they took a festival which they would gather for once a year, where the women would display themselves to the men, and the men would adorn themselves for them. A man from the people of the mountain came upon them during that festival, saw the women and their beauty, went to his companions and informed them, so they moved to them, settled with them, and indecency spread among them. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance﴾." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (22/4).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And establish prayer, and give zakah, and obey Allah and His Messenger﴾. He first forbade them from evil, then commanded them to good, namely establishing prayer, which is the worship of Allah alone with no partner, and giving zakah, which is kindness to the created beings, ﴿and obey Allah and His Messenger﴾. This is a case of mentioning the general after the specific (atf al-'amm 'ala al-khass).

His saying: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with complete purification﴾. This is an explicit text that the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) are included among the People of the House here, because they are the cause of the revelation of this verse, and the cause of revelation is included in it without dispute, either alone according to one opinion or together with others according to the sound view.
