Ibn Jarir related from Ikrimah that he used to call out in the marketplace: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with complete purification﴾, "It was revealed specifically concerning the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ)." And likewise Ibn Abi Hatim related, saying:

Ali ibn Harb al-Mawsili narrated to us, Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, Husayn ibn Waqid narrated to us, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, the People of the House﴾, he said: "It was revealed specifically concerning the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ)."

Ikrimah also said: "Whoever wishes, I will invoke a mutual curse (mubahalah) with him that it was revealed concerning the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ)."

If what is meant is that they were the cause of the revelation to the exclusion of others, then this is correct. But if what is meant is that they alone are intended to the exclusion of others, then there is room for consideration, for hadiths have come which indicate that what is meant is more general than that:

The first hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Ali ibn Zayd informed us, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to pass by the door of Fatimah for six months when he went out to the Fajr prayer, saying: 'The prayer, O People of the House! ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with complete purification﴾.'"

Al-Tirmidhi related it from Abd ibn Humayd, from Affan with it, and said: "Hasan gharib." [[Musnad (3/259) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3206.]]

Another hadith: Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Waki' narrated to us, Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq narrated to us, Abu Dawud informed me, from Abu al-Hamra' who said: "I stayed in Madinah for seven months during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). [I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)] [[Addition from manuscripts T, F, A, and al-Tabari.]] when dawn broke, he came to the door of Ali and Fatimah and said: 'The prayer, the prayer! ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with complete purification﴾.'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (22/6). Al-Tabarani related it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (22/200) by the route of Mansur ibn al-Aswad, from Abu Dawud, with similar wording.]]

Abu Dawud al-A'ma is Nufay' ibn al-Harith, a liar (kaddhab).

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad also said: Muhammad ibn Mus'ab narrated to us, al-Awza'i narrated to us, Shaddad Abu Ammar narrated to us, who said: "I entered upon Wathilah ibn al-Asqa' and there were some people with him, and they mentioned Ali, may Allah be pleased with him. When they left, he said to me: 'Shall I not inform you of what I saw from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'I came to Fatimah to ask her about Ali, and she said: He has gone to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So I sat waiting for him until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came, with Ali, Hasan, and Husayn, each of them holding one of his hands, until he entered. He brought Ali and Fatimah close and seated them before him, and seated Hasan and Husayn each on one of his thighs. Then he wrapped his garment around them, or he said his cloak, then recited this verse: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with complete purification﴾. Then he said: "O Allah, these are the People of my House, and the People of my House have more right."'" Abu Ja'far Ibn Jarir related it from Abd al-Karim ibn Abi Umayr [[In manuscript A: "Umar."]], from al-Walid ibn Muslim, from Abu Amr al-Awza'i with his chain, similarly, adding at its end: Wathilah said: "I said: 'And I, O Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless you, am I among your family?' He said: 'And you are among my family.'" Wathilah said: "Indeed, this is among the things I hope for most." [[Musnad (4/107) and Tafsir al-Tabari (22/6).]]

Then he also related it from Abd al-A'la ibn Wasil, from al-Fadl ibn Dukayn, from Abd al-Salam ibn Harb, from Kulthum al-Muharibi, from Shaddad Abu Ammar who said: "I was sitting with Wathilah ibn al-Asqa' when they mentioned Ali and insulted him. When they got up, he said: 'Sit, until I inform you about the one they insulted. I was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when Ali, Fatimah, Hasan, and Husayn came, and he (ﷺ) cast his cloak over them, then said: "O Allah, these are the People of my House. O Allah, remove from them the impurity and purify them with complete purification."' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, and I?' He said: 'And you.' He said: 'By Allah, indeed this is the most reliable of my deeds to me.'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (22/7). Al-Tabarani related it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (22/65) by the route of Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz, from al-Fadl ibn Dukayn, Abu Nu'aym with it.]]

**Another hadith:** Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman, from Ata ibn Abi Rabah, who said: One who heard Umm Salamah mention it narrated to me that the Prophet (ﷺ) was in her house. Fatimah, may Allah be pleased with her, came to him with a cooking pot (burmah) containing khazirah (a dish of meat and grain). She entered with it and gave it to him, and he said to her: "Call your husband and your two sons." She said: So Ali, Hasan and Husayn came and entered upon him, and they sat down eating from that khazirah. He was on his couch (manamah) on a raised platform (dukkan), beneath which was a Khaybari cloak. She said: I was in the room praying. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed this verse: ﴿Allah only wishes to remove impurity from you, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification.﴾ She said: He took the edge of the cloak and covered them with it. Then he extended his hand, raised it toward the sky, and said: "O Allah, these are the People of my House and my close family, so remove impurity from them and purify them thoroughly." She said: I put my head into the house and said: "And am I with you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "You are on the good, you are on the good."

(Musnad, 6/292. In a narration of al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (9/11), the teacher of Ata is named: he said, from Ata ibn Abi Rabah, from Umar ibn Abi Salamah, something similar.)

In its chain is an unnamed person, who is the teacher of Ata. The rest of its narrators are trustworthy.

**Another route:** Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Awf narrated to us, from Abu al-Mu'addil, from Atiyyah al-Tufawi, from his father, that Umm Salamah narrated to him, saying: One day while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was in my house, the servant said: "Fatimah and Ali are at the sudda (the porch)." She said: He said to me: "Get up and withdraw from the People of my House." She said: So I got up and withdrew a short distance within the house. Then Ali and Fatimah entered, with them Hasan and Husayn, who were two small boys. He took the two boys and placed them in his lap and kissed them. He embraced Ali with one of his arms and Fatimah with the other, and he kissed Fatimah and kissed Ali. He wrapped them in a black khamisah (a cloak) and said: "O Allah, to You, not to the Fire, (I come), I and the People of my House." She said: I said: "And I, O Messenger of Allah? May Allah bless you." He said: "And you."

(Musnad, 6/296.)

**Another route:** Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Atiyyah narrated to us, Fudayl ibn Marzuq narrated to us, from Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id, from Umm Salamah, that this verse was revealed in her house: ﴿Allah only wishes to remove impurity from you, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification.﴾ She said: I was sitting at the door of the house, and I said: "O Messenger of Allah, am I not of the People of the House?" He said: "You are on the good; you are of the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ)." She said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Ali, Fatimah, Hasan and Husayn were in the house, may Allah be pleased with them all.

(Tafsir al-Tabari, 22/7. Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (23/249) through Fudayl ibn Marzuq, in abridged form.)

**Another route:** Ibn Jarir also narrated it from Abu Kurayb, from Waki', from Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Umm Salamah, similar to the above.

(Tafsir al-Tabari, 22/6. Al-Tahawi narrated it in Mushkil al-Athar (no. 770) through Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram. Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (23/333) through Zubayd, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Umm Salamah.)

**Another route:** Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated to us, Musa ibn Ya'qub narrated to me, Hashim ibn Hashim ibn Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas narrated to me, from Abdullah ibn Wahb ibn Zam'ah, who said: Umm Salamah, may Allah be pleased with her, informed me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gathered Fatimah, Hasan and Husayn, then put them under his garment. Then he turned in supplication to Allah, mighty and majestic, and said: "These are the People of my House." Umm Salamah said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, let me enter with them." He said: "You are of my family."

(Tafsir al-Tabari, 22/7. Al-Tahawi narrated it in Mushkil al-Athar (no. 763) through Khalid ibn Makhlad al-Qatwani.)

**Another route:** Ibn Jarir also narrated it from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tusi, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Isbahani, from Yahya ibn Ubayd al-Makki, from Ata, from Umar ibn Abi Salamah, from his mother, similar to that.

(Tafsir al-Tabari, 22/7. Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (23/286) through Shurayk, from Ata, from Umm Salamah.)

**Another route:** Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Mus'ab ibn al-Miqdam narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Zarbi narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, from Umm Salamah, who said: Fatimah came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with a pot she had made, containing 'asidah (a porridge), carrying it on a tray. She placed it before him, and he said: "Where are your cousin and your two sons?" She said: "In the house." He said: "Call them." So she went to Ali and said: "Answer the Messenger of Allah, you and your two sons." Umm Salamah said: When he saw them approaching, he reached out his hand toward a cloak that was on the manamah. He pulled it, spread it out, and seated them on it. Then he gathered the four corners of the cloak in his left hand and drew it together above their heads. He pointed with his right hand toward his Lord, mighty and majestic, and said: "O Allah, these are the People of my House, so remove impurity from them and purify them thoroughly."

(Tafsir al-Tabari, 22/7.)

**Another route:** Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Quddus narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Hakim ibn Sa'd, who said: We mentioned Ali ibn Abi Talib in the presence of Umm Salamah, and she said: This verse was revealed in my house: ﴿Allah only wishes to remove impurity from you, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification.﴾ Umm Salamah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to my house and said: "Do not permit anyone to enter." Then Fatimah came, and I could not prevent her from entering to her father. Then Hasan came, and I could not prevent him from entering to his mother and grandfather. Then Husayn came, and I could not prevent him. Then Ali came, and I could not prevent him. So they gathered, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) covered them with a cloak he had, then said: "These are the People of my House, so remove impurity from them and purify them thoroughly." This verse was revealed when they had gathered on the bisat (the mat/carpet). She said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, and me?" She said: By Allah, he did not answer, and then he said: "You are on the good."

(Tafsir al-Tabari, 22/7. Al-Tahawi narrated it in Mushkil al-Athar (no. 762) through Jarir ibn Abd al-Hamid, from al-A'mash, similarly.)

**Another hadith:** Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakic narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, from Zakariyya, from Mus'ab ibn Shaybah, from Safiyyah bint Shaybah, who said: Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out one morning wearing a striped cloak of black wool. Then Hasan came and he took him in with him; then Husayn came and he took him in with him; then Fatimah came and he took her in with him; then Ali came and he took him in with him. Then he said: ﴿Allah only wishes to remove impurity from you, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification.﴾

Muslim narrated it from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Muhammad ibn Bishr, with the same chain.

(Tafsir al-Tabari, 22/5; Sahih Muslim, no. 2081.)

**Another route:** Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Surayj ibn Yunus Abu al-Harith narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Yazid narrated to us, from al-Awwam (meaning Ibn Hawshab), from a paternal uncle of his, who said: I entered with my father upon Aishah, and I asked her about Ali, may Allah be pleased with him. She said, may Allah be pleased with her: "You ask me about a man who was among the most beloved people to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and whose wife was his daughter, the most beloved person to him? I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) call Ali, Fatimah, Hasan and Husayn, then he threw a garment over them and said: 'O Allah, these are the People of my House, so remove impurity from them and purify them thoroughly.'" She said: I approached him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, and am I of the People of your House?" He said: "Step aside, for you are on the good."

**Another hadith:** Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna narrated to us, Bakr ibn Yahya ibn Ziban al-Anazi narrated to us, Mandal narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This verse was revealed concerning five: me, Ali, Hasan, Husayn, and Fatimah: ﴿Allah only wishes to remove impurity from you, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification.﴾"

(Tafsir al-Tabari, 22/5.)

It has already been mentioned that Fudayl ibn Marzuq narrated it from Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id, from Umm Salamah, as already stated.

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from the hadith of Harun ibn Sa'd al-Ijli, from Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id, as a mawquf (a report ending with a Companion), and Allah knows best.

**Another hadith:** Ibn Jarir said: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, Bukayr ibn Mismar narrated to us, who said: I heard Amir ibn Sa'd say: Sa'd said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, when revelation came down to him, and he took Ali, his two sons and Fatimah, and put them under his garment, then said: "My Lord, these are my family and the People of my House."

(Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (22/7) and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra (no. 8439) through Abu Bakr al-Hanafi, from Bukayr ibn Mismar, with the same chain.)

**Another hadith:** Muslim said in his Sahih: Zuhayr ibn Harb and Shuja' ibn Makhlad narrated to me, together, from Ibn Ulayyah. Zuhayr said: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Abu Hayyan narrated to me, Yazid ibn Hayyan narrated to me, who said: I set out with Husayn ibn Sabrah and Umar ibn Muslim to Zayd ibn Arqam. When we sat with him, Husayn said to him: "You have indeed attained much good, O Zayd. You saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), heard his hadith, fought alongside him, and prayed behind him. You have indeed attained much good, O Zayd. Tell us what you heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." He said: "O nephew, by Allah, my age has grown great, my time has passed, and I have forgotten some of what I used to memorize from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So accept what I narrate to you, and do not burden me with what I do not." Then he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood among us one day as a speaker at a body of water called Khumm, between Makkah and Madinah. He praised Allah and extolled Him, admonished and reminded, then said: 'To proceed: O people, I am only a human being; the messenger of my Lord is about to come to me and I will respond. I am leaving among you two weighty things: the first of them is the Book of Allah, in which is guidance and light, so take hold of the Book of Allah and hold fast to it.'" He urged them toward the Book of Allah and encouraged them to it. Then he said: "And the People of my House. I remind you of Allah regarding the People of my House, I remind you of Allah regarding the People of my House," three times. Husayn said to him: "And who are the People of his House, O Zayd? Are not his wives of the People of his House?" He said: "His wives are of the People of his House, but the People of his House are those for whom charity has been forbidden after him." He said: "And who are they?" He said: "They are the family of Ali, the family of Aqil, the family of Ja'far, and the family of Abbas." He said: "All of these are forbidden charity?" He said: "Yes."

(Sahih Muslim, no. 2408.)

Then he narrated it from Muhammad ibn Bakkar ibn al-Rayyan, from Hassan ibn Ibrahim, from Sa'id ibn Masruq, from Yazid ibn Hayyan [in A: "Hassan"], from Zayd ibn Arqam, and he mentioned the hadith in a manner similar to what preceded, and in it: "We said to him: Who are the people of his household? Are they his wives?" He said: "No, by Allah, a woman may be with a man for a period of time, then he divorces her and she returns to her father and her people. The people of his household are his root and his 'asabah (agnatic kin) who are forbidden the charity after him." [Sahih Muslim, no. (2408)].

This is how it occurs in this narration. The first (report) is more preferable, and acting upon it is more appropriate. This second report allows for the possibility that he intended to explain the "household" mentioned in the hadith he narrated, that the intended meaning is only his family who are forbidden the charity; or that the intended meaning of "household" is not only the wives, but they together with his family. This latter possibility is more probable, in order to reconcile it with the previous narration, and also to reconcile the Qur'an with the earlier hadiths, if they are authentic, for in some of their chains there is scrutiny. And Allah knows best. Then, what no one who reflects upon the Qur'an doubts is that the wives of the Prophet ﷺ are included in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with thorough purification﴾, for the context of the speech is with them. Therefore, after all of this, He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and wisdom﴾, meaning: act upon what Allah sends down to His Messenger in your houses of the Book and the Sunnah. This was said by Qatadah and others. And remember this blessing with which you have been singled out from among the people, that revelation descends in your houses to the exclusion of the rest of the people. 'A'isha [al-Siddiqah] [addition from A] daughter of al-Siddiq was the foremost of them in this blessing, the most favored of them with this bounty, and the most specially given of them from this widespread mercy, for revelation did not descend upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the bed of any woman other than her, as the Prophet, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, affirmed. Some of the scholars, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Because he did not marry a virgin other than her, and no man lay with her in her bed other than him, so it was fitting that she be singled out with this distinction and be given this exalted rank. But if his wives are from the people of his household, then his relatives are more worthy of this designation, as preceded in the hadith: "And the people of my household are more deserving." This resembles what is established in Sahih Muslim: that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about the mosque that was founded upon piety from the first day, he said: "It is this mosque of mine" [Sahih Muslim, no. (1398), from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him]. So this is of this kind, for the verse was revealed concerning the Mosque of Quba, as occurs in the other hadiths. But if that one was founded upon piety from the first day, then the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is more worthy of being named thus. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu al-Walid narrated to us, Abu 'Awana narrated to us, from Husayn ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Jamila [in T: "And Ibn Abi Hatim narrated with his chain"] who said: Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali was appointed as caliph when 'Ali was killed, may Allah be pleased with both of them [in T, F, A: "with him"]. He said: While he was praying, a man leapt upon him and stabbed him with a dagger. Husayn claimed that it reached him that the one who stabbed him was a man from the Banu Asad, and Hasan was prostrating. He said: They claim that the stab struck his hip, so he fell ill from it for months, then he recovered and sat upon the pulpit and said: "O people of Iraq, fear Allah concerning us, for we are your rulers and your guests, and we are the People of the House about whom Allah said: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with thorough purification﴾." He said: He kept saying it until no one remained in the mosque except that he was weeping aloud.

And al-Suddi said, from Abu al-Daylam, who said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn said to a man from the people of Syria: Have you not read in al-Ahzab: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with thorough purification﴾? He said: Yes. And are you them? He said: Yes.

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle and Acquainted﴾, meaning: by His subtlety toward you, you have reached this station, and by His knowledge of you and that you are worthy of it, He gave you that and singled you out with it.

Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, said: And remember the blessing of Allah upon you in that He placed you in houses in which the verses of Allah and wisdom are recited, so thank Allah for that and praise Him.

﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle and Acquainted﴾, meaning: possessor of subtlety toward you, in that He placed you in the houses in which His verses and wisdom are recited, and wisdom is the Sunnah, Acquainted with you, in that He chose you as wives for His Messenger.

Qatadah said concerning ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and wisdom﴾: He bestows favour upon them by that. Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

'Ata' al-'Awfi said concerning His saying ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle and Acquainted﴾: meaning, Subtle in extracting them (the verses), Acquainted with their place. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Then he said: Likewise al-Rabi' ibn Anas narrated from Qatadah.

Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us, 'Uthman ibn Hakim narrated to us, [[In T: "Imam Ahmad also narrated with his chain from"]] 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Shayba narrated to us. I heard Umm Salama, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, say: I said to the Prophet ﷺ, "Why are we not mentioned in the Qur'an as men are mentioned?" She said: "Then one day I was taken unawares by his calling from the pulpit. I was combing my hair, so I gathered up my hair and went out to one of the rooms of my house, and I put my ear to the palm-stalk (the wooden partition). And he was saying at the pulpit: 'O people, indeed Allah says: Indeed the Muslim men and the Muslim women, the believing men and the believing women...' until the end of the verse."

[[In F: "He said."]]

Similarly, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad, with the same wording. [[Musnad (6/305), al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (1405), and Tafsir al-Tabari (22/9).]]

Another route from her: al-Nasa'i also said: Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to us, Suwayd narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Shurayk informed us, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Abu Salama, from Umm Salama, that she said to the Prophet ﷺ: "O Prophet of Allah, why do I hear men being mentioned in the Qur'an, while women are not mentioned?" So Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed the Muslim men and the Muslim women, the believing men and the believing women﴾. [[Al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (1404).]]

It was also narrated by Ibn Jarir, from Abu Kurayb, from Abu Mu'awiya, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Abu Salama: that Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Hatib told him, from Umm Salama, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, are men mentioned in everything while we are not mentioned?' So Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed the Muslim men and the Muslim women﴾, to the end of the verse." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (22/8).]]

Another route: Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: Umm Salama said: "O Messenger of Allah, men are mentioned and we are not mentioned?" So Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed the Muslim men and the Muslim women﴾, to the end of the verse.

Another hadith: Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, who said: Sayyar ibn Mudhahhir al-'Anazi narrated to us. [[In F and A: "Sinan ibn Mudhahhir al-'Amari."]] Abu Kudayna Yahya ibn al-Muhallab narrated to us, from Qabus ibn Abi Zibyan, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The women said to the Prophet ﷺ: 'Why does He mention the believing men and not the believing women?' So Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed the Muslim men and the Muslim women﴾, to the end of the verse." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (22/8).]]

And Bishr narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, [[In F and A: "Sa'd."]] from Qatada, who said: "Some women entered upon the wives of the Prophet ﷺ and said: 'Allah has mentioned you in the Qur'an, but we have not been mentioned at all. Is there nothing in us that is mentioned?' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Indeed the Muslim men and the Muslim women﴾, to the end of the verse." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (22/8).]]

So His saying: ﴿Indeed the Muslim men and the Muslim women, the believing men and the believing women﴾ is evidence that faith (iman) is other than Islam (islam), and that it is more specific than it, due to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The Bedouins say, "We have believed." Say, "You have not believed; rather say, 'We have submitted,' for faith has not yet entered your hearts."﴾ [al-Hujurat: 14]. And in the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim): "The adulterer does not commit adultery while he is a believer." So faith is stripped from him, yet this does not entail his disbelief by the consensus (ijma') of the Muslims. This shows that it is more specific than Islam, as we established at the beginning of our explanation of Sahih al-Bukhari.

[And His saying] [[Addition from T and A.]]: ﴿And the devout men and the devout women﴾. Qunut (devotion) is obedience with stillness. ﴿Is one who worships devoutly during the hours of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord?﴾ [al-Zumar: 9]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿To Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth; all are devoutly obedient to Him﴾ [al-Rum: 26]; ﴿O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord, and prostrate and bow with those who bow﴾ [Al 'Imran: 43]; ﴿And stand before Allah in devout obedience﴾ [al-Baqara: 238]. So Islam is a station (martaba) one ascends to, and then qunut arises from both of them.

﴿And the truthful men and the truthful women﴾: This refers to speech, for truthfulness is a praiseworthy trait. For this reason some of the Companions were never known to have told a lie, neither in the Jahiliyya nor in Islam. [[In T, F: "in jahiliyya nor in Islam."]] It is a sign of faith, just as lying is a sign of hypocrisy. Whoever is truthful is saved. "Hold fast to truthfulness, for truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. Beware of lying, for lying leads to wickedness, and wickedness leads to the Fire. A man continues to speak the truth and seek it until he is recorded with Allah as a siddiq (truthful one), and a man continues to lie and seek it until he is recorded with Allah as a liar." [[In T, F, A: he quoted the end of the hadith and omitted its beginning.]] The hadiths on this are very numerous.

﴿And the patient men and the patient women﴾: This is the trait of the steadfast, namely patience in the face of calamities, knowing that what is decreed will certainly occur, and meeting it with patience and steadfastness. Patience is most difficult at the first shock, i.e., its hardest moment is at the very beginning, and after that it becomes easier. It is the truthfulness and steadfastness of this disposition.

﴿And the humble men and the humble women﴾: Khushu' is stillness, tranquility, deliberateness, dignity and humility. What drives it is fear of Allah and watchfulness over Him, [as in the hadith] [[Addition from T, F, A.]]: "Worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then He sees you."

﴿And the charitable men and the charitable women﴾: Sadaqa is doing good to people who are needy and weak, who have no earnings and no one earning for them, who are given from the surplus of wealth out of obedience to Allah and kindness to His creation. It is established in the two Sahihs: "Seven will be shaded by Allah under His shade on a day when there is no shade but His shade." He mentioned among them: "And a man who gave charity and concealed it, so that his left hand does not know what his right hand spends." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1423) and Sahih Muslim no. (1031).]] In another hadith: "Charity extinguishes sin as water extinguishes fire." [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan no. (614) from the hadith of Ka'b ibn 'Ujra, may Allah be pleased with him, and he said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith from this route." Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad 3/321 from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with him. Al-Tirmidhi no. (2616) and Ibn Majah no. (3973) narrated it from the hadith of Mu'adh, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

[In al-Tirmidhi, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Indeed charity extinguishes the wrath of the Lord and averts a bad death."

In the two Sahihs, from 'Adi ibn Hatim, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "None of you will be spoken to by his Lord, with no interpreter between them. He will look to his right and see nothing but what he has sent forward; he will look to his left and see nothing but what he has sent forward; and he will look ahead and see nothing but the Fire facing him. So guard yourselves against the Fire, even with half a date."

In the hadith of Abu Dharr, that he said: "I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: What saves a servant from the Fire?" He said: "Faith in Allah." I said: "O Prophet of Allah, along with faith is there any deed?" He said: "Give some of what Allah has entrusted to you," or "some of what Allah has provided you." For this reason, when the Prophet ﷺ delivered the sermon on the day of 'Id, he said in his sermon: "O assembly of women, give charity, even from your jewelry, for I have seen that most of the people of the Fire are women." It was as if he was urging them and encouraging them to give that by which they could ransom themselves from the Fire. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "It has been mentioned to me that the deeds boast, and charity says: 'I am the best of you.'"

In the two Sahihs, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ struck a parable: the stingy man and the charitable man are like two men wearing coats of mail, or two cuirasses of iron, their hands constrained up to their chests and collarbones. Whenever the charitable man gives charity, it expands over him until it covers his fingertips and erases his traces; and whenever the stingy man intends to give charity, it contracts, and each ring takes its place. Abu Hurayra said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ point with his finger like this at his collar. If you had seen him, you would see him try to widen it, yet it does not widen." And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his own soul, it is those who are the successful﴾ [al-Taghabun: 16]. So a man's generosity makes him beloved to his opponents, and his stinginess makes him hated by his own children, as it has been said:

"His stinginess reveals a man's faults among people,
while his generosity covers them all."

"Cloak yourself in the garments of generosity, for I see
every fault, and generosity is its covering."]] ...

The hadiths urging this are very numerous and it has a place of its own.

﴿And the fasting men and the fasting women﴾: In the hadith narrated by Ibn Majah: "Fasting is the zakat of the body," meaning it purifies it, cleanses it and clears it of bad humours, both naturally and by the Law.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Whoever fasts Ramadan and three days of every month enters into His saying: ﴿And the fasting men and the fasting women﴾.

Since fasting is among the greatest aids in breaking desire, as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O assembly of young men, whoever among you is able to marry, let him marry, for it lowers the gaze and guards the private parts; and whoever cannot, let him fast, for it is a shield for him" [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (5066) and Sahih Muslim no. (1400)], it was fitting that He mention after it: ﴿And the men who guard their private parts and the women who guard theirs﴾, meaning from what is forbidden and sinful, except from what is permitted, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And those who guard their private parts, except from their spouses or what their right hands possess, for they are not blameworthy. But whoever seeks beyond that, it is those who are transgressors﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 5-7].

* *

And His saying: ﴿And the men who remember Allah much and the women who remember Him much﴾. Ibn Abi Hatim said:

My father narrated to us, Hisham ibn 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Jabir narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn al-Aqmar, from al-Aghurr Abi Muslim [[In T: "Ibn Abi Hatim narrated with his chain."]], from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If a man wakes his wife at night, and they both pray two rak'as, they are both recorded that night among the men and women who remember Allah much."

It was also narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah, from the hadith of al-A'mash, [from 'Ali ibn al-Aqmar] [[Addition from T, F, and the Sunan of Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah.]], from al-Aghurr Abi Muslim, from Abu Sa'id and Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet ﷺ, with the same wording. [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (1309), al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (11406), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (1335).]]

[[In T: "And narrated."]] Imam Ahmad said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'a narrated to us, Darraj narrated to us, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, which of the servants is highest in rank with Allah on the Day of Resurrection?' He said: 'Those who remember Allah much, men and women.'"

He said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, and what of the one who fights in the cause of Allah?' He said: 'Even if he strikes with his sword against the disbelievers and polytheists until it breaks and is stained with blood, those who remember Allah would still be better than him.'" [[Al-Musnad (3/75). Darraj from Abu al-Haytham is weak.]]

Ibn Kathir narrates through Imam Ahmad: Ibn Kathir said, and Imam Ahmad narrated to us: ʿAffan related to us, ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim related to us, from al-ʿAla, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) was traveling on the road to Makkah, and he came upon Jumdan, and said: "This is Jumdan. Proceed, for the mufarridun (the single-minded ones) have gone ahead." They said: "And who are the mufarridun?" He said: "Those who remember Allah often." Then he said: "O Allah, forgive those who shave their heads." They said: "And those who trim?" He said: "O Allah, forgive those who shave their heads." They said: "And those who trim?" He said: "And those who trim."

This narration is related by Ahmad alone through this chain, and Muslim related it without its beginning. (Al-Musnad 2/411; Sahih Muslim no. 1302. Muslim related only the latter part, and Allah knows best.)

And Imam Ahmad said: Ḥujayn ibn al-Muthanna related to us, ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Abi Salamah related to us, from Ziyad ibn Abi Ziyad, the freedman of ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAyyash ibn Abi Rabiʿah, that it reached him from Muʿadh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No son of Adam has ever done a deed that saves him from the punishment of Allah more than the remembrance of Allah." Muʿadh also said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Shall I not inform you of the best of your deeds, the purest of them in the sight of your Sovereign, the highest of them in your ranks, and better for you than spending gold and silver, and better for you than meeting your enemy tomorrow, striking their necks and they striking yours?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "The remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

And Imam Ahmad said: Hasan related to us, Ibn Lahiʿah related to us, Zabban ibn Fa'id related to us, from Sahl ibn Muʿadh ibn Anas al-Juhani, from his father, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): that a man asked him, "Which of the fighters in the way of Allah has the greatest reward, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The one among them who remembers Allah most." He said: "And which of the fasting ones has the greatest reward?" He said: "The one among them who remembers Allah most." Then he mentioned prayer, zakah, Hajj and charity, and to each the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The one among them who remembers Allah most." Then Abu Bakr said to ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both: "The remembrance-makers have taken every good." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed."

We will mention the rest of the hadiths concerning the abundance of remembrance at His saying in this surah: ﴿O you who believe, remember Allah with much remembrance, and glorify Him morning and evening﴾ [al-Ahzab: 41-42], and so on, if Allah wills.

* *

His saying: ﴿Allah has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward﴾, meaning: He has readied for them, for their sins, forgiveness from Him, and a great reward, which is Paradise.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 33, verse 36:

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman﴾ to the end of the verse, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out to propose on behalf of his freedman Zayd ibn Harithah. He entered upon Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyyah and proposed to her, and she said: "I am not going to marry him." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Yes, you will marry him." She said: "O Messenger of Allah, let me consult myself." While they were talking, Allah revealed this verse to His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decreed a matter, that they should have any choice in their affair﴾ to the end of the verse. She said: "Have I accepted him for me as a husband, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes." She said: "Then I will not disobey the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; I have given myself to him in marriage."[[Tafsir al-Tabari (22/9).]]

Ibn Lahi'ah related from Ibn Abi 'Amrah, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ proposed Zaynab bint Jahsh to Zayd ibn Harithah, but she disdained him and said: "I am better than him in lineage," and she was a woman of sharpness of temper. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman﴾ the whole verse.

Mujahid, Qatadah and Muqatil ibn Hayyan likewise said that it was revealed concerning Zaynab bint Jahsh [al-Asadiyyah][[Addition from A.]] when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ proposed her on behalf of his freedman Zayd ibn Harithah; she refused, then she consented.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: It was revealed concerning Umm Kulthum bint 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt, [[In A: "Umm Maktum".]] who was the first woman to emigrate among the women, meaning after the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyyah. She gave herself to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: "I have accepted." Then he married her to Zayd ibn Harithah, meaning, and Allah knows best, after his divorce from Zaynab. She and her brother were displeased and said: "We only wanted the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he married us to his slave." He said: So the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decreed a matter﴾ to the end of the verse. He said: And there came a more comprehensive command than this: ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves﴾. He said: That was specific, and this is general.

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Razzaq related to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas, who said: The Prophet ﷺ proposed to a woman among the Ansar on behalf of Julaybib to her father. He said: "Let me consult her mother." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Yes, then." The man went to his wife and mentioned that to her. She said: "No, by Allah, not at all! Does the Messenger of Allah ﷺ find no one but Julaybib? We have refused to give her to so-and-so and so-and-so." He said: And the girl was behind her screen listening. He said: The man set out intending to inform the Prophet ﷺ of that. The girl said: "Do you wish to reject the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? If he has approved him for you, then marry him to him." He said: So it was as if she had lifted the matter from her parents, and they both said: "You have spoken the truth." Her father went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "If you have approved him, then we approve him." He said: "I have indeed approved him." He said: So he married her to him. Then the people of Madinah were alarmed, and Julaybib mounted and they found him slain, with people of the polytheists around him whom he had killed. Anas said: I indeed saw her, and she was among the most bounteous households in Madinah.

Imam Ahmad also said: 'Affan related to us, Hammad, that is Ibn Salamah, related to us, from Thabit, from Kinanah ibn Nu'aym al-'Adawi, from Abu Barzah al-Aslami, that Julaybib was a man who would enter upon the women, pass by them and joke with them. I said to my wife: "Julaybib must not enter upon you today, for if he enters upon you I will certainly do such-and-such." He said: The Ansar, when one of them had a widowed daughter, would not marry her until he knew whether the Prophet ﷺ had any need of her or not. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to a man of the Ansar: "Marry me your daughter." He said: "Yes, and it is an honour, O Messenger of Allah, and a delight to the eye." He said: "I do not want her for myself." He said: "Then for whom, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "For Julaybib."

He said: "O Messenger of Allah, let me consult her mother." He went to her mother and said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ is proposing your daughter." She said: "Yes, and a delight to the eye." He said: "He is not proposing her for himself; he is proposing her for Julaybib." She said: "Julaybib? Julaybib? No, by the life of Allah, I will not marry her to him." When he was about to rise to go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and inform him of what her mother had said, the girl said: "Who has proposed me to you?" Her mother informed her. She said: "Will you reject the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? Give me to him, for he will not waste me." So her father went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "Take her in your charge." So he married her to Julaybib.

He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out on a campaign, and when Allah granted him victory, he said to his companions: "Do you miss anyone?" They said: "We miss so-and-so and so-and-so." He said: "Look again, do you miss anyone?" They said: "No." He said: "But I miss Julaybib." He said: "Search for him among the slain." They searched and found him beside seven whom he had killed, and then they had killed him. [They said: "O Messenger of Allah, here he is beside seven whom he had killed, and then they killed him."] The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to him and stood over him and said: "He killed seven, and then they killed him. He is from me and I am from him." He said it twice or three times. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ placed him on his forearms, and he had no bier except the forearms of the Prophet ﷺ. Then he placed him in his grave, and it is not mentioned that he washed him, may Allah be pleased with him. Thabit said: There was no widow among the Ansar more bounteous than she. Ishaq ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Talhah related to Thabit: Do you know what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed for her? He said: "O Allah, pour good upon her abundantly, and do not make her life hardship," or so he said. There was no widow among the Ansar more bounteous than she.

Imam Ahmad narrated it in full like this,[[Musnad (4/422).]] and Muslim and al-Nasa'i in al-Fada'il extracted from it the story of his killing.[[Sahih Muslim no. (2482) and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (8246).]] The memorizer Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr mentioned in "al-Isti'ab" that when the girl said from behind her screen: "Will you reject the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?", she recited this verse: ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decreed a matter, that they should have any choice in their affair﴾.[[Al-Isti'ab (1/259).]]

Ibn Jurayj said: [Ibn Abi Mus'ab informed me, from Tawus, that he asked Ibn 'Abbas about two rak'ahs after 'Asr, and he forbade him. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, recited: ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decreed a matter, that they should have any choice in their affair﴾.][[Addition from T, F, A.]]

So this verse is general in all matters: when Allah and His Messenger have judged something, it is not permissible for anyone to oppose it, and there is no choice for anyone in that matter, nor any opinion or statement, as the Exalted said: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves and then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have decided and submit in full submission﴾ [An-Nisa: 65]. And in the hadith: "By He in whose hand is my soul, none of you believes until his desire is a follower of what I have brought." Therefore He was severe in opposing that, saying: ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error﴾, like His saying: ﴿So let those who oppose his order beware lest a trial befall them or a painful punishment strike them﴾ [An-Nur: 63].

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said, relating about His Prophet (may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him) that he said to his freed slave Zayd ibn Harithah, "and he is the one upon whom Allah bestowed favour" — that is, with Islam and following the Messenger (upon him be the best of prayers and peace) — ﴿and you bestowed favour upon him﴾, that is, by freeing him from slavery. Zayd was a noble master of great standing and high rank, beloved to the Prophet ﷺ; he was called "al-Hibb" (the Beloved), and his son Usamah was called "al-Hibb, son of al-Hibb."

'Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never sent him on an expedition except that he appointed him over them, and had he lived after him, he would have made him his successor." Ahmad narrated it from Sa'id ibn Muhammad al-Warraq and Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd, from Wa'il ibn Dawud, from 'Abd Allah al-Bahi, from her [(Musnad 6/227)].

Al-Bazzar said: Khalid ibn Yusuf narrated to us, Abu 'Awanah narrated to us (ḥ); and Muhammad ibn Ma'mar narrated to us, Abu Dawud narrated to us, Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, 'Imran ibn Abi Salamah informed me, from his father: Usamah ibn Zayd narrated to me, he said: "I was in the mosque when al-'Abbas and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with them both) came to me and said, 'O Usamah, ask permission for us to enter upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.'" He said: "So I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and informed him, and I said, 'Ali and al-'Abbas are asking permission?' He said, 'Do you know what their need is?' I said, 'No, O Messenger of Allah.' He said, 'But I know.'" He said: "So he gave them permission. They said, 'O Messenger of Allah, we have come to you so that you may tell us: which of your family is most beloved to you?' He said, 'The most beloved of my family to me is Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad.' They said, 'O Messenger of Allah, we are not asking you about Fatimah.' He said, 'Then Usamah ibn Zayd ibn Harithah, the one upon whom Allah bestowed favour and upon whom I bestowed favour.'" [Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in his Sunan, no. 3819, through Abu 'Awanah in similar wording, and al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih."]

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had married him to his paternal aunt's daughter, Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyyah, whose mother was Umaymah bint 'Abd al-Muttalib. He gave her as dowry ten dinars, sixty dirhams, a head-covering, a wrapper, a shift, fifty mudd of food, and ten mudd of dates. This was stated by Muqatil ibn Hayyan. Then he remained with her for about a year or more, after which discord arose between them, and Zayd came complaining of her to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah kept saying to him, "Keep your wife to yourself, and fear Allah." Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And you concealed within yourself that which Allah was to disclose, and you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you should fear Him﴾.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned here reports from some of the early generations (salaf), may Allah be pleased with them, which we have chosen to pass over without mention, as they are not authentic.

Imam Ahmad also narrated here a hadith, from the narration of Hammad ibn Zayd, from Thabit, from Anas, which contains strangeness, and we have likewise left out its wording. [The hadith is in al-Musnad (3/149); the strangeness lies in the phrase "the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw his wife Zaynab and it entered him," for Mu'ammal doubted in the narration, and he had poor memory.]

Al-Bukhari also narrated part of it in abridged form, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahim narrated to us, Mu'alla ibn Mansur narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Zayd, Thabit narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik who said: "This verse: ﴿And you concealed within yourself that which Allah was to disclose﴾ was revealed concerning Zaynab bint Jahsh and Zayd ibn Harithah, may Allah be pleased with them both." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4787.]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Hashim ibn Marzuq narrated to us, Ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, who said: "'Ali ibn al-Husayn asked me what al-Hasan says about His words: ﴿And you concealed within yourself that which Allah was to disclose [and you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you should fear Him]﴾?" I mentioned it to him, and he said: "No, but Allah informed His Prophet that she would be among his wives before he married her. When Zayd came to complain to him, he said: 'Fear Allah, and keep your wife to yourself.' He said: 'I have informed you that I will marry her to you,' and [this is] 'And you concealed within yourself that which Allah was to disclose.'"

Similarly, it is narrated from al-Suddi that he said something similar.

Ibn Jarir said: Ishaq ibn Shahin narrated to me, Khalid narrated to me, from Dawud, from 'Amir, from 'Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her), that she said: "If Muhammad ﷺ had concealed anything of what was revealed to him from the Book of Allah, he would have concealed: ﴿And you concealed within yourself that which Allah was to disclose, and you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you should fear Him﴾." [Tafsir al-Tabari (22/11); its origin in the Sahih is with the wording: "Whoever tells you of three things..."]

* *

As for His words: ﴿So when Zayd had no longer any need for her, We married her to you﴾: al-Watar means need and desire. That is, when he finished with her and separated from her, We married her to you. The one who undertook her marriage was Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in the sense that He revealed to him that he should enter upon her without a guardian, without a dowry, without a contract, and without witnesses from among the people.

Imam Ahmad said: Hashim — meaning Ibn al-Qasim Abu al-Nadr — narrated to us, Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "When the waiting period of Zaynab had ended, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Zayd ibn Harithah, 'Go and mention her to me.' So he set out until he came to her while she was kneading her dough. He said: When I saw her, she became great in my heart — so much so that I could not look at her — because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had mentioned her. So I turned my back to her and walked backwards, and I said: 'O Zaynab, rejoice! The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has sent me to mention you.' She said: 'I will do nothing until I consult my Lord, Mighty and Majestic.' So she stood up to her place of prayer, and the Qur'an was revealed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and entered upon her without permission. We were given bread and meat to eat when he went in to her, so the people left, but some men remained talking in the house after the meal. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out [and I followed him] and began to go round the chambers of his wives, greeting them, and they would say: 'O Messenger of Allah, how did you find your family?' I do not know whether I told him that the people had left or whether he was informed. He went on until he entered the house, and I tried to enter with him, but he drew the curtain between me and him, and the veil was revealed, and he admonished the people with what they had been admonished: ﴿Do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless permission is given to you﴾, and the rest of the verse."

Muslim and al-Nasa'i narrated it through several chains, from Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah, with the same. [Musnad (3/195); Sahih Muslim no. 1428; Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/79).]

Al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, that Zaynab bint Jahsh used to boast over the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, saying: "Your guardians married you off, but Allah married me from above the seven heavens." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 7420.]

We have previously mentioned in "Surat al-Nur," from Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Jahsh, who said: Zaynab and 'Aishah boasted to each other. Zaynab (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "I am the one whose marriage was sent down from heaven." 'Aishah said: "I am the one whose innocence was sent down from heaven." Zaynab then acknowledged her superiority. [At verse 11.]

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from al-Mughirah, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Zaynab used to say to the Prophet ﷺ: "I take pride in you over three things, none of your wives can take pride in them: my grandfather and your grandfather are one; Allah married me to you from the heaven; and the emissary was Jibril (peace be upon him)." [Tafsir al-Tabari (22/11).]

As for His words: ﴿In order that there be no discomfort for the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they have no longer any need for them﴾: that is, We only permitted you to marry her and did that so that there would be no difficulty for the believers in marrying the divorced wives of adopted sons. The reason is that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, before prophethood, had adopted Zayd ibn Harithah, so he was called "Zayd ibn Muhammad." When Allah cut off this attribution by His saying: ﴿Nor has He made your adopted sons your sons. That is your saying from your mouths. And Allah says the truth, and He guides to the [right] way. Call them by [the names of] their fathers; it is more just in the sight of Allah﴾, He then increased this clarification and confirmation by the marriage of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to Zaynab bint Jahsh after Zayd ibn Harithah divorced her. For this reason, in the verse on prohibitions He said: ﴿And [prohibited to you are] the wives of your sons who are from your loins﴾ [An-Nisa 4:23], to exclude the adopted son, since that was common among them.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And the command of Allah is ever executed﴾: that is, this matter that occurred had been decreed and decided by Allah the Exalted, and it was bound to happen without doubt. Zaynab, in the knowledge of Allah, was going to become one of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ.

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿There is no blame upon the Prophet in what Allah has ordained for him﴾, i.e., in what He made lawful for him and commanded him to do, namely marrying Zaynab, whom his adopted son Zayd ibn Harithah had divorced.

* *

His saying: ﴿The way of Allah with those who passed on before, and the command of Allah is a decree determined﴾. i.e., this is the ruling of Allah concerning the prophets before him: He would not command them to do something while there would be any blame upon them in it. This is a refutation of those among the hypocrites who imagined a deficiency in his marrying the wife of Zayd, his freed slave and adopted son, whom he had taken as a son.

﴿And the command of Allah is a decree determined﴾, i.e., His command which He decrees is bound to happen without doubt, and an event from which there is no escape or deviation. Whatever Allah wills [[Addition from manuscript t.]] comes to be, and whatever He does not will does not come to be.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 33, verses 39–40 (part 1 of 2):

Allah praises: ﴿Those who convey the messages of Allah and fear Him, and fear none but Allah. And sufficient is Allah as Reckoner.﴾ That is, they convey them to His creation and deliver them faithfully, ﴿and fear Him﴾, meaning they fear Him and fear no one besides Him, so the might of no one prevents them from conveying the messages of Allah. ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Reckoner﴾, meaning sufficient is Allah as Helper and Supporter.

The best of mankind in this station, indeed in every station, is Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He undertook the delivery and conveyance of the message to the people of the East and the West, to all kinds of the children of Adam. Allah made His word, His religion and His law supreme over all religions and laws. Every prophet before him was sent only to his own people, but he (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) was sent to all creation, Arabs and non-Arabs alike: ﴿Say: O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all﴾ [al-A'raf: 158]. Then his community inherited the station of conveying his message after him, and the highest of those who fulfilled it after him were his Companions, may Allah be pleased with them. They conveyed from him as he had commanded them, in all his sayings, deeds and states, by night and by day, at home and while travelling, in private and in public. So may Allah be pleased with them and make them pleased. Then each later generation inherited it from its predecessors until our present time. By their light those who are guided are guided, and on their path those granted success proceed. So we ask Allah, the Generous, the Bestower, to make us among their successors.

Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, al-A'mash informed us, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "None of you should belittle himself by seeing a matter of Allah about which he has something to say and then not say it. Allah will say: 'What prevented you from speaking about it?' He will say: 'My Lord, I feared people.' He will say: 'It is I who is more deserving to be feared.'"

He also narrated it from Abd al-Razzaq, from al-Thawri, from Zubayd, from Amr ibn Murrah [al-Musnad (3/30, 73)].

Ibn Majah narrated it from Abu Kurayb, from Abdullah ibn Numayr and Abu Mu'awiya, both from al-A'mash, with the same chain [Sunan Ibn Majah no. 4008. al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/242): "This is a sound chain (isnad)."].

* *

And His saying: ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men﴾. He forbade that after this one should be called "Zayd ibn Muhammad". That is, he was not his father, even though he had adopted him. The Messenger (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) did not have a surviving son who reached puberty. He had sons from Khadijah: al-Qasim, al-Tayyib and al-Tahir, but they died young. He had a son, Ibrahim, from Maria the Copt, who also died while still nursing. He had four daughters from Khadijah: Zaynab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum and Fatimah, may Allah be pleased with them all. Three of them died during his lifetime, while Fatimah lived on until she was afflicted by his loss (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him). Then she died six months after him.

* *

And His saying: ﴿But he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets. And ever is Allah, of all things, Knowing﴾. It is like His saying: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ [al-An'am: 124]. This verse is a clear text (nass) that there is no prophet after him. If there is no prophet after him, then there is no messenger after him, by a stronger and more certain implication, because the station of messengership (risalah) is more specific than the station of prophethood (nubuwwah). Every messenger is a prophet, but not every prophet is a messenger. The mutawatir (widely transmitted) hadiths on this have come from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) through a number of the Companions.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Amir al-Azdi narrated to us, Zuhayr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil, from al-Tufayl ibn Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from his father, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "My example among the prophets is like that of a man who built a house, made it beautiful and complete, but left a place for one brick unfilled. The people went around the building, admiring it, and said: 'If only the place of this brick were completed!' So I am the place of that brick among the prophets."

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Bundar, from Abu Amir al-Aqadi, with the same chain [al-Musnad (5/136) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3613]. He said: "Hasan sahih (good and sound)."

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us, al-Mukhtar ibn Fulful narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, messengership and prophethood have ended. There is no messenger after me and no prophet." He said: That was hard on the people. He (ﷺ) said: "But there remain the good tidings (al-mubashshirat)." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what are the good tidings?" He said: "The true dream of a Muslim man, and it is a part of the parts of prophethood."

Al-Tirmidhi similarly narrated it from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Za'farani, from Affan ibn Muslim, with the same chain [al-Musnad (3/267) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2272]. He said: "Sahih gharib (sound but singular) from the hadith of al-Mukhtar ibn Fulful."

Another hadith: Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Sulaym ibn Hayyan narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Mina, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "My example and the example of the prophets is like that of a man who built a house, completed it and made it beautiful, except for the place of one brick. Whoever entered it and looked at it would say: 'How beautiful it is, except for the place of this brick!' So I am the place of the brick; the prophets were sealed with me (peace be upon them)."

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and al-Tirmidhi narrated it through several chains from Sulaym ibn Hayyan, with the same wording [Musnad al-Tayalisi no. 1785; Sahih al-Bukhari no. 3534; Sahih Muslim no. 2287; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2862]. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Sahih gharib from this route."

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "My example and the example of the prophets before me is like that of a man who built a house and completed it, except for one brick. I came and completed that brick." Muslim alone narrated it from the narration of al-A'mash, with the same chain [al-Musnad (3/9) and Sahih Muslim no. 2286].

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, Uthman ibn Ubayd al-Rasibi narrated to us, who said: I heard Abu al-Tufayl say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no prophethood after me except the good tidings." It was said: "And what are the good tidings, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The good dream, or he said: the righteous dream" [al-Musnad (5/454). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/173): "Its narrators are trustworthy (thiqat)."].

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayra narrated to us, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, my example and the example of the prophets before me is like that of a man who built houses, making them beautiful, complete and lovely, except for the place of one brick in a corner of them. So the people went around, admiring the building, and said: 'Why did you not place a brick here so that your building would be complete?'" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "So I was the brick."

Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it from the narration of Abd al-Razzaq [al-Musnad (2/312) and Sahih Muslim no. 2286. I did not find it in al-Bukhari, and al-Mizzi in Tuhfat al-Ashraf attributed it only to Muslim].

Another hadith, also from Abu Hurayra: Imam Muslim said: Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutayba and Ali ibn Hujr narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from al-Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been favoured over the prophets in six ways: I have been given jawami' al-kalim (concise, comprehensive speech); I have been supported by awe (al-ru'b); the spoils of war have been made lawful for me; the earth has been made pure and a place of prayer for me; I have been sent to all creation; and the prophets have been sealed with me."

Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Isma'il ibn Ja'far, and al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih" [Sahih Muslim no. 523; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 1553; Sunan Ibn Majah no. 567].

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "My example and the example of the prophets before me is like that of a man who built a house and completed it, except for one brick. So I came and completed that brick."

Muslim narrated it from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba and Abu Kurayb, both from Abu Mu'awiya, with the same chain [this hadith was mentioned shortly before].

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, Mu'awiya ibn Salih narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Suwayd al-Kalbi, from Abd al-A'la ibn Hilal al-Sulami, from al-Irbad ibn Sariya, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, I am, with Allah, the Seal of the Prophets, while Adam was still lying in his clay" [al-Musnad (4/127)].

Another hadith: al-Zuhri said: Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im informed me, from his father, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "I have names: I am Muhammad, I am Ahmad, I am al-Mahi (the Eraser) by whom Allah erases disbelief, I am al-Hashir (the Gatherer) at whose feet people will be gathered, and I am al-'Aqib (the Last) after whom there is no prophet." Both al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it in their Sahihs [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 3532; Sahih Muslim no. 2354].

Imam Ahmad also said: Yahya ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'a narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Hubayra, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Amr say: One day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to us as one bidding farewell, and said: "I am Muhammad, the unlettered Prophet" (three times), "and there is no prophet after me. I have been given fawatih al-kalim (opening words), jawami' (comprehensive words) and khawatim (concluding words). I have been informed of the number of the guardians of Hell and the bearers of the Throne. I have been granted indulgence, and I have been granted well-being, and my community has been granted well-being. So listen and obey as long as I am among you. When I am taken away, then hold fast to the Book of Allah: make lawful what it makes lawful and make unlawful what it makes unlawful." Imam Ahmad alone narrated it [al-Musnad (2/12). It contains Ibn Lahi'a, who is weak (da'if)].

Imam Ahmad also narrated it from Yahya ibn Ishaq, from Ibn Lahi'a, from Abdullah ibn Hubayra, from Abdullah ibn Maric (or Surayh) al-Khawlani, from Abu Qays, the freedman of Amr ibn al-As, from Abdullah ibn Amr, and mentioned the same, identically [al-Musnad (2/172). It contains Ibn Lahi'a, who is weak].

Among the reports on this subject there are many. Part of Allah's mercy to His servants is that He sent Muhammad (may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him) to them. Further, as an honour to them, He made him the seal of the prophets and messengers, and He completed the upright monotheistic religion (al-din al-hanif, the pure faith of submission to one God) through him. Allah, the Exalted, has informed us in His Book, and His Messenger has informed us in the widely transmitted (mutawatir, reported by so many chains that its transmission is certain) Sunnah, that there is no prophet after him. This is so that people will know that anyone who claims this rank after him is a liar, a great deceiver, a misguided misleader. Even if he performs feats of trickery and sleight of hand, and brings all kinds of magic, talismans and nayrajiyyat (occult and deceptive practices), all of it is false and misguidance in the sight of people of understanding (ulu al-albab).

Allah, glorified and exalted, let happen at the hands of al-Aswad al-Ansi in Yemen and Musaylima al-Kadhdhab (the Liar) in al-Yamamah such corrupt states and cold, empty sayings that every person of intellect, understanding and insight knows that both of them were liars and misguided. May Allah curse them both. The same is true of every claimant to this status until the Day of Resurrection, until the series ends with al-Masih al-Dajjal (the Antichrist). With each of these liars, Allah creates matters that cause the scholars and the believers to witness the falsehood of the one who brought them. This is part of the perfection of Allah's gentleness toward His creation, for they, by the necessity of reality, do not enjoin good or forbid evil except by coincidence, or for some other aim they have in view. They are at the utmost level of falsehood and wickedness in their words and deeds, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend? They descend upon every lying sinner﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara' 26:221–222].

This is the opposite of the prophets, peace be upon them. They are at the utmost level of righteousness, truthfulness, rectitude, steadfastness and justice in what they say and do, and in what they enjoin and forbid. They are supported with extraordinary signs that break customary patterns, with clear proofs and manifest demonstrations. So may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them, always and continuously, for as long as the earth and the heavens endure.

This is the opposite of the prophets, peace be upon them. They are at the utmost level of righteousness, truthfulness, rectitude, steadfastness and justice in what they say and do, and in what they enjoin and forbid. They are supported with extraordinary signs that break customary patterns, with clear proofs and manifest demonstrations. So may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them, always and continuously, for as long as the earth and the heavens endure.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 33, verses 41–44 (part 1 of 2):

God, exalted is He, says, commanding His believing servants to remember Him often (dhikr, remembrance of God), the One who has bestowed upon them all kinds of blessings and varieties of favours, because of the great reward and the beautiful return that they will have through it.

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us from 'Abd Allah ibn Sa'id [in A: "Sa'd"], from a client (mawla) of Ibn 'Ayyash [in A: "Abbas"], from Abu Bahriyya [in A: "from Abu 'Urwa"], from Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Shall I not inform you of the best of your deeds, the purest of them in the sight of your Sovereign, the highest of them in your ranks, and better for you than giving gold and silver, and better for you than meeting your enemy and striking their necks while they strike your necks?" They said: "What is it, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

It was also related by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, through the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Sa'id ibn Abi Hind, from Ziyad, the client of Ibn 'Ayyash [in A: "Abbas"], from Abu Bahriyya, whose name is 'Abd Allah ibn Qays al-Taraghimi, from Abu al-Darda', with the same wording. [Musnad (5/195), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3377), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3790).] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Some of them related it from him as a mursal (a report whose chain omits a companion)."

I say: This hadith has already been mentioned at the verse of His saying: ﴿and the men and women who remember Allah often﴾ in the Musnad of [Imam] [addition from A] Ahmad, through the hadith of Ziyad ibn Abi Ziyad, client of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ayyash: that it reached him from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), with something similar. And Allah knows best.

Imam Ahmad also said: Waki' narrated to us, Faraj ibn Fudala narrated to us, from Abu Sa'd al-Himsi, who said: I heard Abu Hurayra say: "A supplication I heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which I will never abandon: 'O Allah, make me greatest in thanking You, most faithful in following Your counsel, most abundant in remembering You, and most careful in preserving Your commandment.'" [Musnad (2/477).]

Al-Tirmidhi related it from Yahya ibn Musa, from Waki', from Abu Fudala al-Faraj ibn Fudala, from Abu Sa'id al-Himsi, from Abu Hurayra, and he mentioned the like of it and said: "Gharib (a hadith with a single narrator at some point in its chain)." [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3604).]

And so Imam Ahmad also related it from Abu al-Nadr Hashim ibn al-Qasim, from Faraj ibn Fudala, from Abu Sa'id al-Madani [in A: "al-Muzani"], from Abu Hurayra, and he mentioned it. [Musnad (2/311).]

Imam Ahmad also said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Mu'awiya ibn Salih, from 'Amr ibn Qays, who said: I heard 'Abd Allah ibn Busr say: Two Bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). One of them said: "O Messenger of Allah, which of the people is best?" He said: "The one whose life is long and whose deeds are good." The other said: "O Messenger of Allah, the laws of Islam have become numerous for us [in T: "upon me"], so command me with something I may hold fast to." He said: "Let your tongue remain moist with the remembrance of Allah." [Musnad (4/190).]

Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah related the second part [from it] [addition from F, A], through the hadith of Mu'awiya ibn Salih, with the same chain. [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3375), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3793).] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib."

Imam Ahmad also said: Surayj [in A: "Shurayh"] narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn al-Harith, who said: Darraj Abu al-Samh narrated to him, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Remember Allah abundantly, until they say: 'He is mad.'" [Musnad (3/68), in which there is Darraj, and Abu al-Haytham is weak.]

Al-Tabarani said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad narrated to us, 'Uqba ibn Mukram al-'Ammi narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Sufyan [in A: "Safr"] al-Jahdari narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from 'Uqba ibn Abi Thubayt [in A: "Sabab"] al-Rasibi, from Abu al-Jawza', from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Remember Allah with much remembrance [until] [addition from T, F, A, and al-Mu'jam] the hypocrites say: 'You are showing off.'" [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir of al-Tabarani (12/169); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/76): "In it is al-Husayn ibn Abi Ja'far al-Ja'fari, who is weak."]

Imam Ahmad [in A: "Zaadahu"] also said: Abu Sa'id, client of the Banu Hashim, narrated to us, Shaddad Abu Talha al-Rasibi narrated to us, I heard Abu al-Wazi' Jabir ibn 'Amr narrate from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No people sit in a gathering in which they do not remember Allah, except that it will be a regret for them on the Day of Resurrection." [Musnad (2/224); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/80): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]

'Ali ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿Remember Allah with much remembrance﴾: Allah did not prescribe for His servants any obligation except that He set for it a known limit, then He excused its people in a state of excuse, except for remembrance. For Allah has not set for it a limit at which it ends, and He has not excused anyone in abandoning it, except one who is overpowered in abandoning it. So He said: ﴿So remember Allah standing, sitting, and on your sides﴾ [al-Nisa': 103], by night and by day, on land and at sea, while travelling and at home, in wealth and in poverty, in health and in sickness, in secret and in public, and in every state. And He said: ﴿and glorify Him morning and evening﴾. So when you do that, He and His angels send blessings upon you.

The hadiths, verses and reports urging the remembrance of Allah are very numerous indeed, and in this noble verse is the urging to increase in that (al-ikthar, increasing).

People have composed works on the adhkar (litanies of remembrance) connected with the times of night and day, such as al-Nasa'i, al-Ma'muri and others [in T: "al-Ma'mari, al-Kalim al-Tayyib of Shaykh al-Islam, and others"]. Among the best books composed on this is the Kitab al-Adhkar of Shaykh Muhyi al-Din al-Nawawi, may God Most High have mercy on him. [The Kitab al-Adhkar has been published, edited by Shaykh 'Abd al-Qadir al-Arna'ut at Dar al-Huda, and there is a takhrij (sourcing) of it by Ibn 'Allan entitled "al-Futuhat al-Rabbaniyya," printed in India.]

Furthermore, what follows this paragraph in manuscript "T" is the following:

"Remembrance of Allah is the root of loyalty to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and its head. Heedlessness is the root of enmity toward Him and its head. For the servant continues to remember his Lord until he loves Him and so is loyal to Him, and he continues to be heedless of Him until he hates Him and becomes hostile to Him. Allah the Most High said: (And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance, and who follows his desire and whose affair is excess) [al-Kahf: 28].
