Nothing has drawn the blessings of Allah Most High and warded off His vengeance like the remembrance of Allah. Remembrance is the drawer of blessings and the repeller of vengeance. Allah said: (Indeed, Allah defends those who believe) [al-Hajj: 38], and in the other reading: (Defends [yudafi'u] those who believe). His repelling and defending of them is in proportion to the strength and perfection of their faith, and the material of faith and its strength come from the remembrance of Allah. So whoever is more complete in faith and more abundant in remembrance, Allah's defence of him and His repelling are greater. Whoever is deficient, his remembrance is deficient, and his forgetting is in proportion. Allah said: (And when your Lord proclaimed: If you are grateful, I will surely increase you) [Ibrahim: 7]. Remembrance is the head of gratitude, and gratitude draws blessings and necessitates increase. Some of the early Muslims said: How ugly is heedlessness of the remembrance of One who never ceases to be kind to you. The gatherings of remembrance are the gardens of Paradise, as Ibn Abi al-Dunya related from the hadith of Jabir, from 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to us and said: 'O people, graze in the gardens of Paradise.' We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what are the gardens of Paradise?' He said: 'The gatherings of remembrance.' Then he said: 'Go out in the morning and evening and remember. Whoever wishes to know his standing with Allah, let him look at Allah's standing with him, for Allah lowers the servant to the place where He has lowered him in His own self.' The gatherings of remembrance are the gatherings of the angels, as in the two Sahihs from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Allah has angels who roam the roads beyond the people's scribes, seeking the people of remembrance. When they find a group remembering Allah, they call out to one another: Come to what you seek. Then they surround them with their wings up to the lowest heaven. Their Lord asks them, and He knows best about them: What are My servants saying? They say: They glorify You, magnify You, praise You and extol You. He says: Have they seen Me? They say: No, by Allah, our Lord, they have not seen You. He says: How would it be if they saw Me? They say: If they saw You, they would be even more intense in worship, even more in praise and extolment, and more in glorification. He says: What are they asking of Me? They say: They ask You for Paradise. He says: Have they seen it? They say: No, by Allah, our Lord, they have not seen it. He says: How would it be if they saw it? They say: If they saw it, they would be even more eager for it, even more intent on it, and have even greater desire for it. He says: From what do they seek refuge? They say: From the Fire. He says: Have they seen it? They say: No, by Allah, our Lord, they have not seen it. He says: How would it be if they saw it? They say: If they saw it, they would flee from it even more and be even more fearful of it. He says: I call you to witness that I have forgiven them. One of the angels says: Among them is so-and-so, who is not one of them; he only came for a need. He says: They are a people whose companion does not become wretched." This is from their blessing upon themselves and upon their companions. For them is a share of His saying: (And He made me blessed wherever I am) [Maryam: 31]. Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, boasts of those who remember Him to the angels, as Muslim related in his Sahih from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: Mu'awiya went out to a circle in the mosque and said: What has made you sit? They said: We sat remembering Allah. He said: Did nothing but that make you sit? They said: By Allah, nothing but that made us sit. He said: As for me, I did not ask you out of suspicion of you, and no one has a lower rank of narrating from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) than I do; the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to a circle of his companions and said: 'What has made you sit?' They said: We sat remembering Allah and praising Him for guiding us to Islam and bestowing His favour upon us through you. He said: 'By Allah, did nothing but that make you sit?' They said: By Allah, nothing but that made us sit. He said: 'As for me, I did not make you swear out of suspicion of you, but Jibril came to me and informed me that Allah boasts of you to the angels.' This boasting by the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, is evidence of the honour of remembrance with Him, His love for it, and that it has a distinction over other deeds.

Remembrance is of two kinds. The first: remembering the names and attributes of the Lord, praising Him, and declaring Him free of what does not befit Him. This too is of two kinds. The first: composing praise of Him by the one remembering, and this is the kind mentioned in the hadith, such as: Subhan Allah (Glory be to Allah), al-hamdu lillah (Praise be to Allah), la ilaha illa Allah (There is no god but Allah), Allahu akbar (Allah is greatest), Subhan Allah wa bihamdih (Glory be to Allah and praise Him), la ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah, lahu al-mulk wa lahu al-hamd wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir (There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner; to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs the praise, and He is capable of all things), and the like. The most excellent of this kind is that which is most comprehensive in praise and most general, such as: Subhan Allah 'adada khalqih (Glory be to Allah as many as His creation). This is better than merely saying Subhan Allah. And saying: al-hamdu lillah 'adada ma khalaqa fi al-sama' wa 'adada ma khalaqa fi al-ard wa 'adada ma baynahuma wa 'adada ma huwa khaliq (Praise be to Allah as many as what He created in the heavens, as many as what He created in the earth, as many as what is between them, and as many as what He is yet to create) is better than merely saying al-hamdu lillah. This is in the hadith of Juwayriya, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to her: "I have said after you four words three times, which if weighed against what you have said since today, would outweigh them: Subhan Allah 'adada khalqih (Glory be to Allah as many as His creation); Subhan Allah rida nafsih (Glory be to Allah as much as His own pleasure); Subhan Allah zinat 'arshih (Glory be to Allah as much as the weight of His Throne); Subhan Allah midad kalimatih (Glory be to Allah as much as the ink of His words)." Related by Muslim. In al-Tirmidhi and Sunan Abi Dawud, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, that he entered with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) upon a woman before whom were date-pits or pebbles with which she was counting her glorification. He said: "Shall I inform you of what is easier for you than this and better?" Then he said: "Subhan Allah 'adada ma khalaqa fi al-sama' (Glory be to Allah as many as what He created in the heavens), Subhan Allah 'adada ma khalaqa fi al-ard (Glory be to Allah as many as what He created in the earth), Subhan Allah 'adada ma bayna dhalik (Glory be to Allah as many as what is between that), Subhan Allah 'adada ma huwa khaliq (Glory be to Allah as many as what He is yet to create), Allahu akbar mithl dhalik (Allah is greatest, the same as that), la ilaha illa Allah mithl dhalik (There is no god but Allah, the same as that), and la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah mithl dhalik (There is no power nor strength except with Allah, the same as that)."

The second kind: reporting about the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, through the judgments of His names and attributes, such as your saying: Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, hears the voices of His servants, sees their movements, and nothing of their deeds is hidden from Him; He is more merciful to them than their fathers and mothers; He is capable of all things; and He is more pleased with the repentance of His servant than one who finds what he had lost. And the like. The most excellent of this kind is praising Him with what He praised Himself, and with what His Messenger (ﷺ) praised Him, without distortion (tahrif) or denial (ta'til), and without likening (tashbih) or modelling (tamthil), as He said: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾ [al-Shura: 11]. This kind also has three types: praise (hamd), commendation (thana'), and glorification (majd).

Praise (hamd) is informing about Him with the attributes of His perfection together with loving Him and being pleased with Him. The silent lover is not one who praises, nor is one who commends without love a praiser, until love and commendation are combined for Him. If he repeats praises one after another, they become commendation (thana'). If the praise is with attributes of majesty, grandeur, magnificence and sovereignty, it is glorification (majd). Allah Most High has combined all three types for His servant in the opening chapter, Surat al-Fatiha. When the servant says: ﴿Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, Allah says: "My servant has praised Me." When he says: ﴿The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾, He says: "My servant has commended Me." When he says: ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾, He says: "My servant has glorified Me."

The second kind of remembrance: remembering His command, His prohibition and His rulings. This too is of two kinds. The first: remembering Him through that by informing about Him, that He has commanded such and such, forbidden such and such, loves such and such and is displeased with such and such. The second: remembering Him at His command, so that one hastens to it, and at His prohibition, so that one flees from it. Remembering His command and prohibition is one thing, and remembering Him at His command and prohibition is another. When these kinds are combined in the one who remembers, his remembrance is the most excellent, most sublime and greatest of remembrance.

Benefit:

This, then, is the greatest understanding (al-fiqh al-akbar), and whatever is below it is among the best forms of remembrance when the intention in it is sound. Remembering Him, may He be exalted, also includes remembering His favours, His bounty, His kindness, His blessings, and the places of His grace upon His servants. This is among the most excellent kinds of remembrance. These are five kinds, and they can be done with the heart and with the tongue. The remembrance of the heart alone is better than the remembrance of the tongue, because remembrance of the heart produces knowledge (ma'rifah), makes love (mahabbah) sound, stirs up modesty (haya'), inspires awe (makhafah), calls to self-watchfulness (muraqabah), and restrains one from falling short in obedience and from being careless about sins and misdeeds. Remembrance of the tongue alone does not necessarily bring about any of these fruits, and even if it brings about some of them, its fruit is weak.

Remembrance is also better than supplication (du'a'), because remembrance is praise of Allah, mighty and majestic, for His beautiful attributes, blessings and names, whereas supplication is the servant asking for his need. How can the one be compared with the other? For this reason a hadith says: "Whoever is preoccupied with remembering Me instead of asking Me, I will give him better than what I give those who ask." For this reason it is recommended in supplication that the one supplicating begin by praising Allah and extolling Him before stating his need, and then ask for what he needs. This is as in the hadith of Fadalah ibn 'Ubayd, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard a man supplicating in his prayer without praising Allah and without sending blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This man has been hasty." Then he called him, or someone else, and said: "When one of you prays, let him begin by glorifying his Lord and extolling Him, then let him send blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ), and then let him supplicate with whatever he wishes." Related by Imam Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi, who said: "Hasan sahih (good and authentic)."

Likewise did Dhu al-Nun supplicate, concerning whom the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The supplication of my brother Dhu al-Nun, whenever a distressed person supplicates with it, Allah relieves his distress: 'There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been among the wrongdoers.'" In al-Tirmidhi: "The supplication of my brother Dhu al-Nun, when he supplicated with it in the belly of the fish: 'There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been among the wrongdoers.' No Muslim supplicates with it for anything at all except that Allah responds to him." Likewise are most of the Prophetic supplications, including the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) in the supplication for distress: "There is no god but..."

His saying: ﴿And glorify Him morning and evening﴾, i.e., at the time of morning and evening, like His saying: ﴿So glorify Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning, and to Him belongs praise in the heavens and the earth, and at night and when you are at noon﴾ [al-Rum: 17-18].

* *

His saying: ﴿It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels﴾: this is an incitement to remembrance, meaning: He, glory be to Him, remembers you, so you remember Him, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Just as We have sent among you a messenger from yourselves, reciting to you Our verses and purifying you and teaching you the Book and wisdom and teaching you what you did not know. So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me﴾ [al-Baqarah: 151-152]. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allah says: Whoever remembers Me in himself, I remember him in Myself; and whoever remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a gathering better than theirs." [Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 7405, and Muslim in his Sahih, no. 2675, from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.]

The blessing (salah) from Allah is His praise of the servant in the presence of the angels. Al-Bukhari related this from Abu al-'Aliyah. Abu Ja'far al-Razi related it from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from him.

Others said: the blessing from Allah is mercy. [It is refuted by His saying: ﴿Upon those are blessings from their Lord and mercy﴾.]

It may be said: there is no contradiction between the two statements, and Allah knows best.

As for the blessing from the angels, it means supplication for the people and seeking forgiveness for them, as in His saying: ﴿Those who carry the Throne and those around it glorify their Lord with praise and believe in Him and seek forgiveness for those who believe: "Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who repent and follow Your way and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire. Our Lord, and admit them to gardens of perpetual residence which You have promised them, and whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their descendants. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise. And protect them from evils﴾ [Ghafir: 7-9], the verse.

* *

His saying: ﴿to bring you out of darknesses into light﴾: i.e., because of His mercy towards you, His praise of you, and the supplication of His angels for you, He brings you out of the darknesses of ignorance and misguidance into the light of guidance and certainty. ﴿And He is ever merciful to the believers﴾: i.e., in this world and in the Hereafter. As for His mercy in this world: He guided them to the truth which others were ignorant of, and showed them the path from which those who called to disbelief or innovation, and their followers from the rabble (al-tighaam), had strayed and turned away. As for His mercy to them in the Hereafter: He grants them security from the greatest terror, and commands His angels to receive them with the good news of success in Paradise and deliverance from the Fire. This is only because of His love for them and His tenderness towards them.

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Adiy narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by with a group of his companions, and there was a child in the road. When the child's mother saw the people, she feared for her child that he would be trampled, so she came hurrying and saying: "My son, my son!" She hurried and took him. The people said: "O Messenger of Allah, this woman would never throw her son into the Fire." He said: So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) lowered them (his voice to them), and said: "No, by Allah, Allah does not throw His beloved into the Fire."

Its chain is according to the conditions of the two Sahihs, but none of the authors of the six books (al-kutub al-sittah) related it. However, in the Sahih of Imam al-Bukhari, from the commander of the believers 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw a woman from among the captives who had taken a child of hers, pressed it to her chest and nursed it. He said: "Do you think this woman would throw her child into the Fire while she is able to avoid that?" They said: "No." He said: "By Allah, Allah is more merciful to His servants than this woman is to her child." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5999.]

* *

His saying: ﴿Their greeting on the Day they meet Him will be, "Peace"﴾. The apparent meaning, and Allah knows best, is: ﴿Their greeting﴾, i.e., from Allah, exalted is He, on the Day they meet Him will be ﴿peace﴾, i.e., the Day on which He greets them with peace, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿"Peace," a word from a Lord, Most Merciful﴾ [Ya-Sin: 58].

Qatadah claimed that what is meant is that they greet one another with peace, on the Day they meet Allah in the Hereafter. Ibn Jarir chose this view.

I say: It may be supported by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Their call therein is, "Glory be to You, O Allah," and their greeting therein is, "Peace," and the last of their call is, "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds"﴾ [Yunus: 10], and His saying: ﴿And He has prepared for them a noble reward﴾, meaning: Paradise and what is in it of food and drink, clothing and dwellings, spouses and pleasures, sights that no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and that has not occurred to the heart of any human being.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 33, verses 41–44 (part 1 of 2):

God, exalted is He, says, commanding His believing servants to remember Him often (dhikr, remembrance of God), the One who has bestowed upon them all kinds of blessings and varieties of favours, because of the great reward and the beautiful return that they will have through it.

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us from 'Abd Allah ibn Sa'id [in A: "Sa'd"], from a client (mawla) of Ibn 'Ayyash [in A: "Abbas"], from Abu Bahriyya [in A: "from Abu 'Urwa"], from Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Shall I not inform you of the best of your deeds, the purest of them in the sight of your Sovereign, the highest of them in your ranks, and better for you than giving gold and silver, and better for you than meeting your enemy and striking their necks while they strike your necks?" They said: "What is it, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

It was also related by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, through the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Sa'id ibn Abi Hind, from Ziyad, the client of Ibn 'Ayyash [in A: "Abbas"], from Abu Bahriyya, whose name is 'Abd Allah ibn Qays al-Taraghimi, from Abu al-Darda', with the same wording. [Musnad (5/195), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3377), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3790).] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Some of them related it from him as a mursal (a report whose chain omits a companion)."

I say: This hadith has already been mentioned at the verse of His saying: ﴿and the men and women who remember Allah often﴾ in the Musnad of [Imam] [addition from A] Ahmad, through the hadith of Ziyad ibn Abi Ziyad, client of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ayyash: that it reached him from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), with something similar. And Allah knows best.

Imam Ahmad also said: Waki' narrated to us, Faraj ibn Fudala narrated to us, from Abu Sa'd al-Himsi, who said: I heard Abu Hurayra say: "A supplication I heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which I will never abandon: 'O Allah, make me greatest in thanking You, most faithful in following Your counsel, most abundant in remembering You, and most careful in preserving Your commandment.'" [Musnad (2/477).]

Al-Tirmidhi related it from Yahya ibn Musa, from Waki', from Abu Fudala al-Faraj ibn Fudala, from Abu Sa'id al-Himsi, from Abu Hurayra, and he mentioned the like of it and said: "Gharib (a hadith with a single narrator at some point in its chain)." [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3604).]

And so Imam Ahmad also related it from Abu al-Nadr Hashim ibn al-Qasim, from Faraj ibn Fudala, from Abu Sa'id al-Madani [in A: "al-Muzani"], from Abu Hurayra, and he mentioned it. [Musnad (2/311).]

Imam Ahmad also said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Mu'awiya ibn Salih, from 'Amr ibn Qays, who said: I heard 'Abd Allah ibn Busr say: Two Bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). One of them said: "O Messenger of Allah, which of the people is best?" He said: "The one whose life is long and whose deeds are good." The other said: "O Messenger of Allah, the laws of Islam have become numerous for us [in T: "upon me"], so command me with something I may hold fast to." He said: "Let your tongue remain moist with the remembrance of Allah." [Musnad (4/190).]

Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah related the second part [from it] [addition from F, A], through the hadith of Mu'awiya ibn Salih, with the same chain. [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3375), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3793).] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib."

Imam Ahmad also said: Surayj [in A: "Shurayh"] narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn al-Harith, who said: Darraj Abu al-Samh narrated to him, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Remember Allah abundantly, until they say: 'He is mad.'" [Musnad (3/68), in which there is Darraj, and Abu al-Haytham is weak.]

Al-Tabarani said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad narrated to us, 'Uqba ibn Mukram al-'Ammi narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Sufyan [in A: "Safr"] al-Jahdari narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from 'Uqba ibn Abi Thubayt [in A: "Sabab"] al-Rasibi, from Abu al-Jawza', from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Remember Allah with much remembrance [until] [addition from T, F, A, and al-Mu'jam] the hypocrites say: 'You are showing off.'" [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir of al-Tabarani (12/169); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/76): "In it is al-Husayn ibn Abi Ja'far al-Ja'fari, who is weak."]

Imam Ahmad [in A: "Zaadahu"] also said: Abu Sa'id, client of the Banu Hashim, narrated to us, Shaddad Abu Talha al-Rasibi narrated to us, I heard Abu al-Wazi' Jabir ibn 'Amr narrate from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No people sit in a gathering in which they do not remember Allah, except that it will be a regret for them on the Day of Resurrection." [Musnad (2/224); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/80): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]

'Ali ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿Remember Allah with much remembrance﴾: Allah did not prescribe for His servants any obligation except that He set for it a known limit, then He excused its people in a state of excuse, except for remembrance. For Allah has not set for it a limit at which it ends, and He has not excused anyone in abandoning it, except one who is overpowered in abandoning it. So He said: ﴿So remember Allah standing, sitting, and on your sides﴾ [al-Nisa': 103], by night and by day, on land and at sea, while travelling and at home, in wealth and in poverty, in health and in sickness, in secret and in public, and in every state. And He said: ﴿and glorify Him morning and evening﴾. So when you do that, He and His angels send blessings upon you.

The hadiths, verses and reports urging the remembrance of Allah are very numerous indeed, and in this noble verse is the urging to increase in that (al-ikthar, increasing).

People have composed works on the adhkar (litanies of remembrance) connected with the times of night and day, such as al-Nasa'i, al-Ma'muri and others [in T: "al-Ma'mari, al-Kalim al-Tayyib of Shaykh al-Islam, and others"]. Among the best books composed on this is the Kitab al-Adhkar of Shaykh Muhyi al-Din al-Nawawi, may God Most High have mercy on him. [The Kitab al-Adhkar has been published, edited by Shaykh 'Abd al-Qadir al-Arna'ut at Dar al-Huda, and there is a takhrij (sourcing) of it by Ibn 'Allan entitled "al-Futuhat al-Rabbaniyya," printed in India.]

Furthermore, what follows this paragraph in manuscript "T" is the following:

"Remembrance of Allah is the root of loyalty to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and its head. Heedlessness is the root of enmity toward Him and its head. For the servant continues to remember his Lord until he loves Him and so is loyal to Him, and he continues to be heedless of Him until he hates Him and becomes hostile to Him. Allah the Most High said: (And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance, and who follows his desire and whose affair is excess) [al-Kahf: 28]. Nothing has drawn the blessings of Allah Most High and warded off His vengeance like the remembrance of Allah. Remembrance is the drawer of blessings and the repeller of vengeance. Allah said: (Indeed, Allah defends those who believe) [al-Hajj: 38], and in the other reading: (Defends [yudafi'u] those who believe). His repelling and defending of them is in proportion to the strength and perfection of their faith, and the material of faith and its strength come from the remembrance of Allah. So whoever is more complete in faith and more abundant in remembrance, Allah's defence of him and His repelling are greater. Whoever is deficient, his remembrance is deficient, and his forgetting is in proportion. Allah said: (And when your Lord proclaimed: If you are grateful, I will surely increase you) [Ibrahim: 7]. Remembrance is the head of gratitude, and gratitude draws blessings and necessitates increase. Some of the early Muslims said: How ugly is heedlessness of the remembrance of One who never ceases to be kind to you. The gatherings of remembrance are the gardens of Paradise, as Ibn Abi al-Dunya related from the hadith of Jabir, from 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to us and said: 'O people, graze in the gardens of Paradise.' We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what are the gardens of Paradise?' He said: 'The gatherings of remembrance.' Then he said: 'Go out in the morning and evening and remember. Whoever wishes to know his standing with Allah, let him look at Allah's standing with him, for Allah lowers the servant to the place where He has lowered him in His own self.' The gatherings of remembrance are the gatherings of the angels, as in the two Sahihs from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Allah has angels who roam the roads beyond the people's scribes, seeking the people of remembrance. When they find a group remembering Allah, they call out to one another: Come to what you seek. Then they surround them with their wings up to the lowest heaven. Their Lord asks them, and He knows best about them: What are My servants saying? They say: They glorify You, magnify You, praise You and extol You. He says: Have they seen Me? They say: No, by Allah, our Lord, they have not seen You. He says: How would it be if they saw Me? They say: If they saw You, they would be even more intense in worship, even more in praise and extolment, and more in glorification. He says: What are they asking of Me? They say: They ask You for Paradise. He says: Have they seen it? They say: No, by Allah, our Lord, they have not seen it. He says: How would it be if they saw it? They say: If they saw it, they would be even more eager for it, even more intent on it, and have even greater desire for it. He says: From what do they seek refuge? They say: From the Fire. He says: Have they seen it? They say: No, by Allah, our Lord, they have not seen it. He says: How would it be if they saw it? They say: If they saw it, they would flee from it even more and be even more fearful of it. He says: I call you to witness that I have forgiven them. One of the angels says: Among them is so-and-so, who is not one of them; he only came for a need. He says: They are a people whose companion does not become wretched." This is from their blessing upon themselves and upon their companions. For them is a share of His saying: (And He made me blessed wherever I am) [Maryam: 31]. Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, boasts of those who remember Him to the angels, as Muslim related in his Sahih from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: Mu'awiya went out to a circle in the mosque and said: What has made you sit? They said: We sat remembering Allah. He said: Did nothing but that make you sit? They said: By Allah, nothing but that made us sit. He said: As for me, I did not ask you out of suspicion of you, and no one has a lower rank of narrating from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) than I do; the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to a circle of his companions and said: 'What has made you sit?' They said: We sat remembering Allah and praising Him for guiding us to Islam and bestowing His favour upon us through you. He said: 'By Allah, did nothing but that make you sit?' They said: By Allah, nothing but that made us sit. He said: 'As for me, I did not make you swear out of suspicion of you, but Jibril came to me and informed me that Allah boasts of you to the angels.' This boasting by the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, is evidence of the honour of remembrance with Him, His love for it, and that it has a distinction over other deeds.

Remembrance is of two kinds. The first: remembering the names and attributes of the Lord, praising Him, and declaring Him free of what does not befit Him. This too is of two kinds. The first: composing praise of Him by the one remembering, and this is the kind mentioned in the hadith, such as: Subhan Allah (Glory be to Allah), al-hamdu lillah (Praise be to Allah), la ilaha illa Allah (There is no god but Allah), Allahu akbar (Allah is greatest), Subhan Allah wa bihamdih (Glory be to Allah and praise Him), la ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah, lahu al-mulk wa lahu al-hamd wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir (There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner; to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs the praise, and He is capable of all things), and the like. The most excellent of this kind is that which is most comprehensive in praise and most general, such as: Subhan Allah 'adada khalqih (Glory be to Allah as many as His creation). This is better than merely saying Subhan Allah. And saying: al-hamdu lillah 'adada ma khalaqa fi al-sama' wa 'adada ma khalaqa fi al-ard wa 'adada ma baynahuma wa 'adada ma huwa khaliq (Praise be to Allah as many as what He created in the heavens, as many as what He created in the earth, as many as what is between them, and as many as what He is yet to create) is better than merely saying al-hamdu lillah. This is in the hadith of Juwayriya, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to her: "I have said after you four words three times, which if weighed against what you have said since today, would outweigh them: Subhan Allah 'adada khalqih (Glory be to Allah as many as His creation); Subhan Allah rida nafsih (Glory be to Allah as much as His own pleasure); Subhan Allah zinat 'arshih (Glory be to Allah as much as the weight of His Throne); Subhan Allah midad kalimatih (Glory be to Allah as much as the ink of His words)." Related by Muslim. In al-Tirmidhi and Sunan Abi Dawud, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, that he entered with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) upon a woman before whom were date-pits or pebbles with which she was counting her glorification. He said: "Shall I inform you of what is easier for you than this and better?" Then he said: "Subhan Allah 'adada ma khalaqa fi al-sama' (Glory be to Allah as many as what He created in the heavens), Subhan Allah 'adada ma khalaqa fi al-ard (Glory be to Allah as many as what He created in the earth), Subhan Allah 'adada ma bayna dhalik (Glory be to Allah as many as what is between that), Subhan Allah 'adada ma huwa khaliq (Glory be to Allah as many as what He is yet to create), Allahu akbar mithl dhalik (Allah is greatest, the same as that), la ilaha illa Allah mithl dhalik (There is no god but Allah, the same as that), and la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah mithl dhalik (There is no power nor strength except with Allah, the same as that)."

The second kind: reporting about the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, through the judgments of His names and attributes, such as your saying: Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, hears the voices of His servants, sees their movements, and nothing of their deeds is hidden from Him; He is more merciful to them than their fathers and mothers; He is capable of all things; and He is more pleased with the repentance of His servant than one who finds what he had lost. And the like. The most excellent of this kind is praising Him with what He praised Himself, and with what His Messenger (ﷺ) praised Him, without distortion (tahrif) or denial (ta'til), and without likening (tashbih) or modelling (tamthil), as He said: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾ [al-Shura: 11]. This kind also has three types: praise (hamd), commendation (thana'), and glorification (majd).

Praise (hamd) is informing about Him with the attributes of His perfection together with loving Him and being pleased with Him. The silent lover is not one who praises, nor is one who commends without love a praiser, until love and commendation are combined for Him. If he repeats praises one after another, they become commendation (thana'). If the praise is with attributes of majesty, grandeur, magnificence and sovereignty, it is glorification (majd). Allah Most High has combined all three types for His servant in the opening chapter, Surat al-Fatiha. When the servant says: ﴿Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, Allah says: "My servant has praised Me." When he says: ﴿The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾, He says: "My servant has commended Me." When he says: ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾, He says: "My servant has glorified Me."

The second kind of remembrance: remembering His command, His prohibition and His rulings. This too is of two kinds. The first: remembering Him through that by informing about Him, that He has commanded such and such, forbidden such and such, loves such and such and is displeased with such and such. The second: remembering Him at His command, so that one hastens to it, and at His prohibition, so that one flees from it. Remembering His command and prohibition is one thing, and remembering Him at His command and prohibition is another. When these kinds are combined in the one who remembers, his remembrance is the most excellent, most sublime and greatest of remembrance.

Benefit:

This, then, is the greatest understanding (al-fiqh al-akbar), and whatever is below it is among the best forms of remembrance when the intention in it is sound. Remembering Him, may He be exalted, also includes remembering His favours, His bounty, His kindness, His blessings, and the places of His grace upon His servants. This is among the most excellent kinds of remembrance. These are five kinds, and they can be done with the heart and with the tongue. The remembrance of the heart alone is better than the remembrance of the tongue, because remembrance of the heart produces knowledge (ma'rifah), makes love (mahabbah) sound, stirs up modesty (haya'), inspires awe (makhafah), calls to self-watchfulness (muraqabah), and restrains one from falling short in obedience and from being careless about sins and misdeeds. Remembrance of the tongue alone does not necessarily bring about any of these fruits, and even if it brings about some of them, its fruit is weak.

Remembrance is also better than supplication (du'a'), because remembrance is praise of Allah, mighty and majestic, for His beautiful attributes, blessings and names, whereas supplication is the servant asking for his need. How can the one be compared with the other? For this reason a hadith says: "Whoever is preoccupied with remembering Me instead of asking Me, I will give him better than what I give those who ask." For this reason it is recommended in supplication that the one supplicating begin by praising Allah and extolling Him before stating his need, and then ask for what he needs. This is as in the hadith of Fadalah ibn 'Ubayd, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard a man supplicating in his prayer without praising Allah and without sending blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This man has been hasty." Then he called him, or someone else, and said: "When one of you prays, let him begin by glorifying his Lord and extolling Him, then let him send blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ), and then let him supplicate with whatever he wishes." Related by Imam Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi, who said: "Hasan sahih (good and authentic)."

Likewise did Dhu al-Nun supplicate, concerning whom the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The supplication of my brother Dhu al-Nun, whenever a distressed person supplicates with it, Allah relieves his distress: 'There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been among the wrongdoers.'" In al-Tirmidhi: "The supplication of my brother Dhu al-Nun, when he supplicated with it in the belly of the fish: 'There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been among the wrongdoers.' No Muslim supplicates with it for anything at all except that Allah responds to him." Likewise are most of the Prophetic supplications, including the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) in the supplication for distress: "There is no god but..."

His saying: ﴿And glorify Him morning and evening﴾, i.e., at the time of morning and evening, like His saying: ﴿So glorify Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning, and to Him belongs praise in the heavens and the earth, and at night and when you are at noon﴾ [al-Rum: 17-18].

* *

His saying: ﴿It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels﴾: this is an incitement to remembrance, meaning: He, glory be to Him, remembers you, so you remember Him, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Just as We have sent among you a messenger from yourselves, reciting to you Our verses and purifying you and teaching you the Book and wisdom and teaching you what you did not know. So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me﴾ [al-Baqarah: 151-152]. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allah says: Whoever remembers Me in himself, I remember him in Myself; and whoever remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a gathering better than theirs." [Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 7405, and Muslim in his Sahih, no. 2675, from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.]

The blessing (salah) from Allah is His praise of the servant in the presence of the angels. Al-Bukhari related this from Abu al-'Aliyah. Abu Ja'far al-Razi related it from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from him.

Others said: the blessing from Allah is mercy. [It is refuted by His saying: ﴿Upon those are blessings from their Lord and mercy﴾.]

It may be said: there is no contradiction between the two statements, and Allah knows best.

As for the blessing from the angels, it means supplication for the people and seeking forgiveness for them, as in His saying: ﴿Those who carry the Throne and those around it glorify their Lord with praise and believe in Him and seek forgiveness for those who believe: "Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who repent and follow Your way and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire. Our Lord, and admit them to gardens of perpetual residence which You have promised them, and whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their descendants. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise. And protect them from evils﴾ [Ghafir: 7-9], the verse.

* *

His saying: ﴿to bring you out of darknesses into light﴾: i.e., because of His mercy towards you, His praise of you, and the supplication of His angels for you, He brings you out of the darknesses of ignorance and misguidance into the light of guidance and certainty. ﴿And He is ever merciful to the believers﴾: i.e., in this world and in the Hereafter. As for His mercy in this world: He guided them to the truth which others were ignorant of, and showed them the path from which those who called to disbelief or innovation, and their followers from the rabble (al-tighaam), had strayed and turned away. As for His mercy to them in the Hereafter: He grants them security from the greatest terror, and commands His angels to receive them with the good news of success in Paradise and deliverance from the Fire. This is only because of His love for them and His tenderness towards them.

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Adiy narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by with a group of his companions, and there was a child in the road. When the child's mother saw the people, she feared for her child that he would be trampled, so she came hurrying and saying: "My son, my son!" She hurried and took him. The people said: "O Messenger of Allah, this woman would never throw her son into the Fire." He said: So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) lowered them (his voice to them), and said: "No, by Allah, Allah does not throw His beloved into the Fire."

Its chain is according to the conditions of the two Sahihs, but none of the authors of the six books (al-kutub al-sittah) related it. However, in the Sahih of Imam al-Bukhari, from the commander of the believers 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw a woman from among the captives who had taken a child of hers, pressed it to her chest and nursed it. He said: "Do you think this woman would throw her child into the Fire while she is able to avoid that?" They said: "No." He said: "By Allah, Allah is more merciful to His servants than this woman is to her child." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5999.]

* *

His saying: ﴿Their greeting on the Day they meet Him will be, "Peace"﴾. The apparent meaning, and Allah knows best, is: ﴿Their greeting﴾, i.e., from Allah, exalted is He, on the Day they meet Him will be ﴿peace﴾, i.e., the Day on which He greets them with peace, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿"Peace," a word from a Lord, Most Merciful﴾ [Ya-Sin: 58].

Qatadah claimed that what is meant is that they greet one another with peace, on the Day they meet Allah in the Hereafter. Ibn Jarir chose this view.

I say: It may be supported by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Their call therein is, "Glory be to You, O Allah," and their greeting therein is, "Peace," and the last of their call is, "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds"﴾ [Yunus: 10], and His saying: ﴿And He has prepared for them a noble reward﴾, meaning: Paradise and what is in it of food and drink, clothing and dwellings, spouses and pleasures, sights that no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and that has not occurred to the heart of any human being.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 33, verses 41–44 (part 1 of 2):

God, exalted is He, says, commanding His believing servants to remember Him often (dhikr, remembrance of God), the One who has bestowed upon them all kinds of blessings and varieties of favours, because of the great reward and the beautiful return that they will have through it.

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us from 'Abd Allah ibn Sa'id [in A: "Sa'd"], from a client (mawla) of Ibn 'Ayyash [in A: "Abbas"], from Abu Bahriyya [in A: "from Abu 'Urwa"], from Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Shall I not inform you of the best of your deeds, the purest of them in the sight of your Sovereign, the highest of them in your ranks, and better for you than giving gold and silver, and better for you than meeting your enemy and striking their necks while they strike your necks?" They said: "What is it, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

It was also related by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, through the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Sa'id ibn Abi Hind, from Ziyad, the client of Ibn 'Ayyash [in A: "Abbas"], from Abu Bahriyya, whose name is 'Abd Allah ibn Qays al-Taraghimi, from Abu al-Darda', with the same wording. [Musnad (5/195), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3377), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3790).] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Some of them related it from him as a mursal (a report whose chain omits a companion)."

I say: This hadith has already been mentioned at the verse of His saying: ﴿and the men and women who remember Allah often﴾ in the Musnad of [Imam] [addition from A] Ahmad, through the hadith of Ziyad ibn Abi Ziyad, client of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ayyash: that it reached him from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), with something similar. And Allah knows best.

Imam Ahmad also said: Waki' narrated to us, Faraj ibn Fudala narrated to us, from Abu Sa'd al-Himsi, who said: I heard Abu Hurayra say: "A supplication I heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which I will never abandon: 'O Allah, make me greatest in thanking You, most faithful in following Your counsel, most abundant in remembering You, and most careful in preserving Your commandment.'" [Musnad (2/477).]

Al-Tirmidhi related it from Yahya ibn Musa, from Waki', from Abu Fudala al-Faraj ibn Fudala, from Abu Sa'id al-Himsi, from Abu Hurayra, and he mentioned the like of it and said: "Gharib (a hadith with a single narrator at some point in its chain)." [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3604).]

And so Imam Ahmad also related it from Abu al-Nadr Hashim ibn al-Qasim, from Faraj ibn Fudala, from Abu Sa'id al-Madani [in A: "al-Muzani"], from Abu Hurayra, and he mentioned it. [Musnad (2/311).]

Imam Ahmad also said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Mu'awiya ibn Salih, from 'Amr ibn Qays, who said: I heard 'Abd Allah ibn Busr say: Two Bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). One of them said: "O Messenger of Allah, which of the people is best?" He said: "The one whose life is long and whose deeds are good." The other said: "O Messenger of Allah, the laws of Islam have become numerous for us [in T: "upon me"], so command me with something I may hold fast to." He said: "Let your tongue remain moist with the remembrance of Allah." [Musnad (4/190).]

Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah related the second part [from it] [addition from F, A], through the hadith of Mu'awiya ibn Salih, with the same chain. [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3375), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3793).] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib."

Imam Ahmad also said: Surayj [in A: "Shurayh"] narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn al-Harith, who said: Darraj Abu al-Samh narrated to him, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Remember Allah abundantly, until they say: 'He is mad.'" [Musnad (3/68), in which there is Darraj, and Abu al-Haytham is weak.]

Al-Tabarani said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad narrated to us, 'Uqba ibn Mukram al-'Ammi narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Sufyan [in A: "Safr"] al-Jahdari narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from 'Uqba ibn Abi Thubayt [in A: "Sabab"] al-Rasibi, from Abu al-Jawza', from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Remember Allah with much remembrance [until] [addition from T, F, A, and al-Mu'jam] the hypocrites say: 'You are showing off.'" [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir of al-Tabarani (12/169); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/76): "In it is al-Husayn ibn Abi Ja'far al-Ja'fari, who is weak."]

Imam Ahmad [in A: "Zaadahu"] also said: Abu Sa'id, client of the Banu Hashim, narrated to us, Shaddad Abu Talha al-Rasibi narrated to us, I heard Abu al-Wazi' Jabir ibn 'Amr narrate from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No people sit in a gathering in which they do not remember Allah, except that it will be a regret for them on the Day of Resurrection." [Musnad (2/224); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/80): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]

'Ali ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿Remember Allah with much remembrance﴾: Allah did not prescribe for His servants any obligation except that He set for it a known limit, then He excused its people in a state of excuse, except for remembrance. For Allah has not set for it a limit at which it ends, and He has not excused anyone in abandoning it, except one who is overpowered in abandoning it. So He said: ﴿So remember Allah standing, sitting, and on your sides﴾ [al-Nisa': 103], by night and by day, on land and at sea, while travelling and at home, in wealth and in poverty, in health and in sickness, in secret and in public, and in every state. And He said: ﴿and glorify Him morning and evening﴾. So when you do that, He and His angels send blessings upon you.

The hadiths, verses and reports urging the remembrance of Allah are very numerous indeed, and in this noble verse is the urging to increase in that (al-ikthar, increasing).

People have composed works on the adhkar (litanies of remembrance) connected with the times of night and day, such as al-Nasa'i, al-Ma'muri and others [in T: "al-Ma'mari, al-Kalim al-Tayyib of Shaykh al-Islam, and others"]. Among the best books composed on this is the Kitab al-Adhkar of Shaykh Muhyi al-Din al-Nawawi, may God Most High have mercy on him. [The Kitab al-Adhkar has been published, edited by Shaykh 'Abd al-Qadir al-Arna'ut at Dar al-Huda, and there is a takhrij (sourcing) of it by Ibn 'Allan entitled "al-Futuhat al-Rabbaniyya," printed in India.]

Furthermore, what follows this paragraph in manuscript "T" is the following:

"Remembrance of Allah is the root of loyalty to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and its head. Heedlessness is the root of enmity toward Him and its head. For the servant continues to remember his Lord until he loves Him and so is loyal to Him, and he continues to be heedless of Him until he hates Him and becomes hostile to Him. Allah the Most High said: (And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance, and who follows his desire and whose affair is excess) [al-Kahf: 28]. Nothing has drawn the blessings of Allah Most High and warded off His vengeance like the remembrance of Allah. Remembrance is the drawer of blessings and the repeller of vengeance. Allah said: (Indeed, Allah defends those who believe) [al-Hajj: 38], and in the other reading: (Defends [yudafi'u] those who believe). His repelling and defending of them is in proportion to the strength and perfection of their faith, and the material of faith and its strength come from the remembrance of Allah. So whoever is more complete in faith and more abundant in remembrance, Allah's defence of him and His repelling are greater. Whoever is deficient, his remembrance is deficient, and his forgetting is in proportion. Allah said: (And when your Lord proclaimed: If you are grateful, I will surely increase you) [Ibrahim: 7]. Remembrance is the head of gratitude, and gratitude draws blessings and necessitates increase. Some of the early Muslims said: How ugly is heedlessness of the remembrance of One who never ceases to be kind to you. The gatherings of remembrance are the gardens of Paradise, as Ibn Abi al-Dunya related from the hadith of Jabir, from 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to us and said: 'O people, graze in the gardens of Paradise.' We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what are the gardens of Paradise?' He said: 'The gatherings of remembrance.' Then he said: 'Go out in the morning and evening and remember. Whoever wishes to know his standing with Allah, let him look at Allah's standing with him, for Allah lowers the servant to the place where He has lowered him in His own self.' The gatherings of remembrance are the gatherings of the angels, as in the two Sahihs from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Allah has angels who roam the roads beyond the people's scribes, seeking the people of remembrance. When they find a group remembering Allah, they call out to one another: Come to what you seek. Then they surround them with their wings up to the lowest heaven. Their Lord asks them, and He knows best about them: What are My servants saying? They say: They glorify You, magnify You, praise You and extol You. He says: Have they seen Me? They say: No, by Allah, our Lord, they have not seen You. He says: How would it be if they saw Me? They say: If they saw You, they would be even more intense in worship, even more in praise and extolment, and more in glorification. He says: What are they asking of Me? They say: They ask You for Paradise. He says: Have they seen it? They say: No, by Allah, our Lord, they have not seen it. He says: How would it be if they saw it? They say: If they saw it, they would be even more eager for it, even more intent on it, and have even greater desire for it. He says: From what do they seek refuge? They say: From the Fire. He says: Have they seen it? They say: No, by Allah, our Lord, they have not seen it. He says: How would it be if they saw it? They say: If they saw it, they would flee from it even more and be even more fearful of it. He says: I call you to witness that I have forgiven them. One of the angels says: Among them is so-and-so, who is not one of them; he only came for a need. He says: They are a people whose companion does not become wretched." This is from their blessing upon themselves and upon their companions. For them is a share of His saying: (And He made me blessed wherever I am) [Maryam: 31]. Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, boasts of those who remember Him to the angels, as Muslim related in his Sahih from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: Mu'awiya went out to a circle in the mosque and said: What has made you sit? They said: We sat remembering Allah. He said: Did nothing but that make you sit? They said: By Allah, nothing but that made us sit. He said: As for me, I did not ask you out of suspicion of you, and no one has a lower rank of narrating from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) than I do; the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to a circle of his companions and said: 'What has made you sit?' They said: We sat remembering Allah and praising Him for guiding us to Islam and bestowing His favour upon us through you. He said: 'By Allah, did nothing but that make you sit?' They said: By Allah, nothing but that made us sit. He said: 'As for me, I did not make you swear out of suspicion of you, but Jibril came to me and informed me that Allah boasts of you to the angels.' This boasting by the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, is evidence of the honour of remembrance with Him, His love for it, and that it has a distinction over other deeds.

Remembrance is of two kinds. The first: remembering the names and attributes of the Lord, praising Him, and declaring Him free of what does not befit Him. This too is of two kinds. The first: composing praise of Him by the one remembering, and this is the kind mentioned in the hadith, such as: Subhan Allah (Glory be to Allah), al-hamdu lillah (Praise be to Allah), la ilaha illa Allah (There is no god but Allah), Allahu akbar (Allah is greatest), Subhan Allah wa bihamdih (Glory be to Allah and praise Him), la ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah, lahu al-mulk wa lahu al-hamd wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir (There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner; to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs the praise, and He is capable of all things), and the like. The most excellent of this kind is that which is most comprehensive in praise and most general, such as: Subhan Allah 'adada khalqih (Glory be to Allah as many as His creation). This is better than merely saying Subhan Allah. And saying: al-hamdu lillah 'adada ma khalaqa fi al-sama' wa 'adada ma khalaqa fi al-ard wa 'adada ma baynahuma wa 'adada ma huwa khaliq (Praise be to Allah as many as what He created in the heavens, as many as what He created in the earth, as many as what is between them, and as many as what He is yet to create) is better than merely saying al-hamdu lillah. This is in the hadith of Juwayriya, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to her: "I have said after you four words three times, which if weighed against what you have said since today, would outweigh them: Subhan Allah 'adada khalqih (Glory be to Allah as many as His creation); Subhan Allah rida nafsih (Glory be to Allah as much as His own pleasure); Subhan Allah zinat 'arshih (Glory be to Allah as much as the weight of His Throne); Subhan Allah midad kalimatih (Glory be to Allah as much as the ink of His words)." Related by Muslim. In al-Tirmidhi and Sunan Abi Dawud, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, that he entered with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) upon a woman before whom were date-pits or pebbles with which she was counting her glorification. He said: "Shall I inform you of what is easier for you than this and better?" Then he said: "Subhan Allah 'adada ma khalaqa fi al-sama' (Glory be to Allah as many as what He created in the heavens), Subhan Allah 'adada ma khalaqa fi al-ard (Glory be to Allah as many as what He created in the earth), Subhan Allah 'adada ma bayna dhalik (Glory be to Allah as many as what is between that), Subhan Allah 'adada ma huwa khaliq (Glory be to Allah as many as what He is yet to create), Allahu akbar mithl dhalik (Allah is greatest, the same as that), la ilaha illa Allah mithl dhalik (There is no god but Allah, the same as that), and la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah mithl dhalik (There is no power nor strength except with Allah, the same as that)."

The second kind: reporting about the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, through the judgments of His names and attributes, such as your saying: Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, hears the voices of His servants, sees their movements, and nothing of their deeds is hidden from Him; He is more merciful to them than their fathers and mothers; He is capable of all things; and He is more pleased with the repentance of His servant than one who finds what he had lost. And the like. The most excellent of this kind is praising Him with what He praised Himself, and with what His Messenger (ﷺ) praised Him, without distortion (tahrif) or denial (ta'til), and without likening (tashbih) or modelling (tamthil), as He said: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾ [al-Shura: 11]. This kind also has three types: praise (hamd), commendation (thana'), and glorification (majd).

Praise (hamd) is informing about Him with the attributes of His perfection together with loving Him and being pleased with Him. The silent lover is not one who praises, nor is one who commends without love a praiser, until love and commendation are combined for Him. If he repeats praises one after another, they become commendation (thana'). If the praise is with attributes of majesty, grandeur, magnificence and sovereignty, it is glorification (majd). Allah Most High has combined all three types for His servant in the opening chapter, Surat al-Fatiha. When the servant says: ﴿Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, Allah says: "My servant has praised Me." When he says: ﴿The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾, He says: "My servant has commended Me." When he says: ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾, He says: "My servant has glorified Me."

The second kind of remembrance: remembering His command, His prohibition and His rulings. This too is of two kinds. The first: remembering Him through that by informing about Him, that He has commanded such and such, forbidden such and such, loves such and such and is displeased with such and such. The second: remembering Him at His command, so that one hastens to it, and at His prohibition, so that one flees from it. Remembering His command and prohibition is one thing, and remembering Him at His command and prohibition is another. When these kinds are combined in the one who remembers, his remembrance is the most excellent, most sublime and greatest of remembrance.

Benefit:

This, then, is the greatest understanding (al-fiqh al-akbar), and whatever is below it is among the best forms of remembrance when the intention in it is sound. Remembering Him, may He be exalted, also includes remembering His favours, His bounty, His kindness, His blessings, and the places of His grace upon His servants. This is among the most excellent kinds of remembrance. These are five kinds, and they can be done with the heart and with the tongue. The remembrance of the heart alone is better than the remembrance of the tongue, because remembrance of the heart produces knowledge (ma'rifah), makes love (mahabbah) sound, stirs up modesty (haya'), inspires awe (makhafah), calls to self-watchfulness (muraqabah), and restrains one from falling short in obedience and from being careless about sins and misdeeds. Remembrance of the tongue alone does not necessarily bring about any of these fruits, and even if it brings about some of them, its fruit is weak.

Remembrance is also better than supplication (du'a'), because remembrance is praise of Allah, mighty and majestic, for His beautiful attributes, blessings and names, whereas supplication is the servant asking for his need. How can the one be compared with the other? For this reason a hadith says: "Whoever is preoccupied with remembering Me instead of asking Me, I will give him better than what I give those who ask." For this reason it is recommended in supplication that the one supplicating begin by praising Allah and extolling Him before stating his need, and then ask for what he needs. This is as in the hadith of Fadalah ibn 'Ubayd, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard a man supplicating in his prayer without praising Allah and without sending blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This man has been hasty." Then he called him, or someone else, and said: "When one of you prays, let him begin by glorifying his Lord and extolling Him, then let him send blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ), and then let him supplicate with whatever he wishes." Related by Imam Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi, who said: "Hasan sahih (good and authentic)."

Likewise did Dhu al-Nun supplicate, concerning whom the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The supplication of my brother Dhu al-Nun, whenever a distressed person supplicates with it, Allah relieves his distress: 'There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been among the wrongdoers.'" In al-Tirmidhi: "The supplication of my brother Dhu al-Nun, when he supplicated with it in the belly of the fish: 'There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been among the wrongdoers.' No Muslim supplicates with it for anything at all except that Allah responds to him." Likewise are most of the Prophetic supplications, including the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) in the supplication for distress: "There is no god but..."

His saying: ﴿And glorify Him morning and evening﴾, i.e., at the time of morning and evening, like His saying: ﴿So glorify Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning, and to Him belongs praise in the heavens and the earth, and at night and when you are at noon﴾ [al-Rum: 17-18].

* *

His saying: ﴿It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels﴾: this is an incitement to remembrance, meaning: He, glory be to Him, remembers you, so you remember Him, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Just as We have sent among you a messenger from yourselves, reciting to you Our verses and purifying you and teaching you the Book and wisdom and teaching you what you did not know. So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me﴾ [al-Baqarah: 151-152]. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allah says: Whoever remembers Me in himself, I remember him in Myself; and whoever remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a gathering better than theirs." [Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 7405, and Muslim in his Sahih, no. 2675, from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.]

The blessing (salah) from Allah is His praise of the servant in the presence of the angels. Al-Bukhari related this from Abu al-'Aliyah. Abu Ja'far al-Razi related it from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from him.

Others said: the blessing from Allah is mercy. [It is refuted by His saying: ﴿Upon those are blessings from their Lord and mercy﴾.]

It may be said: there is no contradiction between the two statements, and Allah knows best.

As for the blessing from the angels, it means supplication for the people and seeking forgiveness for them, as in His saying: ﴿Those who carry the Throne and those around it glorify their Lord with praise and believe in Him and seek forgiveness for those who believe: "Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who repent and follow Your way and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire. Our Lord, and admit them to gardens of perpetual residence which You have promised them, and whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their descendants. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise. And protect them from evils﴾ [Ghafir: 7-9], the verse.

* *

His saying: ﴿to bring you out of darknesses into light﴾: i.e., because of His mercy towards you, His praise of you, and the supplication of His angels for you, He brings you out of the darknesses of ignorance and misguidance into the light of guidance and certainty. ﴿And He is ever merciful to the believers﴾: i.e., in this world and in the Hereafter. As for His mercy in this world: He guided them to the truth which others were ignorant of, and showed them the path from which those who called to disbelief or innovation, and their followers from the rabble (al-tighaam), had strayed and turned away. As for His mercy to them in the Hereafter: He grants them security from the greatest terror, and commands His angels to receive them with the good news of success in Paradise and deliverance from the Fire. This is only because of His love for them and His tenderness towards them.

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Adiy narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by with a group of his companions, and there was a child in the road. When the child's mother saw the people, she feared for her child that he would be trampled, so she came hurrying and saying: "My son, my son!" She hurried and took him. The people said: "O Messenger of Allah, this woman would never throw her son into the Fire." He said: So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) lowered them (his voice to them), and said: "No, by Allah, Allah does not throw His beloved into the Fire."

Its chain is according to the conditions of the two Sahihs, but none of the authors of the six books (al-kutub al-sittah) related it. However, in the Sahih of Imam al-Bukhari, from the commander of the believers 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw a woman from among the captives who had taken a child of hers, pressed it to her chest and nursed it. He said: "Do you think this woman would throw her child into the Fire while she is able to avoid that?" They said: "No." He said: "By Allah, Allah is more merciful to His servants than this woman is to her child." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5999.]

* *

His saying: ﴿Their greeting on the Day they meet Him will be, "Peace"﴾. The apparent meaning, and Allah knows best, is: ﴿Their greeting﴾, i.e., from Allah, exalted is He, on the Day they meet Him will be ﴿peace﴾, i.e., the Day on which He greets them with peace, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿"Peace," a word from a Lord, Most Merciful﴾ [Ya-Sin: 58].

Qatadah claimed that what is meant is that they greet one another with peace, on the Day they meet Allah in the Hereafter. Ibn Jarir chose this view.

I say: It may be supported by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Their call therein is, "Glory be to You, O Allah," and their greeting therein is, "Peace," and the last of their call is, "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds"﴾ [Yunus: 10], and His saying: ﴿And He has prepared for them a noble reward﴾, meaning: Paradise and what is in it of food and drink, clothing and dwellings, spouses and pleasures, sights that no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and that has not occurred to the heart of any human being.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 33, verses 41–44 (part 1 of 2):

God, exalted is He, says, commanding His believing servants to remember Him often (dhikr, remembrance of God), the One who has bestowed upon them all kinds of blessings and varieties of favours, because of the great reward and the beautiful return that they will have through it.

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us from 'Abd Allah ibn Sa'id [in A: "Sa'd"], from a client (mawla) of Ibn 'Ayyash [in A: "Abbas"], from Abu Bahriyya [in A: "from Abu 'Urwa"], from Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Shall I not inform you of the best of your deeds, the purest of them in the sight of your Sovereign, the highest of them in your ranks, and better for you than giving gold and silver, and better for you than meeting your enemy and striking their necks while they strike your necks?" They said: "What is it, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

It was also related by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, through the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Sa'id ibn Abi Hind, from Ziyad, the client of Ibn 'Ayyash [in A: "Abbas"], from Abu Bahriyya, whose name is 'Abd Allah ibn Qays al-Taraghimi, from Abu al-Darda', with the same wording. [Musnad (5/195), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3377), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3790).] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Some of them related it from him as a mursal (a report whose chain omits a companion)."

I say: This hadith has already been mentioned at the verse of His saying: ﴿and the men and women who remember Allah often﴾ in the Musnad of [Imam] [addition from A] Ahmad, through the hadith of Ziyad ibn Abi Ziyad, client of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ayyash: that it reached him from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), with something similar. And Allah knows best.

Imam Ahmad also said: Waki' narrated to us, Faraj ibn Fudala narrated to us, from Abu Sa'd al-Himsi, who said: I heard Abu Hurayra say: "A supplication I heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which I will never abandon: 'O Allah, make me greatest in thanking You, most faithful in following Your counsel, most abundant in remembering You, and most careful in preserving Your commandment.'" [Musnad (2/477).]

Al-Tirmidhi related it from Yahya ibn Musa, from Waki', from Abu Fudala al-Faraj ibn Fudala, from Abu Sa'id al-Himsi, from Abu Hurayra, and he mentioned the like of it and said: "Gharib (a hadith with a single narrator at some point in its chain)." [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3604).]

And so Imam Ahmad also related it from Abu al-Nadr Hashim ibn al-Qasim, from Faraj ibn Fudala, from Abu Sa'id al-Madani [in A: "al-Muzani"], from Abu Hurayra, and he mentioned it. [Musnad (2/311).]

Imam Ahmad also said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Mu'awiya ibn Salih, from 'Amr ibn Qays, who said: I heard 'Abd Allah ibn Busr say: Two Bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). One of them said: "O Messenger of Allah, which of the people is best?" He said: "The one whose life is long and whose deeds are good." The other said: "O Messenger of Allah, the laws of Islam have become numerous for us [in T: "upon me"], so command me with something I may hold fast to." He said: "Let your tongue remain moist with the remembrance of Allah." [Musnad (4/190).]

Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah related the second part [from it] [addition from F, A], through the hadith of Mu'awiya ibn Salih, with the same chain. [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3375), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3793).] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib."

Imam Ahmad also said: Surayj [in A: "Shurayh"] narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn al-Harith, who said: Darraj Abu al-Samh narrated to him, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Remember Allah abundantly, until they say: 'He is mad.'" [Musnad (3/68), in which there is Darraj, and Abu al-Haytham is weak.]

Al-Tabarani said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad narrated to us, 'Uqba ibn Mukram al-'Ammi narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Sufyan [in A: "Safr"] al-Jahdari narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from 'Uqba ibn Abi Thubayt [in A: "Sabab"] al-Rasibi, from Abu al-Jawza', from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Remember Allah with much remembrance [until] [addition from T, F, A, and al-Mu'jam] the hypocrites say: 'You are showing off.'" [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir of al-Tabarani (12/169); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/76): "In it is al-Husayn ibn Abi Ja'far al-Ja'fari, who is weak."]

Imam Ahmad [in A: "Zaadahu"] also said: Abu Sa'id, client of the Banu Hashim, narrated to us, Shaddad Abu Talha al-Rasibi narrated to us, I heard Abu al-Wazi' Jabir ibn 'Amr narrate from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No people sit in a gathering in which they do not remember Allah, except that it will be a regret for them on the Day of Resurrection." [Musnad (2/224); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/80): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]

'Ali ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿Remember Allah with much remembrance﴾: Allah did not prescribe for His servants any obligation except that He set for it a known limit, then He excused its people in a state of excuse, except for remembrance. For Allah has not set for it a limit at which it ends, and He has not excused anyone in abandoning it, except one who is overpowered in abandoning it. So He said: ﴿So remember Allah standing, sitting, and on your sides﴾ [al-Nisa': 103], by night and by day, on land and at sea, while travelling and at home, in wealth and in poverty, in health and in sickness, in secret and in public, and in every state. And He said: ﴿and glorify Him morning and evening﴾. So when you do that, He and His angels send blessings upon you.

The hadiths, verses and reports urging the remembrance of Allah are very numerous indeed, and in this noble verse is the urging to increase in that (al-ikthar, increasing).

People have composed works on the adhkar (litanies of remembrance) connected with the times of night and day, such as al-Nasa'i, al-Ma'muri and others [in T: "al-Ma'mari, al-Kalim al-Tayyib of Shaykh al-Islam, and others"]. Among the best books composed on this is the Kitab al-Adhkar of Shaykh Muhyi al-Din al-Nawawi, may God Most High have mercy on him. [The Kitab al-Adhkar has been published, edited by Shaykh 'Abd al-Qadir al-Arna'ut at Dar al-Huda, and there is a takhrij (sourcing) of it by Ibn 'Allan entitled "al-Futuhat al-Rabbaniyya," printed in India.]

Furthermore, what follows this paragraph in manuscript "T" is the following:

"Remembrance of Allah is the root of loyalty to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and its head. Heedlessness is the root of enmity toward Him and its head. For the servant continues to remember his Lord until he loves Him and so is loyal to Him, and he continues to be heedless of Him until he hates Him and becomes hostile to Him. Allah the Most High said: (And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance, and who follows his desire and whose affair is excess) [al-Kahf: 28]. Nothing has drawn the blessings of Allah Most High and warded off His vengeance like the remembrance of Allah. Remembrance is the drawer of blessings and the repeller of vengeance. Allah said: (Indeed, Allah defends those who believe) [al-Hajj: 38], and in the other reading: (Defends [yudafi'u] those who believe). His repelling and defending of them is in proportion to the strength and perfection of their faith, and the material of faith and its strength come from the remembrance of Allah. So whoever is more complete in faith and more abundant in remembrance, Allah's defence of him and His repelling are greater. Whoever is deficient, his remembrance is deficient, and his forgetting is in proportion. Allah said: (And when your Lord proclaimed: If you are grateful, I will surely increase you) [Ibrahim: 7]. Remembrance is the head of gratitude, and gratitude draws blessings and necessitates increase. Some of the early Muslims said: How ugly is heedlessness of the remembrance of One who never ceases to be kind to you. The gatherings of remembrance are the gardens of Paradise, as Ibn Abi al-Dunya related from the hadith of Jabir, from 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to us and said: 'O people, graze in the gardens of Paradise.' We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what are the gardens of Paradise?' He said: 'The gatherings of remembrance.' Then he said: 'Go out in the morning and evening and remember. Whoever wishes to know his standing with Allah, let him look at Allah's standing with him, for Allah lowers the servant to the place where He has lowered him in His own self.' The gatherings of remembrance are the gatherings of the angels, as in the two Sahihs from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Allah has angels who roam the roads beyond the people's scribes, seeking the people of remembrance. When they find a group remembering Allah, they call out to one another: Come to what you seek. Then they surround them with their wings up to the lowest heaven. Their Lord asks them, and He knows best about them: What are My servants saying? They say: They glorify You, magnify You, praise You and extol You. He says: Have they seen Me? They say: No, by Allah, our Lord, they have not seen You. He says: How would it be if they saw Me? They say: If they saw You, they would be even more intense in worship, even more in praise and extolment, and more in glorification. He says: What are they asking of Me? They say: They ask You for Paradise. He says: Have they seen it? They say: No, by Allah, our Lord, they have not seen it. He says: How would it be if they saw it? They say: If they saw it, they would be even more eager for it, even more intent on it, and have even greater desire for it. He says: From what do they seek refuge? They say: From the Fire. He says: Have they seen it? They say: No, by Allah, our Lord, they have not seen it. He says: How would it be if they saw it? They say: If they saw it, they would flee from it even more and be even more fearful of it. He says: I call you to witness that I have forgiven them. One of the angels says: Among them is so-and-so, who is not one of them; he only came for a need. He says: They are a people whose companion does not become wretched." This is from their blessing upon themselves and upon their companions. For them is a share of His saying: (And He made me blessed wherever I am) [Maryam: 31]. Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, boasts of those who remember Him to the angels, as Muslim related in his Sahih from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: Mu'awiya went out to a circle in the mosque and said: What has made you sit? They said: We sat remembering Allah. He said: Did nothing but that make you sit? They said: By Allah, nothing but that made us sit.
