He said: As for me, I did not ask you out of suspicion of you, and no one has a lower rank of narrating from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) than I do; the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to a circle of his companions and said: 'What has made you sit?' They said: We sat remembering Allah and praising Him for guiding us to Islam and bestowing His favour upon us through you. He said: 'By Allah, did nothing but that make you sit?' They said: By Allah, nothing but that made us sit. He said: 'As for me, I did not make you swear out of suspicion of you, but Jibril came to me and informed me that Allah boasts of you to the angels.' This boasting by the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, is evidence of the honour of remembrance with Him, His love for it, and that it has a distinction over other deeds.

Remembrance is of two kinds. The first: remembering the names and attributes of the Lord, praising Him, and declaring Him free of what does not befit Him. This too is of two kinds. The first: composing praise of Him by the one remembering, and this is the kind mentioned in the hadith, such as: Subhan Allah (Glory be to Allah), al-hamdu lillah (Praise be to Allah), la ilaha illa Allah (There is no god but Allah), Allahu akbar (Allah is greatest), Subhan Allah wa bihamdih (Glory be to Allah and praise Him), la ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah, lahu al-mulk wa lahu al-hamd wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir (There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner; to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs the praise, and He is capable of all things), and the like. The most excellent of this kind is that which is most comprehensive in praise and most general, such as: Subhan Allah 'adada khalqih (Glory be to Allah as many as His creation). This is better than merely saying Subhan Allah. And saying: al-hamdu lillah 'adada ma khalaqa fi al-sama' wa 'adada ma khalaqa fi al-ard wa 'adada ma baynahuma wa 'adada ma huwa khaliq (Praise be to Allah as many as what He created in the heavens, as many as what He created in the earth, as many as what is between them, and as many as what He is yet to create) is better than merely saying al-hamdu lillah. This is in the hadith of Juwayriya, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to her: "I have said after you four words three times, which if weighed against what you have said since today, would outweigh them: Subhan Allah 'adada khalqih (Glory be to Allah as many as His creation); Subhan Allah rida nafsih (Glory be to Allah as much as His own pleasure); Subhan Allah zinat 'arshih (Glory be to Allah as much as the weight of His Throne); Subhan Allah midad kalimatih (Glory be to Allah as much as the ink of His words)." Related by Muslim. In al-Tirmidhi and Sunan Abi Dawud, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, that he entered with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) upon a woman before whom were date-pits or pebbles with which she was counting her glorification. He said: "Shall I inform you of what is easier for you than this and better?" Then he said: "Subhan Allah 'adada ma khalaqa fi al-sama' (Glory be to Allah as many as what He created in the heavens), Subhan Allah 'adada ma khalaqa fi al-ard (Glory be to Allah as many as what He created in the earth), Subhan Allah 'adada ma bayna dhalik (Glory be to Allah as many as what is between that), Subhan Allah 'adada ma huwa khaliq (Glory be to Allah as many as what He is yet to create), Allahu akbar mithl dhalik (Allah is greatest, the same as that), la ilaha illa Allah mithl dhalik (There is no god but Allah, the same as that), and la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah mithl dhalik (There is no power nor strength except with Allah, the same as that)."

The second kind: reporting about the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, through the judgments of His names and attributes, such as your saying: Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, hears the voices of His servants, sees their movements, and nothing of their deeds is hidden from Him; He is more merciful to them than their fathers and mothers; He is capable of all things; and He is more pleased with the repentance of His servant than one who finds what he had lost. And the like. The most excellent of this kind is praising Him with what He praised Himself, and with what His Messenger (ﷺ) praised Him, without distortion (tahrif) or denial (ta'til), and without likening (tashbih) or modelling (tamthil), as He said: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾ [al-Shura: 11]. This kind also has three types: praise (hamd), commendation (thana'), and glorification (majd).

Praise (hamd) is informing about Him with the attributes of His perfection together with loving Him and being pleased with Him. The silent lover is not one who praises, nor is one who commends without love a praiser, until love and commendation are combined for Him. If he repeats praises one after another, they become commendation (thana'). If the praise is with attributes of majesty, grandeur, magnificence and sovereignty, it is glorification (majd). Allah Most High has combined all three types for His servant in the opening chapter, Surat al-Fatiha. When the servant says: ﴿Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, Allah says: "My servant has praised Me." When he says: ﴿The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾, He says: "My servant has commended Me." When he says: ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾, He says: "My servant has glorified Me."

The second kind of remembrance: remembering His command, His prohibition and His rulings. This too is of two kinds. The first: remembering Him through that by informing about Him, that He has commanded such and such, forbidden such and such, loves such and such and is displeased with such and such. The second: remembering Him at His command, so that one hastens to it, and at His prohibition, so that one flees from it. Remembering His command and prohibition is one thing, and remembering Him at His command and prohibition is another. When these kinds are combined in the one who remembers, his remembrance is the most excellent, most sublime and greatest of remembrance.

Benefit:

This, then, is the greatest understanding (al-fiqh al-akbar), and whatever is below it is among the best forms of remembrance when the intention in it is sound. Remembering Him, may He be exalted, also includes remembering His favours, His bounty, His kindness, His blessings, and the places of His grace upon His servants. This is among the most excellent kinds of remembrance. These are five kinds, and they can be done with the heart and with the tongue. The remembrance of the heart alone is better than the remembrance of the tongue, because remembrance of the heart produces knowledge (ma'rifah), makes love (mahabbah) sound, stirs up modesty (haya'), inspires awe (makhafah), calls to self-watchfulness (muraqabah), and restrains one from falling short in obedience and from being careless about sins and misdeeds. Remembrance of the tongue alone does not necessarily bring about any of these fruits, and even if it brings about some of them, its fruit is weak.

Remembrance is also better than supplication (du'a'), because remembrance is praise of Allah, mighty and majestic, for His beautiful attributes, blessings and names, whereas supplication is the servant asking for his need. How can the one be compared with the other? For this reason a hadith says: "Whoever is preoccupied with remembering Me instead of asking Me, I will give him better than what I give those who ask." For this reason it is recommended in supplication that the one supplicating begin by praising Allah and extolling Him before stating his need, and then ask for what he needs. This is as in the hadith of Fadalah ibn 'Ubayd, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard a man supplicating in his prayer without praising Allah and without sending blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This man has been hasty." Then he called him, or someone else, and said: "When one of you prays, let him begin by glorifying his Lord and extolling Him, then let him send blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ), and then let him supplicate with whatever he wishes." Related by Imam Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi, who said: "Hasan sahih (good and authentic)."

Likewise did Dhu al-Nun supplicate, concerning whom the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The supplication of my brother Dhu al-Nun, whenever a distressed person supplicates with it, Allah relieves his distress: 'There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been among the wrongdoers.'" In al-Tirmidhi: "The supplication of my brother Dhu al-Nun, when he supplicated with it in the belly of the fish: 'There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been among the wrongdoers.' No Muslim supplicates with it for anything at all except that Allah responds to him." Likewise are most of the Prophetic supplications, including the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) in the supplication for distress: "There is no god but..."

His saying: ﴿And glorify Him morning and evening﴾, i.e., at the time of morning and evening, like His saying: ﴿So glorify Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning, and to Him belongs praise in the heavens and the earth, and at night and when you are at noon﴾ [al-Rum: 17-18].

* *

His saying: ﴿It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels﴾: this is an incitement to remembrance, meaning: He, glory be to Him, remembers you, so you remember Him, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Just as We have sent among you a messenger from yourselves, reciting to you Our verses and purifying you and teaching you the Book and wisdom and teaching you what you did not know. So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me﴾ [al-Baqarah: 151-152]. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allah says: Whoever remembers Me in himself, I remember him in Myself; and whoever remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a gathering better than theirs." [Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 7405, and Muslim in his Sahih, no. 2675, from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.]

The blessing (salah) from Allah is His praise of the servant in the presence of the angels. Al-Bukhari related this from Abu al-'Aliyah. Abu Ja'far al-Razi related it from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from him.

Others said: the blessing from Allah is mercy. [It is refuted by His saying: ﴿Upon those are blessings from their Lord and mercy﴾.]

It may be said: there is no contradiction between the two statements, and Allah knows best.

As for the blessing from the angels, it means supplication for the people and seeking forgiveness for them, as in His saying: ﴿Those who carry the Throne and those around it glorify their Lord with praise and believe in Him and seek forgiveness for those who believe: "Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who repent and follow Your way and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire. Our Lord, and admit them to gardens of perpetual residence which You have promised them, and whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their descendants. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise. And protect them from evils﴾ [Ghafir: 7-9], the verse.

* *

His saying: ﴿to bring you out of darknesses into light﴾: i.e., because of His mercy towards you, His praise of you, and the supplication of His angels for you, He brings you out of the darknesses of ignorance and misguidance into the light of guidance and certainty. ﴿And He is ever merciful to the believers﴾: i.e., in this world and in the Hereafter. As for His mercy in this world: He guided them to the truth which others were ignorant of, and showed them the path from which those who called to disbelief or innovation, and their followers from the rabble (al-tighaam), had strayed and turned away. As for His mercy to them in the Hereafter: He grants them security from the greatest terror, and commands His angels to receive them with the good news of success in Paradise and deliverance from the Fire. This is only because of His love for them and His tenderness towards them.

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Adiy narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by with a group of his companions, and there was a child in the road. When the child's mother saw the people, she feared for her child that he would be trampled, so she came hurrying and saying: "My son, my son!" She hurried and took him. The people said: "O Messenger of Allah, this woman would never throw her son into the Fire." He said: So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) lowered them (his voice to them), and said: "No, by Allah, Allah does not throw His beloved into the Fire."

Its chain is according to the conditions of the two Sahihs, but none of the authors of the six books (al-kutub al-sittah) related it. However, in the Sahih of Imam al-Bukhari, from the commander of the believers 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw a woman from among the captives who had taken a child of hers, pressed it to her chest and nursed it. He said: "Do you think this woman would throw her child into the Fire while she is able to avoid that?" They said: "No." He said: "By Allah, Allah is more merciful to His servants than this woman is to her child." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5999.]

* *

His saying: ﴿Their greeting on the Day they meet Him will be, "Peace"﴾. The apparent meaning, and Allah knows best, is: ﴿Their greeting﴾, i.e., from Allah, exalted is He, on the Day they meet Him will be ﴿peace﴾, i.e., the Day on which He greets them with peace, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿"Peace," a word from a Lord, Most Merciful﴾ [Ya-Sin: 58].

Qatadah claimed that what is meant is that they greet one another with peace, on the Day they meet Allah in the Hereafter. Ibn Jarir chose this view.

I say: It may be supported by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Their call therein is, "Glory be to You, O Allah," and their greeting therein is, "Peace," and the last of their call is, "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds"﴾ [Yunus: 10], and His saying: ﴿And He has prepared for them a noble reward﴾, meaning: Paradise and what is in it of food and drink, clothing and dwellings, spouses and pleasures, sights that no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and that has not occurred to the heart of any human being.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 33, verses 45–48:

Imam Ahmad said: Musa ibn Dawud related to us, Fulayh ibn Sulayman related to us, from Hilal ibn Ali [[In T: "Imam Ahmad narrated with his chain."]] from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, who said: I met 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As and I said: "Tell me about the description of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the Tawrah (Torah)." He said: "Yes, by Allah, indeed he is described in the Tawrah with his description in the Qur'an: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness, a bearer of good news and a warner﴾ and a guardian for the unlettered. You are My servant and My Messenger. I have named you al-Mutawakkil (the one who relies upon Allah). You are not harsh, nor coarse, nor one who raises his voice in the markets, and he does not repel evil with evil, but he pardons and forgives [[In F: "he pardons, overlooks and forgives."]]. Allah will not take him until he has established through him the crooked community, by [people] saying there is no god but Allah, so that by it He opens blind eyes, deaf ears and veiled hearts."

Al-Bukhari also narrated it in "al-Buyu' (Sales)" from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Fulayh ibn Sulayman, from Hilal ibn Ali, with it. He narrated it in the Tafsir section from 'Abdullah, said to be Ibn Raja' and said to be Ibn Salih, from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abi Salamah, from Hilal, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, with it [[Al-Musnad (2/174) and Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (2125) and (4838).]]. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it from his father, from 'Abdullah ibn Raja', from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abi Salamah al-Majishun, with it.

Al-Bukhari said in "al-Buyu'": Sa'id narrated from Hilal, from 'Ata', from 'Abdullah ibn Salam.

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Allah revealed to a prophet from the prophets of the Children of Israel, who was called Sha'ya': "Stand up among your people, the Children of Israel, for I shall make your tongue speak by revelation, and I shall raise up an unlettered man from among the unlettered. I shall send him as a bearer of good news [[Addition from T, F.]], not harsh, nor coarse, nor one who raises his voice in the markets. If he were to pass by the side of a lamp, he would not extinguish it, because of his tranquility. If he were to walk on reeds, their sound would not be heard beneath his feet. I shall send him as a bearer of good news and a warner, who does not speak obscenity. I shall open with him blind eyes, deaf ears and veiled hearts. I shall guide him to every good matter, grant him every noble character, make tranquility his garment, righteousness his emblem, piety his inner self, wisdom his speech, truthfulness and fidelity his nature, pardon and kindness his character, truth his law, justice his way, guidance his leader, Islam his religion, and Ahmad his name. Through him I shall guide [people] after misguidance, teach them after ignorance, raise them up after lowliness, make them known after obscurity, multiply them after scarcity, enrich them after poverty, gather them after division, and join with him nations that are scattered, hearts that differ and desires that are dispersed. Through him I shall rescue great multitudes of people from destruction. I shall make his community the best community brought forth for mankind, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, monotheists, believers, sincere, affirming what My messengers brought. I shall inspire them with glorification, praise, extolling, magnification and affirmation of Oneness, in their mosques and their gatherings, in their beds, their returns and their abodes. They will pray to Me standing and sitting, and they will fight in the way of Allah in ranks and hosts, and they will leave their homes seeking My pleasure in thousands. They will purify their faces and their limbs, and they will gird their garments up to the middle. Their sacrifice is their blood, and their Gospels are in their breasts. They are monks by night and lions by day. I shall place among the people of his household and his offspring the foremost, the truthful, the martyrs and the righteous. His community after him will guide by the truth and by it they will act justly. I shall honour whoever helps them, support whoever supplicates for them, and I shall make the circle of evil fall upon whoever opposes them, transgresses against them, or intends to snatch anything from what is in their hands. I shall make them the heirs of their Prophet and the callers to their Lord, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, establishing the prayer and giving the zakah, and fulfilling their covenant. I shall seal with them the good that I began with their first [ones]. That is My bounty which I bestow on whom I will, and I am the Owner of mighty bounty."

Thus Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamani, may Allah have mercy on him.

Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Salih related to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ubaydullah al-'Arzami related to us, from Shayban al-Nahwi, Qatadah informed me, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas [[In T: "Then Ibn Abi Hatim narrated with his chain to Ibn 'Abbas."]] who said: "When the verse was revealed: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness, a bearer of good news and a warner﴾ —and he had commanded 'Ali and Mu'adh to travel to Yemen— he said: 'Go, give good news and do not cause aversion, make things easy and do not make them difficult. Indeed there has been revealed to me: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness, a bearer of good news and a warner﴾."

Al-Tabarani also narrated it from Muhammad ibn Nasr ibn Humayd al-Bazzaz al-Baghdadi, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Salih al-Azdi, from 'Abd al-Rahman [ibn Muhammad] [[Addition from T, F, and al-Mu'jam.]] ibn 'Ubaydullah al-'Arzami, with its chain, the like of it [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/312). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/92): "In it is 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ubaydullah al-'Arzami, who is weak."]]. At its end he said: "Indeed there has been revealed to me [[In T, A: "were revealed."]]: O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness over your community and a bearer of good news of Paradise, a warner from the Fire, a caller to the testimony that there is no god but Allah by His permission, and a radiant lamp by the Qur'an."

* *

As for His saying ﴿witness﴾, it means: a witness for Allah to His Oneness, and that there is no god besides Him, and a witness over the people concerning their deeds on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And We bring you as a witness over these﴾ [An-Nisa: 41]. Like His saying: ﴿that you may be witnesses over the people and that the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 143].

* *

As for His saying ﴿and a bearer of good news and a warner﴾, it means: a bearer of good news to the believers of abundant reward, and a warner to the disbelievers of dreadful punishment.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and a caller to Allah by His permission﴾, it means: a caller of creation to worship their Lord, by His command to you to do so. ﴿And a radiant lamp﴾ means: your affair is manifest in what you have brought of the truth, like the sun in its brightness and its shining, which none denies except a stubborn obstinate person.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and disregard their harm﴾, it means: do not obey them, and do not listen to them regarding what they say. ﴿And disregard their harm﴾, i.e., overlook and pass over them, and entrust their affair to Allah, for in Him is sufficiency for them. Therefore He said: ﴿And rely upon Allah, and sufficient is Allah as a Trustee﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 48].

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 33, verses 45–48:

This noble verse contains many rulings. Among them: the word *nikah* (marriage contract) is used for the contract alone, and there is no verse in the Qur'an more explicit in this than it. The scholars differ over whether *nikah* is literally (*haqiqah*) the contract alone, or the consummation, or both, according to three opinions. Elsewhere in the Qur'an it is used for the contract and for the intercourse that follows it, but in this verse it is used for the contract alone, by His saying: ﴿When you marry (*nakahtum*) believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them﴾. The verse also indicates the permissibility of divorcing a woman before consummation.

* *

His saying: ﴿believing women﴾ comes in the form of what is usual, since there is no difference in the ruling between a believing woman and a woman of the People of the Book in this matter, by consensus. Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, al-Hasan al-Basri, Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin, and a group of the early scholars (*salaf*) cited this verse to show that divorce does not take effect unless it is preceded by a marriage, because Allah the Exalted said: ﴿When you marry believing women and then divorce them﴾, so He linked divorce to marriage, which indicates that it is not valid and does not take effect before it. This is the position of al-Shafi'i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and a great many of the early and later scholars, may Allah have mercy on them all.

Malik and Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on them both, held that divorce before marriage is valid in the case where a man says: "If I marry so-and-so, she is divorced." According to them, whenever he marries her, she is divorced by him. They differed in the case where he says: "Every woman I marry is divorced." Malik said: she is not divorced until he specifies the woman. Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, said: every woman he marries after this statement is divorced by him. The majority, however, argued that divorce does not take effect by this verse.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Marwazi narrated to us, al-Nadr ibn Shumayl narrated to us, Yunus (meaning Ibn Abi Ishaq) narrated to us, I heard Adam, the client (*mawla*) of Khalid, narrating from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: [when someone said] "Every woman I marry is divorced," he said: "It is nothing, because Allah the Exalted says: ﴿O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them﴾," and so on.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ahmasi narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Mattar, from al-Hasan ibn Muslim ibn Yanaq, from Ibn Abbas who said: "Allah the Exalted only said: ﴿When you marry believing women and then divorce them﴾. Do you not see that divorce comes after marriage?!"

Similarly, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas who said: Allah said: ﴿When you marry believing women and then divorce them﴾, so there is no divorce [before marriage].

The hadith has also been reported to this effect from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no divorce for the son of Adam in what he does not own." It was related by Imam Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, Abu Dawud, and Ibn Majah. Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan (good) hadith," and it is the best thing reported on this subject. Likewise Ibn Majah related from Ali and from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "There is no divorce before marriage."

[And in the verse there is evidence that *al-mass* (touching) is general and is meant to denote intercourse.]

* *

His saying: ﴿So you have no waiting period (*iddah*) for them that you need to count﴾: this is a matter agreed upon among the scholars: that when a woman is divorced before consummation, she has no waiting period, so she may go and marry immediately whomever she wishes. The only exception is a widow whose husband has died, for she observes a waiting period of four months and ten days, even if he has not consummated the marriage with her, also by consensus.

* *

His saying: ﴿Then provide for them (*mattiʿuhunna*) and release them with a fair release﴾: the *mut'ah* (provision) here is more general than being half of the stipulated dowry (*sadaq*), or the special *mut'ah* if no dowry was specified for her. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if you divorce them before you have touched them, and you have already specified for them an obligation, then half of what you specified﴾ [al-Baqarah: 237], and He said: ﴿There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them or specified for them an obligation; and provide for them, the wealthy according to his means and the poor according to his means, a provision according to what is reasonable, a duty upon the doers of good﴾ [al-Baqarah: 236].

In Sahih al-Bukhari, from Sahl ibn Sa'd and Abu Usayd, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married Umaymah bint Sharahil, and when she was brought in to him, he extended his hand toward her, and it seemed she disliked that, so he commanded Abu Usayd to prepare her and clothe her with two Raziqi garments.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: If he had specified a dowry for her, she has only half; and if he had not specified a dowry for her, then provide for her according to his means and his circumstances, and this is the graceful release.

Allah, exalted is He, says, addressing His Prophet, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, that He has made lawful for him the wives to whom he has given their dowries (ujur, here meaning dowries), as Mujahid and others said. His dowry for his wives was twelve uqiyya and a nash, and the nash is half an uqiyya. The total was five hundred dirhams. The exception is Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan, for whom al-Najashi (may Allah have mercy on him) paid a dowry of four hundred dinars on his behalf. The exception is also Safiyyah bint Huyayy, whom he chose from the captives of Khaybar, then freed, making her freedom her dowry. Likewise Juwayriyah bint al-Harith al-Mustaliqiyyah, whose manumission contract (kitabah) he paid to Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, and then he married her. May Allah be pleased with all of them.
* *
His saying: ﴿And those whom your right hand possesses from what Allah has given you﴾ means: and He permitted you to take concubines (tasarri) from what you obtained of the spoils of war. He owned Safiyyah and Juwayriyah, then freed them and married them. He also owned Rayhanah bint Shamʿun al-Nadriyyah, and Mariyah al-Qibtiyyah, the mother of his son Ibrahim, peace be upon him. Both of them were among the concubines (saraari). May Allah be pleased with them both.
* *
His saying: ﴿And the daughters of your paternal uncles, and the daughters of your paternal aunts, and the daughters of your maternal uncles, and the daughters of your maternal aunts, who emigrated with you﴾: this is a middle course between excess and negligence. The Christians do not marry a woman unless there are seven generations or more between the man and her. The Jews marry a man to his brother's daughter and his sister's daughter. This perfect and pure law came to demolish the excess of the Christians, so it permitted the daughter of the paternal uncle, the daughter of the paternal aunt, the daughter of the maternal uncle and the daughter of the maternal aunt, and it prohibited what the Jews had gone to excess in permitting, namely marrying the daughter of one's brother and the daughter of one's sister. This is abominable and monstrous.
He said ﴿the daughters of your paternal uncles, paternal aunts, maternal uncles and maternal aunts﴾, using the singular masculine for the men because of their nobility, and the plural feminine for the women because of their lesser status, as in His saying: ﴿on the right and the left﴾ [An-Nahl: 48], ﴿He brings them out from darknesses into the light﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 257], and ﴿and made the darknesses and the light﴾ [Al-An'am: 1]. There are many similar examples.
* *
His saying: ﴿who emigrated with you﴾. Ibn Abi Hatim, may Allah have mercy on him, said:
Muhammad ibn Ammar ibn al-Harith al-Razi told us: Ubaydullah ibn Musa told us: Israʼil told us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Salih, from Umm Hani, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ proposed to me, and I excused myself to him. Then Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have made lawful for you your wives whose dowries you have given, and those whom your right hand possesses from what Allah has given you, and the daughters of your paternal uncles…﴾ up to His saying ﴿who emigrated with you﴾. She said: So I was not lawful for him, and I was not among those who emigrated with him; I was among the Freed Captives (al-Tulaqa').
Ibn Jarir narrated it from Abu Kurayb, from Ubaydullah ibn Musa, with the same chain. [Tafsir al-Tabari (22/15).]
Then Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Ismaʼil ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, from her, in similar wording.
It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Jami'. [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3214, where he said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith, which we only know through this route, from the hadith of al-Suddi."]
Abu Razin and Qatadah said the same: the intended meaning is those who emigrated with him to Madinah. In a report from Qatadah: ﴿who emigrated with you﴾ means: who embraced Islam. Al-Dahhak said: Ibn Mas'ud recited: "wal-lati hajarna maʻak" (and those who emigrated with you).
* *
His saying: ﴿And a believing woman, if she gives herself to the Prophet, if the Prophet wishes to take her in marriage﴾ means: and it is lawful for you, O Prophet, that a believing woman, if she gives herself to you, you may marry her without a dowry, if you wish that. This verse contains two conditions following one another, like His saying, exalted is He, quoting Nuh, peace be upon him, that he said to his people: ﴿My advice will not benefit you if I wish to advise you, if Allah wills to lead you astray﴾ [Hud: 34], and like Musa's saying: ﴿O my people, if you have believed in Allah, then rely upon Him, if you are Muslims﴾ [Yunus: 84].
Here He said: ﴿And a believing woman, if she gives herself to the Prophet, if the Prophet wishes to take her in marriage﴾. Imam Ahmad said:
Ishaq told us, Malik informed us, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi: that a woman came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have given myself to you." She stood for a long time, then a man stood and said: "O Messenger of Allah, marry her to me, if you have no need of her." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do you have anything to give her as a dowry?" He said: "I have nothing except this lower garment of mine." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If you give her your garment, you will sit without a garment, so look for something." He said: "I cannot find anything." He said: "Look even for an iron ring." He searched but found nothing. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "Do you know any of the Qur'an?" He said: "Yes, such-and-such surah and such-and-such surah," naming surahs. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have married her to you for what you know of the Qur'an."
Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Malik. [Musnad Ahmad (5/336); Sahih al-Bukhari no. 5135; Sahih Muslim no. 1425, but in Muslim it is through the routes of Ya'qub, Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abi Hazim, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, al-Darawardi and Za'idah, all from Abu Hazim, with similar wording.]
Imam Ahmad also said: Affan told us: Marhum told us: I heard Thabit say: "I was sitting with Anas, and with him was his daughter. Anas said: A woman came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: 'O Prophet of Allah, do you have any need of me?' His daughter said: 'How little shame she had!' He said: 'She is better than you; she desired the Prophet, so she offered herself to him.'"
Al-Bukhari alone narrated it, from the hadith of Marhum ibn Abd al-Aziz [al-Attar], from Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas, with the same wording. [Musnad Ahmad (3/268); Sahih al-Bukhari no. 5120.]
Ahmad also said: Abdullah ibn Bakr told us: Sinan ibn Rabi'ah told us: from al-Hadrami, from Anas ibn Malik, that a woman came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have a daughter, such-and-such," and she described her beauty and attractiveness, "and I have preferred you over her." He said: "I have accepted her." She kept praising her until she mentioned that she had never been ill and had never complained of anything. He said: "I have no need of your daughter." They did not narrate it. [Musnad Ahmad (3/155).]
Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us: Mansur ibn Abi Muzahim told us: Ibn Abi al-Wadah, meaning Muhammad ibn Muslim, told us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, who said: The one who gave herself to the Prophet ﷺ was Khawlah bint Hakim. [Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra (7/55) through Mansur ibn Abi Muzahim, with the same chain.]
Ibn Wahb said, from Sa'id ibn Abd al-Rahman and Ibn Abi al-Zinad, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father: that Khawlah bint Hakim ibn al-Awqas, of Banu Sulaym, was among those women who gave themselves to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. [Al-Tabari in his Tafsir (22/23).]
In another report from him, from Sa'id ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Hisham, from his father: "We used to talk about how Khawlah bint Hakim had given herself to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and she was a righteous woman." [Al-Tabari in his Tafsir (22/23).]
It is possible that Umm Sulaym is Khawlah bint Hakim, or that she is another woman.
Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ahmasi told us: Waki' told us: Musa ibn Ubaydah told us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, Umar ibn al-Hakam and Abdullah ibn Ubaydah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married thirteen women: six from Quraysh: Khadijah, 'A'ishah, Hafsah, Umm Habibah, Sawdah and Umm Salamah; three from Banu 'Amir ibn Sa'sa'ah; two women from Banu Hilal ibn 'Amir: Maymunah bint al-Harith, who is the one who gave herself to the Prophet ﷺ, and Zaynab Umm al-Masakin, a woman from Banu Abi Bakr ibn Kilab of the Qartaʼ, who is the one who chose this world; a woman from Banu al-Jawn, who is the one who sought refuge from him; Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyyah; and the two captives: Safiyyah bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab, and Juwayriyah bint al-Harith ibn 'Amr ibn al-Mustaliq al-Khuza'iyyah. [Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it in al-Musannaf (5/270) through Waki' with the wording: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married a woman from Banu al-Jawn, then divorced her, and she is the one who sought refuge from him."]
Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah said, from Qatadah, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning ﴿And a believing woman, if she gives herself to the Prophet﴾: "She is Maymunah bint al-Harith."
This report has a break in its chain (inqita'): it is mursal. The well-known view is that Zaynab, who was called Umm al-Masakin, is Zaynab bint Khuzaymah al-Ansariyyah, and she died during the Prophet's ﷺ lifetime. Allah knows best.
The point of all this is that those women who gave themselves to the Prophet ﷺ were many, as al-Bukhari said: Zakariyya ibn Yahya told us: Abu Usamah told us, saying: Hisham ibn 'Urwah narrated to us, from his father, from 'A'ishah, who said: "I used to be jealous of those women who gave themselves to the Prophet ﷺ, and I would say: 'Does a woman give herself?' Then when Allah revealed: ﴿You may postpone whom you will of them and take to you whom you will, and whoever you desire of those you have set aside, there is no blame upon you﴾, I said: 'I see that your Lord only hastens to your desire.'" [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4788.]
Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Ali ibn al-Husayn told us: Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Ju'fi told us: Yunus ibn Bukayr told us, from 'Anbasah ibn al-Azhar, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "There was no woman with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ who had given herself to him."
Ibn Jarir narrated it from Abu Kurayb, from Yunus ibn Bukayr. [Tafsir al-Tabari (22/17).] That is, he did not accept any of those who gave themselves to him, even though that was permitted for him and specific to him, because it was subject to his will, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿if the Prophet wishes to take her in marriage﴾, meaning: if he chooses that.
* *
His saying: ﴿exclusively for you, apart from the believers﴾. 'Ikrimah said: This means that the woman who was given (in this way) is not lawful for anyone other than you. Even if a woman gave herself to a man, she would not be lawful for him until he gave her something. Mujahid, al-Sha'bi and others said the same.
That is: if a woman entrusts herself to a man (tafwid), then once he consummates the marriage with her, she is owed the mahr al-mithl (the customary dowry of women like her) from him, as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled in the case of Bar'a bint Washiq, when she had entrusted herself (in marriage without a set dowry). When her husband died, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that she was owed the customary dowry. Death and consummation are equal in establishing the dowry and making the mahr al-mithl obligatory for a woman who entrusted herself to a man other than the Prophet ﷺ. As for him, peace be upon him, nothing is obligatory for a woman who entrusted herself to him, even if he consummated with her, because he was permitted to marry without a dowry, without a guardian (wali), and without witnesses, as in the story of Zaynab bint Jahsh, may Allah be pleased with her. For this reason Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿exclusively for you, apart from the believers﴾, said: "It means that there is no woman who gives herself to a man without a guardian and without a dowry, except for the Prophet ﷺ."

[And His Exalted saying: ﴿We have certainly known what We have enjoined upon them concerning their wives and what their right hands possess﴾] [[Addition from manuscripts T and A.]] Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Mujahid, al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ibn Jarir said, regarding His saying ﴿We have certainly known what We have enjoined upon them concerning their wives﴾: that is, [the restriction] to four free wives, and whatever concubines they wished [[In manuscript T: "and whatever He wished".]], and the conditions of the guardian (wali), the bridal gift (mahr) and the witnesses for them, and they are the community (ummah). "And We have granted you dispensation in that, so We did not obligate you to any of it," ﴿so that there will be no discomfort upon you, and Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Bishr [in A: "Bashir"] narrated to us: Hisham ibn 'Urwah narrated to us, from his father [in T: "Imam Ahmad narrated with his chain"], from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that she used to rebuke the women who had given themselves to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). She said: "Is a woman not ashamed to offer herself without a dowry?" Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿You may postpone whom you will of them, and take to yourself whom you will, and there is no blame on you if you seek [back] any whom you had set aside﴾. She said: "I see that your Lord hastens to fulfil your desire."

It has already been mentioned that al-Bukhari narrated it from the hadith of Abu Usamah, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah. This indicates that what is meant by His words ﴿You may postpone﴾, i.e., delay, ﴿whom you will of them﴾, i.e., of those women who had given themselves, ﴿and take to yourself whom you will﴾, i.e., whomever you wish you may accept, and whomever you wish you may reject. And whomever you rejected, you also have the choice concerning her afterward: if you wish, you may return to her and take her to yourself. Therefore He said: ﴿and there is no blame on you if you seek [back] any whom you had set aside﴾. 'Amir al-Sha'bi said regarding His words ﴿You may postpone whom you will of them and take to yourself whom you will﴾: "They were women who had given themselves to the Prophet (ﷺ). He consummated [the marriage] with some of them and deferred some of them, and they were not married after him. Among them was Umm Sharik."

Others said: Rather, what is meant by His words ﴿You may postpone whom you will of them and take to yourself whom you will﴾ is: of your wives, there is no harm upon you in leaving off the equal division (qasm) among them, so you may give precedence to whom you will, delay whom you will, have intercourse with whom you will, and leave whom you will.

This is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan, Qatadah, Abu Razin, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and others. Despite this, he (may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him) used to divide [his time] equally among them. Therefore a group of jurists among the Shafi'ites and others held that equal division was not obligatory for him (may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him), and they used this noble verse as evidence.

Al-Bukhari said: Habban ibn Musa narrated to us: 'Abdullah, that is Ibn al-Mubarak, narrated to us: 'Asim al-Ahwal informed us, from Mu'adhah, from 'A'ishah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to seek permission regarding the day of whichever of us [wives] he wished, after this verse was revealed: ﴿You may postpone whom you will of them and take to yourself whom you will, and there is no blame on you if you seek [back] any whom you had set aside﴾. I said to her: "What did you used to say?" She said: "I used to say: If that is up to me, then I do not wish, O Messenger of Allah, to prefer anyone over you."

This hadith from her indicates that what is meant by that is the non-obligation of equal division. Her first hadith implies that the verse was revealed concerning the women who had given themselves. From here, Ibn Jarir chose that the verse is general, covering both the women who had given themselves and the wives who were with him, that he has the choice regarding them: if he wishes he may divide equally, and if he wishes he need not divide equally. What he chose is good, sound, and strong, and in it there is a reconciliation between the hadiths. Therefore He, the Exalted, said: ﴿That is more suitable that their eyes may be comforted and they will not grieve, and they will be pleased with what you give them, all of them﴾. That is: when they know that Allah has removed from you the blame regarding equal division, so if you wish you may divide equally, and if you wish you need not divide equally, and there is no blame on you in whichever of these you do. Then, even so, you divide [your time] among them by your own choice, not as an obligation. So they rejoiced at this, were delighted by it, acknowledged your goodness in it, and recognized your favour toward them in your dividing for them, your equality among them, your fairness toward them, and your justice concerning them.

* *

His words ﴿And Allah knows what is in your hearts﴾, i.e., of inclination toward some of them over others, which cannot be prevented, as Imam Ahmad said:

Yazid narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from 'Abdullah ibn Yazid, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to divide [his time] among his wives equally, and he would be just, then he would say: "O Allah, this is my division in what I control, so do not blame me for what You control and I do not control."

The four authors of the Sunan narrated it from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah [in the Musnad (6/144), Sunan Abi Dawud no. 2134, Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 1140, Sunan al-Nasa'i (7/63), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. 1971]. Abu Dawud added after his words "do not blame me for what You control" and "I do not control": i.e., the heart. Its chain is sound, and all its narrators are trustworthy. Therefore He followed that with His words ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing﴾, i.e., of the hidden contents of the inner selves, ﴿Forbearing﴾, i.e., He is forbearing and forgiving.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 33, verse 52:

A number of scholars, including Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, Ibn Zayd, Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari), and others, have mentioned that this verse was revealed as a reward for the wives of the Prophet ﷺ and as an expression of Allah's pleasure with them, for their good conduct in choosing Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Abode when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave them the choice, as was mentioned earlier in the verse. So when they chose the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, their reward was that [Allah] [[Addition from manuscripts T and A.]] restricted him to them and forbade him to marry anyone other than them, or to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty pleased him, except for the slave-women and concubines, for there was no restriction on him regarding them. Then, He, exalted is He, lifted the restriction [[In manuscript T: "al-haraj" (the hardship).]] concerning that, abrogated the ruling of this verse, and permitted him to marry [[In manuscript A: "al-tazwij".]], but he did not marry after that, so that the favour would belong to the Messenger ﷺ over them.

Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr, from 'Ata', from 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not die until Allah made lawful for him women.

He also narrated it through the route of Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', from 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr [[In manuscript A: "from 'Umayr ibn 'Ubayd".]], from 'Aishah. It was also related by al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i in their Sunan.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abd al-Malik ibn Shaybah narrated to us, Umar ibn Abi Bakr narrated to me, al-Mughirah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Hizami [[In manuscript A: "al-Khuza'i".]] narrated to me, from Abu al-Nadr, the client of Umar ibn 'Ubayd Allah [[In manuscript A: "'Abd Allah".]], from 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb ibn Zam'ah, from Umm Salamah, that she said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not die until Allah made lawful for him to marry from among women whomever he wished, except a woman within the prohibited degrees. This is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿You may postpone whom you wish of them and take to yourself whom you wish﴾.

Accordingly, this verse was made to abrogate the one that comes after it in recitation, like the two verses on the waiting period for widowhood in al-Baqarah; the first one abrogates the one that follows it. And Allah knows best.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of the verse, ﴿Women are not lawful for you after this﴾, is: after what We have mentioned to you of the description of the women whom We made lawful for you, namely your wives whose dowries you have given, and those whom your right hand possesses, and the daughters of your paternal uncles and aunts and of your maternal uncles and aunts, and those who emigrated with you, and a woman who believes and gives herself to the Prophet; and any other categories of women are not lawful for you. This is narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Dahhak (in one narration), Abu Razin (in one narration from him), Abu Salih, al-Hasan, Qatadah (in one narration), al-Suddi, and others.

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub narrated to us, Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, Muhammad ibn Abi Musa narrated to me, from Ziyad, a man of the Ansar [[In manuscript T: "Ibn Jarir narrated with his chain from a man of the Ansar."]], who said: I said to Ubayy ibn Ka'b: Do you see, if the wives of the Prophet ﷺ had died, would it not have been lawful for him to marry? He said: What would prevent him from that? I said: His saying: ﴿Women are not lawful for you after this﴾. He said: Allah only made lawful for him a certain kind of women, when He said: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful for you your wives﴾ up to His saying: ﴿if a woman gives herself to the Prophet﴾. Then it was said to him: ﴿Women are not lawful for you after this﴾ [[In manuscripts T and A: "Women are not lawful for you."]].

'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad narrated it through several routes, from Dawud, with the same wording [[Tafsir al-Tabari (22/21) and Zawa'id al-Musnad (5/132).]]. Al-Tirmidhi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade certain categories of women, except those who were among the believing emigrant women, by His saying: ﴿Women are not lawful for you after this, nor is it lawful to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty pleases you, except what your right hand possesses﴾ [[In manuscript A: "Women are not lawful for you."]]. So Allah made lawful your believing slave-girls, ﴿and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet﴾, and He forbade every woman of a religion other than Islam. Then He said: ﴿Whoever disbelieves in the faith, his deed has become void, and he will be in the Hereafter among the losers﴾. And He said: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful for you your wives whose dowries you have given, and what your right hand possesses [[In manuscript A, after this: "from what Allah has bestowed upon you."]]﴾ up to His saying: ﴿exclusively for you, apart from the believers﴾, and He forbade all other categories of women [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3215, where he said: "This is a good hadith; we only know it from the hadith of 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram." He said: I heard Ahmad ibn al-Hasan say: Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: There is no harm in the hadith of 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram from Shahr ibn Hawshab.]].

Mujahid said: ﴿Women are not lawful for you after this﴾ means: after what has been named for you, neither a Muslim woman, nor a Jewish woman, nor a Christian woman, nor any disbelieving woman.

Abu Salih said: ﴿Women are not lawful for you after this﴾: He was commanded not to marry a Bedouin woman or a foreign woman [[In manuscript A: "an Arab woman."]], and then he could marry from the women of Tihamah, and whomever he wished of the daughters of paternal uncles and aunts and of maternal uncles and aunts, even three hundred if he wished.

'Ikrimah said: ﴿Women are not lawful for you after this﴾ means: those whom Allah has named.

Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, chose that the verse is general, covering the categories of women mentioned and the women who were in his marriage, who were nine. What he said is good, and it is probably what many of the early scholars whom we have quoted intended, for many of them are reported to have said both this and that, and there is no contradiction. And Allah knows best.

Then Ibn Jarir raised an objection to himself, regarding what is reported: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ divorced Hafsah and then took her back, and that he resolved to separate from Sawdah until she gave her day to 'Aishah. He then answered that this was before the revelation of: ﴿Women are not lawful for you after this, nor is it lawful to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty pleases you﴾. What he said, that this was before the revelation of the verse, is correct, but there is no need for that, for the verse only indicates that he may not marry anyone other than those in his marriage, and that he may not exchange them for others; it does not indicate that he may not divorce any one of them without exchanging her. And Allah knows best.

As for the case of Sawdah, it is in the Sahih from 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, and it is the occasion of revelation for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if a woman fears ill-treatment or aversion from her husband, there is no blame upon them if they make terms of settlement between them; and settlement is best﴾ [al-Nisa': 128], the verse [[See the takhrij of this hadith under the commentary on verse 128 of surah al-Nisa'.]].

As for the case of Hafsah, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih related it through several routes from Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'idah, from Salih ibn Salih ibn Hayy, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, from Umar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ divorced Hafsah and then took her back. This chain is strong [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 2283; Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/213); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 2016.]].

Abu Ya'la al-Hafiz said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Umar, who said: Umar entered upon Hafsah while she was weeping, and he said: What makes you weep? Perhaps the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has divorced you? He had indeed divorced you once and then took you back for my sake. By Allah, if he has divorced you again, I will never speak to you again. Its narrators are on the conditions of the two Sahihs [[Musnad Abi Ya'la (1/160).]].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿nor is it lawful to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty pleases you﴾, He forbade him from taking additional wives beyond them, or from divorcing any one of them and exchanging her for another, except what his right hand possesses.

The hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar related a relevant hadith, which he mentioned here, saying:

Ibrahim ibn Nasr narrated to us, Malik ibn Isma'il narrated to us, 'Abd al-Salam ibn Harb narrated to us, from Ishaq ibn 'Abd Allah al-Qurashi, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar [[In manuscript T: "al-Bazzar narrated with his chain."]], from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The custom in the Jahiliyyah was that a man would say to another man: Exchange your wife with me and I will exchange mine with you; that is, you give up your wife to me and I give up my wife to you. So Allah revealed: ﴿nor is it lawful to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty pleases you﴾. He said: 'Uyaynah ibn Hisn [[In manuscript A: "'Uyaynah al-Fazari."]] entered upon the Prophet ﷺ while 'Aishah was with him, and he entered without permission. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Where is the seeking of permission?" He said: O Messenger of Allah, I have not sought permission from any man of Mudar since I came of age. Then he said: Who is this humayra' beside you? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "This is 'Aishah, Mother of the Believers." He said: Shall I not give up for you the best of creation? [[In manuscript T: "He said: Give her up for me and I will give up for you the best of creation." In manuscript A: "He said: I will give up for you the best of creation."]] He said: "O 'Uyaynah, Allah has forbidden that." When he left, 'Aishah said: Who is this? He said: This is a foolish man who is obeyed, and indeed, as you see, he is the chief of his people.

Then al-Bazzar said: In its chain is Ishaq [[In manuscript T: "Al-Bazzar said: In its chain is Ishaq."]] ibn 'Abd Allah, who is very weak in narration. We mentioned it only because we did not know it except through this route, and we explained the defect in it [[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 2251 (Kashf al-Astar). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/92): "In it is Ishaq ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Farwah, who is abandoned (matruk)."]].

This is the verse of the hijab, and it contains legal rulings and etiquette. Its revelation coincided with what ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) had said, as is established in the two Sahihs (the two authentic collections, al-Bukhari and Muslim) from him, that he said: "I agreed with my Lord in three matters. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, why do you not take the station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer?' So Allah revealed: ﴿And take from the station of Ibrahim a place of prayer﴾ [al-Baqarah: 125]. And I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, indeed your wives are entered upon by the righteous and the wicked, so why do you not veil them?' So Allah revealed the verse of the hijab. And I said to the wives of the Prophet ﷺ when they conspired against him in jealousy: ﴿It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will substitute for him wives better than you﴾ [al-Tahrim: 5]; and it was revealed just as I had said."
[Footnote: Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 402.]

In a narration of Muslim there is mention of the captives of Badr, and this is a fourth occasion.

Al-Bukhari said: Musaddad narrated to us, from Yahya, from Humayd, that Anas ibn Malik said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab said: "O Messenger of Allah, the righteous and the wicked enter upon you. Would you not command the Mothers of the Believers to observe the hijab?" So Allah revealed the verse of the hijab.
[Footnote: Sahih Muslim, no. 2399.]

The time of its revelation was on the morning of the wedding (ʿurs) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with Zaynab bint Jahsh, whose marriage Allah Himself had arranged. That was in Dhu al-Qaʿdah of the fifth year, according to the opinion of Qatadah, al-Waqidi and others.

Abu ʿUbaydah Maʿmar ibn al-Muthanna and Khalifah ibn Khayyat claimed that it was in the third year, but Allah knows best.

Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Raqashi narrated to us, Muʿtamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, I heard my father, Abu Mijlaz narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married Zaynab bint Jahsh, he invited the people, and they ate, then sat conversing. He appeared as if he was preparing to rise, but they did not rise. When he saw that, he got up, and whoever was going to get up got up, but three men remained seated. The Prophet ﷺ came to enter, but the people were still sitting. Then they got up and left, so I went and informed the Prophet ﷺ that they had gone. He came and entered, and I went to enter, but he placed the curtain (ḥijāb) between me and him. Then Allah revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet...﴾ to the end of the verse.

He also narrated it in another place, and Muslim and al-Nasaʾi narrated it through several routes from Muʿtamir ibn Sulayman, with the same wording.
[Footnote: Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 4791, 6239, 6271; Sahih Muslim, no. 1428; al-Nasaʾi in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 11420.]

Then al-Bukhari alone narrated it from the hadith of Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him), in similar terms.
[Footnote: Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4792.]

Then al-Bukhari said: Abu Maʿmar narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Warith narrated to us, ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Suhayb narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Prophet ﷺ held his wedding feast (bunī) with Zaynab bint Jahsh, with bread and meat. I sent out a summoner to the food, so a group would come, eat and leave, then another group would come, eat and leave. I kept inviting until I could find no one left to invite. I said: "O Prophet of Allah, I cannot find anyone to invite." He said: "Lift up your food." Three men remained in the house conversing. The Prophet ﷺ went out and walked to the room of ʿAʾishah and said: "Peace be upon you, people of the house, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings." She said: "And upon you be peace and the mercy of Allah. How did you find your family? May Allah bless you." So he went around to the rooms of all his wives, saying to each what he had said to ʿAʾishah, and they said to him what ʿAʾishah had said. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned, and there were the three men still conversing in the house. The Prophet ﷺ was extremely shy, so he went out walking toward the room of ʿAʾishah. I do not know whether I informed him or whether he was informed that the people had left. He returned until he placed one foot on the threshold of the door, inside, and the other outside, and he let the curtain fall between me and him. Then the verse of the hijab was revealed.
[Footnote: Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4793; al-Nasaʾi in al-Yawm wa al-Laylah, no. 10101.]

Al-Bukhari alone among the authors of the Six Books narrated it from the hadith of ʿAbd al-Warith.

Then he narrated it from Ishaq, that is Ibn Mansur, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Bakr al-Sahmi, from Humayd, from Anas, in similar terms, and he said "two men" [instead of three]. Al-Bukhari alone narrated it through this route. It has already been mentioned among the individual narrations of Muslim from the hadith of Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah, from Thabit, from Anas.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu al-Muzaffar narrated to us, Jaʿfar ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from al-Jaʿd (Abu ʿUthman al-Yashkuri), from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ held a wedding (aʿrasa) with one of his wives. Umm Sulaym prepared ḥays (a dish of dates, butter and cheese), then placed it in a bowl and said: "Go with this to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, convey my greetings to him, and tell him that this is a little from us for him." Anas said: At that time people were in hardship. So I came to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, Umm Sulaym has sent this to you, and she conveys her greetings to you and says: 'Tell him this is a little from us for him.'" He looked at it, then said: "Put it down." I put it in a corner of the house. Then he said: "Go and call for me so-and-so and so-and-so," and he named many men, and he said: "And whomever you meet of the Muslims." So I called those who had been named to me, and whomever I met of the Muslims. I came back, and the house, the bench (ṣuffah) and the room were full of people. I said: "O Abu ʿUthman, how many were they?" He said: "They were about three hundred." Anas said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "Bring it." So I brought it to him. He placed his hand upon it, supplicated, and said: "Mā shāʾ Allāh (what Allah wills)." Then he said: "Let them sit in circles of ten, and let them mention the name of Allah, and let each person eat from what is in front of him." So they began mentioning the name of Allah and eating, until they had all eaten. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "Lift it up." I came and took the bowl, and I do not know whether it was fuller when I placed it down or when I picked it up. He said: Some men stayed behind, conversing in the house of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the wife of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ whom he had consummated with (dakhala bihā) was with them, turning her face toward the wall. They prolonged the conversation, and this troubled the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and he was the most shy of people. Had they been informed, that would have been difficult for them. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ got up and went out and greeted his rooms and his wives. When they saw him coming, they assumed they had burdened him, so they hurried to the door and left. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and let the curtain fall and entered the house, while I was in the room. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained in his house briefly, and Allah revealed the Qur'an to him. He came out reciting this verse: ﴿O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless permission is given to you for a meal, without waiting for its readiness; but when you are invited, then enter; and when you have eaten, disperse without seeking to remain for conversation...﴾ up to His words: ﴿...and Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing.﴾ Anas said: He recited them to me before the people, so I am the one among the people most recently acquainted with them.
[Footnote: Sahih Muslim, no. 1428; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3218; Sunan al-Nasaʾi (6/136).]

Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih." Al-Bukhari suspended it (taʿlīq) in the Book of Marriage, saying:
Ibrahim ibn Tahman narrated, from al-Jaʿd Abi ʿUthman, from Anas, and he mentioned something similar.
[Footnote: Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5163.]

Muslim also narrated it from Muhammad ibn Rafiʿ, from ʿAbd al-Razzaq, from Maʿmar, from al-Jaʿd, in the same form.
[Footnote: Sahih Muslim, no. 1428.] This hadith was also narrated by ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, from Sharik, from Bayan ibn Bishr, from Anas, in similar terms.

Al-Bukhari and al-Tirmidhi narrated it through two other routes, from Bayan ibn Bishr al-Ahmasi al-Kufi, from Anas, in similar terms.
[Footnote: Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5170; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3219.]

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it from the hadith of Abu Nadrah al-ʿAbdi, from Anas ibn Malik, in similar terms. Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of ʿAmr ibn Saʿid, and from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from Anas, in similar terms.
[Footnote: Tafsir al-Tabari (22/27).]

Imam Ahmad said: Bahz and Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, both saying: Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: When the ʿiddah of Zaynab ended, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Zayd: "Go and mention her to me." He said: So Zayd went until he came to her, and she was kneading her dough. When I saw her, she became great in my heart... and he mentioned the full hadith, as we have already cited it at the words: ﴿So when Zayd had no more need of her...﴾ And he added at its end, after the words: "and he admonished the people with what they had been admonished with." Hashim said in his narration: ﴿Do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless permission is given to you for a meal, without waiting for its readiness; but when you are invited, then enter; and when you have eaten, disperse, and do not remain for conversation. Indeed, that would cause harm to the Prophet, and he is shy of you, but Allah is not shy of the truth.﴾
[Footnote: Musnad Ahmad (3/195); Sahih Muslim, no. 1428; Sunan al-Nasaʾi (6/79).]
Muslim and al-Nasaʾi narrated it from the hadith of Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah, in the same form. [Text in the manuscripts: "Jaʿfar ibn Sulayman," corrected from the other copies and Muslim.]

Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, the nephew of Ibn Wahb, narrated to me; my uncle ʿAbd Allah ibn Wahb narrated to me; Yunus narrated to me from al-Zuhri, from ʿUrwah, from ʿAʾishah, who said: The wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to go out at night when they relieved themselves, to al-Manasiʿ, which was a wide open area. ʿUmar used to say to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Veil your wives." But the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not do it. Then Sawdah bint Zamʿah, the wife of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, went out, and she was a tall woman. ʿUmar called to her in a loud voice: "We have recognised you, O Sawdah," out of eagerness that the hijab would be revealed. She said: Then Allah revealed the hijab.
[Footnote: Tafsir al-Tabari (22/28).]

That is how it occurs in this narration. But the well-known account is that this happened after the hijab had been revealed, as Imam Ahmad, al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated from the hadith of Hisham ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿAʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: Sawdah went out after the hijab had been imposed, for a need of hers. She was a large woman who could not be concealed from anyone who knew her. ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab saw her and said: "O Sawdah, by Allah, you are not hidden from us, so look how you go out." She said: So I turned back, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in my house, having his evening meal, and in his hand was a bone with meat (ʿaraq). I entered and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I went out for some need of mine, and ʿUmar said to me such-and-such." She said: Then Allah revealed to him, and when that revelation was lifted from him, the bone was still in his hand, he had not put it down. He said: "Indeed it has been permitted for you to go out for your needs." This is the wording of al-Bukhari.
[Footnote: Musnad Ahmad (6/56); Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4795; Sahih Muslim, no. 2170.]

Tafsir Ibn Kathir on Surah al-Ahzab, verses 53–54 (part 2 of 2)

So His saying: ﴿Do not enter the houses of the Prophet﴾ prohibits the believers from entering the dwellings of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ without permission, as they used to do in their houses during the Jahiliyyah (the Age of Ignorance) and at the beginning of Islam. Then Allah became jealous (ghara) for this Ummah and commanded them regarding this, and that is part of His honouring this Ummah. For this reason the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Beware of entering upon women" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (5232), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2172), from the hadith of Uqbah ibn Amir, may Allah be pleased with him.]].

Then He made an exception from this, saying: ﴿Except when you are given permission for a meal, without waiting for its preparation (ghayra nazirina inahu).﴾

Mujahid, Qatadah and others said: that is, without anticipating its being cooked and ready; i.e., do not watch for the food until, when it is nearly ready, you present yourselves for entry. This is because Allah dislikes and censures such conduct. This is evidence for the prohibition of tatfil (gate-crashing or uninvited sponging on others' food), which the Arabs call al-Dayfan, and al-Khatib al-Baghdadi (al-Khatib al-Baghdadi) authored a book on this subject, condemning the tufayliyyun (gate-crashers), and he mentioned from their reports many things whose citation would be lengthy.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿But when you are invited, then enter; and when you have eaten, disperse﴾. In Sahih Muslim, from Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When one of you invites his brother, let him accept, whether it is a wedding feast or otherwise" [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1429).]]. Its origin is in the two Sahihs, and also in the Sahih, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "If I were invited to a foreleg (dhira') I would accept, and if a shank (kura') were presented to me I would accept it. When you have finished what you were invited to, lighten the burden on the people of the house and disperse through the land" [[In Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (5768), from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.]].

For this reason He said: ﴿Nor seeking to remain for conversation﴾, i.e., as occurred with those three men whom conversation carried away, so that they forgot themselves, until that troubled the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, that was troubling the Prophet, and he is shy of you﴾ [[Followed in A by: "But Allah is not shy of the truth."]].

It was also said: the meaning is that your entering his home without his permission used to distress him and cause him harm, but he disliked to forbid them from that out of his great modesty (may peace be upon him), until Allah sent down the prohibition concerning it. For this reason He said: ﴿And Allah is not shy of the truth﴾, i.e., for this reason He forbade you from that and restrained you from it.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a screen﴾. That is: just as I forbade you to enter upon them, likewise do not look at them at all. Even if one of you has a need he wishes to obtain from them, let him not look at them, and let him not ask them for any need except from behind a screen.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: My father related to us, Ibn Abi Umar related to us, Sufyan related to us, from Mis'ar, from Musa ibn Abi Kathir, from Mujahid, from Aishah, who said: I was eating hays (a mixture of dates, butter and cheese) with the Prophet ﷺ from a wooden bowl, when Umar passed by and he called him, and his finger touched my finger. He said: "Hass" (or "Awwih") — "If he were obeyed regarding you (women), no eye would see you." Then the screen (hijab) was revealed [[Also narrated by al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (11419), by way of Zakariyya ibn Yahya from Ibn Abi Umar, with the same chain.]].

﴿That is purer for your hearts and their hearts﴾: that is, this which I have commanded you and legislated for you regarding the hijab is purer and more wholesome.

* *

His saying: ﴿And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah, nor to marry his wives after him, ever. Indeed, that would be an enormity in the sight of Allah﴾. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: Ali ibn al-Husayn related to us, Muhammad ibn Abi Hammad related to us, Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah﴾, he said: It was revealed concerning a man who intended to marry one of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ. A man said to Sufyan: Was it Aishah? He said: They have mentioned that.

Likewise said Muqatil ibn Hayyan and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam. And he mentioned with his chain from al-Suddi that the one who resolved upon that was Talhah ibn Ubaid Allah, may Allah be pleased with him, until the warning against that prohibition was revealed. For this reason the scholars are unanimous that whoever among the wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed away while married to him, it is forbidden for anyone else to marry her after him, because they are his wives in this world and the Hereafter and the Mothers of the Believers, as has already been mentioned. They differed concerning one who consummated marriage with a woman and then divorced her during his lifetime: is it lawful for another to marry her? There are two opinions, the basis of which is: does she fall under the generality of His saying ﴿after him﴾ or not? As for one who married her and then divorced her before consummation, we know of no dispute regarding its being lawful for another in such a case, and Allah knows best.

Ibn Jarir narrated: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to me, Abd al-Wahhab related to us, Dawud related to us, from Amir: that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ died while he had taken Qaylah daughter of al-Ash'ath (i.e., Ibn Qays) as a wife, and Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl married her after that, which caused Abu Bakr great distress. Umar said to him: "O Caliph of the Messenger of Allah, she is not among his wives; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not give her the choice, nor did he veil her, and Allah has cleared her of him through the apostasy she committed along with her people." He said: Abu Bakr was reassured and calmed, may Allah be pleased with them both [[Tafsir al-Tabari (22/29).]].

Allah, may He be blessed and exalted, has magnified this and emphasized it and threatened for it by His saying: ﴿Indeed, that would be an enormity in the sight of Allah﴾. Then He said: ﴿Whether you show a thing or conceal it, indeed Allah is ever Knowing of all things﴾, i.e., whatever your hearts harbour and your inner selves conceal, Allah knows it, for nothing is hidden from Him: ﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal﴾ [Ghafir: 19].

This is the verse of the hijab, and it contains legal rulings and etiquette. Its revelation coincided with what ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) had said, as is established in the two Sahihs (the two authentic collections, al-Bukhari and Muslim) from him, that he said: "I agreed with my Lord in three matters. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, why do you not take the station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer?' So Allah revealed: ﴿And take from the station of Ibrahim a place of prayer﴾ [al-Baqarah: 125]. And I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, indeed your wives are entered upon by the righteous and the wicked, so why do you not veil them?' So Allah revealed the verse of the hijab. And I said to the wives of the Prophet ﷺ when they conspired against him in jealousy: ﴿It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will substitute for him wives better than you﴾ [al-Tahrim: 5]; and it was revealed just as I had said."
[Footnote: Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 402.]

In a narration of Muslim there is mention of the captives of Badr, and this is a fourth occasion.

Al-Bukhari said: Musaddad narrated to us, from Yahya, from Humayd, that Anas ibn Malik said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab said: "O Messenger of Allah, the righteous and the wicked enter upon you. Would you not command the Mothers of the Believers to observe the hijab?" So Allah revealed the verse of the hijab.
[Footnote: Sahih Muslim, no. 2399.]

Abu ʿUbaydah Maʿmar ibn al-Muthanna and Khalifah ibn Khayyat claimed that it was in the third year, but Allah knows best.

Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Raqashi narrated to us, Muʿtamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, I heard my father, Abu Mijlaz narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married Zaynab bint Jahsh, he invited the people, and they ate, then sat conversing. He appeared as if he was preparing to rise, but they did not rise. When he saw that, he got up, and whoever was going to get up got up, but three men remained seated. The Prophet ﷺ came to enter, but the people were still sitting. Then they got up and left, so I went and informed the Prophet ﷺ that they had gone. He also narrated it in another place, and Muslim and al-Nasaʾi narrated it through several routes from Muʿtamir ibn Sulayman, with the same wording.
[Footnote: Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 4791, 6239, 6271; Sahih Muslim, no. 1428; al-Nasaʾi in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 11420.]

Then al-Bukhari alone narrated it from the hadith of Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him), in similar terms.
[Footnote: Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4792.]

Then al-Bukhari said: Abu Maʿmar narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Warith narrated to us, ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Suhayb narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Prophet ﷺ held his wedding feast (bunī) with Zaynab bint Jahsh, with bread and meat. I sent out a summoner to the food, so a group would come, eat and leave, then another group would come, eat and leave. I kept inviting until I could find no one left to invite. [Footnote: Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4793; al-Nasaʾi in al-Yawm wa al-Laylah, no. 10101.]

Al-Bukhari alone among the authors of the Six Books narrated it from the hadith of ʿAbd al-Warith.

Then he narrated it from Ishaq, that is Ibn Mansur, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Bakr al-Sahmi, from Humayd, from Anas, in similar terms, and he said "two men" [instead of three]. Al-Bukhari alone narrated it through this route. It has already been mentioned among the individual narrations of Muslim from the hadith of Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah, from Thabit, from Anas.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu al-Muzaffar narrated to us, Jaʿfar ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from al-Jaʿd (Abu ʿUthman al-Yashkuri), from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ held a wedding (aʿrasa) with one of his wives.
