I said: "O Abu ʿUthman, how many were they?" He said: "They were about three hundred." Anas said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "Bring it." So I brought it to him. He placed his hand upon it, supplicated, and said: "Mā shāʾ Allāh (what Allah wills)." Then he said: "Let them sit in circles of ten, and let them mention the name of Allah, and let each person eat from what is in front of him." So they began mentioning the name of Allah and eating, until they had all eaten. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "Lift it up." He came out reciting this verse: ﴿O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless permission is given to you for a meal, without waiting for its readiness; but when you are invited, then enter; and when you have eaten, disperse without seeking to remain for conversation...﴾ up to His words: ﴿...and Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing.﴾ Anas said: He recited them to me before the people, so I am the one among the people most recently acquainted with them.
[Footnote: Sahih Muslim, no. 1428; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3218; Sunan al-Nasaʾi (6/136).]

Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih." Al-Bukhari suspended it (taʿlīq) in the Book of Marriage, saying:
Ibrahim ibn Tahman narrated, from al-Jaʿd Abi ʿUthman, from Anas, and he mentioned something similar.
[Footnote: Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5163.]

Muslim also narrated it from Muhammad ibn Rafiʿ, from ʿAbd al-Razzaq, from Maʿmar, from al-Jaʿd, in the same form.
[Footnote: Sahih Muslim, no. 1428.] This hadith was also narrated by ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, from Sharik, from Bayan ibn Bishr, from Anas, in similar terms.

Al-Bukhari and al-Tirmidhi narrated it through two other routes, from Bayan ibn Bishr al-Ahmasi al-Kufi, from Anas, in similar terms.
[Footnote: Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5170; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3219.]

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it from the hadith of Abu Nadrah al-ʿAbdi, from Anas ibn Malik, in similar terms. Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of ʿAmr ibn Saʿid, and from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from Anas, in similar terms.
[Footnote: Tafsir al-Tabari (22/27).]

Imam Ahmad said: Bahz and Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, both saying: Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: When the ʿiddah of Zaynab ended, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Zayd: "Go and mention her to me." He said: So Zayd went until he came to her, and she was kneading her dough. When I saw her, she became great in my heart... and he mentioned the full hadith, as we have already cited it at the words: ﴿So when Zayd had no more need of her...﴾ And he added at its end, after the words: "and he admonished the people with what they had been admonished with." Hashim said in his narration: ﴿Do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless permission is given to you for a meal, without waiting for its readiness; but when you are invited, then enter; and when you have eaten, disperse, and do not remain for conversation. Indeed, that would cause harm to the Prophet, and he is shy of you, but Allah is not shy of the truth.﴾
[Footnote: Musnad Ahmad (3/195); Sahih Muslim, no. 1428; Sunan al-Nasaʾi (6/79).]
Muslim and al-Nasaʾi narrated it from the hadith of Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah, in the same form. [Text in the manuscripts: "Jaʿfar ibn Sulayman," corrected from the other copies and Muslim.]

Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, the nephew of Ibn Wahb, narrated to me; my uncle ʿAbd Allah ibn Wahb narrated to me; Yunus narrated to me from al-Zuhri, from ʿUrwah, from ʿAʾishah, who said: The wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to go out at night when they relieved themselves, to al-Manasiʿ, which was a wide open area. ʿUmar used to say to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Veil your wives." But the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not do it. Then Sawdah bint Zamʿah, the wife of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, went out, and she was a tall woman. ʿUmar called to her in a loud voice: "We have recognised you, O Sawdah," out of eagerness that the hijab would be revealed. She said: Then Allah revealed the hijab.
[Footnote: Tafsir al-Tabari (22/28).]

That is how it occurs in this narration. But the well-known account is that this happened after the hijab had been revealed, as Imam Ahmad, al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated from the hadith of Hisham ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿAʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: Sawdah went out after the hijab had been imposed, for a need of hers. She was a large woman who could not be concealed from anyone who knew her. ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab saw her and said: "O Sawdah, by Allah, you are not hidden from us, so look how you go out." She said: So I turned back, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in my house, having his evening meal, and in his hand was a bone with meat (ʿaraq). I entered and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I went out for some need of mine, and ʿUmar said to me such-and-such." She said: Then Allah revealed to him, and when that revelation was lifted from him, the bone was still in his hand, he had not put it down. He said: "Indeed it has been permitted for you to go out for your needs." This is the wording of al-Bukhari.
[Footnote: Musnad Ahmad (6/56); Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4795; Sahih Muslim, no. 2170.]

Tafsir Ibn Kathir on Surah al-Ahzab, verses 53–54 (part 2 of 2)

So His saying: ﴿Do not enter the houses of the Prophet﴾ prohibits the believers from entering the dwellings of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ without permission, as they used to do in their houses during the Jahiliyyah (the Age of Ignorance) and at the beginning of Islam. Then Allah became jealous (ghara) for this Ummah and commanded them regarding this, and that is part of His honouring this Ummah. For this reason the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Beware of entering upon women" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (5232), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2172), from the hadith of Uqbah ibn Amir, may Allah be pleased with him.]].

Then He made an exception from this, saying: ﴿Except when you are given permission for a meal, without waiting for its preparation (ghayra nazirina inahu).﴾

Mujahid, Qatadah and others said: that is, without anticipating its being cooked and ready; i.e., do not watch for the food until, when it is nearly ready, you present yourselves for entry. This is because Allah dislikes and censures such conduct. This is evidence for the prohibition of tatfil (gate-crashing or uninvited sponging on others' food), which the Arabs call al-Dayfan, and al-Khatib al-Baghdadi (al-Khatib al-Baghdadi) authored a book on this subject, condemning the tufayliyyun (gate-crashers), and he mentioned from their reports many things whose citation would be lengthy.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿But when you are invited, then enter; and when you have eaten, disperse﴾. In Sahih Muslim, from Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When one of you invites his brother, let him accept, whether it is a wedding feast or otherwise" [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1429).]]. Its origin is in the two Sahihs, and also in the Sahih, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "If I were invited to a foreleg (dhira') I would accept, and if a shank (kura') were presented to me I would accept it. When you have finished what you were invited to, lighten the burden on the people of the house and disperse through the land" [[In Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (5768), from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.]].

For this reason He said: ﴿Nor seeking to remain for conversation﴾, i.e., as occurred with those three men whom conversation carried away, so that they forgot themselves, until that troubled the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, that was troubling the Prophet, and he is shy of you﴾ [[Followed in A by: "But Allah is not shy of the truth."]].

It was also said: the meaning is that your entering his home without his permission used to distress him and cause him harm, but he disliked to forbid them from that out of his great modesty (may peace be upon him), until Allah sent down the prohibition concerning it. For this reason He said: ﴿And Allah is not shy of the truth﴾, i.e., for this reason He forbade you from that and restrained you from it.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a screen﴾. That is: just as I forbade you to enter upon them, likewise do not look at them at all. Even if one of you has a need he wishes to obtain from them, let him not look at them, and let him not ask them for any need except from behind a screen.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: My father related to us, Ibn Abi Umar related to us, Sufyan related to us, from Mis'ar, from Musa ibn Abi Kathir, from Mujahid, from Aishah, who said: I was eating hays (a mixture of dates, butter and cheese) with the Prophet ﷺ from a wooden bowl, when Umar passed by and he called him, and his finger touched my finger. He said: "Hass" (or "Awwih") — "If he were obeyed regarding you (women), no eye would see you." Then the screen (hijab) was revealed [[Also narrated by al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (11419), by way of Zakariyya ibn Yahya from Ibn Abi Umar, with the same chain.]].

﴿That is purer for your hearts and their hearts﴾: that is, this which I have commanded you and legislated for you regarding the hijab is purer and more wholesome.

* *

His saying: ﴿And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah, nor to marry his wives after him, ever. Indeed, that would be an enormity in the sight of Allah﴾. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: Ali ibn al-Husayn related to us, Muhammad ibn Abi Hammad related to us, Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah﴾, he said: It was revealed concerning a man who intended to marry one of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ. A man said to Sufyan: Was it Aishah? He said: They have mentioned that.

Likewise said Muqatil ibn Hayyan and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam. And he mentioned with his chain from al-Suddi that the one who resolved upon that was Talhah ibn Ubaid Allah, may Allah be pleased with him, until the warning against that prohibition was revealed. For this reason the scholars are unanimous that whoever among the wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed away while married to him, it is forbidden for anyone else to marry her after him, because they are his wives in this world and the Hereafter and the Mothers of the Believers, as has already been mentioned. They differed concerning one who consummated marriage with a woman and then divorced her during his lifetime: is it lawful for another to marry her? There are two opinions, the basis of which is: does she fall under the generality of His saying ﴿after him﴾ or not? As for one who married her and then divorced her before consummation, we know of no dispute regarding its being lawful for another in such a case, and Allah knows best.

Ibn Jarir narrated: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to me, Abd al-Wahhab related to us, Dawud related to us, from Amir: that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ died while he had taken Qaylah daughter of al-Ash'ath (i.e., Ibn Qays) as a wife, and Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl married her after that, which caused Abu Bakr great distress. Umar said to him: "O Caliph of the Messenger of Allah, she is not among his wives; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not give her the choice, nor did he veil her, and Allah has cleared her of him through the apostasy she committed along with her people." He said: Abu Bakr was reassured and calmed, may Allah be pleased with them both [[Tafsir al-Tabari (22/29).]].

Allah, may He be blessed and exalted, has magnified this and emphasized it and threatened for it by His saying: ﴿Indeed, that would be an enormity in the sight of Allah﴾. Then He said: ﴿Whether you show a thing or conceal it, indeed Allah is ever Knowing of all things﴾, i.e., whatever your hearts harbour and your inner selves conceal, Allah knows it, for nothing is hidden from Him: ﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal﴾ [Ghafir: 19].

When Allah, the Exalted, commanded the women to observe hijab before non-mahram men, He made clear that these relatives are not required to be veiled from. He excepted them in Surah al-Nur, at His words: ﴿And not reveal their adornment except to their husbands, or their fathers, or the fathers of their husbands, or their sons, or the sons of their husbands, or their brothers, or the sons of their brothers, or the sons of their sisters, or their women﴾, up to its end [an-Nur: 31], and that passage contains additions beyond these. Its tafsir and discussion have already been given earlier, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary. Some of the al-salaf (the early pious predecessors) asked: "Why are the paternal uncle and the maternal uncle not mentioned in these two verses?" Ikrimah and al-Sha'bi answered: "They are not mentioned because they may describe the woman to their sons."

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Hajjaj ibn Minhal narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Dawud narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi and Ikrimah, concerning His words: ﴿There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers, nor their sons, nor their brothers, nor the sons of their brothers, nor the sons of their sisters, nor their women, nor those whom their right hands possess﴾. I said: "What about the paternal uncle and the maternal uncle, that they were not mentioned?" They said: "They both [[In manuscript A: "because they both".]] describe her to their sons. And she disliked to remove her khimar (headcovering) in front of her maternal uncle and her paternal uncle."

* *

As for His words: ﴿nor their women﴾, it means: there is no requirement to veil from believing women.

* *

As for His words: ﴿nor those whom their right hands possess﴾, it means: their male and female slaves, as was previously pointed out, and the narration on this has been cited [[Citing the hadith's takhrij was presented at the tafsir of verse 31 of Surah al-Nur.]].

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: It refers only to the female slaves (imaa'). Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, Witness﴾, meaning: fear Him in privacy and in public, for He is a Witness over everything; nothing is hidden from Him. So be watchful of the Watcher.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 33, verse 56 (part 1 of 7):

Al-Bukhari said: Abu al-'Aliyah said: "The prayer (salah) of Allah is His praise of him before the angels, and the prayer of the angels is supplication." Ibn 'Abbas said: "Yusalluna" means "yubarrikun" (they bless). Al-Bukhari transmitted this as a suspended report (mu'allaq) from both of them. [[Sahih al-Bukhari (8/532) "Fath".]]

Abu Ja'far al-Razi narrated it from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, in the same way, and something similar was also narrated from al-Rabi'. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas exactly as he said, and Ibn Abi Hatim recorded both.

Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi said: It was narrated from Sufyan al-Thawri and others of the scholars that they said: "The prayer of the Lord is mercy, and the prayer of the angels is seeking forgiveness."

Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: Amr al-Awdi narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, who said: al-A'mash said, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, regarding ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet﴾: "His prayer, blessed and exalted is He, is: Subbuh, Quddus, my mercy has preceded my wrath."

The purpose of this verse is that Allah, glorified is He, informed His servants of the rank of His servant and Prophet with Him in the Highest Assembly, that He praises him before the nearest angels, and that the angels send blessings upon him. Then Allah, exalted is He, commanded the inhabitants of the lower world to send blessings and salutations upon him, so that praise of him would be gathered from the inhabitants of both the upper and lower worlds together.

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ashath ibn Ishaq, from Ja'far – meaning Ibn al-Mughirah – from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: that the Children of Israel said to Musa, peace be upon him: "Does your Lord pray?" So his Lord called out to him: "O Musa, they have asked you: 'Does your Lord pray?' Then say: Yes, indeed I and My angels send blessings upon My prophets and My messengers." So Allah, mighty and majestic is He, revealed to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and greet him with complete greeting.﴾

He has informed that He, glorified and exalted is He, sends blessings upon His believing servants in His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, remember Allah with much remembrance and glorify Him morning and evening. It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels, that He may bring you out from darkness into light. And ever is He to the believers Merciful.﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 41-43]. And He said: ﴿And give good tidings to the patient, who, when disaster strikes them, say: "Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return." Those are the ones upon whom are blessings from their Lord and mercy, and those are the rightly guided.﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 155-157]. And in a hadith: "Indeed Allah and His angels send blessings upon the right sides of the rows." And in another hadith: "O Allah, send blessings upon the family of Abu Awfa." And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the wife of Jabir – when she had asked him to pray for her and her husband – "May Allah bless you, and your husband [[In F and A: "and the family of your husband".]] [[Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (3/398) and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, no. (1951) "Mawarid", through al-Aswad ibn Qays from Nubayh al-'Anazi from Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him.]]."

Mutawatir hadiths have come from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning the command to send blessings upon him and the manner of sending blessings upon him, and we will mention from them, God willing, what is easily available, and Allah is the One sought for help.

Al-Bukhari said – when interpreting this verse [[In T: "Al-Bukhari narrated in his Sahih."]] –: Sa'id ibn Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Mis'ar, from al-Hakam, from Ibn Abi Layla, from Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah, who said: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, as for the greeting upon you, we already know it, so how is the prayer (upon you)?" He said: "Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, [as You sent blessings upon the family of Ibrahim, indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad] [[Addition from T, F and al-Bukhari.]] as You blessed the family of Ibrahim, indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4797).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us [[In T: "Imam Ahmad also narrated with his chain."]], from al-Hakam, who said: I heard Ibn Abi Layla say: Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah met me and said: "Shall I give you a gift? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us and we said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we know – or: we have recognised – how to greet you, so how is the prayer?' He said: 'Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon [the family of] [[Addition from T, F and the Musnad.]] Ibrahim, indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed the family of Ibrahim, indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.'"

This hadith has been recorded by the compilers in their books through multiple chains, from al-Hakam – and he is Ibn 'Utbah [[In A: "'Uyaynah".]] – Al-Bukhari added: and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Isa, both of them from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, and he mentioned it [[Musnad (4/241), Sahih al-Bukhari nos. (3370), (6357) and (4797), Sahih Muslim no. (406), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (976), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (483), Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/47), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (904).]].

Ibn Abi Hatim [[In A: "Al-Bukhari said."]] said: al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah narrated to us, Hushaym ibn Bashir narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, narrated to us 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah, who said: When this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and greet him with complete greeting.﴾ He said: We said: "O Messenger of Allah, we already know the greeting [[In T, F, A: "the greeting upon you".]], so how is the prayer upon you?" He said: "Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim and upon the family of Ibrahim, indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. And bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim. Indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious." And 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla used to say: "And upon us along with them."

al-Tirmidhi narrated it with this addition. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (483), and he said: "Hasan sahih."]]

The meaning of their words, "As for the greeting upon you, we already know it," refers to the tashahhud which he used to teach them, just as he used to teach them a surah of the Qur'an. In it: "Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings."

Another hadith: al-Bukhari said: 'Abd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us, al-Layth narrated to us, from Ibn al-Had, from 'Abd Allah ibn Khabbab, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: We said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is the greeting [[In A: "This is the greeting upon you."]], so how should we send blessings upon you?" He said: "Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad, Your servant and Your messenger, as You sent blessings upon the family of Ibrahim. And bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed the family of Ibrahim." [And in a narration] [[Addition from T.]]: Abu Salih said, from al-Layth: "upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed the family of Ibrahim."

Ibrahim ibn Hamzah narrated to us, Ibn Abi Hazim and al-Darawardi narrated to us, from Yazid – meaning Ibn al-Had – he said: "As You sent blessings upon Ibrahim, and bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim."

al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah also recorded it from the hadith of Ibn al-Had, with it. [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4798).]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: I read to 'Abd al-Rahman: Malik, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, from his father, from 'Amr ibn Sulaym, that he said: Abu Humayd al-Sa'idi informed me that they said: "O Messenger of Allah, how should we send blessings upon you?" He said: "Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad, and his wives and his descendants, as You sent blessings upon [the family of] [[Addition from T, F, A and the Musnad.]] Ibrahim, and bless Muhammad and his wives and his descendants, as You blessed the family of Ibrahim, indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious."

The rest of the compilers, except al-Tirmidhi, also recorded it from the hadith of Malik, with it. [[Musnad (5/424), Sahih al-Bukhari no. (3369), Sahih Muslim no. (407), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (979), Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/49), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (905).]]

Another hadith: Muslim said: Yahya al-Tamimi narrated to us, he said: I read to Malik, from Nu'aym ibn 'Abd Allah al-Mujammar, that Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Zayd al-Ansari informed me – he said: and 'Abd Allah ibn Zayd is the one who was shown the call to prayer – he informed him from Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us while we were in the assembly of Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah, and Bashir ibn Sa'd said to him: "Allah has commanded us to send blessings upon you [O Messenger of Allah], so how should we send blessings upon you?" He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained silent until we wished he had not asked him. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad, and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon the family of Ibrahim, and bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed the family of Ibrahim among the worlds, indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. And the greeting is as you already know."

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i also recorded it from the hadith of Malik, with it. [[Sahih Muslim no. (405), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (980), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3220), and Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/45).]] al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan sahih.

Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Khuzaymah, Ibn Hibban and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak narrated, from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Taymi, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Zayd ibn 'Abd Rabbih, from Abu Mas'ud al-Badri, that they said: "O Messenger of Allah, as for the greeting, we already know it, so how should we send blessings upon you when we pray in our prayer?" He said: "Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad..." and he mentioned it. [[Musnad (4/119), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (981), al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (9877), and al-Mustadrak (1/668), where al-Hakim said: "This is a hadith sahih according to the condition of Muslim."]]

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, commentary on Surah 33, verse 56 (part 2 of 7):

Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, also narrated it in his *Musnad*, from Abu Hurayrah, with the same wording.[[*Musnad al-Shafi'i*, no. (268), *Bada'i' al-Minan* edition. Al-Nasa'i narrated it in *al-Sunan al-Kubra*, no. (9875), through Dawud ibn Qays, from Nu'aym ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]] From this, al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, held that it is obligatory for the one praying to send blessings upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the final sitting (*tashahhud*), and that if he omits it, his prayer is not valid. Some later Malikis and others have criticized al-Shafi'i for making this a condition of the prayer, claiming that he stood alone in this view. Abu Ja'far al-Tabari, al-Tahawi, al-Khattabi and others reported a consensus against him, as transmitted by al-Qadi 'Iyad. But this speaker went too far in rejecting al-Shafi'i and overreached in claiming a consensus on the matter, saying what he had no knowledge of. We have indeed narrated that it is obligatory, and that the command to send blessings upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in prayer is as the apparent meaning of the verse indicates. It is also explained by this hadith from a group of the Companions, among them Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Mas'ud al-Badri, and Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah; and from the Successors: al-Sha'bi, Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan. Al-Shafi'i held this view, with no disagreement from him or from his companions. Ahmad also adopted this view in his final opinion, as reported from him by Abu Zur'ah al-Dimashqi. Ishaq ibn Rahawayh said the same, as did the jurist and imam Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, known as Ibn al-Mawwaz the Maliki, may Allah have mercy on them all. Indeed, some imams of the Hanbalis held that one must say in the prayer upon him (ﷺ) what he taught them when they asked him. And some of our companions held that the blessings upon the family (*al-al*) are obligatory, as reported by al-Bandaniji, Sulaym al-Razi, and his companion Nasr ibn Ibrahim al-Maqdisi. Imam al-Haramayn and his companion al-Ghazali transmitted this as an opinion from al-Shafi'i. The correct view is that it is a position (*wajh*) within the school, while the majority hold the opposite and report a consensus against it. The view that it is obligatory is supported by the apparent meanings of the hadith. And Allah knows best.

The point is that al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, held that sending blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ) in prayer is obligatory, as his predecessors and successors held, as has been mentioned. To Allah belongs praise and grace. Therefore there is no consensus against him on this issue, neither in earlier nor later times. And Allah knows best.

Among what supports this is another hadith, narrated by Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi (who graded it sound), al-Nasa'i, Ibn Khuzaymah, and Ibn Hibban in their *Sahihs*, through Haywah ibn Shurayh al-Misri, from Abu Hani' Humayd ibn Hani', from 'Amr ibn Malik Abu 'Ali al-Janbi, from Fadalah ibn 'Ubayd, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard a man supplicating in his prayer without glorifying Allah or sending blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This one is hasty." Then he called him and said to him and to others: "When one of you prays, let him begin by praising Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and extolling Him, then let him send blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ), then let him supplicate with whatever he wishes."[[*Musnad* (6/18); *Sunan Abi Dawud*, no. (1481); *Sunan al-Tirmidhi*, no. (3477); *Sunan al-Nasa'i* (3/44).]]

Similarly, the hadith narrated by Ibn Majah, through 'Abd al-Muhaymin ibn 'Abbas ibn Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "There is no prayer for one who has no ablution, and no ablution for one who does not mention the name of Allah over it, and there is no prayer for one who does not send blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ), and there is no prayer for one who does not love the Ansar."[[*Sunan Ibn Majah*, no. (400). Al-Busiri said in *al-Zawa'id* (1/167): "This chain is weak, because they agree that 'Abd al-Muhaymin is weak."]]

However, this 'Abd al-Muhaymin is *matruk* (abandoned, i.e., a narrator whose narrations are rejected). It was also narrated by al-Tabarani through his brother "Ubayy ibn 'Abbas," but there is scrutiny regarding that.[[*al-Mu'jam al-Kabir* of al-Tabarani (6/121).]] It is known only through the narration of "'Abd al-Muhaymin." And Allah knows best.

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Isma'il informed us, from Abu Dawud al-A'ma, from Buraydah, who said: We said, "O Messenger of Allah, we know how to greet you with peace, but how should we send blessings upon you?" He said: "Say: 'O Allah, send Your blessings, mercy, and blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent them upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim. Indeed You are Praiseworthy and Glorious.'"

Abu Dawud al-A'ma, his name is Nufay' ibn al-Harith, and he is *matruk*.[[*Musnad* (5/353).]]

Another hadith, a *mawquf* (a report traced to a Companion, not the Prophet): We narrated it through the chains of Sa'id ibn Mansur, Zayd ibn al-Hubab, and Yazid ibn Harun, all three from Nuh ibn Qays: Salamah al-Kindi narrated to us that 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, used to teach people this supplication: "O Allah, Spreader of the spread (earth), Creator of the raised (heavens), and Compeller of hearts upon their nature, wretched and happy. Make the most noble of Your blessings, the most abundant of Your blessings, and the tenderest of Your compassion, upon Muhammad, Your servant and Messenger, the Seal of what came before, the Opener of what was closed, the Proclaimer of truth through truth, the Crusher of the assaults of falsehoods, as he was entrusted, so he rose to Your command in obedience to You, striving for Your pleasure, not faltering in step nor weakening in resolve, attentive to Your revelation, guarding Your covenant, persisting in the execution of Your command, until he kindled a flame for the seeker. The blessings of Allah reach his people through him. Through him hearts were guided after the immersion in trials and sin, and he established the clear signs, the shining lights of Islam, and the luminous rulings. He is Your trustworthy, entrusted one, the treasurer of Your hidden knowledge, Your witness on the Day of Religion, Your sent one as a blessing, and Your Messenger with truth as a mercy. O Allah, widen for him wide expanses in Your justice, and reward him with multiplied good from Your grace; pleasant gifts for him, undisturbed, from the success of Your reward that is continuous and from Your abundant bounty that is complete. O Allah, raise his building above the buildings of the builders, honor his abode and his lodging with You, complete his light for him, and reward him for his being sent with an accepted testimony, a pleased speech, a just word, a decisive address, a great proof and evidence."[[Abu Nu'aym narrated it in *'Awali Sa'id ibn Mansur*, no. (18), saying: Sulayman ibn Ahmad narrated to us, Mas'adah ibn Sa'd narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated to us, and he mentioned it. Al-Hunna'i narrated it in *al-Fawa'id* (10/162/b), as noted in the margin of *al-'Awali*, through Yazid ibn Harun, with the same chain.]]

This is a well-known statement of 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him. Ibn Qutaybah discussed it in *Mushkil al-Hadith*, and likewise Abu al-Husayn Ahmad ibn Faris the linguist in a treatise he compiled on the virtue of sending blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ), though its chain has problems.

Our shaykh, the hafiz Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi, said: Salamah al-Kindi is not well known, and he did not meet 'Ali. Thus he said. But the hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani narrated this report from Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Sa'igh, from Sa'id ibn Mansur, who said: Nuh ibn Qays narrated to us, from Salamah al-Kindi, who said: 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, used to teach us the blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ), saying: "O Allah, Spreader of the spread (earth)," and he mentioned it.[[*al-Mu'jam al-Awsat*, no. (4653), *Majma' al-Bahrayn*; but there it reads: "Mas'adah ibn Sa'd narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated to us," so perhaps the hafiz transmitted it here from *Musnad al-'Ashara*. Salamah al-Kindi was mentioned by al-Bukhari in *al-Tarikh al-Kabir* (4/195) and by Ibn Abi Hatim in *al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil* (4/300), and Ibn Abi Hatim pointed to this hadith and said: "Mursal" (a report where the Successor omits the Companion).]]

Another *mawquf* hadith: Ibn Majah said: [al-Husayn ibn Bayan narrated to us], Ziyad ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, al-Mas'udi narrated to us, from 'Awn ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abu Fakhitah, from al-Aswad ibn Yazid, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When you send blessings upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), perfect your blessings upon him, for you do not know, perhaps they are presented to him. They said to him: "Teach us." He said: "Say: 'O Allah, make Your blessings, mercy, and blessings upon the master of the messengers, the leader of the righteous, the seal of the prophets, Muhammad, Your servant and Messenger, the leader of goodness, the guide to goodness, and the messenger of mercy. O Allah, raise him to a praiseworthy station that the first and the last will envy. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad [and upon the family of Muhammad], as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim; indeed You are Praiseworthy and Glorious. O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim; indeed You are Praiseworthy and Glorious.'"[[*Sunan Ibn Majah*, no. (906). Al-Busiri said in *al-Zawa'id* (1/311): "This chain has reliable narrators, except that al-Mas'udi, whose name is 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Utbah ibn Mas'ud, became confused at the end of his life, and his earlier narrations were not distinguished from his later ones, so he deserves to be abandoned. Ibn Hibban said this."]]

This is a *mawquf* report. Isma'il al-Qadi narrated something close to this from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, or 'Umar, with doubt from the narrator.[[*Fadl al-Salah 'ala al-Nabi* (*The Virtue of Sending Blessings upon the Prophet*), no. (62).]]

Another hadith: Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Malik ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Abu Isra'il narrated to us, from Yunus ibn Khabbab, who said: He addressed us in Fars, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who believe, send blessings upon him and greet him with peace.﴾ Then he said: "Someone informed me that he heard Ibn 'Abbas say: That is how it was revealed." We said, or they said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have learned how to greet you with peace, so how is the blessing upon you?" He said: "O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim; indeed You are Praiseworthy and Glorious. And have mercy upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You had mercy upon the family of Ibrahim; indeed You are Praiseworthy and Glorious. [And bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim; indeed You are Praiseworthy and Glorious.]"[[*Tafsir al-Tabari* (22/31).]]

Those who hold that it is permissible to invoke mercy upon the Prophet (ﷺ) cite this hadith, as is the view of the majority. It is reinforced by the hadith of the Bedouin who said: "O Allah, have mercy upon me and upon Muhammad, and have mercy on no one with us." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You have narrowed a vast thing."

Al-Qadi 'Iyad reported from the majority of the Malikis that it is forbidden, and said: Abu Muhammad ibn Abi Zayd permitted it.

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah informed us, from 'Asim ibn 'Ubayd Allah, who said: I heard 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah narrate from his father, who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Whoever sends one blessing upon me, the angels will continue to send blessings upon him as long as he sends blessings upon me. So let a servant send fewer or more of them."

Ibn Majah also narrated it from the hadith of Shu'bah, with the same chain.[[*Musnad* (3/445); *Sunan Ibn Majah*, no. (907).]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Abu Salamah Mansur ibn Salamah al-Khuza'i and Yunus, that is Ibn Muhammad, told us, saying: Layth narrated to us, from Yazid ibn al-Had, from Amr ibn Abi Amr, from Abu al-Huwayrith, from Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out, and I followed him until he entered a palm grove and prostrated, and he prolonged the prostration until I feared, or I was concerned, that Allah had taken him or seized his soul. He said: So I came to look, and he raised his head and said: "What is the matter with you, O Abd al-Rahman?" He said: So I mentioned that to him, and he said: "Jibril (peace be upon him) said to me: Shall I not give you good news? Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: Whoever sends blessings upon you, I send blessings upon him, and whoever sends peace upon you, I send peace upon him."

Another route: Imam Ahmad said: Abu Sa'id, the client of the Banu Hashim, told us, Sulayman ibn Bilal told us, Amr ibn Abi Amr told us, from Abd al-Wahid ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out and headed toward his charity (or: his sadaqah grounds), then he entered and faced the qiblah and fell into prostration, and he prolonged the prostration until I thought that Allah had taken his soul during it. So I drew near to him and then sat down, and he raised his head and said: "Who is this?" I said: Abd al-Rahman. He said: "What is your matter?" I said: O Messenger of Allah, you prostrated a prostration, and I feared that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had taken your soul during it. He said: "Jibril came to me and gave me good news that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says to you: Whoever sends blessings upon you, I send blessings upon him, and whoever sends peace upon you, I send peace upon him." So I prostrated to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in gratitude.

Another hadith: Al-Hafiz (the memorizer) Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahim ibn Bahir ibn Abd Allah ibn Mu'awiyah ibn Bahir ibn Raysan [narrated to us], [Amr ibn al-Rabi' ibn Tariqah narrated to us], Yahya ibn Ayyub narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Umar narrated to us, from al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, from al-Aswad ibn Yazid, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out for a need and did not find anyone to follow him, so Umar became anxious, and he came to him from behind with a water vessel, and he found the Prophet (ﷺ) prostrating in a small room, so he withdrew from him from behind until the Prophet (ﷺ) raised his head. He said: "You did well, O Umar, when you found me prostrating and withdrew from me. Jibril came to me and said: Whoever sends blessings upon you from your community once, Allah sends blessings upon him ten times, and raises him ten degrees."

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Hasan (Diya' al-Maqdisi) chose this hadith in his book "al-Mustakhraj 'ala al-Sahihayn" [the Selected (al-Mukhtarah)]. (Al-Mu'jam al-Saghir 2/89 and al-Mukhtarah, no. 93. Al-Tabarani said: "No one narrated it from Ubayd Allah ibn Umar except Yahya ibn Ayyub; Amr ibn al-Rabi' is alone in narrating it.")

It was also narrated by Isma'il al-Qadi, from al-Qa'nabi, from Salamah ibn Wardan, from Anas, from Umar, similar to it. (Fadl al-Salah 'ala al-Nabi (ﷺ), no. 4.)

He also narrated it from Ya'qub ibn Humayd, from Anas ibn Iyad, from Salamah ibn Wardan, from Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadathan, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, similar to it. (Fadl al-Salah 'ala al-Nabi (ﷺ), no. 5.)

Another hadith: Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi said: Bundar told us, Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Atha'mah told us, Musa ibn Ya'qub al-Zam'i told me, Abd Allah ibn Kaysan told me, that Abd Allah ibn Shaddad informed him, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The people nearest to me on the Day of Resurrection are those who send the most blessings upon me."

Al-Tirmidhi alone narrated it, may Allah have mercy on him, then he said: This is a hasan gharib hadith (a fair, strange hadith).

Another hadith: Isma'il al-Qadi said: Ali ibn Abd Allah told us, Sufyan told us, from Ya'qub ibn Zayd ibn Talhah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A messenger came to me from my Lord and said to me: No servant sends a blessing upon you with a blessing except that Allah sends blessings upon him with it ten times." A man stood up and said: O Messenger of Allah, shall I not make half of my supplication for you? He said: "If you wish." He said: Shall I not make two-thirds of my supplication for you? He said: "If you wish." He said: Shall I not make all my supplication for you? He said: "Then Allah will suffice you for the concern of this world and the concern of the Hereafter." Then a shaykh, who was in Makkah, called Mani' (in one version: Sab'), said to Sufyan: From whom did he narrate it to you? He said: I do not know.

(Fadl al-Salah 'ala al-Nabi (ﷺ), no. 13.)

Another hadith: Isma'il al-Qadi said: Sa'id ibn Salam al-Attar told us, Sufyan, that is al-Thawri, told us, from Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil, from al-Tufayl ibn Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to go out in the middle of the night and say: "The Quaking has come, followed by the Second Quaking; death has come with what it brings." Ubayy said: O Messenger of Allah, I pray during the night; shall I make a third of my prayer for you? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Half." He said: Shall I make half of my prayer for you? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Two-thirds." He said: Shall I make all my prayer for you? He said: "Then Allah will forgive all your sins."

(Fadl al-Salah 'ala al-Nabi (ﷺ), no. 14.)

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it similarly: Hannad told us, Qabisah told us, Sufyan told us, from Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil, from al-Tufayl ibn Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from his father, who said: When two-thirds of the night had passed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would stand and say: "O people, remember Allah, remember Allah. The Quaking has come, followed by the Second Quaking; death has come with what it brings, death has come with what it brings." Ubayy said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, I send a great deal of blessings upon you; how much of my prayer shall I make for you? He said: "As much as you wish." I said: A quarter? He said: "As much as you wish, and if you increase, it is better for you." I said: Half? He said: "As much as you wish, and if you increase, it is better for you." I said: Two-thirds? He said: "As much as you wish, and if you increase, it is better for you." I said: Shall I make all my prayer for you? He said: "Then you will be relieved of your concern, and your sin will be forgiven for you."

Then he said: This is a hasan hadith.

(Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2457.)

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' told us, Sufyan told us, from Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil, from al-Tufayl ibn Ubayy, from his father, who said: A man said: O Messenger of Allah, what do you think if I make all my prayer for you? He said: "Then Allah will suffice you for whatever concerns you of your worldly life and your Hereafter."

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Abu Kamil told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, from Thabit, from Sulayman, the client of al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Talhah, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came one day, and joy could be seen on his face. They said: O Messenger of Allah, we see joy on your face. He said: "The angel came to me and said: O Muhammad, does it not please you that your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, says: Indeed, no one from your community sends blessings upon you except that I send blessings upon him ten times, and no one from your community sends peace upon you except that I send peace upon him ten times?" He said: "Yes."

Al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah, with the same chain. (Al-Musnad 4/30, and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 9888.) Isma'il al-Qadi also narrated it, from Isma'il ibn Abi Uways, from his brother, from Sulayman ibn Bilal, from Ubayd Allah ibn Umar, from Thabit, from Abu Talhah, similar to it. (Fadl al-Salah 'ala al-Nabi (ﷺ), no. 1.)

Another route: Imam Ahmad said: Surayj told us, Abu Ma'shar told us, from Ishaq ibn Ka'b ibn Ujrah, from Abu Talhah al-Ansari, who said: One morning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) woke up in high spirits, and cheerfulness could be seen on his face. They said: O Messenger of Allah, you woke up today in high spirits, and cheerfulness can be seen on your face? He said: "Indeed, a messenger came to me from my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and said: Whoever from your community sends a single blessing upon you, Allah records for him ten good deeds by it, erases ten bad deeds from him, raises him ten degrees, and returns to him the like of it."

This is also a good chain, though they did not include it (in the six books).

Another hadith: Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i narrated, from the hadith of Isma'il ibn Ja'far, from al-Ala' ibn Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever sends a single blessing upon me, Allah sends blessings upon him ten times by it."

Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan sahih hadith. In the chapter, there are also narrations from Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, Amir ibn Rabi'ah, Ammar, Abu Talhah, Anas, and Ubayy ibn Ka'b. (Sahih Muslim, no. 408; Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1530; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 485; Sunan al-Nasa'i 3/50.)

Imam Ahmad also said: Husayn ibn Muhammad told us, Sharik told us, from Layth, from Ka'b, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Send blessings upon me, for they are a purification for you. And ask Allah for me the wasilah, for it is a degree in the highest part of Paradise, which none will attain except one man, and I hope that I am he." Ahmad alone narrated it. (Al-Musnad 2/365.) Al-Bazzar narrated it through the route of Mujahid, from Abu Hurayrah, similar to it, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Bakkali told us, Uthman ibn Sa'id told us, Dawud ibn Uliyyah told us, from Layth, from Mujahid, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Send blessings upon me, for they are a purification for you, and ask Allah for me the wasilah, the degree of Paradise." We asked him, or he informed us, and he said: "It is a degree in the highest part of Paradise, and it is for one man, and I hope that I am that man."

In its chain is some narrator who has been criticized. (Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 363, Kashf al-Astar. Al-Haythami said: "In it is Dawud ibn Uliyyah, whom Ibn Ma'in and al-Nasa'i and others declared weak, while Ibn Numayr declared him trustworthy. Musa ibn Dawud al-Dabbi said: Dhu'ad ibn Ulbah narrated to us, and he praised him highly. Ibn Adi said: He is among the weak whose hadith is written." In it, as it stands, is "Dhu'ad ibn Ulbah," and that is the correct reading. See al-Kamil 3/121, al-Tahdhib 3/221, and al-Mizan 2/32.)

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Ishaq told us, Ibn Lahi'ah told us, [from Abd Allah ibn Hubayrah], from Abd al-Rahman ibn Maraj al-Khawlani, who said: I heard Abu Qays, the client of Amr ibn al-As, say: I heard Abd Allah ibn Amr say: Whoever sends a blessing upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Allah and His angels send seventy blessings upon him for it, so let a servant do this little or much. And I heard Abd Allah ibn Amr say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to us one day as one who bids farewell, and said: "I am Muhammad the unlettered Prophet," he said it three times, "and there is no prophet after me. I have been given the opening words of speech, its closing words and its comprehensive words. I have been taught the number of the guardians of the Fire and the bearers of the Throne. I have been granted a passage, I have been protected, and my community has been protected. So listen and obey as long as I am among you. When I am taken away, then hold fast to the Book of Allah, make lawful what it makes lawful, and make unlawful what it makes unlawful."

(Al-Musnad 2/172.)

**Another hadith:** Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Abu Salamah al-Khurasani narrated to us, Abu Ishaq narrated to us, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever is mentioned in his presence, let him send blessings upon me, and whoever sends blessings upon me once, Allah will send blessings upon him ten times."

al-Nasa'i related it in *al-Yawm wa'l-Laylah* from the hadith of Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, from Abu Salamah, who is al-Mughirah ibn Muslim al-Khurasani, from Abu Ishaq 'Amr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Sab'i, from Anas, with the same wording. [[al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (9889).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, Yunus ibn 'Amr narrated to us (meaning Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq), from Buraid [[In A: "Zayd".]] ibn Abi Maryam, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever sends blessings upon me once, Allah will send blessings upon him ten times, and will remove ten sins from him." [[al-Musnad (3/102).]]

**Another hadith:** Imam Ahmad narrated: 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Amr and Abu Sa'id [both said]: Sulayman ibn Bilal narrated to us, from 'Imarah ibn Ghaziyyah [[In A: "Numayr".]], from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Husayn, from his father 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The miser is the one in whose presence I am mentioned, and he does not send blessings upon me." Abu Sa'id said: "and he does not send blessings upon me."

al-Tirmidhi related it from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Bilal, then said: "This is a hasan (good), gharib (strange), sahih (authentic) hadith." [[al-Musnad (1/201).]]

Some narrators traced it to the musnad of "al-Husayn ibn 'Ali," and some traced it to the musnad of 'Ali himself.

**Another hadith:** Isma'il al-Qadi said: Hajjaj ibn Minhal narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Ma'bad ibn Hilal al-'Anazi, a man from the people of Damascus narrated to us, from 'Awf ibn Malik, from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The most miserly of people is the one in whose presence I am mentioned and who does not send blessings upon me." [[Fadl al-Salah 'ala al-Nabi (ﷺ), no. (37).]]

**Another hadith, mursal (a hadith whose isnad omits the Companion):** Isma'il said: Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us, Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us, I heard al-Hasan say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is enough of miserliness for a person that I am mentioned in his presence and he does not send blessings upon me," may the blessings of Allah be upon him. [[Fadl al-Salah 'ala al-Nabi (ﷺ), no. (38).]]

**Another hadith:** al-Tirmidhi said: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Dawraqi narrated to us, Rib'i ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May he be humbled into the dust, a man in whose presence I am mentioned and he does not send blessings upon me. [And may he be humbled into the dust, a man who lived to see the month of Ramadan, and it passed before he was forgiven.] And may he be humbled into the dust, a man whose parents reached old age in his presence and they did not admit him to Paradise." Then he said: "hasan gharib." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3545).]]

I say: It was also related by al-Bukhari in *al-Adab* from Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Allah, who narrated to us from Ibn Abi Hazim, from Kathir ibn Zayd, from al-Walid ibn Rabah, from Abu Hurayrah, raised (to the Prophet), with similar wording. [[al-Adab al-Mufrad of al-Bukhari, no. (21).]] We also narrated it from the hadith of Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, with the same. al-Tirmidhi said: "And on this topic there are reports from Jabir and Anas."

I say: And (there are reports) from Ibn 'Abbas and Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah. I have mentioned the chains of this hadith at the beginning of the Book of Fasting and at the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Whether one or both of them reach old age with you﴾ [al-Isra' 23].

This hadith and the one before it are evidence for the obligation of sending blessings upon him (ﷺ) whenever he is mentioned, and this is the view of a group of scholars [among them al-Tahawi and al-Halimi]. [[Addition from T, F, A.]] It is strengthened by another hadith which Ibn Majah related:

Jubarah ibn al-Mughallis narrated to us, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, 'Amr ibn Dinar narrated to us, from Jabir ibn Zayd, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever forgets to send blessings upon me has strayed from the path to Paradise." [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (908); al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (1/313): "This isnad is weak because of the weakness of Jubarah ibn al-Mughallis."]]

Jubarah is weak. However, Isma'il al-Qadi related it through more than one route, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Baqir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever forgets to send blessings upon me has strayed from the path to Paradise." This is a mursal report which is strengthened by the one before it. [And Allah knows best.] [[Addition from F, A.]] [[Fadl al-Salah 'ala al-Nabi (ﷺ), no. (41).]]

Others held that blessings upon him are obligatory once in the gathering, and then are not obligatory for the rest of that gathering, but are recommended. al-Tirmidhi transmitted this from some of them, and it is supported by the hadith which al-Tirmidhi related:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Salih, mawla al-Tawama, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "No people sit in a gathering in which they do not remember Allah, and do not send blessings upon their Prophet, except that it will be a deficiency (tirah) for them. If He wills, He will punish them, and if He wills, He will forgive them."

al-Tirmidhi alone transmitted it by this route. Imam Ahmad related it from Hajjaj and Yazid ibn Harun, both from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from Salih, mawla al-Tawama, from Abu Hurayrah, raised, the same. Then al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan hadith." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3380); al-Musnad (2/453).]]

It has also been reported from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), through more than one route. Isma'il al-Qadi related it from the hadith of Shu'bah, from Sulayman, from Dhakwan, from Abu Sa'id, who said: "No people sit and then stand without sending blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ), except that it will be a regret for them, and even if they enter Paradise, they will see the reward (they had lost)." [[Fadl al-Salah 'ala al-Nabi (ﷺ), no. (55).]]

It is related from some of them that blessings upon him, peace be upon him, are obligatory only once in a lifetime, in compliance with the command of the verse, and then they are recommended in every situation. This is the view which al-Qadi 'Iyad supported, after he had reported the consensus on the obligation of blessings upon him (ﷺ) in general. He said: al-Tabari [in T: "al-Tabarani"] reported that the verse is to be understood as a recommendation (nadb), and he claimed consensus on it. He said: Perhaps that refers to what exceeds one time, and what is obligatory of it is once, like the testimony to his prophethood. Whatever exceeds that is recommended and encouraged among the Sunnah of Islam and the sign of its people.

I say: This is a strange view, for the command to send blessings upon him has come at many times. Some of them are obligatory, and some are recommended, as we shall explain.

Among them: after the call to prayer (adhan), based on the hadith which Imam Ahmad related:

Abu 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Haywah narrated to us, Ka'b ibn 'Alqamah narrated to us, that he heard 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr say that he heard 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As say that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "When you hear the muezzin, say the same as he says, then send blessings upon me, for whoever sends blessings upon me once, Allah will send blessings upon him ten times because of it. Then ask Allah for al-Wasilah for me, for it is a station in Paradise which is fitting only for one of the servants of Allah, and I hope that I will be he. Whoever asks Allah for al-Wasilah for me, my intercession becomes due for him."

Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i also related it from the hadith of Ka'b ibn 'Alqamah. [[al-Musnad (2/168); Sahih Muslim, no. (384); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (523); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3614); Sunan al-Nasa'i (2/25).]]

Another route: Isma'il al-Qadi said: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr narrated to us, 'Amr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, from Abu Bakr al-Jushami, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever asks Allah for al-Wasilah for me, my intercession becomes due for him on the Day of Resurrection." [[Fadl al-Salah 'ala al-Nabi (ﷺ), no. (50).]]

**Another hadith:** Isma'il al-Qadi said: Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Layth, from Ka'b, that is Ka'b al-Ahbar, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Send blessings upon me, for your blessings upon me are a purification (zakah) for you, and ask Allah for al-Wasilah for me." He said: "Whether he narrated it to us or we asked him, he said: 'al-Wasilah is the highest rank in Paradise, which none attains except one man, and I hope that I will be that man.'"

He then related it from Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, from Mu'tamir, from Layth, that is Ibn Abi Sulaym, with the same. [[Fadl al-Salah 'ala al-Nabi (ﷺ), nos. (46, 47).]] The same applies to the following hadith:

Imam Ahmad said: Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Bakr ibn Sawadah narrated to us, from Ziyad ibn Nu'aym, from Wafa' [in A: "Waraqa'"] al-Hadrami, from Ruwaifi' ibn Thabit al-Ansari, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever sends blessings upon Muhammad and says, 'O Allah, cause him to dwell in the nearest station to You on the Day of Resurrection,' my intercession becomes due for him."

This isnad is acceptable (la ba'sa bihi), but they did not record it. [[al-Musnad (4/108).]]

**Another report:** Isma'il al-Qadi said: 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, Ma'mar related to me, from Ibn [in A: "Abi"] Tawus, from his father, I heard Ibn 'Abbas say: "O Allah, accept the great intercession of Muhammad, raise his highest rank, and give him his request in the Hereafter and in this world, as You gave to Ibrahim and Musa, peace be upon them both." This isnad is good, strong, sahih. [[Fadl al-Salah 'ala al-Nabi (ﷺ), no. (52).]]

Among these are: upon entering the mosque and leaving it, based on the hadith which Imam Ahmad related: [[In T: "And among them, upon entering the mosque, as Imam Ahmad related."]]

Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Layth ibn Abi Sulaym narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Hasan [in T, A: "al-Husayn"], from his mother Fatimah bint al-Husayn, from her grandmother [Fatimah] [[Addition from T, F, A, and the Musnad.]], daughter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered the mosque, he would send blessings upon Muhammad and greet him with peace, and say: "O Allah, forgive me my sins, and open for me the gates of Your mercy." And when he left, he would send blessings upon Muhammad and greet him with peace, then say: "O Allah, forgive me my sins, and open for me the gates of Your bounty." [[al-Musnad (6/282).]]

Isma'il al-Qadi said: Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, Sufyan [in A: "Sayf"] ibn 'Umar al-Tamimi narrated to us, from Sulayman al-Dabbi, from 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, who said: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "When you pass by the mosques, send blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ)." [[Fadl al-Salah 'ala al-Nabi (ﷺ), no. (80).]]

As for sending blessings upon him (ﷺ) during the prayer, we have already discussed it at the final tashahhud (testification in prayer), and the scholars who held that it is obligatory there include al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him. [In T, A: "with al-Shafi'i and Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on them both."] As for the first tashahhud, it is not obligatory in it by unanimous opinion; is it recommended? There are two opinions of al-Shafi'i.

And among these is sending blessings upon him (ﷺ) in the funeral prayer. The Sunnah (the prophetic practice) is that in the first takbir (the opening "Allahu akbar" of each part of the prayer) one recites al-Fatihah (the Opening chapter of the Qur'an). In the second, one sends blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ). In the third, one supplicates for the deceased. In the fourth, one says: "O Allah, do not deprive us of his reward, and do not put us to trial after him."

Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Mutarrif ibn Mazin narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri: Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf informed me that a man from among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) informed him that the Sunnah in the funeral prayer is that the imam says the takbir, then recites al-Fatihah after the first takbir silently to himself, then sends blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ), and sincerely makes supplication for the deceased. In the (other) takbirs he recites nothing, and then he gives the salam silently to himself.

Al-Nasa'i narrated it from Abu Umamah himself, that he said: "It is from the Sunnah," and then mentioned it.

This, from a Companion, has the ruling of a marfu' report (one traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ)), according to the sound view.

Isma'il al-Qadi also narrated it, from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from Abd al-A'la, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Umamah ibn Sahl, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, that he said: "The Sunnah in the funeral prayer is..." and then mentioned it.

This has also been narrated from Abu Hurayrah, Ibn Umar, and al-Sha'bi.

And among these is sending blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ) in the Eid prayer. Isma'il al-Qadi said: Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Hisham al-Dastawa'i narrated to us, Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman narrated to us, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah: that Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Musa, and Hudhayfah were visited one day before the Eid by al-Walid ibn Uqbah, who said to them: "The Eid is near, so how is the takbir in it?" Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud) said: "You begin by saying a takbir with which you open the prayer, and you praise your Lord and send blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ), then you supplicate. Then you say the takbir and do the same, then you say the takbir and do the same, then you say the takbir and do the same. Then you recite, then you say the takbir and bow. Then you stand, recite, praise your Lord, send blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ), then supplicate and say the takbir, and do the same, then you bow." Hudhayfah and Abu Musa said: "Abu Abd al-Rahman has spoken truly." Its isnad (chain of narration) is sound.

And among these: it is recommended to end supplication with sending blessings upon him (ﷺ). Al-Tirmidhi said:

Abu Dawud narrated to us, al-Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us, from Abu Qurrah al-Asadi, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, who said: "Supplication is suspended between heaven and earth; it does not rise until you send blessings upon your Prophet."

This was also narrated by Ayyub ibn Musa, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, as his own saying (mawquf). Mu'adh ibn al-Harith narrated it from Abu Qurrah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Umar, as a marfu' report. Likewise Razin ibn Mu'awiyah narrated it in his book as a marfu' report from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Supplication is suspended between heaven and earth; it does not rise until blessings are sent upon me. So do not make me like the cup of the rider. Send blessings upon me at the beginning of supplication, in its middle, and at its end."

This addition is only narrated through the narration of Jabir ibn Abdullah in the Musnad of the Imam Abd ibn Humayd al-Kashshi, who said: Ja'far ibn Awn narrated to us, Musa ibn Ubaydah informed us, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from his father, who said: Jabir said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to us: "Do not make me like the cup of the rider: when he hangs up his bags, he takes his cup and fills it with water. If he needs it for ablution, he performs ablution; if he needs it for drinking, he drinks; otherwise he pours out what is in it. Put me at the beginning of supplication, in the middle of supplication, and at the end of supplication." This is a gharib (singular, weak-chained) hadith, and Musa ibn Ubaydah is weak in hadith.

And among these: the most emphatic is the supplication of qunut (the supplication in the witr prayer). This is based on what Imam Ahmad, the authors of the Sunan collections, Ibn Khuzaymah, Ibn Hibban, and al-Hakim narrated, through the hadith of Abu al-Hawra', from al-Hasan ibn Ali, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) taught me words to say in the witr: "O Allah, guide me among those You have guided, grant me well-being among those You have granted well-being, take me into Your care among those You have taken into Your care, bless for me what You have given, and protect me from the evil of what You have decreed, for You decree and none can decree against You, and surely he whom You befriend is not humbled, blessed are You, our Lord, and exalted." (Al-Nasa'i added after this: "And may Allah send blessings upon the Prophet Muhammad.")

And among these: it is recommended to increase sending blessings upon him (ﷺ) on Friday and on the night of Friday. Imam Ahmad said: Husayn ibn Ali al-Ju'fi narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir, from Abu al-Ash'ath al-San'ani, from Aws ibn Aws al-Thaqafi, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Among the best of your days is Friday. On it Adam was created, on it he died, on it is the blowing (of the trumpet), and on it is the swoon. So increase sending blessings upon me on it, for your blessings are presented to me." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, how will our blessings be presented to you when you will have decayed?" – meaning, when you will have become old – He said: "Allah has forbidden the earth to consume the bodies of the Prophets."

Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Majah also narrated it through the hadith of Husayn ibn Ali al-Ju'fi. Ibn Khuzaymah, Ibn Hibban, al-Daraqutni, and al-Nawawi in al-Adhkar declared this hadith sound.

Another hadith: Abu Abdullah Ibn Majah said: Amr ibn Sawwad al-Misri narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to us, from Amr ibn al-Harith, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, from Zayd ibn Aymin, from Ubadah ibn Nusayy, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Increase sending blessings upon me on Friday, for it is a witnessed day, which the angels attend. No one sends blessings upon me except that his blessing is presented to me until he finishes." I said: "And after death?" He said: "Indeed Allah has forbidden the earth to consume the bodies of the Prophets, so the Prophet of Allah is alive and provided for."

This is a gharib hadith from this route, and there is a break (inqita') in its chain between Ubadah ibn Nusayy and Abu al-Darda', for he did not meet him. And Allah knows best.

Al-Bayhaqi narrated from the hadith of Abu Umamah and Abu Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning the command to increase sending blessings upon him on the night of Friday and the day of Friday. However, there is weakness in their chains. And Allah knows best. It has also been narrated as a mursal (a report in which the Successor omits the Companion) from al-Hasan al-Basri. Isma'il al-Qadi said:

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us, Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us, I heard al-Hasan (that is, al-Basri) say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The earth does not consume the body of one whom the Holy Spirit has spoken to." A mursal, sound hadith.

Al-Shafi'i said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad informed us, Safwan ibn Sulaym informed us, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When it is Friday and the night of Friday, then increase sending blessings upon me." This is a mursal hadith.

And thus it is obligatory upon the khatib (the one delivering the sermon) to send blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ) on Friday from the pulpit during the two sermons, and the two sermons are not valid without that, because they are an act of worship, and mentioning Allah within them is a condition, so mentioning the Messenger (ﷺ) within them is obligatory, like the adhan (call to prayer) and the prayer. This is the position of al-Shafi'i and Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on them both.

And among these: it is recommended to send prayers and peace upon him (ﷺ) when visiting his grave, may the blessings of Allah and His peace be upon him. Abu Dawud said:

Ibn Awf (that is, Muhammad) narrated to us, al-Muqri narrated to us, Haywah narrated to us, from Abu Sakhr Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Yazid ibn Abdullah ibn Qusayt, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no one among you who gives salam to me except that Allah returns my soul to me, until I return his salam."

Abu Dawud alone narrated it, and al-Nawawi declared it sound in al-Adhkar. Then Abu Dawud said:

Ahmad ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: I read to Abdullah ibn Nafi', Ibn Abi Dhi'b informed me, from Sa'id al-Maqbari, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not make your houses graves, and do not make my grave a festival, and send blessings upon me, for your blessings reach me wherever you are."

Abu Dawud alone narrated this as well. Imam Ahmad narrated it from Surayj, from Abdullah ibn Nafi' (al-Sa'igh), with this chain. Al-Nawawi also declared it sound. It has also been narrated through another route from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him. Al-Qadi Isma'il ibn Ishaq said in his book "Fadl al-Salah ala al-Nabi" (The Virtue of Sending Blessings upon the Prophet):

Isma'il ibn Abi Uways narrated to us, Ja'far ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Talib narrated to us, from one who informed him from his family, from Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali: that a man used to come every morning, visit the grave of the Prophet (ﷺ), and send blessings upon him, and he did from that what Ali ibn al-Husayn became known for. Ali ibn al-Husayn said to him: "What brings you to this?" He said: "I love to give salam to the Prophet (ﷺ)." Ali ibn al-Husayn said to him: "Would you like me to narrate to you a hadith from my father?" He said: "Yes." Ali ibn al-Husayn said to him: "My father informed me, from my grandfather, that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Do not make my grave a festival, do not make your houses graves, send blessings upon me and give salam wherever you are, for your blessings and your salam will reach me.'"

In its chain there is an unnamed man who was not identified. It has also been narrated by another route as a *mursal* (a report in which the Companion is omitted from the chain). ʿAbd al-Razzaq said in his *Musannaf*, from al-Thawri, from Ibn ʿAjlan, from a man called Suhayl, from al-Hasan ibn al-Hasan ibn ʿAli: that he saw some people at the grave and forbade them, and said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do not take my grave as a festival, do not make your houses graves, and send blessings upon me wherever you are, for your blessings reach me." [Al-Musannaf, no. 6726.] Perhaps he saw them behaving discourteously by raising their voices beyond what was needed, so he forbade them.

It is also narrated that he saw a man frequenting the grave and said: "O you, you and a man in al-Andalus are no different concerning him," meaning that all reach him. The blessings of Allah and His peace be upon him, always, until the Day of Religion.

Al-Tabarani said in his *al-Mu jam al-Kabir*: Ahmad ibn Rishdin al-Misri told us, Saʿid ibn Abi Maryam told us, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, Humayd ibn Abi Zaynab informed me, from al-Hasan ibn al-Hasan ibn ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with them, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Send blessings upon me wherever you are, for your blessings reach me." [Al-Mu jam al-Kabir (3/82). Al-Haythami said in *al-Majma* (10/162): "Humayd ibn Abi Zaynab, I do not know him; the rest of its narrators are narrators of the Sahih."]

Then al-Tabarani said: al-ʿAbbas ibn Himdan al-Asbahani told us, Shuʿayb ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid al-Haddan told us, Yazid ibn Harun informed us, from [in some manuscripts "Ibn Abi", but the correct reading is what we have recorded, from al-Tabarani's *al-Mu jam al-Kabir*] Shayban, from al-Hakam ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Khattaf [in some manuscripts "Khattab", but the correct reading is what we have recorded, from al-Tabarani's *al-Mu jam al-Kabir* and the books of biographies], from Umm Unays bint al-Hasan ibn ʿAli, from her father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Have you considered the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet﴾?" He said: "This is the hidden matter. Had you not asked me about it, I would not have informed you. Allah has appointed two angels for me; I am not mentioned in the presence of a Muslim servant who sends blessings upon me except that those two angels say: 'May Allah forgive you.' And Allah and His angels say, in response to those two angels: 'Amin.' And no one sends blessings except that those two angels say: 'May Allah forgive you,' and Allah and His angels say, in response to those two angels: 'Amin.'"

It is very strange (*gharib jiddan*), and its chain contains severe weakness. [Al-Mu jam al-Kabir (3/89). Al-Haythami said in *al-Majma* (7/93): "It contains al-Hakam ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Khattaf, who is a liar."]

Imam Ahmad said: Waki ʿ told us, from Sufyan, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Sa'ib, from Zadhan, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, Allah has angels who travel about the earth, who convey to me the peace from my Ummah."

Al-Nasa'i narrated it likewise from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri and Sulayman ibn Mihran al-Aʿmash, both from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Sa'ib, with the same wording. [Al-Musnad (1/441) and Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/43).]

As for the other hadith: "Whoever sends blessings upon me at my grave, I hear him, and whoever sends blessings upon me from afar, it is conveyed to me," its chain is questionable. Muhammad ibn Marwan al-Suddi al-Saghir was alone in narrating it, and he is *matruk* (abandoned as a narrator), from al-Aʿmash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ). [Al-Khatib narrated it in *Tarikh Baghdad* (3/292) through al-Asmaʿi from al-Suddi. Then he narrated with his chain from Ibn Qutayba, who said: I asked Ibn Numayr about the hadith "Whoever sends blessings upon me at my grave," and he said: "Leave that alone; Muhammad ibn Marwan is worth nothing."]

Our companions (the Shafiʿis) said: It is recommended for the one in *ihram* (pilgrim's state), when he has recited the *talbiyah* and finished it, to send blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ), based on what was narrated from al-Shafiʿi and al-Daraqutni, through the narration of Salih ibn Muhammad ibn Zaʾida, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq, who said: A man used to be commanded, when he finished his *talbiyah*, to send blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ) in every circumstance. [Al-Umm (2/134).]

Isma'il al-Qadi said: Aramm ibn al-Fadl told us, ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mubarak told us, Zakariyya told us, from al-Shaʿbi, from Wahb ibn al-Ajda', who said: I heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab say: "When you arrive, circumambulate the House seven times, pray two rak'ahs at the Station, then come to al-Safa and stand upon it facing the House, and say takbir seven times, with between each takbir praise of Allah, extolling Him, blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ), and a supplication for yourself. And at al-Marwah, the same." [Fadl al-Salat ʿala al-Nabi (ﷺ), no. 81.]

This is a good, sound, strong chain.

They also said: It is recommended to send blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ) together with the remembrance of Allah at slaughter, and they took as evidence the words of Allah, Exalted: ﴿And We raised high your remembrance﴾ [al-Sharh: 4]. Some of the exegetes said: Allah, Exalted, says: "I am not mentioned except that you are mentioned along with Me." The majority disagreed with them on this and said: This is a situation in which the remembrance of the Lord, Exalted, is to be singled out, as at eating, entering, intercourse, and other such occasions, in which the Sunnah has not reported sending blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ).

Another hadith: Isma'il al-Qadi said: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami told us, ʿUmar ibn Harun told us, from Musa ibn ʿUbayda, from Muhammad ibn Thabit, from Abu Hurayra, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Send blessings upon the prophets of Allah and His messengers, for Allah sent them just as He sent me."

Its chain contains two weak narrators: ʿUmar ibn Harun and his shaykh. [Fadl al-Salat ʿala al-Nabi (ﷺ), no. 45. ʿUmar ibn Harun is *matruk*, and Musa ibn ʿUbayda is weak.] And Allah knows best. ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated it from al-Thawri, from Musa ibn ʿUbayda al-Rabadhi, with the same. [Al-Musannaf of ʿAbd al-Razzaq, no. 3118.]

Among this: it is recommended to send blessings upon him when the ear rings (*tanin al-udhun*), if the report about that is sound. Imam Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Khuzayma narrated it in his *Sahih*, saying: Ziyad ibn Yahya told us, Maʿmar ibn Muhammad ibn ʿUbayd Allah told us, from his father Muhammad [in the manuscripts "from ʿAli ibn Abi Rafiʿ", but the correct reading is what we have recorded], from his father Abu Rafiʿ, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the ear of one of you rings, let him remember me, send blessings upon me, and say: 'Allah has remembered the one who remembers me with goodness.'"
