Its chain is strange, and its authenticity is questionable. [Al-Tabarani narrated it in *al-Mu jam al-Saghir* (2/120), and Ibn ʿAdi in *al-Kamil* (6/451) through Maʿmar with the same. Ibn ʿAdi said: "Maʿmar ibn Muhammad ibn ʿUbayd Allah ibn Abi Rafiʿ, from his father, is munkar al-hadith (weak in narration), and what he narrates is not followed by others."] And Allah knows best.

[Here is a question:]

The scholars of writing have recommended that the scribe repeat the blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ) whenever he writes his name. It has come in a hadith through the route of Kadih ibn Rahma, from Nahshal, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever sends blessings upon me in a book, the blessing will continue to be his for as long as my name is in that book." [Abu al-Qasim al-Asbahani narrated it in *al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib*, no. 1699, through Ahmad ibn Jaʿfar al-Hashimi from Sulayman ibn al-Rabiʿ from Kadih ibn Rahma.]

This hadith is not sound from many routes. It has been narrated from the hadith of Abu Hurayra, and that is not sound either. [Al-Tabarani narrated it in *al-Mu jam al-Awsat*, no. 234, through Yazid ibn Iyad from al-Aʿraj, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him.] The hafiz Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Dhahabi, our shaykh, said: "I consider it fabricated (*mawdu*ʿ)." A similar thing has been narrated from Abu Bakr and Ibn ʿAbbas, but nothing of that is sound. [The hadith of Ibn ʿAbbas has already passed. As for the hadith of Abu Bakr, Ibn ʿAdi narrated it in *al-Kamil* (3/249) through Abu Dawud al-Nakhaʿi, from Ayyub ibn Musa, from al-Qasim, from Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him; and Abu Dawud al-Nakhaʿi was a fabricator of hadith.] And Allah knows best.

Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi mentioned in his book *al-Jami li-Akhlaq al-Rawi wa al-Sami* (The Compendium of the Etiquette of the Narrator and the Listener) that he said: I saw in the handwriting of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah have mercy on him, that he often wrote the name of the Prophet (ﷺ) without writing the blessing upon him. He said: And it reached me that he used to say the blessing upon him verbally. [Al-Jami li-Akhlaq al-Rawi (1/271). He then said after it: "Other early imams have disagreed with him on this."]

[Section]

As for sending blessings upon others than the prophets: if it is by way of following, as has passed in the hadith, "O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and his family, his wives and his offspring," this is permissible by consensus (*ijma'*). The dispute only arises when others than the prophets are singled out for blessings. Some said that this is permissible, and they argued with the words of Allah: ﴿It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels﴾; and with His words: ﴿Upon them are blessings from their Lord, and mercy﴾ [al-Baqarah: 157]; and with His Exalted words: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to grow, and send blessings upon them; indeed, your blessings are a comfort for them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 103]; and with the hadith of ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Awfa, who said: When people came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with their charity, he would say: "O Allah, send blessings upon them." And my father came to him with his charity, and he said: "O Allah, send blessings upon the family of Abi Awfa." Both of them [al-Bukhari and Muslim] narrated it in the two *Sahihs*. And with the hadith of Jabir: that his wife said: "O Messenger of Allah, send blessings upon me and upon my husband." He said: "May Allah bless you and your husband." [The takhrij of these two hadiths has already passed in this surah.]

The majority of scholars said: It is not permissible to single out others than the prophets with blessings, because this has become a distinctive mark (*shi ar*) of the prophets when they are mentioned, so it should not be extended to others. So it is not said: "Abu Bakr said, may Allah bless him," or "ʿAli said, may Allah bless him," even if the meaning is correct, just as one does not say: "Muhammad said, Mighty and Majestic," even though he is mighty and majestic, because this is a distinctive mark of the remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. They interpreted what came in the Qur'an and Sunnah on this matter as supplication for them. For this reason it did not become a distinctive mark for the family of Abi Awfa, nor for Jabir and his wife. This is a good approach.

Others said: It is not permissible, because blessing upon others than the prophets has become a distinctive mark of the people of desires (*ahl al-ahwa'*), who send blessings upon those whom they believe in, so one should not follow them in this. And Allah knows best.

Then those who forbid this differed: is it of the category of prohibition (tahrim), or disliked reprehensible (karahah tanzihiyyah), or contrary to what is preferable (khilaf al-awla)? There are three opinions on this, related by Shaykh Abu Zakariyya al-Nawawi in his book al-Adhkar. Then he said: The correct view, which most scholars hold, is that it is disliked as reprehensible (karahah tanzih), because it is a distinguishing mark of the people of innovation (ahl al-bid'ah), and we have been forbidden from their distinguishing marks. And the disliked (makruh) is that concerning which a specific prohibition has been reported. Our companions (the Shafi'i scholars) said: The reliance in this matter is that prayer (al-salah) has become, in usage, specific to the Prophets, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them, just as our saying "'Azza wa jall" (Mighty and Majestic) is specific to Allah, Glorified and Exalted. So just as one does not say "Muhammad 'azza wa jall," even though he is mighty and majestic, one does not say "Abu Bakr" or "'Ali" (or another) "sallallahu 'alayhi." This is his wording exactly. He said: As for peace (salam), Shaykh Abu Muhammad al-Juwayni of our companions said: it has the meaning of prayer, so it is not used for an absent person, and it is not singled out for anyone other than the Prophets. Thus one does not say "'Ali 'alayhi al-salam." This applies equally to the living and the dead. As for one who is present, he is addressed with it, so one says: "Salamun 'alaykum," or "Salamun 'alayka," or "As-salamu 'alayka" or "'alaykum." This is agreed upon. End of what he mentioned. (al-Adhkar, pp. 159-160.)

I say: This practice has become prevalent in the writing of many copyists of books, where 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, is singled out by saying "'alayhi al-salam," to the exclusion of the rest of the Companions, or "karrama Allah wajhahu" (may Allah honor his face). Although its meaning is correct, it should be made equal among the Companions in this, for this is a matter of honoring and esteem. The two Shaykhs (Abu Bakr and 'Umar) and the Commander of the Faithful 'Uthman ibn 'Affan are more deserving of this than him, may Allah be pleased with them all.

Isma'il al-Qadi said: Abdullah ibn Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, from Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad, who narrated to me, from Uthman ibn Hakim ibn 'Abbad ibn Hunayf, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: Prayer (salah) is not valid upon anyone except the Prophet ﷺ, but one may supplicate for the Muslim men and Muslim women with forgiveness (al-maghfirah). [Virtues of Sending Prayers upon the Prophet ﷺ, no. 75, whose wording in his version is: "Do not send prayers upon anyone except the Prophet ﷺ, but supplicate for the Muslim men and Muslim women with forgiveness (istighfar)."]

He also said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, from Husayn ibn 'Ali, from Ja'far ibn Burqan, who said: 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, may Allah have mercy on him, wrote: "To proceed: some people have sought worldly gain through the deeds of the Hereafter, and some storytellers (qussas) have introduced into prayer upon their caliphs and their rulers the equivalent of the prayer upon the Prophet ﷺ. So when this letter of mine reaches you, instruct them that their prayer should be upon the Prophets, and their supplication for the Muslims in general, and that they leave aside anything other than that." A good report. [Virtues of Sending Prayers upon the Prophet ﷺ, no. 76.]

Isma'il al-Qadi said: Mu'adh ibn Asad narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, from Ibn Lahi'ah, who narrated to me Khalid ibn Yazid, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, from Nubayh ibn Wahb, that Ka'b entered upon 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, and they mentioned the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Ka'b said: No dawn rises except that seventy thousand angels descend, surrounding the grave, beating their wings and sending prayers upon the Prophet ﷺ; seventy thousand by night and seventy thousand by day, until, when the earth splits open over him, he comes out with seventy thousand angels escorting him. [Virtues of Sending Prayers upon the Prophet ﷺ, no. 102.]

[Branch]:

Al-Nawawi said: When one sends prayers upon the Prophet ﷺ, he should combine the prayer (salah) and the greeting of peace (taslim), and not limit himself to one of them, so he should not say only "sallallahu 'alayhi," nor only "'alayhi al-salam." What he said is derived from this noble verse, which is His saying: ﴿O you who believe, send prayers upon him and greet him with peace (taslima)﴾. So it is preferable to say: ﷺ.

Allah, the Exalted, says, threatening and warning those who harm Him by opposing His commands, committing what He has forbidden, and persisting in that, and who harm His Messenger by faulting or disparaging him, seeking refuge with Allah from that.

Ikrimah said regarding His words, ﴿Indeed, those who harm Allah and His Messenger﴾: "It was revealed concerning the makers of images (al-musawwirin)."

In the Two Sahihs, from the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: The son of Adam harms Me; he curses time (al-dahr), while I am time (al-dahr). I alternate its night and its day." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4826) and Sahih Muslim no. (2246).]]

The meaning of this is that the people of the Jahiliyyah used to say, "Woe to the misfortune of time (ya khaybat al-dahr), it has done such and such to us." They would attribute the actions of Allah, Exalted is He, to time and curse it, whereas the one who does that is Allah, Mighty and Majestic, so He forbade that. This is how al-Shafi'i, Abu 'Ubayd, and other scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, established it.

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words, ﴿who harm Allah and His Messenger﴾: "It was revealed concerning those who slandered the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding his marriage to Safiyyah bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab."

The apparent meaning is that the verse is general concerning everyone who harms him in any way. Whoever harms him has harmed Allah, and whoever obeys him has obeyed Allah, as Imam Ahmad said:

Yunus narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from 'Ubayd ibn Abi Ra'itah al-Hadhdha' al-Tamimi, from 'Abd al-Rahman [ibn Ziyad] [[Addition from T, A, and al-Musnad.]], from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughaffal al-Muzani, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Fear Allah concerning my Companions. Do not take them as targets after me. Whoever loves them, it is out of love for me that he loves them; and whoever hates them, it is out of hatred for me that he hates them. Whoever harms them has harmed me, and whoever harms me has harmed Allah, and whoever harms Allah, He is about to seize him."

It was also related by al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of 'Ubayd ibn Abi Ra'itah, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughaffal, with the same. He then said: "This is a gharib hadith; we do not know it except through this route."

* *

As for His words, ﴿And those who harm believing men and believing women without their having earned it﴾, meaning: they attribute to them what they are innocent of, what they neither did nor committed, ﴿then they have born the burden of slander and manifest sin.﴾ This is the clear slander: relating or transmitting about believing men and believing women what they did not do, in the manner of faulting and disparaging them. Among the most included in this threat are the disbelievers in Allah and His Messenger, then the Rafidah, who disparage the Companions and fault them with what Allah has cleared them of, and describe them with the opposite of what Allah has told about them. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has informed that He is pleased with the Muhajirun and the Ansar and has praised them, yet these ignorant fools revile them, disparage them, and relate about them what never existed and what they never did at all. In reality, they are upside-down of heart: they blame those who are praised and praise those who are blameworthy.

Abu Dawud related: al-Qa'nabi narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz (meaning Ibn Muhammad) narrated to us, from al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that it was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is backbiting (al-ghibah)?" He said: "Your mentioning your brother with what he dislikes." It was said: "What do you think if what I say is true of my brother?" He said: "If what you say is in him, you have backbited him; and if it is not in him, you have slandered him (bahattahu)."

Thus al-Tirmidhi also related it, from Qutaybah, from al-Darawardi, with the same. He said: "Hasan sahih." [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4874) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1934).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham narrated to us, from 'Ammar ibn Anas, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his Companions: "Which usury is the most grievous with Allah?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "The most grievous usury with Allah is the violation of the honour of a Muslim man," then he recited: ﴿And those who harm believing men and believing women without their having earned it, then they have born the burden of slander and manifest sin.﴾ [[Also related by al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman no. (6711) through Yahya ibn Wadih from 'Ammar ibn Anas, with the same.]]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 33, verses 59–62:

Allah, the Exalted, says, commanding His Messenger ﷺ, that he should instruct the believing women, especially his wives and daughters because of their nobility, to draw their outer garments (jalabib) down over themselves, so that they may be distinguished from the appearance of the women of the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic era) and the appearance of slave-women. The jilbab is: the cloak worn over the khimar (headcover). This was said by Ibn Mas'ud, 'Ubaidah, Qatadah, al-Hasan al-Basri, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, and others besides them. It is today in the place of the izar (wrapper).

Al-Jawhari said: the jilbab is the milhafa (wrap). A woman from Hudhayl, lamenting a man slain by her people, said:

"The vultures walk toward him, heedless, / walking like maidens, over whom are jalabib."
[al-Sihah (1/101).]

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: Allah commanded the wives of the believers, when they go out of their houses for some need, to cover their faces from above their heads with the jalabib, and to show only one eye.

Muhammad ibn Sirin said: I asked 'Ubaidah al-Salmani about the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿They should draw their jalabib over themselves﴾, and he covered his face and head and showed his left eye.

'Ikrimah said: she covers the opening of her chest with her jilbab, drawing it over herself.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Zahrani [in a: "al-Tabarani"] informed us, in what he wrote to me: 'Abd al-Razzaq related to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Khutaym, from Safiyyah bint Shaybah, from Umm Salamah, who said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿They should draw their jalabib over themselves﴾, the women of the Ansar went out as if there were crows upon their heads, from their tranquillity, and they were wearing black garments they put on.
[Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (2/101), and al-Hasan ibn Muslim related it from Safiyyah bint Shaybah from 'A'ishah the like of it; al-Bukhari also recorded it in his Sahih, no. (4759).]

Ibn Abi Hatim also related: my father told us, Abu Salih told us, al-Layth told me, Yunus ibn Yazid told us, who said: We asked him (i.e., al-Zuhri) — [in t: "He was asked"] — : Must a slave-girl (walidah) wear a khimar, whether she is married or not? He said: She must wear the khimar if she is married, and she is forbidden from the jilbab, because it is disliked for them to imitate free women, except for the chaste ones. Allah, the Exalted, has said: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers: they should draw their jalabib over themselves﴾.

It is related from Sufyan al-Thawri that he said: There is no harm in looking at the adornment of the women of the dhimmis; it is only forbidden because of the fear of temptation, not because of their sanctity, and he took as evidence the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿and the women of the believers﴾.

* *

His words: ﴿That is more suitable that they may be recognized and not be harmed﴾ mean: when they do that, they are recognized as free women, not slave-women nor prostitutes. al-Suddi said concerning the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿[O Prophet] say to your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers, they should draw their jalabib over themselves; that is more suitable that they may be recognized and not be harmed﴾ [addition from a]: Some of the debauched people of Madinah used to go out at night, when darkness mixed, to the roads of Madinah, pursuing women. The houses of the people of Madinah were cramped, so when night came the women went out to the roads to attend to their needs, and those debauched men sought that from them. When they saw a woman wearing a jilbab, they said: "This is a free woman, leave her alone." And when they saw a woman without a jilbab, they said: "This is a slave-girl," and they pounced upon her.

Mujahid said: They wear the jilbab so that it is known that they are free women, and so no debauched man approaches them with harm or suspicion.

* *

His words: ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ mean: for what had passed in the days of Jahiliyyah, when they had no knowledge of this.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said, threatening the hypocrites, who are those who show faith and conceal disbelief: ﴿And those in whose hearts is a disease﴾. 'Ikrimah and others said: they are the fornicators here. ﴿And the agitators in the city﴾, meaning: those who say, "The enemies have come" and "The wars have come," and that is a lie and a fabrication. ﴿If they do not desist from that and return to the truth, We will surely incite you against them﴾. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: that is, We will surely empower you over them. Qatadah, may Allah have mercy on him, said: We will surely stir you up against them. al-Suddi said: We will surely inform you about them.

﴿Then they will not remain your neighbours therein﴾, that is, in Madinah, ﴿except for a little, [cursed]﴾, a state of theirs during their residence in Madinah, for a short period, expelled and distanced. ﴿Wherever they are found﴾, that is, wherever they are found, ﴿they will be seized﴾ because of their humiliation and their scarcity, ﴿and killed, with [severe] killing﴾.

Then He said: ﴿The way of Allah with those who passed on before, and never will you find in the way of Allah any change﴾. That is: this is His way regarding the hypocrites when they persist in their hypocrisy and disbelief and do not return from what they are in, that the people of faith will be empowered over them and will subdue them. ﴿And never will you find in the way of Allah any change﴾, that is: the way of Allah in that is not altered or changed.

Al-Bukhari said, while explaining this verse: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Rawh ibn Ubadah narrated to us, Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan [and Muhammad] and Khilas, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Musa was a man of great modesty, and this is what is meant by His saying: ﴿O you who believe, do not be like those who hurt Musa, but Allah cleared him of what they said, and he was honourable in the sight of Allah﴾."

Ibn Kathir: Al-Bukhari has cited this hadith here in a very abridged form. He narrated it in the chapter on the Prophets with this same chain, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Musa, peace be upon him, was a man of great modesty and concealment; no part of his skin was seen out of shyness. Those among the Children of Israel who wished to hurt him said: 'He conceals himself in this way only because of a defect in his skin: either leprosy, or a swollen testicle, or some other ailment.' Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, wished to clear him of what they said. One day he went off alone, removed his garments and placed them on a rock, then bathed. When he finished, he came to take his clothes, but the rock fled with his garment. Musa took his staff and went after the rock, saying: 'My garment, O rock! My garment, O rock!' until he reached a gathering of the Children of Israel, and they saw him naked, in the finest form Allah had created, and Allah cleared him of what they said. The rock stopped, he took his garment and put it on, and he began striking the rock with his staff. By Allah, there are indeed marks on the rock from the blows: three, four or five." He said: "This is the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O you who believe, do not be like those who hurt Musa, but Allah cleared him of what they said, and he was honourable in the sight of Allah﴾."

This is a good, lengthy narration, and this hadith is one that al-Bukhari alone reported without Muslim.

Imam Ahmad said: Rawh narrated to us, Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from the Prophet ﷺ [and Khilas and Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ] that he said concerning this verse: ﴿O you who believe, do not be like those who hurt Musa, but Allah cleared him of what they said﴾. He said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Musa was a man of great modesty and concealment; scarcely any part of his skin could be seen out of shyness from him."

He then related the hadith as al-Bukhari narrated it at length, and he narrated it in his Tafsir from Rawh, from Awf, with the same chain. Ibn Jarir also narrated it through al-Thawri, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, from Amir al-Sha'bi, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, in similar wording. Likewise, he narrated it through Sulayman ibn Mihran al-A'mash, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Do not be like those who hurt Musa﴾: He said: His people said to him: "You are a man with a swollen testicle (adar)." So one day he went out to bathe, placed his garments on a rock, and the rock ran off with his clothes, and he went after it naked until he reached the gatherings of the Children of Israel. He said: They saw that he was not adar. That is the meaning of His saying: ﴿But Allah cleared him of what they said﴾.

Likewise, al-Awfi narrated it from Ibn Abbas in the same way.

The Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Rawh ibn Hatim and Ahmad ibn al-Mu'alla al-Adami narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Hammad narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Musa, peace be upon him, was a man of great modesty. He came to the water, I think he said, to bathe, and placed his garments on a rock, and his private parts were hardly ever exposed. The Children of Israel said: 'Musa is adar' — or: 'he has a defect' — meaning that he does not take off his clothes. The rock then carried his garments until it stood opposite the gatherings of the Children of Israel, and they looked at Musa, as the finest of men, or as he said. That is the meaning of His saying: ﴿But Allah cleared him of what they said, and he was honourable in the sight of Allah﴾."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Abbad ibn al-Awwam narrated to us, from Sufyan ibn Husayn, al-Hakam narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, [and he narrated with his chain] from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with them, regarding His saying: ﴿But Allah cleared him of what they said﴾: He said: Musa and Harun ascended the mountain, and Harun died. The Children of Israel said to Musa, peace be upon him: "You killed him; he was gentler towards us than you and more modest." So they hurt him for that. Allah commanded the angels, and they carried him and passed by him over the gatherings of the Children of Israel, and his death was spoken of. No one knew the place of his grave except the vulture, and Allah made him deaf and mute.

Likewise, Ibn Jarir narrated it from Ali ibn Musa al-Tusi, from Abbad ibn al-Awwam, with this same chain.

Then he said: It is possible that this is what is meant by the hurt, and it is possible that the first account is what is meant, and there is no saying more correct than the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

I say: It is possible that all of these are meant, and that there is something else along with them, and Allah knows best.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Shaqiq, from Abdullah, who said: One day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ distributed a portion, and a man of the Ansar said: "This distribution was not intended for the sake of Allah." I said: "O enemy of Allah, I will surely inform the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of what you said." So I mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and his face reddened, then he said: "May Allah have mercy on Musa; he was hurt with more than this and was patient."

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both recorded it in their Sahihs from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Mihran al-A'mash, with this same chain.

Another route: Imam Ahmad said: Hajjaj narrated to us, I heard Isra'il ibn Yunus, from al-Walid ibn Abi Hashim, mawla of al-Hamdani, from Zayd ibn Za'id, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his companions: "None of my companions should convey to me anything about anyone, for I wish to come out to you while my heart is sound." Then wealth came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he distributed it. He said: I passed by two men, one of whom said to his companion: "By Allah, Muhammad did not intend by his distribution the countenance of Allah or the Last Abode." He said: So I paused until I heard what they said. Then I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, you told us: 'None of my companions should convey to me anything,' and I passed by so-and-so and so-and-so, and they were saying such-and-such." The face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reddened and it grieved him, then he said: "Leave us from yourself. Musa was hurt with more than this, and he was patient."

Abu Dawud also narrated it in al-Adab, from Muhammad [ibn Yahya al-Dhuhli, from Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Firyabi, from Isra'il, from al-Walid] ibn Abi Hashim, in abridged form: "None of my companions should convey to me anything about anyone; I wish to come out to you while my heart is sound."

Likewise al-Tirmidhi narrated it in "al-Manaqib" from al-Dhuhli in the same way, except that he said "Zayd ibn Za'idah." He also narrated it from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ubaydullah ibn Musa and Husayn ibn Muhammad, both from Isra'il, from al-Suddi, from al-Walid ibn Abi Hashim, likewise in abridged form, and al-Suddi was added to the chain. Then he said: "Gharib from this route."

* *

His saying: ﴿and he was honourable in the sight of Allah﴾ means: he had standing and rank with his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: His supplication was answered by Allah. Others among the early Muslims said: He never asked Allah for anything except that He gave it to him, but he was denied the vision of Allah, as Allah willed.

Some of them said: Among his great standing with Allah is that he interceded for his brother Harun, that Allah send him with him, and Allah answered his request, and said: ﴿And We gave him, out of Our mercy, his brother Harun as a prophet﴾ [Maryam: 53].

Allah, the Exalted, says, commanding His believing servants to be mindful of Him (taqwa), to worship Him as one who sees Him, and to speak ﴿a upright speech﴾, meaning: straightforward, with no crookedness or deviation in it. He promised them that when they do this, He will reward them by setting their deeds right for them, meaning He will guide them to righteous deeds, and by forgiving them their past sins. As for what may befall them in the future, He will inspire them to repent from it.

Then He said: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly achieved a great attainment﴾. That is because he will be protected from the Fire and will arrive at lasting bliss.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Amr ibn 'Awn narrated to us, Khalid narrated to us, from Layth, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) led us in the Dhuhr prayer. When he finished, he gestured to us with his hand, so we sat down. He said: "Indeed Allah has commanded me to command you that you fear Allah and speak an upright speech." Then he went to the women and said: "Indeed Allah has commanded me to command you: that you fear Allah and speak an upright speech." (Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad (4/391) through the route of Shaiban from Layth, with the same wording.)

Ibn Abi al-Dunya said in the book "at-Taqwa": Muhammad ibn 'Abbad ibn Musa narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Imran al-Zuhri narrated to us, 'Isa ibn Sumrah narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, with his chain, from 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) never stood on the pulpit without my hearing him recite: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah and speak an upright speech﴾, and the rest of the verse. (This report is extremely strange, gharib jiddan.)

He also narrated, through the hadith of 'Abd al-Rahim ibn Zayd al-'Ammi, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, from Ibn 'Abbas as a statement of his own (mawquf), [in the copy T: "marfu'" (traced to the Prophet)]: "Whoever wishes to be the most honored of people, let him fear Allah."

'Ikrimah said: The upright speech is: There is no god but Allah.

Others said: al-Sadid is truthfulness (al-sidq). Mujahid said: it is al-sadad (rightness). Others said: it is al-sawab (correctness). All of these are true.

Allah, the Exalted, says, commanding His believing servants to be mindful of Him (taqwa), to worship Him as one who sees Him, and to speak ﴿a upright speech﴾, meaning: straightforward, with no crookedness or deviation in it. He promised them that when they do this, He will reward them by setting their deeds right for them, meaning He will guide them to righteous deeds, and by forgiving them their past sins. As for what may befall them in the future, He will inspire them to repent from it.

Then He said: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly achieved a great attainment﴾. That is because he will be protected from the Fire and will arrive at lasting bliss.

When he finished, he gestured to us with his hand, so we sat down. He said: "Indeed Allah has commanded me to command you that you fear Allah and speak an upright speech." Then he went to the women and said: "Indeed Allah has commanded me to command you: that you fear Allah and speak an upright speech." (Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad (4/391) through the route of Shaiban from Layth, with the same wording.)

Ibn Abi al-Dunya said in the book "at-Taqwa": Muhammad ibn 'Abbad ibn Musa narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Imran al-Zuhri narrated to us, 'Isa ibn Sumrah narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, with his chain, from 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) never stood on the pulpit without my hearing him recite: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah and speak an upright speech﴾, and the rest of the verse. (This report is extremely strange, gharib jiddan.)

He also narrated, through the hadith of 'Abd al-Rahim ibn Zayd al-'Ammi, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, from Ibn 'Abbas as a statement of his own (mawquf), [in the copy T: "marfu'" (traced to the Prophet)]: "Whoever wishes to be the most honored of people, let him fear Allah."

'Ikrimah said: The upright speech is: There is no god but Allah.

Others said: al-Sadid is truthfulness (al-sidq). Mujahid said: it is al-sadad (rightness). Others said: it is al-sawab (correctness). All of these are true.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 33, verses 72–73 (part 1 of 2):

Al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: "By the trust (al-amanah) is meant obedience. He presented it to them before He presented it to Adam, but they were not able to bear it [[In T: "yutiqha" (yuṭqahā); in A: "yut'anha".]]. Then He said to Adam: 'I have presented the trust to the heavens, the earth and the mountains, but they were not able to bear it [[In A: "yut'anha".]]. Will you take it with what is in it?' He said: 'O Lord, and what is in it?' He said: 'If you do good, you will be rewarded, and if you do evil, you will be punished.' So Adam took it and bore it. This is His saying: ﴿And man bore it; indeed he was wrongdoing and ignorant﴾."

And 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas: "The trust is the obligations (al-fara'id). Allah presented it to the heavens, the earth and the mountains: if they fulfilled it, He would reward them, and if they neglected it, He would punish them [[In T and A: "punish them, Allah."]]. So they disliked that and feared it, not out of disobedience, but out of glorifying the religion of Allah, that they should not undertake it. Then He presented it to Adam, and he accepted it with what is in it. This is His saying: ﴿And man bore it; indeed he was wrongdoing and ignorant﴾, meaning: unaware of the command of Allah."

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from Abu Bishr [[In A: "Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr."]], from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said concerning this verse: ﴿Indeed We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they refused to bear it and feared it﴾. He said: "It was presented to Adam, and he was told: 'Take it with what is in it. If you obey, I will forgive you, and if you disobey, I will punish you.' He said: 'I accept.' And there was no more than the time between the afternoon prayer and night of that day before he committed the sin."

Al-Dahhak has narrated something similar to this from Ibn 'Abbas, but there is scrutiny (nazar) in it and a break in the chain (inqita') between al-Dahhak and him, and Allah knows best. Likewise said Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan al-Basri and others: that the trust is the obligations.

Others said: it is obedience.

Al-A'mash narrated from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, who said: Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: "Among the trust is that the woman has been entrusted with her private part."

Qatadah said: "The trust is the religion, the obligations and the prescribed punishments (al-hudud)."

Some of them said: "It is the ritual bath from major impurity (al-ghusl min al-janabah)."

Malik narrated from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: "The trust is three: the prayer, the fast, and the ritual bath from major impurity."

All these sayings do not contradict one another; rather, they are in agreement and all refer back to the fact that it is the obligation (al-taklif), and accepting the commands and prohibitions on their condition, namely that whoever carries them out is rewarded, and whoever abandons them is punished. So man accepted it despite his weakness, his ignorance and his wrongdoing, except those whom Allah guided. And in Allah is the seeking of help.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn al-Mughirah [al-Basri] [[Addition from A.]] narrated to us, Hammad ibn Waqid narrated to us, meaning Abu 'Umar al-Saffar, I heard Abu Ma'mar, meaning 'Awn ibn Ma'mar, narrating from al-Hasan, meaning al-Basri [[In T: "Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri."]], that he recited this verse: ﴿Indeed We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains﴾, and said: "He presented it to the seven layered heavens, the ones adorned with stars, and to the bearers of the mighty Throne. It was said to them: 'Will you bear the trust and what is in it?' They said: 'And what is in it?' It was said to them: 'If you do good, you will be rewarded, and if you do evil, you will be punished.' They said: 'No.' Then He presented it to the seven firm earths, which were fastened with pegs and made submissive with cradles. It was said to them: 'Will you bear the trust and what is in it?' They said: 'And what is in it?' It was said to them: 'If you do good, you will be rewarded, and if you do evil, you will be punished.' They said: 'No.' Then He presented it to the lofty, towering, hard and firm mountains. It was said to them: 'Will you bear the trust and what is in it?' They said: 'And what is in it?' It was said to them: 'If you do good, you will be rewarded, and if you do evil, you will be punished.' They said: 'No.'"

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "When Allah created His creation, He gathered together mankind and jinn, the heavens, the earth and the mountains. He began with the heavens and presented to them the trust, which is obedience, and said to them: 'Will you bear this trust, but on the basis of bounty, honour and reward in the Garden...?' They said: 'O Lord, we are not able for this matter, we have no strength, but we are obedient to You.' Then He presented the trust to the earths and said to them: 'Will you bear this trust and accept it from Me, and I will give you bounty and honour?' They said: 'We have no patience for this, O Lord, and we cannot bear it, but we are hearing and obedient to You, we will not disobey You in anything You command us.' Then He brought Adam near and said to him: 'Will you bear this trust and keep it as it should be kept?' Adam said at that: 'What do I have with You?' He said: 'O Adam, if you do good, obey and keep the trust, then for you with Me is honour, bounty and good reward in the Garden. But if you disobey, do not keep it as it should be kept, and do evil, then I will punish you, and I will send you to the Fire.' He said: 'I am content, O Lord.' And he bore it. Allah, mighty and majestic, said: 'I have made you bear it.' This is His saying: ﴿And man bore it﴾." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

And from Mujahid, that he said: "He presented it to the heavens and they said: 'O Lord, You have burdened me with the stars and the inhabitants of the heaven and what was mentioned. I do not want a reward and I will not bear an obligation.' He said: He presented it to the earth and it said: 'O Lord, You planted trees in me, You made rivers flow in me, and the inhabitants of the earth and what was mentioned. I do not want a reward and I will not bear an obligation.' The mountains said the same. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And man bore it; indeed he was wrongdoing and ignorant﴾, in the end of his affair." Likewise said Ibn Jurayj.

From Ibn Ash'a, that he said: "When Allah presented it to them, and they were to bear the trust, they cried out to Allah for three days and their nights, and said: 'Our Lord, we have no strength for the action, and we do not want the reward.'"

Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Harun ibn Zayd ibn Abi al-Zarqa' al-Mawsili narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Hisham ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam concerning this verse: ﴿Indeed We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains﴾ [the verse] [[Addition from T, F, A.]], and that man said: "Between my ear and my shoulder." Then Allah, exalted is He, said: "I will help you with it," that is: "I will help you with your two eyes, with two lids. When they contend with you toward what I dislike, then close them. And I will help you with your tongue, with two lids. When it contends with you toward what I dislike, then close it. And I will help you with your private part, with a garment, so do not uncover it toward what I dislike."

Then it was narrated from Abu Hazim something similar to this.

Ibn Jarir said: Yunus narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, who said: Ibn Zayd said concerning the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿Indeed We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they refused to bear it and feared it﴾: "Allah presented to them the trust, that He would make the religion obligatory upon them, and make for them reward and punishment, and entrust them with the religion. They said: 'No, we are subjected to Your command. We do not want reward or punishment.'" He said: "Allah presented it to Adam and he said: 'Between my ear and my shoulder.'" Ibn Zayd said: "Allah, exalted is He, said to him: 'As for when you have taken this upon yourself, I will help you. I will make a screen for your sight, so when you fear that you will look at what is not lawful for you, then lower its screen. And I will make a door and a lock for your tongue, so when you fear, then lock it. And I will make a garment for your private part, so do not uncover it except for what I have made lawful for you.'"

Ibn Jarir said: Sa'id ibn 'Amr al-Sakuni narrated to me, Baqiyyah narrated to us, 'Isa ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Musa ibn Abi Habib, from al-Hakam ibn 'Umayr [[In T: "Ibn Jarir narrated with his chain to."]] — and he was one of the companions of the Prophet ﷺ — who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed the trust and the faithfulness descended upon the children of Adam with the prophets, so they were sent with it. Among them was the Messenger of Allah, and among them was a prophet, and among them was a prophet who was a messenger. The Qur'an descended, and it is the speech of Allah, and the Arabic and the non-Arabic descended, so they knew the matter of the Qur'an and they knew the matter of the sunnah through their tongues. Allah did not leave any part of His command, of what they do and what they avoid, and which are the proofs against them, except that He made it clear to them. There is no people of a language except that they know the good and the evil. Then the trust is the first thing that will be lifted, and its trace will remain in the roots of people's hearts. Then faithfulness, covenant and pledges will be lifted, and the books will remain. So there is a scholar who acts, and an ignorant one who knows it and denies it and does not bear it, until it reaches me and my community. No one perishes before Allah except the one who perishes, and no one is heedless of it except the one who abandons it. So beware, O people, and beware of the whisperer who withdraws (al-waswas al-khannas), for He will test you: which of you is best in action."[[Tafsir al-Tabari (22/39), and it has a witness from a hadith of Hudhayfah narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (6497), and it will come.]]

This is a very strange hadith (hadith gharib jiddan), and it has witnesses from other routes.

Then Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-'Asqalani narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Majid al-Hanafi narrated to us, Abu al-'Awwam al-Qattan informed us, Qatadah narrated to us, and Aban ibn Abi 'Ayyash [[In A: "Abi 'Abbas."]], from Khulayd al-'Asri [[In T: "Then Ibn Jarir narrated with his chain."]], from Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Five, whoever comes with them on the Day of Resurrection with faith, enters the Garden: whoever preserves the five prayers with their ablutions, their bowings, their prostrations and their appointed times, and gives the zakat from his wealth willingly, and he used to say: 'By Allah, none does that except a believer,' [and fasts Ramadan, and performs the Hajj to the House if he is able to make his way to it,] and discharges the trust." They said: "O Abu al-Darda', what is the discharge of the trust?" He said: "The ritual bath from major impurity, for Allah did not entrust the son of Adam with any part of his religion other than it."

Thus Abu Dawud narrated it from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-'Anbari, from Abu 'Ali 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Majid [[In A: "'Abd al-Hamid."]] al-Hanafi, from Abu al-'Awwam 'Imran ibn Dawur [[In A: "Dawud."]] al-Qattan, with it.[[Tafsir al-Tabari (22/39) and Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (429).]]

Ibn Jarir also said: Tamim ibn al-Muntasir narrated to us, Ishaq informed us, from Sharik, from al-A'mash, from Abdullah ibn al-Sa'ib, from Zadhan, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "Killing in the way of Allah expiates all sins" – or he said: "expiates everything" – "except trust (amanah). The one entrusted is brought forward and it is said to him: 'Render your trust.' He says: 'How, O Lord, when the world has gone?' It is said to him: 'Render your trust.' He says: 'How, O Lord, when the world has gone?' It is said to him: 'Render your trust.' He says: 'How, O Lord, when the world has gone?' Then it is said: 'Take him to his mother, the Abyss (al-Hawiyah).' He is taken to the Abyss and he plunges into it until he reaches its bottom, where he finds it as it was. He takes it, places it on his shoulder, and climbs with it to the edge of Hell. When he sees that he has come out, it slips from him, and he plunges after it forever and ever."

He also said: "Trust is in fasting, trust is in ablution, trust is in speech, and the gravest of these is deposits."

[Ibn Jarir continues:] I met al-Bara' and said: "Did you not hear what your brother Abdullah says?" He said: "He spoke the truth."

Sharik said: Ayyash al-Amiri also narrated to us, from Zadhan, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, in similar terms, but he did not mention: "Trust is in prayer and in everything." Its chain is good, but they did not record it.

Among what relates to trust is the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad:

Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from Hudhayfah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ related to us two hadiths, I have seen one of them while I await the other. He told us: "Trust descended into the root of men's hearts, then the Qur'an descended, and they learned from the Qur'an and learned from the Sunnah." Then he told us about the lifting of trust, saying: "A man sleeps a sleep and trust is taken from his heart, and its trace remains like the trace of a blister (wakt), like a glowing ember that you have rolled over your foot; you see it swollen but there is nothing in it." Then he took a pebble and rolled it over his foot. He said: "People will rise in the morning trading, and hardly anyone will fulfill trust, until it is said: 'In such-and-such a tribe there is a trustworthy man,' until it is said of a man: 'How strong he is, how witty he is, how intelligent he is,' while there is not in his heart a grain of mustard seed of faith. There has come upon me a time when I did not care which of you I dealt with: if he was a Muslim, his religion would return him to me; if he was a Christian or a Jew, his employer would return him to me. But today I only deal with such-and-such and such-and-such."

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both recorded it in their Sahihs through the hadith of al-A'mash, with the same wording.

Imam Ahmad also said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from al-Harith ibn Yazid al-Hadrami, from Abdullah ibn 'Amr, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Four things, if they are in you, then you will not mind what of the world has escaped you: safeguarding trust, truthfulness of speech, good character, and chastity in eating."

Thus Imam Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad from Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As.

Al-Tabarani said in the Musnad of Abdullah ibn Umar ibn al-Khattab: Yahya ibn Ayyub al-'Allaf al-Misri narrated to me, Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from al-Harith ibn Yazid, from Ibn Hujayrah, from Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Four things, if they are in you, then you will not mind what of the world has escaped you: safeguarding trust, truthfulness of speech, good character, and chastity in eating." In this chain he added "Ibn Hujayrah" and made it part of the Musnad of Ibn Umar.

The prohibition of swearing by trust has also been reported. Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said in Kitab al-Zuhd: Sharik narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq al-Shaybani, from Khunas ibn Suhaym – or he said: Jabalah ibn Suhaym – who said: I came with Ziyad ibn Hudayr from al-Jabiyah, and in my speech I said: "No, by trust!" Ziyad began to weep and weep, so I thought I had committed a grave matter, and I said to him: "Was this disliked?" He said: "Yes. Umar ibn al-Khattab used to forbid swearing by trust most strictly."

A hadith marfu' has also been reported on this. Abu Dawud said: Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Tha'labah al-Ta'i narrated to us, from Ibn Buraydah, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever swears by trust is not of us." Abu Dawud alone recorded it, may Allah have mercy on him.

* *

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So that Allah may punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women, and the polytheist men and polytheist women﴾ means: the son of Adam bore the trust, which is the obligations, so that Allah may punish among them the hypocrite men and hypocrite women, who display faith out of fear of its people while concealing disbelief in conformity with its people; ﴿and the polytheist men and polytheist women﴾, who are those whose outward and inward state is upon associating partners with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and opposing His messengers; ﴿and that Allah may turn in mercy to the believing men and believing women﴾ means: and that Allah may show mercy to the believers among the creation, who believed in Allah, His angels, His books and His messengers, and acted in obedience to Him; ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

[End of the commentary on Surat al-Ahzab]

He said: 'O Adam, if you do good, obey and keep the trust, then for you with Me is honour, bounty and good reward in the Garden. But if you disobey, do not keep it as it should be kept, and do evil, then I will punish you, and I will send you to the Fire.' He said: 'I am content, O Lord.' And he bore it. Allah, mighty and majestic, said: 'I have made you bear it.' This is His saying: ﴿And man bore it﴾." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

And from Mujahid, that he said: "He presented it to the heavens and they said: 'O Lord, You have burdened me with the stars and the inhabitants of the heaven and what was mentioned. I do not want a reward and I will not bear an obligation.' He said: He presented it to the earth and it said: 'O Lord, You planted trees in me, You made rivers flow in me, and the inhabitants of the earth and what was mentioned. I do not want a reward and I will not bear an obligation.' The mountains said the same. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And man bore it; indeed he was wrongdoing and ignorant﴾, in the end of his affair." Likewise said Ibn Jurayj.

From Ibn Ash'a, that he said: "When Allah presented it to them, and they were to bear the trust, they cried out to Allah for three days and their nights, and said: 'Our Lord, we have no strength for the action, and we do not want the reward.'"

Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Harun ibn Zayd ibn Abi al-Zarqa' al-Mawsili narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Hisham ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam concerning this verse: ﴿Indeed We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains﴾ [the verse] [[Addition from T, F, A.]], and that man said: "Between my ear and my shoulder." Then Allah, exalted is He, said: "I will help you with it," that is: "I will help you with your two eyes, with two lids. When they contend with you toward what I dislike, then close them. And I will help you with your tongue, with two lids. When it contends with you toward what I dislike, then close it. And I will help you with your private part, with a garment, so do not uncover it toward what I dislike."

Then it was narrated from Abu Hazim something similar to this.

Ibn Jarir said: Yunus narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, who said: Ibn Zayd said concerning the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿Indeed We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they refused to bear it and feared it﴾: "Allah presented to them the trust, that He would make the religion obligatory upon them, and make for them reward and punishment, and entrust them with the religion. They said: 'No, we are subjected to Your command. We do not want reward or punishment.'" He said: "Allah presented it to Adam and he said: 'Between my ear and my shoulder.'" Ibn Zayd said: "Allah, exalted is He, said to him: 'As for when you have taken this upon yourself, I will help you. I will make a screen for your sight, so when you fear that you will look at what is not lawful for you, then lower its screen. And I will make a door and a lock for your tongue, so when you fear, then lock it. And I will make a garment for your private part, so do not uncover it except for what I have made lawful for you.'"

Ibn Jarir said: Sa'id ibn 'Amr al-Sakuni narrated to me, Baqiyyah narrated to us, 'Isa ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Musa ibn Abi Habib, from al-Hakam ibn 'Umayr [[In T: "Ibn Jarir narrated with his chain to."]] — and he was one of the companions of the Prophet ﷺ — who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed the trust and the faithfulness descended upon the children of Adam with the prophets, so they were sent with it. Among them was the Messenger of Allah, and among them was a prophet, and among them was a prophet who was a messenger. The Qur'an descended, and it is the speech of Allah, and the Arabic and the non-Arabic descended, so they knew the matter of the Qur'an and they knew the matter of the sunnah through their tongues. Allah did not leave any part of His command, of what they do and what they avoid, and which are the proofs against them, except that He made it clear to them. There is no people of a language except that they know the good and the evil. Then the trust is the first thing that will be lifted, and its trace will remain in the roots of people's hearts. Then faithfulness, covenant and pledges will be lifted, and the books will remain. So there is a scholar who acts, and an ignorant one who knows it and denies it and does not bear it, until it reaches me and my community. No one perishes before Allah except the one who perishes, and no one is heedless of it except the one who abandons it. So beware, O people, and beware of the whisperer who withdraws (al-waswas al-khannas), for He will test you: which of you is best in action."[[Tafsir al-Tabari (22/39), and it has a witness from a hadith of Hudhayfah narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (6497), and it will come.]]

This is a very strange hadith (hadith gharib jiddan), and it has witnesses from other routes.

Then Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-'Asqalani narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Majid al-Hanafi narrated to us, Abu al-'Awwam al-Qattan informed us, Qatadah narrated to us, and Aban ibn Abi 'Ayyash [[In A: "Abi 'Abbas."]], from Khulayd al-'Asri [[In T: "Then Ibn Jarir narrated with his chain."]], from Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Five, whoever comes with them on the Day of Resurrection with faith, enters the Garden: whoever preserves the five prayers with their ablutions, their bowings, their prostrations and their appointed times, and gives the zakat from his wealth willingly, and he used to say: 'By Allah, none does that except a believer,' [and fasts Ramadan, and performs the Hajj to the House if he is able to make his way to it,] and discharges the trust." They said: "O Abu al-Darda', what is the discharge of the trust?" He said: "The ritual bath from major impurity, for Allah did not entrust the son of Adam with any part of his religion other than it."

Thus Abu Dawud narrated it from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-'Anbari, from Abu 'Ali 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Majid [[In A: "'Abd al-Hamid."]] al-Hanafi, from Abu al-'Awwam 'Imran ibn Dawur [[In A: "Dawud."]] al-Qattan, with it.[[Tafsir al-Tabari (22/39) and Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (429).]]

Ibn Jarir also said: Tamim ibn al-Muntasir narrated to us, Ishaq informed us, from Sharik, from al-A'mash, from Abdullah ibn al-Sa'ib, from Zadhan, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "Killing in the way of Allah expiates all sins" – or he said: "expiates everything" – "except trust (amanah). The one entrusted is brought forward and it is said to him: 'Render your trust.' He says: 'How, O Lord, when the world has gone?' It is said to him: 'Render your trust.' He says: 'How, O Lord, when the world has gone?' It is said to him: 'Render your trust.' He says: 'How, O Lord, when the world has gone?' Then it is said: 'Take him to his mother, the Abyss (al-Hawiyah).' He is taken to the Abyss and he plunges into it until he reaches its bottom, where he finds it as it was. He takes it, places it on his shoulder, and climbs with it to the edge of Hell. When he sees that he has come out, it slips from him, and he plunges after it forever and ever."

He also said: "Trust is in fasting, trust is in ablution, trust is in speech, and the gravest of these is deposits."

[Ibn Jarir continues:] I met al-Bara' and said: "Did you not hear what your brother Abdullah says?" He said: "He spoke the truth."

Sharik said: Ayyash al-Amiri also narrated to us, from Zadhan, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, in similar terms, but he did not mention: "Trust is in prayer and in everything." Its chain is good, but they did not record it.

Among what relates to trust is the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad:

Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from Hudhayfah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ related to us two hadiths, I have seen one of them while I await the other. He told us: "Trust descended into the root of men's hearts, then the Qur'an descended, and they learned from the Qur'an and learned from the Sunnah." Then he told us about the lifting of trust, saying: "A man sleeps a sleep and trust is taken from his heart, and its trace remains like the trace of a blister (wakt), like a glowing ember that you have rolled over your foot; you see it swollen but there is nothing in it." Then he took a pebble and rolled it over his foot. He said: "People will rise in the morning trading, and hardly anyone will fulfill trust, until it is said: 'In such-and-such a tribe there is a trustworthy man,' until it is said of a man: 'How strong he is, how witty he is, how intelligent he is,' while there is not in his heart a grain of mustard seed of faith. There has come upon me a time when I did not care which of you I dealt with: if he was a Muslim, his religion would return him to me; if he was a Christian or a Jew, his employer would return him to me. But today I only deal with such-and-such and such-and-such."

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both recorded it in their Sahihs through the hadith of al-A'mash, with the same wording.

Imam Ahmad also said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from al-Harith ibn Yazid al-Hadrami, from Abdullah ibn 'Amr, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Four things, if they are in you, then you will not mind what of the world has escaped you: safeguarding trust, truthfulness of speech, good character, and chastity in eating."

Thus Imam Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad from Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As.

Al-Tabarani said in the Musnad of Abdullah ibn Umar ibn al-Khattab: Yahya ibn Ayyub al-'Allaf al-Misri narrated to me, Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from al-Harith ibn Yazid, from Ibn Hujayrah, from Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Four things, if they are in you, then you will not mind what of the world has escaped you: safeguarding trust, truthfulness of speech, good character, and chastity in eating." In this chain he added "Ibn Hujayrah" and made it part of the Musnad of Ibn Umar.

The prohibition of swearing by trust has also been reported. Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said in Kitab al-Zuhd: Sharik narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq al-Shaybani, from Khunas ibn Suhaym – or he said: Jabalah ibn Suhaym – who said: I came with Ziyad ibn Hudayr from al-Jabiyah, and in my speech I said: "No, by trust!" Ziyad began to weep and weep, so I thought I had committed a grave matter, and I said to him: "Was this disliked?" He said: "Yes. Umar ibn al-Khattab used to forbid swearing by trust most strictly."

A hadith marfu' has also been reported on this. Abu Dawud said: Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Tha'labah al-Ta'i narrated to us, from Ibn Buraydah, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever swears by trust is not of us." Abu Dawud alone recorded it, may Allah have mercy on him.

* *

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So that Allah may punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women, and the polytheist men and polytheist women﴾ means: the son of Adam bore the trust, which is the obligations, so that Allah may punish among them the hypocrite men and hypocrite women, who display faith out of fear of its people while concealing disbelief in conformity with its people; ﴿and the polytheist men and polytheist women﴾, who are those whose outward and inward state is upon associating partners with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and opposing His messengers; ﴿and that Allah may turn in mercy to the believing men and believing women﴾ means: and that Allah may show mercy to the believers among the creation, who believed in Allah, His angels, His books and His messengers, and acted in obedience to Him; ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

[End of the commentary on Surat al-Ahzab]
